ex: The Central Committee decision on unifying Party leadership in the anti-Japanese base areas and adjusting relations among organizations. It was adopted on 29 August and issued on 1 September 1942.
The structure adopted in 2017: the Party constitution plus four blocks of regulations on organisation, leadership, self-development and supervision/guarantees.
China's national development plan for 2006–2010. Five-year plans set economic and social targets for each period.
A list in the Decision of the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) of strengths claimed for China's national system and governance, from Party leadership to foreign affairs.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2016–2020. The article cites its call for all-round opening up.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2021–2025, the last in a series of medium-term plans.
China's national development plan covering 2021–2025.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2021–2025, issued together with the long-range objectives to 2035.
A planning standard under which residents can reach basic services such as education, healthcare, elderly care and shopping within a 15-minute walk of home.

The key industrial projects built in the 1950s during the First Five-Year Plan (1953–57), largely with Soviet technical assistance. They covered steel, nonferrous metallurgy, coal, power, chemicals and machinery.
China's national development plan outline for 2026–2030.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the fifth-year-plan cycle following the 14th.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose drafting Recommendations were adopted by the Party in October 2025.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the successor to the 14th Five-Year Plan.
The 2026–2030 period of China's national medium-term economic and social development planning.
The 2012 Party congress that began Xi Jinping's leadership as General Secretary and launched the anti-corruption and Party discipline campaign.
The Communist Party congress of 2012, after which Xi Jinping became General Secretary. The article treats it as the start of the current anti-corruption campaign.
The Communist Party congress of 2012 at which Xi Jinping became General Secretary; official texts use it to mark the start of the "new era".
The 1952 coup by the Free Officers that ended the Egyptian monarchy. The author treats it as the dividing point between the early phase and the Nasser era.
The first constitution of the People's Republic of China, adopted in September 1954 by the First National People's Congress.

zh: 关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议
en: 1981 Resolution on certain questions in the Party's history
q: 1981 Resolution on certain questions in the Party's history
py: Guānyú jiànguó yǐlái dǎng de ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
ex: A resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1981. It assessed Mao Zedong and the post-1949 period and defined Mao Zedong Thought.

Term used by Beijing for a 1992 understanding between mainland and Taiwan representatives that both sides adhere to one China. Its content and existence are interpreted differently across the Taiwan Strait.
The Communist Party of China's national congress held in October 2017, which wrote the community with a shared future idea into Party documents.
The Communist Party of China's National Congress held in October 2022. Its report called for improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
The 1973 programme to import 26 large projects of complete plant and equipment from Western countries and Japan, worth about 4.3 billion US dollars. It is named after the total sum.
Xi Jinping's speech of 17 May 2016 at a symposium on philosophy and social sciences work, which called for building disciplinary, academic and discourse systems with Chinese characteristics.
An emergency meeting of the Chinese Communist Party held in August 1927 after the collapse of the First United Front. It shifted the Party toward armed struggle.
A label used in Chinese scholarship for the move of dropping Engels's philosophy in order to keep Marx's thought intact. The article attributes it to the scientistic current.
Hegel's supreme spiritual substance, which the article presents as the core of his idealist system and the source from which he derives state and society.
In Mészáros's account, the inner limits of capital that cannot be overcome within the capital system and that ultimately require going beyond it.
The article uses absolute poverty for material deprivation and relative poverty for unjust distribution and spiritual hardship, reading both back into Marx.
The article's name for the secret of capitalist religion: abstract labour and value rule over people through the commodity form.
A term the authors use for historiography that collects isolated facts without grasping their connections, laws or essence.
A term drawn from Marx's critique of bourgeois thought, meaning an isolated, ahistorical, self-interested person. The author contrasts it with Marx's 'real individual'.
In Marx's analysis, labour considered as the expenditure of undifferentiated human effort, which creates the value of commodities, as opposed to concrete labour, which creates their use-values.
The author's term for general constructs such as religion, philosophy, the state, morality and capital. In the author's account Marx criticised them for being raised above real sensuous life.

en: Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council
q: Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council
ex: The Chinese state body that sets the catalogue of disciplines and the rules for awarding degrees. Its decisions fix which disciplines and sub-disciplines universities may establish.
In the Party's three-part scheme (discipline, academic and discourse systems), the body of concepts, categories, propositions and methods that makes up a discipline's knowledge.

A proposal to develop theology as a scholarly field within Chinese universities, including Chinese-language Christian theology. The authors surveyed oppose it as a challenge to Marxist religious studies.
Hartmut Rosa's characterisation of modern capitalism as driven by technological acceleration, social change and an increasing pace of life.
The author's label for the modern dynamic of ever-faster production, shortening labour time and quickening social life, which reinforces productivism and consumerism.

lit: public accumulation fund and public welfare fund
ex: Deductions from the income of agricultural cooperatives. The accumulation fund financed expanded production, and the welfare fund financed public welfare, health and relief for members.
David Harvey's concept, from the early 2000s, for the continuing use of privatisation, finance and state power to seize wealth under contemporary capitalism, extending Marx's primitive accumulation.

David Harvey's term, rendered in the article as predatory accumulation, for the continuing use of primitive-accumulation methods such as privatisation, financial manipulation and debt crises to transfer assets to capital.
A term from political economy for the institutional arrangement that sustains profit-making over a period. Here it refers to neoliberal, financialised, dollar-led accumulation.

en: acting with justification, to advantage and with restraint
q: acting with justification, to advantage and with restraint
py: yǒu lǐ yǒu lì yǒu jié
lit: with reason, with advantage, with restraint
ex: Mao's 1940 formula for struggle against Guomindang hardliners. It stresses self-defence, limited aims and knowing when to stop.
A military doctrine associated with Mao Zedong. It favours mobile and guerrilla warfare to destroy enemy forces, in contrast to passive, positional defence.
The author's term for free-time activity that serves all-round human development and free labour, as opposed to rest or consumption that merely restores the capacity to work.
Socialism as practised in the twentieth century and today, which the author treats as a transitional stage short of Marx's future society.

zh: 宗教与社会主义社会相适应
py: zōngjiào yǔ shèhuì zhǔyì shèhuì xiāng shìyìng
ex: The Party's guideline that religions should adjust themselves to socialist society and obey its laws, and contribute positively to it. It forms the fourth clause of the basic guideline on religious work.

zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化大众化
en: the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, the needs of our times and the general public
q: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, the needs of our times and the general public
ex: A formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions, to contemporary developments, and to ordinary people's understanding. The wording here is a close rendering of the 2016 phrasing.

zh: 马克思主义哲学时代化
en: adaptation of Marxist philosophy to the needs of our times
q: adaptation of Marxist philosophy to the needs of our times
ex: Derived from the official formula of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, applied here to Marxist philosophy.

en: adaptation to Chinese conditions, to the times and to the wider public
q: adaptation to Chinese conditions, to the times and to the wider public
py: Zhōngguó huà, shídài huà, dàzhòng huà
lit: Sinification, modernisation to the times, popularisation
ex: A formula adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 17th Central Committee (2009) for developing Marxism. The article applies it to the Marxist view of religion.

zh: 马克思主义本土化时代化
ex: A formulation, related to the official idea of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, that the article applies to foreign parties' efforts to fit Marxism to their own countries and the present era.

en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
q: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
ex: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions, first used by Mao Zedong in 1938 and now extended to “adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times”.

zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
q: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
ex: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to each historical period.

zh: 马克思主义政治经济学中国化时代化
en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
q: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
ex: The official formula for adapting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to contemporary developments.

zh: 马克思主义时代化、中国化
en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
q: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
ex: Official formula for the ongoing effort to apply and develop Marxism in light of Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances.

zh: 马克思主义时代化、大众化
en: adapting Marxism to the needs of our times and making it popular
q: adapting Marxism to the needs of our times and making it popular
lit: the epochal-isation and popularisation of Marxism
ex: A formula in Chinese Party theory for making Marxism fit contemporary conditions and spreading it among the masses. Zhou also applies it to Marx and Engels's own efforts in the nineteenth century.

lit: suit the state of mind, unblock and guide
ex: A principle of propaganda and education in which the content is matched to the audience's outlook and conditions. Listeners are encouraged to speak freely and are then led patiently toward what the Party regards as correct views.

en: addressing symptoms and root causes together
q: addressing symptoms and root causes together
lit: treating both the branches and the root
ex: A principle of dealing with both the visible manifestations of a problem and its underlying causes. In anti-corruption work it pairs punishment with institutional and cultural prevention.

Disciplinary penalties imposed on public officials for duty-related violations of law, such as warnings and demerits. They are governed by the Law on Sanctions for Public Officials and are distinct from Party discipline and from criminal punishment.
A scholarly term for the way higher levels of government assign tasks and targets to lower levels, which carry them out with considerable discretion. It is used in Chinese political sociology.
A system that grouped natural villages into larger administrative units, set in Shandong in 1941 at 100 or more households or 400 or more people. It replaced the earlier centre-village arrangement.

A concept the Communist Party of China put forward in the early 2000s, notably in the Three Represents. It denotes culture seen as fitting the needs of the era and promoting productive forces, social progress and human development.
Party-historiographical term for the educated radicals of the New Culture and May Fourth period who adopted Marxism and helped found the Communist Party.
The quality attributed to Marxist parties of being the vanguard in politics, practice and theory. Official discourse treats it as the essential attribute of the Communist Party.
Official qualities said to define a Marxist party: advanced nature refers to its guiding ideology and aims, purity to loyalty and integrity in thought, politics, organisation and conduct.
A Party term for the culture the state promotes under socialism, drawing on Marxism, fine traditional culture and revolutionary heritage.
A term in official moral-construction discourse for the higher tier of morality expected of Party members and exemplary citizens, as distinct from basic norms for all.
A group of people bound together by shared aesthetic experience, here created through theatre. The authors use it to describe the bond between theatre workers and the masses in Yan'an.
Education in aesthetic appreciation and ability, treated in Chinese policy as part of moral and cultural cultivation.
Phrase used by Xi Jinping in 2016 for making political education more approachable and better matched to students' needs.
The authors' label for the orthodox Marxist-Leninist regimes that emerged in Africa from the late 1960s, such as Congo, Ethiopia, Angola and Mozambique.
Engels's term for the period of developed division of labour, exchange and commodity production, running from slavery through serfdom to wage labour.
Mao's term in On Protracted War for the historical epoch in which China stood in the 1930s, with new social forces and international conditions favourable to resistance.
Here it denotes the independent, self-directed character of Marx's own theoretical construction, as opposed to its being derived from Feuerbach.
A communication-studies concept that media can direct public attention to particular issues by choosing what to cover. The authors apply it to the spread of Marxism.
A concept from Western communication studies, in which media shape which issues the public attends to. The author uses it for what is described as the deliberate hyping of negative incidents.
A governance approach stressing rapid response and continuous adjustment of policy tools, proposed here for fast-moving technologies like AI.
The view that the existence of God cannot be known. The article treats it as close to, but distinct from, atheism.
The Party's term for the period of about 1927–1937, when the Communists fought the Nationalist government and built rural base areas.
The Party's term for 1927–1937, when it fought the Kuomintang while building rural base areas and redistributing land.
The 1950s campaign to organise individual peasant households into mutual-aid teams and then cooperatives, and later higher-stage cooperatives with collective ownership.
The author's label for an emerging stage of digital capitalism in which production, exchange and distribution are increasingly run by AI systems.
A national initiative to integrate AI into the economy, society and research. The State Council issued an opinion on implementing it in depth, which the article cites.
A national initiative to integrate AI into industries and public services, formally launched in the 2024–2025 government work reports.
A State Council policy programme for integrating artificial intelligence into economic and social sectors, set out in opinions issued in August 2025.

lit: spirit of resisting America and aiding Korea
ex: An official term for the values attributed to the Chinese volunteers and home front in the war, such as courage, sacrifice and patriotism.

A term used by the author for the dominance that Western states and technology firms are said to hold over algorithmic technology, data and the information environment. It is used to criticise unequal power in the digital sphere.
The idea that a state should control the algorithms, data and rules that shape information within its borders and in global governance. It extends the concept of digital or cyber sovereignty.
A concept from Marx's 1844 Manuscripts: labour that, under capitalist relations, confronts the worker as an alien power rather than as an expression of their own capacities.
Marx's concept, from the 1844 manuscripts, of workers being estranged from their products, their activity, their species-being and other people under capitalism.

The process by which humans' own creations come to stand over them as foreign powers. Wang traces Marx's theory from religious alienation in the dissertation to political, labour and money alienation.
The alienation of human exchange and social interaction, which Marx discusses in the Mill Notes through money and exchange. It contrasts with the alienation of labour.

The theory of alienated labour developed in Marx's 1844 manuscripts, in which the worker's product and activity confront them as alien powers. Chinese debates ask whether the mature Marx kept or abandoned it.

en: all under heaven belongs to all
q: all under heaven belongs to all
lit: the world is for the public
ex: A classical Confucian phrase from the Book of Rites describing a just social order. The article treats it as the core of the Chinese civilizational tradition.
The traditional Chinese worldview of a culturally centred order in which the civilised centre transforms peripheral peoples through moral and ritual education.
A term for the converged media environment of integrated traditional and digital media, in which, as Xi Jinping has put it, media is omnipresent and everyone can take part in producing information.

lit: comprehensive development of the human being
ex: A Marxist idea of the full development of human capacities, social relations and individuality. Chinese official discourse treats it as the ultimate goal of socialism and modernization.
A state model based on the idea of a universal order 'under heaven' rather than a bounded nation-state. Huang counts it among China's six basic paradigms.
The slogan of putting US national interest above multilateral commitments, associated with the Trump administration. The article treats it as a long-standing driver of US hegemony now made explicit.
The idea that the United States is unique and not bound by the rules applied to other states. The article treats it as the reverse side of the "universal values" claim.

The claim that the United States is exempt from the general laws of capitalist development, so that socialism does not fit it. The article rejects the bourgeois version but also warns against over-emphasising national particularity.

en: amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness
q: amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness
ex: A principle for neighbourhood diplomacy put forward by Xi Jinping at the 2013 symposium on neighbourhood diplomacy.
A decision-making method that breaks a goal into a hierarchy of criteria and derives weights from pairwise comparisons. It includes a consistency check on the comparisons.

A school that emerged in the late 1970s and 1980s. It combines analytic philosophy and modern social-science methods with Marxism, and its figures include G. A. Cohen, John Roemer and Jon Elster. Its 'September Group' formed in 1981.

An academic community of heterodox and Marxist economists who use formal, analytical methods. It began with a 1991 workshop at Notre Dame and revived after 2007. The article treats it as the economics-side revival of Analytical Marxism.
The doctrine opposing the state, influential among Chinese radicals in the early twentieth century. The article shows it was often conflated with "nihilism".
A phrase from Chinese historiography used here for the transformation of Chinese philosophy after the Opium War, under the impact of Western thought.
A management model associated with the Anshan Iron and Steel Company, promoted in the 1960s. It stressed worker participation in management and cadre participation in labour.

A French school of historiography founded around the journal Annales d'histoire économique et sociale (1929) by Marc Bloch and Lucien Febvre. It stressed economic and social history, interdisciplinarity and long-term structures.
A proposed geological epoch in which human activity is the dominant force changing the Earth system. The term was popularised by Paul Crutzen in the early 2000s.
The usual Chinese label for Feuerbach's philosophy, which the article describes as a unity of 'natural science' (nature) and anthropology (humanity).

Here it means a philosophy that understands the world from humanity's anthropological characteristics. The authors treat it as the basis of Marx's thought, in contrast to a reading centred on economics.
Mao Zedong's phrase for the simultaneous hostility towards China from the US, India, the Soviet Union and others around 1959–1962.
A movement of the early 1920s, led by students and intellectuals, against Christianity and missionary activity. It framed Christianity as a vehicle of imperialist influence.
The Red Army's campaigns against the Nationalist government's repeated military "encirclement and suppression" drives on the Communist base areas. The fifth campaign (1933–34) ended in defeat.

The Party's policy from the mid-1930s of uniting all classes and political forces willing to resist Japan, including the Nationalists. The article links its formulation to the Wayaobu meeting of December 1935.
A 1922 campaign in which early Communists and public figures criticised religion, especially Christianity, as a tool of imperialist cultural control.
A term from world-systems theory for movements that resist the capitalist world system; the author cites Wang Zhengyi on them.
A label used in Chinese discussions for Deng's philosophical thought, stressing its use in solving practical problems rather than abstract system-building.

en: applying both the government and market hands
q: applying both the government and market hands
ex: One of the four elements of Xi's 2014 water-management approach. Water governance should combine the decisive role of the market in allocating resources with a stronger role for government.

One of four aims of the 2021 Party history study and education campaign, alongside learning history to understand principle, strengthen belief and uphold virtue. It stresses turning study into practical action.

lit: appoint people by virtue and merit alone
ex: A traditional Chinese principle of selecting officials by virtue and ability, adopted by the Party as its cadre line in 1938.
The author's label for scholarship that mainly imitates or applies foreign or Soviet theories without originality. The author treats it as a transitional stage.
Wu's term for the long phase in which Chinese scholarship learned from and depended on foreign, mainly Western, theory.

A set of doctrines, developed from the 1940s, that combined Arab nationalism, Islamic ideas and a socialist programme as a 'third way' between capitalism and communism. It was adopted in several Arab states such as Egypt, Syria and Iraq.
The wave of protests and uprisings that began in Tunisia in late 2010 and spread across the Arab world in 2011, toppling several governments.

A major archaeology programme launched by the National Cultural Heritage Administration in 2017. It covers human origins, the origins of civilization and the formation of a unified multi-ethnic state.

A field in China devoted to the in-depth study of particular regions and countries, including their history, culture, politics and society. It was formally established as a first-level discipline in China in 2022.
A field in Chinese academia studying particular regions and countries, promoted as a priority discipline in support of foreign policy.

The strategy of building armed forces and rural base areas under CPC control, associated with Mao Zedong in the late 1920s and 1930s. The article contrasts it with the short-lived armed uprising of the October Revolution model.
Small units combining military action, political work and mobilisation of villagers behind Japanese lines. The article credits Nie Rongzhen with proposing them in 1942.

en: arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
q: arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
lit: theoretical arming with the Party's innovative theory
ex: The Party's practice of systematically educating cadres, teachers and students in its latest theoretical achievements, currently centred on Xi Jinping Thought.
A principle of Chinese Party cultural policy, rooted in Mao Zedong's Yan'an talks and repeated by Xi Jinping. It holds that literature and art should be people-centred and serve the masses.

lit: technique or art of ecological-environmental governance
ex: A phrase echoing the Foucauldian notion of governmentality. The authors use it for the set of neoliberal policies and practices applied to environmental management.
Laclau's and Hall's idea that ideological elements have no fixed identity and take meaning from contingent connections that can be broken and remade.

Marx's term, used in the Introduction to the Critique of Political Economy, for art as a branch of spiritual production under capitalism. Chinese aesthetics treats it as a core concept linking art to political economy.
The 1967 policy document issued by Nyerere and the ruling party that set out 'socialism and self-reliance' as Tanzania's goal.

en: ascending from the abstract to the concrete
q: ascending from the abstract to the concrete
ex: Marx's method of presenting a system of economic categories, starting from simple abstractions and building up to the concrete whole. It was a major topic of Soviet work on Capital.

en: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
q: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
ex: Marx's method of presentation in the Grundrisse and Capital, which builds up from simple abstract categories to a concrete totality in thought. Lin uses it to reconstruct how the city develops historically.

en: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
q: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
py: cóng chōuxiàng shàngshēng dào jùtǐ fǎ
ex: The method Marx describes in the 1857 Introduction to the Grundrisse, in which thought starts from simple, abstract determinations and reconstructs the concrete as a rich totality. It is often treated as the main method of Capital.

en: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
q: ascent from the abstract to the concrete
ex: Marx's method of presentation, which begins with simple abstract categories and builds up to the concrete whole.

Marx's term for forms of landownership in Asian societies, in which the despot or state is the supreme owner and village communities hold land. It is linked to his idea of an Asiatic mode of production.
A term Marx used for a pre-capitalist Eastern social form with no private landownership, in which a despotic centre stands above village communities. Its meaning has been long debated among scholars.

zh: 宏观政策取向一致性评估
ex: A review mechanism intended to check that economic and non-economic policies point in the same direction and do not work against one another. The Central Economic Work Conference stressed it at the end of 2024.
Marx's term, used in Capital and earlier in the Communist Manifesto, for a future society in which producers work with commonly owned means of production and consciously plan social labour.
The Chinese rendering of Marx and Engels's idea of a future society in which people associate freely and in common. The author treats it as the highest form of real community.
The collective subject of planning in the article's reading of Marx: all members of society freely joined as producers, rather than a government body or particular organisations.
The denial of gods. The article presents it as the required position of Communists and as a subject for public propaganda and education.
Efforts to promote a materialist worldview and atheism. Chen treats this as central to Soviet Marxist psychology of religion, and as a task for the Party and its members in China.

A long-standing Party task of spreading a materialist, atheist worldview and countering religion and superstition through ideas and persuasion. In the article it is presented as compatible with state protection of religious belief.
A term used in Chinese translations of Marx and Engels on the Paris Commune and later by Mao for officials. It presents them as servants of the people rather than rulers.
The article's term for the audience attention that users, creators and firms can attract and convert into income, influence or social connections.
A communication approach that divides audiences into groups and tailors content to each; the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) applied it to online moral and ideological education.
A 1935 appeal drafted by the Chinese Communist Party delegation to the Comintern. It called on all classes and parties to stop civil war and unite against Japan.

The research framework in Western political science that classifies regimes as authoritarian and studies their resilience or transition. The authors treat it as a biased, ideologically loaded approach.

en: the authority of the Party Central Committee
q: authority of the Party Central Committee
ex: A formula in Party discourse stressing that the Central Committee holds unified leadership. The Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) listed institutions to uphold it.

The Italian current (operaismo and its successors) emerging in the 1960s–70s that stresses working-class subjectivity and autonomy from parties and unions. Negri, Hardt and Federici are associated with it.
The author's proposed underlying framework for classifying all knowledge, treated as a deeper layer beneath individual disciplines' knowledge systems.
A phrase used in Xi Jinping's speeches for a Chinese-originated body of social science knowledge, made up of disciplinary, academic and discourse systems.
A policy term in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, meaning opening that China designs and paces on its own terms rather than in response to outside models or pressure.

The armed uprising of September 1927 on the Hunan–Jiangxi border, led by Mao Zedong after the collapse of the first Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. Its surviving forces went to the Jinggang Mountains.
A principle drawn from the Paris Commune: party leaders and MPs receive only an average worker's pay, and the remainder goes to the party.
The authors' term for the research paradigm that, in a given period, breaks the balance among coexisting paradigms and takes the leading role.
Yuan's term for Marx's approach of analysing the most developed form, bourgeois society, so as to understand the structures of earlier social forms.

lit: Comprehensive discussions in the White Tiger Hall
ex: A Han text recording the Confucian classical debates held at the White Tiger Hall under Emperor Zhang in 79 CE. Ren treats it as completing a state religion.

en: balance learning and conduct, cultivate both virtue and vocation
q: balance learning and conduct, cultivate both virtue and vocation
py: xué xíng bìngzhòng, dé yè shuāngxiū
lit: learning and conduct equally weighted; virtue and work both cultivated
ex: Fang Keli's guiding principle for graduate students, first stated in 1982. It joins knowledge with practice and moral character with scholarship.

lit: overall planning and taking all sides into account
ex: A long-standing Party method of planning several interests or tasks together rather than one at a time. Mao Zedong used it in 1956, and it was revived in the early 2000s.
A strategic principle in Xi Jinping Thought that treats development and security as mutually dependent and to be planned together.
The ideals of solidarity, friendship and cooperation associated with the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, as the article presents them.
In Engels's use, drawing on Morgan, the stage of clan society without class oppression. The article also uses the term for the barbarous, violent features that persist within civilization.
Rural health workers with basic training who provided primary care in villages from the 1960s. They are commonly associated with the Mao-era rural cooperative medical system.
Territories behind Japanese lines governed by the CPC during the war, which served as bases for guerrilla warfare and for the Party's wartime policies.
Territories under Communist administration and military control during the anti-Japanese war and civil war, used as bases for government, production and operations.
Territories behind Japanese lines, governed and defended by Communist-led forces, which served as bases for guerrilla warfare and mobilisation.

lit: anti-Japanese base areas in the enemy's rear
ex: Territories behind Japanese lines, such as Jin-Cha-Ji, where the Party built armed forces, government and an economy during the war.
In Marxist theory, the contradiction between socialised production and private appropriation. The authors argue that financial domination sharpens it.

lit: basic institutions for the data factor
ex: Official policy term for the basic rules governing data as a factor of production, covering ownership, circulation, use and distribution.
The official description of China's economic order, with public ownership as the mainstay and diverse forms of ownership developing together, established at the 15th Party Congress (1997).

zh: 社会主义初级阶段基本经济制度
en: the basic economic system of the primary stage of socialism
q: basic economic system of the primary stage of socialism
py: shèhuìzhǔyì chūjí jiēduàn jīběn jīngjì zhìdù
ex: The official formulation of China's core economic institutions, with public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership and a socialist market economy.
The proposal that every member of society receive an unconditional income. The article presents it as an offshoot of the New Left in Korea, associated with Philippe Van Parijs.
The Party's overarching guideline for the primary stage of socialism, centred on economic development, with the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up as the "two basic points".

zh: 科学社会主义基本原则
ex: In Zhou's account these include Communist Party leadership, the dictatorship of the proletariat, public ownership, distribution according to work, and Marxism as guiding ideology.
The system built on household contract operation within a two-tier structure combining collective and household management, with land collectively owned.

zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
ex: The official term for China's system of public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work with other factors participating, and the socialist market economy.

The foundational institutional order of socialist states, in China meaning the leadership of the Communist Party and public ownership as the main body of the economy. Official texts say it must be upheld and improved.
The standard Party term for the core, lasting propositions of Marxism, distinguished from particular judgements made by the classics in specific circumstances.
A term associated with Fidel Castro for the ideological struggle against hostile forces. The article treats it as a long-standing Cuban Party strategy.
The theatre in Japanese-occupied areas where Communist-led forces such as the Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army set up base areas and waged guerrilla war.
A voting method for illiterate voters, in which each candidate had a bowl and voters dropped a bean into the bowl of their choice.
A goal of ecological civilization construction, put forward in Party documents from the 18th Party Congress (2012) and later made a target of building a modern socialist country.
The region comprising Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei province, treated in Chinese policy as a single area for coordinated development.

lit: to take charge of the household and make decisions
ex: A standard phrase in Party discourse meaning that the people hold ultimate power in the state.
Heidegger's Sein-zum-Tode: anticipating one's own death as the most personal, non-relational and unsurpassable possibility, which individualises Dasein.

en: believe in ghosts and spirits rather than Marx and Lenin
q: believe in ghosts and spirits rather than Marx and Lenin
py: bù xìn Mǎ Liè xìn guǐshén
lit: do not believe in Marx and Lenin but believe in ghosts and spirits
ex: A stock phrase in Party disciplinary reports for officials accused of superstition or religious practice in place of Marxist belief.
A standard Party term for ordinary religious followers, treated as part of the people whom the Party seeks to unite and rely on.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to finance and build infrastructure and trade links across Asia, Africa and Europe.
A policy idea promoted by Xi Jinping that treats food security as more than grain. It seeks food from the whole national territory and a wider range of products.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political teaching beyond classrooms into society and practice, drawing on varied resources.
A concept that treats ideological and political education as a task for all schools, society and Party committees, not only for political theory courses.
A framework for coordinating all resources, personnel and channels inside and outside a university so that ideological and political education covers every part of student life.
The author's term for viewing Party building broadly, as linked with Party leadership and the Party's cause, rather than only as the Party's internal self-construction.
The idea that propaganda and ideology work is the task of the whole Party and government, not only of propaganda departments.
Slang for influential social-media users with verified accounts and large followings, often critical commentators.
A term in the literature reviewed for the seizure of biological resources and the exploitation of bodies worldwide by powerful states and corporations. It is closely linked to 'biocolonialism'.
The article's term for both biotechnology workers and "volunteers" who supply tissue, services or trial participation to biotech firms.
A term for the form of capitalism that earns profit and accumulates capital through the life sciences and biotechnology. It is associated with Kaushik Sunder Rajan's concept of 'biocapital'.
Foucault's term for forms of power that manage life itself, such as population regulation and health policy, rather than relying on repression alone.
A field of theory associated with Michel Foucault that studies how modern states manage populations and bodies through health, birth rates and similar mechanisms.
A term associated with Foucault and later Marxist writers on immaterial labour. Here it denotes capital's control over workers' life time beyond the workplace.
Chen Yun's metaphor from the early 1980s: the market is a bird that must be kept alive within the cage of state planning.

en: black swan and grey rhino events
q: black swan and grey rhino events
ex: Risk metaphors in official language: a black swan is an unpredictable shock, and a grey rhino is a visible but neglected major threat.
The fact that the internal workings of an algorithm are not visible or understandable to its users or even its designers.
A chalk-written board in a village or workplace, laid out like a newspaper with news, criticism and cartoons. In the Party-led areas it served as the lowest-level medium.
The doctrine, named after Auguste Blanqui, of seizing power through a small conspiratorial minority instead of mass action. Marxists often use it as a term of criticism.

en: blow the whistle and report in
q: blow the whistle and report in
lit: blow the whistle, report for duty
ex: A governance mechanism in which grassroots units raise a problem ("blow the whistle") and higher-level departments must send staff to help resolve it.

A Comintern slogan and campaign launched in 1924 to remodel member parties on the organisational and ideological lines of the Russian Bolshevik party. It stressed centralism, discipline and loyalty to the Comintern.
Lan's label, drawn from Jodi Dean, for a relation in which users work unpaid for a chance at a rare reward. He contrasts it with the wage model of industrial capitalism.
An ancient divination and philosophical classic, comprising the Yijing text and the Yizhuan commentaries. It is traditionally ranked first among the Confucian classics.
Mao's term, used in his 1930 writings, for treating books and received doctrine as authoritative without testing them against actual conditions.

lit: revitalise the border, enrich the people
ex: A state policy to develop border regions and raise the incomes of residents there.
The Communist-led Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, with Yan'an as its centre, which the Kuomintang government restricted and blockaded during the war.
The representative assembly of the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, elected at border-region, county and township levels, with legislative and oversight powers.

A formula in the Vietnamese Party's foreign-policy line, applied even to a single country across different issues. Partners and adversaries are defined by their stance on Vietnam's sovereignty and can change category.

lit: fragrant in both virtue and art
ex: A traditional ideal, now used in official cultural policy, that artists should combine moral integrity with artistic excellence.
Mao's formula for cadres in the socialist period. It joins firm political stance (red) with professional competence (expert), with politics given priority.
A united-front principle in Mao's writings. It holds that the Party must cooperate with allies while struggling against them where necessary, so as to keep its independence.
A mode of thinking that prepares for the worst case in order to secure the best result. Xi Jinping has promoted it since the 18th Party Congress.
A Party term for tendencies to adopt Western-style liberal political ideas and to question Party leadership and the socialist system. Deng used it in campaigns of the late 1970s and 1980s.
A label used by Marxist scholars for Western academic Marx studies that, in their view, separate Marx's thought into disconnected parts. It is used critically here.
The mainland view that the 1911 Revolution was a bourgeois-democratic revolution arising from the growth of national capitalism and class conflict in the late Qing.
A category from the Communist Manifesto for reformers within the bourgeoisie who want to cure social ills without abolishing capitalism. The article applies it to figures such as Macron and Sanders.
The society dominated by the bourgeoisie. The review discusses whether it can be distinguished from civil society and from capitalist society.
The basic unit of Party organization. The Fourth Congress (1925) renamed the earlier "group" as "branch", and the Fifth Congress (1927) defined it as the Party's basic organization.
A reform slogan to end evaluation based solely on papers, titles, diplomas, awards and student admissions.
A reform slogan against evaluating researchers only by papers, titles, academic credentials and awards.
A grouping of major emerging economies that began with Brazil, Russia, India and China and later expanded. Chinese writers often cite it as evidence of a shifting global balance.
Official description of mass organisations such as trade unions as connecting the Party with workers and other groups.
Li Da's proposal for an economics guided by historical materialism. It would cover both general laws of economic evolution and the particular laws of the Chinese economy.

The Third Plenum Decision's phrase for a wider united front effort. The united front is the Party's work of building alliances with non-Party groups, ethnic and religious communities, and overseas Chinese.
The author's term for treating employment as a concern across the whole cycle of admissions, training, further study and career, not only the graduation season.
Tai's proposed category. It gathers the various Marxist currents of the developed capitalist countries into one field of study organised around political economy and Capital.
A group of Hungarian philosophers around Georg Lukács, including Ágnes Heller and György Márkus, who developed a humanist, renewed Marxism from the 1960s and 1970s.

zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家
en: building a modern socialist country in all respects
q: building a modern socialist country in all respects
ex: The task set by the 20th Party Congress (2022) for the period after the completion of a moderately prosperous society, with the aim of making China a modern socialist country by 2035 and by mid-century.
A policy theme in Party and state planning for making China a leading power across fields such as science, manufacturing, finance and agriculture. The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline lists 16 such goals.

en: building Party branches at company level
q: building Party branches at company level
ex: A principle of Party control over the army, put forward in the late 1920s. Party branches are set up in each company so that Party leadership reaches the lowest units.

Stalin's doctrine, developed in the mid-1920s against Trotsky and others, that the USSR could build a socialist society on its own resources without waiting for revolutions in advanced capitalist countries.

The Party's current ethnic policy line, which stresses the shared identity of all of China's ethnic groups as one nation and places it above group-specific identities. Related slogans include forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.
The article's rendering of Heller's idea that human nature, including feelings, is not given in advance but is built into the individual by social and historical factors over time.
A supply-chain term for the way small changes in demand are amplified as information passes upstream from customers to suppliers.
Mao's term for the big capitalists who fused with state power and served imperialism. He associated them with the Guomindang government and its control of the economy.
In Party usage, an official style marked by detachment from the people, indifference to their problems and reliance on orders. The Party has repeatedly campaigned against it.
Official terms for faults in Party work style: detachment from the people and empty, box-ticking performance of tasks. Campaigns against them have been a recurring theme of Party discipline.
An official umbrella term for enterprises, individual businesses and other registered market participants.
The ideological and practical training of Party and government cadres (officials), a long-standing function of the Party.
The Chinese label for the Japanese strategy of blockhouses, strongpoints, roads and trenches built to divide and blockade Communist-held areas in North China.
A group of mainly US-based historians, including Pomeranz, Wong and Frank, who challenge Eurocentric accounts by stressing the similarities between early modern Europe and Asia.
Texts regarded as embodying fundamental principles and values. The article treats canonicity as the defining feature of Chinese classical studies.
A large anti-imperialist strike of 1925–1926 by workers in Guangzhou and Hong Kong, launched after the 30 May 1925 incident in Shanghai and the Shaji killings in Guangzhou.
A term used in Chinese economics for an active government that guides development. It is often paired with the "effective market" in the socialist market economy.
Marx's term for the appearance that social relations of production are natural properties of things, so that capital seems to produce value on its own.
Marx's term for capital in its abstract, inner nature, as distinct from the 'many capitals' that compete in reality.

The authors' label for the conception of justice that classical economics defends. It treats the separation of labour from its product, and the capitalist's appropriation of that product, as natural and legitimate.

A concept in recent Chinese Marxist scholarship for the power relations and mechanisms that serve capitalist exploitation and the self-expansion of capital. The article uses it to name the substance of power under capitalism.

In this article, the historical social form of European capitalism in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, defined by developed division of labour, exchange and commodity production, and spread through colonial expansion.
The social, cultural and institutional order produced by capitalism's development, treated in Chinese Marxist scholarship as a target of critique and as a historical form to be surpassed.
The author's term for the process by which capital turns games, once a leisure activity, into a means of self-expansion and surplus extraction.
Jason Moore's alternative to the Anthropocene, which holds that capitalism as a world-ecology, not humanity as a whole, drives ecological crisis.
China's announced goals of peaking carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060, often called the "dual carbon" goals.
China's declared climate goals: carbon emissions to peak before 2030 and net-zero to be reached by 2060. Often abbreviated as the "dual carbon" goals.
China's declared goals of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060.

en: Carry the Revolution Through to the End
q: Carry the Revolution Through to the End
ex: Title of Mao Zedong's New Year message of 1 January 1949, which rejected a negotiated halt to the civil war. The Party presented it as a call to defeat the Guomintang completely.

en: catching the rat without breaking the vase
q: catching the rat without breaking the vase
lit: catch the rat, smash the vase theory
ex: A saying Nguyen Phu Trong used in 2014, attributed to Ho Chi Minh and earlier leaders. It means pursuing corrupt officials without damaging political stability and development.
Marx's late metaphor, in his writings on Russia, for the possibility of a society bypassing the full capitalist stage of development. Chinese scholars apply it to China's socialist modernization.

Marx's image, in his late letters to Zasulich, for whether a society such as Russia could reach socialism without undergoing the full capitalist stage and its sufferings. Chinese theorists use it in discussing China's path.
A 1945 Yan'an conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall, often cited in Party discourse on popular support.

en: centenary goal of the armed forces
q: centenary goal of the armed forces
lit: goal of striving for the 100th anniversary of the founding of the army
ex: The official target to reach specified military-modernization objectives by 2027, the 100th anniversary of the People's Liberation Army.

py: liǎng gè yìbǎi nián fèndòu mùbiāo
ex: Two official targets: a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

zh: 中央全面深化改革委员会
en: Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform
q: Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform
ex: A Party body chaired by Xi Jinping that reviews and coordinates major reform plans. It replaced the Central Leading Group for Comprehensively Deepening Reform in 2018.
The Communist Party's top internal discipline body, which works closely with the state supervisory commission.
The Party's top internal body for enforcing discipline and investigating corruption; it holds annual plenary sessions that set anti-corruption priorities.
The Party body that translates and edits the works of Marx, Engels, Lenin and other classics into Chinese. Its Capital translation of 1974 replaced Guo and Wang's as the standard version.
A high-level Party meeting held in April 2025 that set the goals and approach of China's policy towards neighbouring countries.
The 1982 Party document on the basic viewpoint and policy on religious questions in China's socialist period. It remains a key reference for Party religious policy.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders that sets economic policy priorities for the coming year.
High-level Party meetings that set the principles and policies for ethnic affairs. The first was held in 1992, and later ones were held in 2014 and 2021.
The central leading body elected by the Second to Fourth Congresses. Its name later changed to the Central Committee.

en: Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission
q: Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission
ex: A Party body chaired by Xi Jinping that sets the direction of major economic policy.
A Party body set up in 2023 to provide centralised leadership over financial work, alongside the Central Financial Work Commission.
A body dispatched by the Party Central Committee, also set up in 2023, to lead Party work in the financial system.
A high-level Party meeting on financial policy. The one held in October 2023 introduced the aim of building a financial powerhouse.
Follow-up action required of an organisation after a Party inspection team has reported problems in it.
A Party-run college that trains non-Communist Party members, including members of the democratic parties and non-Party figures, for united front work.
Party bodies, first created in 1958, that coordinate policy and decisions in a given field, such as finance, foreign affairs or politics and law.
A Party formulation, used by Mao Zedong and later leaders, describing ideological education as the pivotal element in uniting the Party and people for their tasks.
The supreme military body of the Chinese Soviet Republic and the Red Army in the early 1930s. It sent the telegraphed orders to the Sixth Army Corps.

The main revolutionary base area of the Communist Party, in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian in the early 1930s, where the Chinese Soviet Republic was founded in 1931. The period is a staple of Party history writing.

Large enterprises owned by the central government and supervised by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, concentrated in strategic sectors such as energy, telecoms and heavy industry.
Large state-owned firms supervised by the central government through SASAC.
A high-level Party meeting on united front work, which covers relations with religious, ethnic and non-Party groups. The May 2015 conference issued new guidance on religious work.
A high-level Party and government meeting that sets national urban policy. The article cites sessions in 2015 and 2025.
The principle that the whole Party and all other organisations act under the unified direction of the Party Centre. It is a core concept in the Party's account of its own authority.
A standard Party formula for the Central Committee's overall authority over all work. Official discourse presents it as the basic principle of the Party's leadership system.

en: centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee
q: centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee
ex: An official formulation stressing that authority over major decisions and their implementation is concentrated in the Party Central Committee.
A model of the world economy, common in dependency and world-system theory, in which advanced core countries dominate less developed peripheral ones.

zh: 中心—外围二元组织形态
ex: The article's term for the Soviet-led pattern in which the Soviet party held absolute leadership authority over other communist parties. It is criticised in the article as great-party and great-power chauvinism.
The article's term for a strategy of broadening a left party's electoral base towards middle-ground voters, by moving away from a class-based vanguard identity.
A historical narrative about China's subjection to foreign powers from the mid-19th to the mid-20th century, central to Chinese national identity.
The large family-controlled conglomerates, such as Samsung and Hyundai, that dominate the South Korean economy.
A leading firm, often a central state-owned enterprise, tasked with organising and coordinating the upstream and downstream firms in an industrial chain.
A governance practice in which a designated official or leading enterprise takes responsibility for the stability and security of a particular industrial chain.
Leading actors who organise and anchor an innovation chain or industrial chain. The article names strategic scientists and technology entrepreneurs as chain leaders.

en: chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission
q: chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission
lit: Central Military Commission chairman responsibility system
ex: The constitutional and Party arrangement under which the CMC chairman, currently Xi Jinping, bears overall responsibility for the armed forces.
A school of Chinese Buddhism (Zen in Japanese) emphasising meditation and direct insight, which strongly influenced Chinese art and poetry.
Émigré and domestic intellectuals who backed Soviet power in the 1920s because they believed the NEP would lead Russia back to an ordinary bourgeois state.
A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since about 2017 for a perceived deep transformation of the global order, including the shift of power towards emerging economies.
A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since about 2017 for a perceived deep shift in the global balance of power and international order.
The school of Song-dynasty Confucianism associated with Cheng Yi, Cheng Hao and Zhu Xi, which treats li (principle) as the ultimate reality. It became state orthodoxy in later imperial China.
The attempt of Salvador Allende's government (1970–1973) to reach socialism by constitutional and peaceful means. The 1973 military coup ended it.
A Chinese state-linked organisation that campaigns against groups the authorities classify as cults, including Falun Gong.
A scholarly society promoting atheism research and education in China, associated with the journal Science and Atheism.
A label used in China for Western predictions that China's economic, political or social system will collapse. Chinese commentators generally treat it as a hostile argument.

en: China Federation of Literary and Art Circles (CFLAC)
q: China Federation of Literary and Art Circles (CFLAC)
lit: China Federation of Literary and Art Circles
ex: The national people's organisation of artists and writers' associations, led by the Party. It coordinates the arts sector and its programmes.
The Party's body for leading the labour movement, founded in 1921. It was the organisational base of Zhang Guotao's activist group.
A term for the distinctive path of the People's Republic's development. Pan Wei and colleagues theorised it around 2009 as resting on the continuity of Chinese civilization.

zh: 关心下一代工作委员会
en: China National Committee for the Care of the Next Generation
q: China National Committee for the Care of the Next Generation
lit: Committee for Work of Caring for the Next Generation
ex: A Party-sponsored organisation approved by the Central Committee in 1990, staffed largely by retired officials and professionals. It engages in ideological, moral and welfare work with children and young people.

A comprehensive field studying China's history, culture, society and economy. In recent Chinese usage it is promoted as an international field, with World Conferences on China Studies held since 2023.
An official phrase for China's system of governance and its record, often paired with "the China miracle" in Party discourse.
A slogan from Xi Jinping's speeches, calling for Chinese philosophy and social science to develop their own concepts and discourse rather than rely on Western frameworks.

A slogan calling for philosophy and social science in China to rest on Chinese practice and tradition rather than on imported Western frameworks. It is closely tied to Xi Jinping's calls for Chinese discourse and academic systems.
The long-term national project of making China a modern, developed country. Here it appears in a general historical sense, as the goal for which the victory of 1945 laid the foundations.

en: China-Africa community with a shared future
q: China-Africa community with a shared future
ex: A concept Xi Jinping first put forward in 2013 during a visit to Africa. It describes China and Africa as partners bound by common history and interests.
A research body established in 2019 under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. The article describes it as entrusted with coordinating national historical research.
A phrase used in official discourse for China's proposals on international problems, here global governance. The article treats it as a systematic body of ideas drawn from Xi Jinping's speeches.
The authors' term for the practical effectiveness with which institutional strengths are turned into governance results.

zh: 中国话语和中国叙事体系
py: Zhōngguó huàyǔ hé Zhōngguó xùshì tǐxì
lit: Chinese discourse and Chinese narrative system
ex: A Party slogan calling for China to develop its own concepts and ways of telling its story, especially in international communication. It features in the 20th Party Congress report and the Third Plenum decision.
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
In this article, the concrete, scattered ideas and practices that the CPC drew from the Chinese revolution, as opposed to the systematised "Chinese theory".

en: Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application
q: Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application
ex: A late-Qing reformist formula that kept Chinese values as the core while adopting Western technology and methods.
The traditional legal system that took shape in imperial China, culminating in the Tang Code, and which influenced neighbouring East and Southeast Asian states.

The phrase Deng Xiaoping used in talks with foreign leaders to say that China had its own path of development. The article distinguishes it from the Western use of 'China model' as a product to be exported.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
A formula used in Party discourse, first in the reform era, for a modernization path said to be specific to Chinese conditions. The article uses it for the reform-era path.

en: the Chinese nation as a community
ex: An official concept presenting China's 56 recognised ethnic groups as one national community. The Party promotes it as the basis of its ethnic policy, including the drive to 'forge a sense of community'.
A thesis debated in the 1930s, associated with Gu Jiegang, that China's peoples form a single nation. Gao treats it as a response to frontier crisis.
A youth organisation founded in Beiping in February 1936 under Communist leadership, abbreviated Minxian dui. It posed as non-partisan and was dissolved in 1938.
Official shorthand for China's distinctive route of development under Communist Party leadership, often presented as an alternative to Western models.

en: Chinese path of human rights development
q: Chinese path of human rights development
ex: The official phrase for China's approach to human rights, which stresses national conditions, the rights to subsistence and development, and Party leadership. It is set against what official discourse calls a single Western model.
A national and local advisory body that brings together the Party, the democratic parties, non-Party figures and social groups. It is officially treated as a main channel of consultative democracy.
A national and local advisory body bringing together representatives of the Communist Party, other parties, and social groups. It is a main venue for consultative democracy.

lit: China's reasoning / Chinese way of reasoning
ex: Used in the article for the systematised, theorised principles and worldview that explain Chinese practice, rooted in Marxism and traditional Chinese culture.
A proposed school of IR theory with Chinese characteristics, built on Chinese history and thought. Whether to found one has long been debated among Chinese IR scholars.
A debate of the late 1920s and 1930s among Chinese intellectuals over the nature of Chinese society and its stages of historical development, closely tied to disputes over revolutionary strategy.
The Communist-led government proclaimed in 1931 in the Jiangxi base area. It existed until the Red Army's Long March began in 1934.

A term Xi Jinping uses for the national spirit centred on patriotism together with the spirit of the times centred on reform and innovation. It is presented as necessary for realizing the Chinese Dream.
A phrase in official discourse for China's institutional system. It is paired with 'Chinese governance' (中国之治), the order and results the system is said to produce.
The systematic body of theory raised from Chinese experience. For the revolutionary period the author identifies it with Mao Zedong Thought.
The authors' term for the Party's guiding ideas, which they present as social consciousness reflecting China's social being.

zh: 中国青年新闻记者学会
ex: A journalists' organisation founded in Wuhan on 30 March 1938, abbreviated "Qingji". It brought together young reporters and published the journal Journalist.

zh: 中国式农业农村现代化
ex: The official description of China's own path to modernizing agriculture, villages and farmers' livelihoods under Party leadership. It is the rural component of the wider Chinese modernization agenda.
The cultural dimension of the official concept of Chinese modernization, referring to the Party-led modernization of China's cultural forms and of the people's cultural consciousness.
A colloquial term for key technologies or components on which China depends on foreign suppliers, which can be restricted by others.
A current that combines Christian ethics with socialist aims and favours reform by peaceful, legal means. The authors present it as a source of confusion in the workers' movement.
Official language for the flow of production, distribution, exchange and consumption in the domestic economy. It is linked to the "dual circulation" strategy.
The PCF's formula under Robert Hue for mobilising citizens and social forces to take part directly in political change alongside alliances with left parties.
A policy programme to raise public moral standards and civilised conduct, reaffirmed in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
Correa's slogan for his political project, which the article describes as shifting power relations in favour of the majority and building a state serving the people.
A Party-led programme to raise public moral standards and civility, which the 20th Party Congress report listed as a strategic task.
The moral norms expected of citizens in social life. The Party has issued implementation outlines on its construction, in 2001 and again for the new era.
Hegel's term for the sphere of material life relations and market exchange. Marx took it as the base from which the state and legal forms must be explained.
A policy of linking the defence and civilian sectors in technology, industry and resources. Xi Jinping elevated it to a national strategy.
A Japanese Marxist current, represented here by Mochizuki Seiji, that reads Marx's theory of history as the formation of civil society through human labour on nature.
A concept in Chinese Marxist scholarship for the historically specific shape of a civilisation. The authors distinguish it from "social formation" and tie it to the character of labour.
The author's counterpart to the 'civilization of capital'. It means a civilization in which labour governs capital, which the author associates with socialist society.

A designation for China as a state defined by a long-continuous civilization rather than a Western-style nation-state. Gan Yang advanced it in 2003, and Martin Jacques and Zhang Weiwei developed related formulations.
Confidence in Chinese civilization and in the new form of human civilization. Xi Jinping first used the term in 2019 at the Dialogue of Asian Civilizations.
A concept used by some Chinese scholars to describe China as a polity defined by continuous civilization rather than by the Western nation-state model.
The idea that one civilization, usually the West, is inherently superior to others. The article treats it as a colonialist doctrine.
Samuel Huntington's thesis that post-Cold War conflicts would run along cultural and civilizational lines. Chinese Marxist writers often criticise it as ahistorical.

A Marxist distinction between a class defined by its objective position and a class 'for itself' that is conscious and organised. The author says the American working class has not yet been organised into the latter.
The Marxist method of explaining people and events through class position and interests. The article defends it against claims that it is outdated.
The Marxist method of analysing social phenomena through class relations and class struggle.
A Marxist method that explains social and political events through the interests and conflicts of social classes. The article presents it as the only way to understand Western developments.
The psychological traits and behavioural pattern shared by members of a class, determined by the class's political and economic position.

Marx's term, drawn from Hegel's "being-for-itself", for a class that has become conscious of its own interests and acts politically as a class, as opposed to a class merely defined by its place in production.

en: the class nature of the state (guoti)
ex: Guoti refers to which class holds state power; zhengti refers to the form in which power is organised. Chinese Marxist theory holds that the former determines the latter.
The authors' term for the process by which a ruling class controls power, whether economic, political or cultural, and keeps its dominance over the ruled classes.
A phrase from Lenin's speech, used by the authors for the ideology of the exploiting class that permeates the education system of a class society.

A modern academic field, modelled partly on Western classics, devoted to the study of China's ancient foundational texts and ideas. The article argues that the discipline emerged in the twentieth century from the modernization of traditional scholarship.

The tradition of Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School and similar thinkers. Chinese scholarship usually sees it as stressing philosophical critique over the economic analysis of Soviet Marxism.
An idiom for using canonical texts to develop one's own ideas. The article applies it to the creative interpretation of Western Marxism.
The LCP's proposed organisational form for revolution: a broad alliance of classes, parties and organisations under the party's leadership, opposed to imperialism and dependent capitalism.

lit: clear and bright series of special actions
ex: Recurring special campaigns run by the cyberspace authorities against illegal or harmful online content and behaviour.

In the article, a form of late capitalism that seeks to decarbonise through carbon markets and technology while keeping growth and accumulation intact. The term comes from Western critical literature on green capitalism.
The article's term for Western hegemony over international climate affairs, exercised through energy wars, shifting diplomacy and evasion of historical responsibility.

en: closed loop from citizen complaints to feedback
q: closed loop from citizen complaints to feedback
lit: respond to complaints as soon as received
ex: A municipal governance practice, associated with Beijing, of handling citizen complaints promptly and feeding the results back into management.

zh: 投资于物与投资于人紧密结合
en: closely combining investment in things with investment in people
q: closely combining investment in things with investment in people
py: tóuzī yú wù yǔ tóuzī yú rén jǐnmì jiéhé
lit: investing in things and investing in people closely combined
ex: A policy formula in recent Party documents that pairs spending on physical capital and infrastructure with spending on education, health, social security and similar areas. The article treats it as a value principle as well as an economic policy.
The term for digital platforms viewed as fiefs: monopolised digital domains that replace markets. The authors treat them as virtual land.

In the techno-feudalism literature, the rent that platform owners collect from users for access to digital platforms and cloud services. The authors argue it is a form of ground-rent-like income derived from surplus value.

lit: jointly build, jointly govern, jointly share
ex: An official formula for social governance in which the Party, government, enterprises, social organisations and residents all take part and share the results. It has been promoted in Party documents since the 2010s.

lit: joint decision by labour and capital
ex: Arrangements, especially in Germany and Sweden, by which workers and employers share decision-making in firms. The article counts them as strengthening workers' democratic rights.
The CPC's 1944–45 demand to end Kuomintang one-party rule and form a government of all anti-Japanese parties. Mao Zedong set it out in his 1945 report "On Coalition Government".
The Western export-control body formed in 1949 to restrict exports of strategic goods and technology to socialist countries. Wu calls it "Batong" and treats it as an instrument of blockade.
Lu's perspective that makes shared responsibility and risk, and the prevention of existential risks to humanity, the highest value in AI ethics.

A concept associated with Yann Moulier-Boutang for a phase of capitalism in which knowledge, information and immaterial labour become the main sources of accumulation. Deng uses it to analyse platform and data capitalism.
A social-psychological theory by Leon Festinger holding that people seek consistency among their beliefs, attitudes and behaviour. The discomfort of inconsistency drives them to change one of them.
A term for contests over perception and thinking, seen here as an upgrade of earlier information, propaganda and public-opinion warfare.

en: the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe
q: collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe
ex: The standard Chinese term for the end of the Soviet bloc regimes in 1989–91. It is treated as a turning point for the international communist movement.

A term from the Chinese translation of Marx's Capital, for the productive force created by cooperation and division of labour. The authors extend it into a general category for social productive power.
Amin's term for the present triad of the United States, Europe and Japan acting together as the imperialist centre, with their mutual rivalries now secondary.
A concept from the CPV's 4th Congress meaning that the organised working people collectively act as masters of society. The article says the 7th Congress (1991) stopped using it.
In China, a form of socialist public ownership in which resources, notably rural land, belong to a village collective. It is distinct from ownership by the whole people, i.e. the state.
The right to use force in defence of an allied state under attack. Debate in Japan concerns whether Article 9 permits exercising it.

en: collective study sessions of the Political Bureau
q: collective study sessions of the Political Bureau
ex: Regular sessions in which members of the Party's Political Bureau study a chosen topic together, led by invited experts. The practice dates back to the 1990s and is presented as setting an example for the whole Party.
Marx's term (Gesamtarbeiter) for the combined workforce of manufacture, in which each worker performs a partial function. Yu renders it with a stress on totality.
The principle that collective interests take precedence over individual ones. Official documents name it the principle of socialist morality.
A thesis developed from the 1950s by the SACP and adopted by the ANC in 1969, holding that colonizer and colonized coexist within one South African state under white minority rule.
Term used in Chinese official discourse for Western-backed mass movements that overthrow governments, such as those in post-Soviet states.

en: combination of rule by law and rule by virtue
q: combination of rule by law and rule by virtue
ex: A governance principle that pairs legal enforcement with moral education and persuasion.

lit: leniency and strictness complementing each other
ex: A policy approach that pairs tolerance with firm limits. The author uses it to characterise Cuba's policy towards intellectuals.

zh: 有效市场和有为政府相结合
en: combining an efficient market with a capable government
q: combining an efficient market with a capable government
py: yǒuxiào shìchǎng hé yǒuwéi zhèngfǔ xiāng jiéhé
lit: effective market and promising/active government combined
ex: Official formula for the relationship between market and state in the socialist market economy. It pairs the market's decisive role in allocating resources with a strategic role for government.
Mao Zedong's policy of uniting traditional Chinese practitioners and drugs with Western-style medicine, in order to expand medical capacity in the border regions.

zh: 教育与生产劳动相结合
py: jiàoyù yǔ shēngchǎn láodòng xiāng jiéhé
ex: A principle derived from Marx and Engels that Chinese Party documents adopted as an educational policy. It has been applied in forms ranging from work-study schemes to present-day labour education.
A principle drawn from Marx's account of the Paris Commune, in which the representative body both makes and carries out laws. It is contrasted with the separation of powers.

zh: 马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合
en: combining Marxism with China's fine traditional culture
q: combining Marxism with China's fine traditional culture
py: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì jīběn yuánlǐ tóng Zhōnghuá yōuxiù chuántǒng wénhuà xiāng jiéhé
ex: The formula, part of the 'Two Integrations', that Marxism's basic tenets should be joined with elements of traditional Chinese culture that the Party regards as valuable.

en: combining of the posts of general secretary and state president
q: combining of the posts of general secretary and state president
lit: Party and government on one shoulder
ex: The practice of one person holding both the top Party post and the top state post. In Vietnam it was long debated, and the article reports its realisation in 2018.

zh: 依法治国和以德治国相结合
en: combining rule of law with rule by virtue
q: combining rule of law with rule by virtue
py: yīfǎ zhìguó hé yǐdé zhìguó xiāng jiéhé
ex: A governing principle pairing legal governance with moral education and moral norms.

en: combining self-governance, rule of law and moral governance
q: combining self-governance, rule of law and moral governance
