ex: An official model of grassroots governance, often called the 'three-governance integration'. It combines resident self-government, legal norms and moral or cultural guidance, all under Party leadership.
The Communist International (1919–1943), the Moscow-led organisation to which national communist parties belonged as sections. Its principle of one party per country shaped the Bureau's status.
Environmental regulation that sets fixed standards and bans enforced by the state. The authors contrast it with market-based instruments such as emissions trading.
The error of issuing orders to the masses beyond their level of consciousness and without their willing consent.
In Marx's analysis, the condition under which workers must sell their capacity to work as a commodity. The author treats it as the basis of wage labour and of surplus value.

Marx's concept, set out in Capital, that social relations between producers appear as properties of and relations between things. The article treats it as both an objective economic structure and an ideology.
Deposits valued in units tied to the prices of a basket of goods, which protected savers from inflation.
The programme adopted by the PCF as its guiding document, intended to develop a twenty-first-century "new communism" and set out an action plan.

Xi Jinping's formulation, first stated at the UN in 2015, of peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as shared human values. Official texts present it as distinct from Western "universal values".
Official term for the shared goal of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, distinguished from the long-term communist ideal.

zh: 中国特色社会主义共同理想
en: the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The official medium-term shared goal of building a modern socialist country and achieving national rejuvenation, usually paired with the long-term communist ideal.
The shared commitment to socialism with Chinese characteristics and national rejuvenation that official education seeks to instil, especially in students.

zh: 中国人民政治协商会议共同纲领
py: Zhōngguó Rénmín Zhèngzhì Xiéshāng Huìyì Gòngtóng Gāngling
ex: Provisional constitutional document adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in September 1949. It served as the basic law until the 1954 Constitution.
The provisional governing programme adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in September 1949, which served as a temporary constitution before 1954.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics stressing shared wealth for all, given prominence in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

The cultural and spiritual side of common prosperity, stressed in Xi Jinping's formulation that people be rich in both material and spiritual life. Scholars treat it as covering access to cultural products, services and meaningful exchange.

lit: common values of the whole of humankind
ex: A formula Xi Jinping introduced in 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. It is offered as an alternative to Western "universal values".
Small local production or processing sites, set up in villages under the common prosperity agenda, that provide nearby jobs and income for rural residents.
Rural enterprises run by people's communes and production brigades; they were the forerunners of the township and village enterprises of the reform era.
Habermas's term for social action coordinated through mutual understanding and the raising of validity claims, as opposed to strategic action.
A type of digital socialism developed by Christian Fuchs and Dimitris Boucas. It stresses solidarity-based, non-capitalist media and communication forms within digital capitalism.
The Third International, founded in Moscow in 1919 to coordinate communist parties worldwide. It guided the early CPC until its dissolution in 1943.
The international workers' organisation founded in 1847 for which Marx and Engels drafted the Manifesto.
The ruling party of the People's Republic of China, founded in 1921. The article treats its birth as the result of the spread of Marxism-Leninism.

en: the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
q: Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
ex: The ruling party of the USSR until 1991. In Chinese official discourse its fall is a standard cautionary reference.

zh: 共产主义星期六义务劳动
ex: Unpaid voluntary work first organised by Russian railway workers in 1919, which Lenin hailed as a 'great beginning' of communist labour.
The Party's mass organisation for young people, which works under Party leadership to mobilise and educate youth.
The Bolivian version of new socialism, based on community, reciprocity, solidarity and harmony with nature. Some politicians call it "Bolivarian Indian socialism".
The term used to translate the German Gemeinschaft and related concepts in Marx. In the article it covers forms of collective life from the original community to the communist association.

The awareness that individuals share responsibility for public affairs and common interests. The article draws on this idea, linked to official calls to forge a sense of community among the Chinese nation.
The author's term for a group of audiences who share and express common interests and values through new media platforms.

zh: 山水林田湖草沙是生命共同体
py: shān shuǐ lín tián hú cǎo shā shì shēngmìng gòngtóngtǐ
lit: mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert form a community of life
ex: An official formulation holding that natural elements are interdependent and should be managed as one system rather than separately.

zh: 人与自然是生命共同体
py: rén yǔ zìrán shì shēngmìng gòngtóngtǐ
lit: humanity and nature are a life community
ex: A thesis stated in Xi Jinping's report to the 19th Party Congress (2017). It holds that humans and nature are interdependent and that people must respect, adapt to and protect nature.
A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy, applied both globally (a community with a shared future for mankind) and to bilateral relations, including with Vietnam and Laos.

en: a community with a shared future for mankind
q: community with a shared future for mankind
lit: community of common destiny for humankind
ex: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.

zh: community with a shared future for mankind
en: a community with a shared future for mankind
q: community with a shared future for mankind
ex: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, calling for shared development and cooperation among states.

en: a community with a shared future in cyberspace
q: community with a shared future in cyberspace
ex: Xi Jinping's proposal, an application of the broader idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, that states jointly govern cyberspace through cooperation. It is usually presented alongside respect for cyber sovereignty.

en: a community with a shared future with neighbouring countries
q: community with a shared future with neighbouring countries
ex: A Chinese foreign-policy aim of closer political, economic and security ties with bordering and nearby states, derived from the broader concept of a community with a shared future for mankind.
Payments, often fiscal transfers, to those who protect ecosystems, including between regions.
The author's term for the contest between mainstream and non-mainstream ideologies to win people's acceptance and allegiance. It is described as the essence of "winning hearts and minds".
A principle that state-owned and private firms should compete on equal terms, without advantages from government ownership or support.
A concept from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), covering upgraded consumption, optimised investment and a dynamic balance between supply and demand.
A theory from the life sciences that treats systems as interacting agents adapting non-linearly to an open environment. It is applied here to the Party.
Originally local intermediaries for foreign firms in semi-colonial China. In Marxist usage it describes groups or ideas serving foreign interests.
Comprador originally meant local intermediaries for foreign firms. Chinese Marxist writing uses it for elites seen as serving foreign capital and states against national interests.

lit: comprehensive balance of the national economy
ex: A planning concept of the planned-economy era that sought balance among materials, finance, credit and foreign exchange, with fiscal balance as its key.
A planning concept associated with Chen Yun, calling for overall balance among finance, credit, materials and other economic sectors.
The cultural theory associated with Zhang Dainian: creating a new Chinese culture by synthesising Marxism, Chinese tradition and Western thought, with Marxism as the guiding axis.
A policy concept for governing cyberspace through coordinated Party, government, corporate, social and technical means. The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for improving it.

lit: comprehensively governing the country according to law
ex: A Party policy line, prominent since the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014), aiming to govern the country according to law under Party leadership.

A national strategy launched in 2017 and elevated in later Party documents. It aims to modernise agriculture, the countryside and farmers' livelihoods across industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.

zh: 全面战略合作伙伴关系
ex: The formal level of China–Vietnam relations, declared in 2008.

The official name for the reform agenda launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It covers economic, political, cultural, social, ecological, military and Party-building reforms.
The authors' phrase for capital's inherent drive to expand its value, which they present as an everyday, hidden form of power.

An interdisciplinary field that uses large-scale data, network analysis and simulation to study social behaviour. The authors present it as the source of methods that ideological and political education can borrow.
A phrase attributed to Ho Chi Minh describing the revolutionary bond between China and Vietnam, widely used in official narratives of bilateral ties.

en: concentrating all efforts on economic construction
q: concentrating all efforts on economic construction
ex: The North Korean line adopted at the April 2018 plenum of the Seventh Central Committee, which shifted the Party's main task to economic development. The Eighth Congress confirmed it.

lit: concentrate strength to accomplish big things
ex: A phrase used officially for the state's ability to mobilise resources nationwide for large strategic projects. It is often paired with 'the whole nation as one chessboard'.
A metaphor from Xi Jinping's speeches for uniting people of all groups around the Party's leadership. The article extends it to online and offline spaces.
The author's term, drawn from Hegel's logic, for the development of concepts in a system. Liu argues that in Marx this development mirrors the real contradictions of capitalism.
A traditional imperial approach to frontier peoples that relies on soft control and inducements rather than direct rule. Chiang Kai-shek used it for his 1934 policy of "soft" restraint.
Justice understood as a real condition in which everyone controls the conditions of their own development. It is contrasted with the abstract, formal justice of capitalist right.
A concept from Marx's 1857 Introduction: the concrete as a synthesis of many determinations, reproduced in thought. Yuan treats it as the proper object of social knowledge.
The process of applying a general theory to particular objects. Tang argues it should also enrich the general theory itself.

The author's term for treating labour as a specific, historically determined mode of production, such as wage labour under capitalism, rather than as an abstract principle. It is a scholarly formulation, not an official slogan.
The Party's long-standing effort to correct the working style and behaviour of its members and cadres. It has been a central strand of Party-building campaigns since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Lebanon's system of allocating state posts and parliamentary seats among religious communities, such as Christian and Muslim groups, by fixed quotas. The article treats it as a political tool that masks class conflict.

One of the 'Four-sphere Confidence' formulations: confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is used in Party discourse to affirm the chosen course of development.

zh: 道路自信、理论自信和制度自信
en: confidence in the path, theory and system
q: confidence in the path, theory and system
py: dàolù zìxìn, lǐlùn zìxìn hé zhìdù zìxìn
lit: path confidence, theory confidence and system confidence
ex: Official slogan, promoted by Xi Jinping's leadership, calling for confidence in China's socialist road, theoretical system and institutions; later extended to a fourth, culture.
Confidence in China's socialist system, presented in official discourse as an extension of confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A vote by which the National Assembly may express confidence in senior officials it elected or approved. It can lead to dismissal. It is preceded by a confidence evaluation.

en: configurations of the process as a whole
q: configurations of the process as a whole
lit: the forms/configurations of the total process
ex: Marx's formulation of the theme of Volume III, in which production and circulation are considered together. It includes the concrete forms capital takes, such as industrial, commercial and interest-bearing capital and landed property.

en: conformity to law and conformity to purpose
q: conformity to law and conformity to purpose
py: hé guīlǜ xìng yǔ hé mùdì xìng
ex: Two requirements that Chinese Marxist theory places on practice. Practice must follow objective laws, and it must also serve human goals.
A common scholarly phrase saying that imperial rulers professed Confucian ideals while governing by Legalist methods of law and interest.
The early Republican proposal, backed by Kang Youwei and others, to make Confucianism a state religion or write it into the constitution. New Youth contributors opposed it.
Chinese-language and culture centres established abroad since 2004 with Chinese government support, usually in partnership with local universities.
A term from Chinese logic for the set of essential attributes a concept reflects, as opposed to its extension (外延), the range of things it covers.
A development path that stresses quality, depth and internal substance rather than expansion in scale.

Mao Zedong's term in On Protracted War for people's ability to act on the world by forming ideas, plans and policies from objective facts. The authors treat it as a step in the formation of the concept.
Dallas Smythe's concept, as presented in the article, for the industry that produces audiences as commodities and manages consciousness through communication systems.
Habermas's earlier view that a statement is true if all potential participants in discourse would agree to it under ideal conditions.

zh: 增强宏观政策取向一致性
lit: strengthen the consistency of macro-policy orientation
ex: A requirement repeated in central documents since late 2023. It means that fiscal, monetary, industrial and other policies should point in the same direction and be assessed together.

en: consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
q: consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
lit: consolidate the root, cast the soul
ex: A slogan from the 2025 education-strengthening outline describing the aim of ideological and political education: securing the political and ideological base of education and shaping students' convictions.
Proudhon's term for a value whose proportions are fixed by labour time, intended to resolve the contradiction between use-value and exchange-value. He presented it as the basis of equal exchange.

A Western-style model of constitutional government with multiparty competition and separation of powers. Chinese official writing treats advocacy of it as a challenge to Party leadership, and the author does so here.

A common term in Party discourse for the deliberate building of institutions, the economy and the Party itself, as in Party building, economic construction and socialist modernization. The article treats it as an academic concept.
A stance of opposing the government within the existing political system, cooperating on some national initiatives. The article uses it to describe the CPPK's position.

A principle for settling differences among communist parties through equal discussion, so that only points of agreement are written into joint documents. The article presents it as proposed by Mao Zedong and the CPC around the 1957 Moscow conference.
A Chinese term for democratic consultation, for example through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Official texts describe it as a distinctive form of socialist democracy.
Services aimed at everyday life and household consumption, such as elderly care, childcare, tourism and domestic services.
The field studying the history of the People's Republic of China since 1949, also called 国史 (national history) in official usage. It is institutionally distinct from modern Chinese history.

zh: 当代中国马克思主义、21世纪马克思主义
en: contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism
q: contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism
ex: Official formulation describing the Party's current theory as a continuing development of Marxism, associated with Xi Jinping's statements on Marxism's development.
An approach in the philosophy of science and language that explains meaning and knowledge by reference to context. The article cites the Chinese philosopher Guo Guichun on it.
The term used in Chinese historiography for Meiji and later Japan's strategy of expansion onto the Asian mainland, especially Korea and China.

The author's term for the established post-war arrangement of mutual obligations between states, parties and citizens, such as welfare, representation and security. The article argues it is eroding and that populists seek to rewrite the "social contract".
Mao's 1957 category for non-antagonistic contradictions within society, to be handled by democratic methods and distinguished from antagonistic contradictions between the people and their enemies.

The view that shared technology pushes different social systems towards one common form. Xu says digital socialism risks this view, which would erase the basic differences between socialism and capitalism.
The top-down relaying of a decision or the spirit of a meeting to lower levels. The article treats it as the first, largely passive stage of dissemination.
A rural health scheme in which peasants and the collective jointly raised funds so that members paid reduced fees for treatment. It developed from the mid-1950s.

A concept used in Chinese policy and scholarship for the integrated, mutually reinforcing development of components within a system. Here the authors present it as an extension of Marx's theory of division of labour and cooperation.
Joint or coordinated lawmaking among different localities on similar matters, without changing their territorial scope or powers.

zh: 以习近平同志为核心的党中央
en: core of the Party Central Committee
q: core of the Party Central Committee
py: yǐ Xí Jìnpíng tóngzhì wéi héxīn de dǎngzhōngyāng
ex: A formulation formally adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2016 to affirm Xi Jinping's central leadership position. The article calls it the Plenum's most historic result.
A colloquial phrase for one's fundamental, signature competence. Zhang uses it to describe historical materialism as the Party's basic strength.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.
Education in the core socialist values promoted by the Party-state, a central task of ideological and political education in schools and universities.

en: correct approach to justice and interests
q: correct approach to justice and interests
lit: correct view of righteousness and interests
ex: A formulation Xi Jinping introduced in 2013 for relations with developing countries. It asks that moral considerations take priority alongside material benefit.

zh: 坚持经济全球化正确方向
en: the correct direction of economic globalization
lit: adhere to the correct direction of economic globalization
ex: A formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It presents China as supporting open trade and investment and multilateral cooperation while opposing protectionism, decoupling and unilateral sanctions.

en: correct view of Chinese national history
q: correct view of Chinese national history
lit: view of history of the Chinese nation
ex: The official interpretation that all ethnic groups jointly built the unified multi-ethnic Chinese state and its culture. It is used to counter views seen as divisive.
The official stance, stressed by Xi Jinping from 2021, that Party history should be assessed through historical materialism, with attention to its main theme and mainstream.

en: a correct view of Party history
ex: A formulation Xi Jinping first used at the Party history study and education mobilisation meeting in February 2021. It calls on Party members to interpret Party history in line with official assessments.
An official concept concerning how officials understand and pursue achievements in office. Party documents contrast it with vanity projects and short-term growth chasing.

en: a correct view of the history of the Second World War
q: correct view of the history of the Second World War
lit: correct Second World War historical outlook
ex: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse for an interpretation that stresses Axis responsibility and China's contribution, and opposes revisionist accounts, especially in Japan.
A Han Confucian doctrine, developed by Dong Zhongshu, that Heaven responds to human conduct with omens and disasters, rewarding or punishing rulers.
Full-time staff in Chinese universities who handle students' daily ideological education, discipline, welfare and career guidance, usually Party-supervised.

py: nì zhōuqī hé kuà zhōuqī tiáojié
ex: Counter-cyclical policy offsets short-term swings in the economy. Cross-cyclical policy looks across several cycles, aiming at structural balance and avoiding long-term side effects.
A Communist-run cadre training school founded during the War of Resistance, known in short as Kangda. It trained political and military cadres, including many young intellectuals.
A concept from Badiou's Being and Event. A structure that presents the pure multiple as unified objects, so that the "one" is an operation rather than something given.
A national goal of raising product, service and engineering quality and industrial competitiveness. It was elaborated in the 2023 Outline for Building a Country Strong in Quality.

A goal of making law a source of national strength, placed by the author alongside other "strong country" strategies such as those for industry, technology and education. The author notes it has not yet been formally proposed by the Central Committee.

An approach modelled on Mizoguchi's "China as method" and Chen Kuan-Hsing's "Asia as method". It uses the countryside and urban–rural relations as a standpoint for analysing development, history and global capitalism.
Local bodies that merge county-level newspapers, broadcasters and online platforms, promoted nationally since 2018 for information and public communication.
The head of the Chinese Communist Party committee in a county, usually the most powerful local official and a key post in China's cadre system.

lit: ideology and politics in the curriculum
ex: A policy of building ideological and moral education into all university subjects, not only dedicated political courses.
Dedicated ideological and political theory courses are distinguished from the integration of ideological and moral content into ordinary subject courses.
The established Chinese term for intelligence, counter-espionage and state security work. Its history and heroes are used in internal education.

lit: Study of CPC history and Party building
ex: A first-level academic discipline that the article says was created in 2022. It brings together the study of Party history, Party leadership and Party building, which were previously spread across other disciplines.
The academic discipline devoted to the history of the Communist Party of China, closely tied to Party education and to the Party's official historical narrative.

en: the CPC's War of Resistance against Japan
q: CPC's War of Resistance against Japan
lit: history of the CPC's resistance war
ex: The history of the Chinese Communist Party's role in the 1937–1945 war against Japan, known in China as the War of Resistance (14 years if counted from 1931). It is a major sub-field of Party history research.

lit: National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference
ex: The Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, a national advisory body that brings together Party and non-Party figures and is part of the united front system.
A policy adopted in the border regions in the early 1940s to cut down military and government staff and reduce the burden on the population during economic difficulty.
A value promoted in official discourse: devotion to precision, quality and continual improvement in one's work.

en: creating a better life for the people
q: creating a better life for the people
ex: A Party slogan, prominent after the 19th Party Congress (2017), that frames the Party's goal as meeting people's growing needs for a better life.

en: creation of model areas for ethnic unity and progress
q: creation of model areas for ethnic unity and progress
ex: A campaign in which localities, institutions and schools are evaluated and recognised for promoting ethnic solidarity.
The doctrine that humans and species were created by a deity. The article treats it as the main target of evolutionary theory.
Converting inherited cultural elements into forms suited to present needs. Here the authors use it for Mao turning the doctrine of contradiction into leadership methods.

zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
ex: An official formula for handling traditional Chinese culture: reworking its content and forms to suit present needs, rather than either discarding or simply reviving it.
Official formula for the approach to traditional culture: transforming it creatively and developing it innovatively to fit contemporary needs.

zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
ex: A Party formula for how traditional culture should be treated: reworked and given new forms and meanings suited to contemporary society.
Mass-membership lending bodies in the Soviet areas that offered low-interest loans to members as an alternative to usurers.
Sun's name for the claim that labour time can no longer measure value under cognitive capitalism, which would undermine the labour theory of value.

zh: 批判的马克思主义学派
ex: A post-Soviet Russian current associated with Alexander Buzgalin and Andrei Kolganov. It seeks a new Marxist political economy distinct from Soviet Marxism.
A Party practice, drawn from Leninist tradition, of members openly criticising each other and themselves. It is used in meetings such as democratic life meetings.

A long-standing Communist Party practice of members openly criticising one another and examining their own faults, usually in meetings such as democratic life meetings. The Party describes it as a core method of internal discipline and a political strength.

The article's label for Western Left approaches that treat use-value, via exchange-value, as alienated into spectacle, symbols or subject identities. They focus on micro-level power that shapes subjects.
Marx's name for his project of analysing capitalism by criticising the political economy that took its categories as natural and eternal. It is the subtitle of Capital.
The transfer of data out of or into China, which Chinese law subjects to security assessment and regulation.

en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
q: crossing the river by feeling the stones
lit: feeling the stones to cross the river
ex: A phrase associated with the reform era, describing gradual, pilot-based experimentation when the path is not yet clear.

en: cultivating oneself to bring peace to others
q: cultivating oneself to bring peace to others
ex: A phrase from the Analects (Confucius). It expresses the idea that personal moral self-cultivation leads to social peace and good governance.
The Chinese rendering of the Western term "cult", used in Chinese scholarship for groups regarded as harmful or deviant. It is closely tied in Chinese usage to the category of "evil cults" (xiéjiào).

The official Chinese term for religious or quasi-religious groups the state deems illegal and harmful. It is applied to groups such as Falun Gong and Almighty God, and its scope is contested outside China.
The authors' term for the JCP's strategy of reconciling Marxism with local traditions such as Confucian ethics and Buddhism to reduce resistance.

The idea that poverty has a cultural and ideological dimension, such as illiteracy and backward attitudes, to be tackled alongside material poverty. Here the author applies it to Lenin's educational and propaganda policies.

A phrase from Mao Zedong, who said that besides the armed forces the revolution needed a cultural force of writers, artists and scholars. It is used for intellectuals organised under Party leadership.
A bookshop and organisation founded by Mao in Changsha in 1920 to circulate new periodicals and books, including Marxist and Russian revolutionary writings.
Chinese scholars who engage with Christianity as an academic or cultural subject, and who may or may not be church members. The author treats them as covert propagators of theism.
The authors' term for the composite formed by Marxism, fine traditional Chinese culture and absorbed Western elements. They present it as dynamic and evolving.
A Party concept, part of the Four-sphere Confidence, calling for confidence in China's cultural tradition and in the culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Official slogan calling for confidence in China's own cultural tradition, revolutionary culture and socialist culture. It is presented as a basis for national rejuvenation.

An official formula stressing confidence in China's own cultural tradition and socialist culture, and the drive to strengthen them. It features in recent Party documents on building a strong socialist culture.
A communication-studies concept for the loss of value when a cultural product is decoded by audiences from a different culture. The author uses it to explain obstacles to foreign understanding.
The capacity to set the terms, concepts and narratives through which culture and values are understood and communicated. It is a common concept in Chinese discussions of ideology.
A Communist-side term for the Guomindang's suppression of left-wing publications and writers in the 1930s, modelled on the 'encirclement campaigns' against the Red Army.
A principle, associated with France, that cultural goods should be exempt from ordinary free-trade rules so that states may protect and support national culture.

A biological metaphor for deep, stable and inheritable cultural patterns of thought and value that shape a people's behaviour. Chinese official and academic discourse uses it often in discussing traditional culture.
The management and guidance of cultural affairs through state and social institutions, a topic in Chinese policy and academic debate.
A concept from Gramsci about ruling-class leadership through culture and consent. In the article, left and right accuse each other of seeking it.

The extension of imperialist domination into culture, through unequal relations in cultural power, media, knowledge and values. In this article it is analysed mainly through Western left-wing critics.

The sector producing and distributing cultural goods and services, such as games, film, animation and online literature. In Chinese policy it is treated as a field for both economic growth and cultural development.

The Party's claimed authority over the direction of culture and ideology, linked to the Gramscian notion of hegemony. Xi Jinping stressed it at the June 2023 symposium on cultural inheritance and development.
Here used for Marxist-influenced critical theory that stresses culture and ideology over economics. In Western right-wing discourse the label is often polemical, and the article reports both uses.
The task Xi Jinping set out in June 2023: to promote cultural prosperity, build China into a cultural power and build the modern civilization of the Chinese nation.

zh: 担负新时代的文化使命
en: cultural mission of the new era
q: cultural mission of the new era
py: dānfù xīn shídài de wénhuà shǐmìng
lit: shouldering the cultural mission of the new era
ex: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping, who at the 2023 national conference on propaganda and ideological work stressed the task of developing socialist culture with Chinese characteristics and advancing Chinese civilization.

The transformation of the cultural sphere from traditional to modern forms, treated in Party discourse as one component of socialist modernization alongside the economic, political, social and ecological ones.

In Chinese official discourse, a label for attitudes that wholly negate a nation's traditional culture or its own cultural path. Xi Jinping has repeatedly criticised it since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A term used by the author and others for religious outreach carried out through academic seminars, translated theology, courses and lectures. It is not official policy vocabulary.
A term the author uses for an excessive affirmation of tradition and a wish to revive Confucian culture in place of other ideas, including Marxism.
Lenin's term, used in the early 1920s, for raising literacy and general cultural level in Soviet Russia as a precondition of socialism. It is not the Chinese Cultural Revolution of 1966–76.
The idea that a country's cultural identity, values and ideology are part of national security and must be protected from outside influence.
A concept associated with the sociologist Fei Xiaotong, meaning a society's reflective understanding of its own culture. It is widely used in Chinese discussions of culture.
The influence a country gains through culture and values rather than coercion. In Chinese policy discourse it is treated as part of comprehensive national strength.
Xi's term, used since 2023, for a culture's capacity to stand on its own, develop itself and respond to challenges. Official texts treat it as the basis of cultural confidence.
The shift in historiography from socio-economic analysis towards culture, consciousness and mentalities. The article credits Thompson with initiating it among British Marxist historians.
The extension of the Party's united-front strategy to writers, artists and intellectuals of differing political views who were willing to support resistance to Japan.
An official goal of building China into a country with strong cultural soft power and influence, set as part of the wider aim of a modern socialist strong country.
Horkheimer and Adorno's term for the standardised mass production of film, radio and magazines. They saw it as manipulating the public.
A term used in Party anti-corruption work for values, norms and education that promote honesty and probity among officials and society.
Hegel's idea that absolute reason works through individuals' passions to realise ends they did not intend.

zh: 整治形式主义为基层减负
en: curbing formalism to reduce burdens on the grassroots
q: curbing formalism to reduce burdens on the grassroots
py: zhěngzhì xíngshì zhǔyì wèi jīcéng jiǎnfù
lit: rectifying formalism to lighten the load on the grassroots
ex: A campaign to limit excessive paperwork, meetings, inspections and online reporting demanded of local cadres by higher levels.

en: curing the illness to save the patient
q: curing the illness to save the patient
lit: treat the disease, save the person
ex: A long-standing Party principle for handling erring members: criticise and educate them rather than simply punish them.

en: cutting overcapacity, destocking, deleveraging, lowering costs and strengthening weak links
q: cutting overcapacity, destocking, deleveraging, lowering costs and strengthening weak links
py: sān qù yī jiàng yī bǔ
lit: three cuts, one reduction, one supplement
ex: The five priority tasks of supply-side structural reform set by the Central Economic Work Conference in December 2015.
A strategic goal promoted under Xi Jinping since 2014 to make China strong in internet technology, cybersecurity and the digital economy.

lit: strategy of a strong network country
ex: A policy goal, promoted under Xi Jinping, of making China strong in internet technology, governance and information security. It is usually tied to the broader work of cyberspace administration.
Chen's term for the large and widening body of workers and users subject to digital capital's control and exploitation. He sees it as a potential revolutionary subject.

The idea that a state holds supreme authority within its borders and independence abroad over network infrastructure, actors, conduct and data. China promotes it in global internet governance, and a 2023 World Internet Conference document set out this definition.
A theory associated with Paul Cockshott and others, holding that modern computing makes rational, real-time planning of a socialist economy feasible.

en: cycle of order and disorder, rise and fall
q: cycle of order and disorder, rise and fall
lit: periodic law of order, disorder, rise and decline
ex: A phrase for the recurring pattern of dynastic rise and collapse in Chinese history. It is associated with the 1945 Yan'an conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei, and is often cited in Party discourse on long-term rule.

The views set out in 1925 by the Kuomintang theorist Dai Jitao, who grounded Sun Yat-sen's doctrine in Confucian benevolence, rejected class struggle and urged Communists to leave their party. Communist writers treated it as the ideological preparation of the KMT right wing.
A central concept in Chinese philosophy, especially Daoism and Confucianism, denoting the underlying way of nature and of right human conduct.
Relating to the school of thought associated with Laozi and Zhuangzi. Its texts use xuwu for the formless, empty nature of the Dao.
An official ideal of hard work and self-reliance, drawn from the development of the Daqing oilfield in the Northeast from the 1960s.

en: dare to struggle and be good at struggle
q: dare to struggle and be good at struggle
ex: A formula stressed in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress as one of three things the whole Party must uphold. It pairs willingness to confront challenges with skill in strategy and tactics.
Heidegger's term for the human being as the entity that questions and understands Being. Chinese translations render it as "此在".

en: data as a factor of production
q: data as a factor of production
ex: Official Chinese policy and academic term for treating data as a production factor alongside land, labour, capital and technology. Chinese policy documents have promoted it since around 2019–2020.
The author's term for individuals who, under digital capitalism, have been shaped to trust and obey data and platforms. It echoes the article's idea of data fetishism.
The article's term for data treated as a valuable productive asset, built up chiefly by firms and platforms from users' and employees' digital labour.
A concept from Nick Couldry and Ulises Mejias, who compare large-scale data extraction by technology firms to historical colonial appropriation. Zhang applies it to Western tech giants' global reach.
The author's extension of Marx's fetishism of commodities, money and capital. It describes reverence for data as the source of knowledge and the good life.
The authors' term for workers hired by platforms to clean, process and analyse data into commodities. They distinguish them from ordinary users, whose traces merely supply raw data.
A proposed arrangement in which an independent third party manages public data assets to prevent platforms' private interests from eroding the public interest.

lit: datafication of ideological and political education
ex: The authors' term for applying big data, AI and computational methods to the subjects, content, methods and platforms of ideological and political education.

Measures such as labour law, welfare provision and union bargaining that shield labour-power from pure market determination. The usage follows Polanyi's account of the protective counter-movement against the labour market.
The removal of communist symbols, institutions and legitimacy after the Soviet collapse. Lü uses it for a long process from the Cold War to the present.
In the article, the policy of reducing or abandoning use of the US dollar in international settlement, payment and reserves in favour of other currencies.
A term Tai Lihua uses for Western Marxism's drift away from political economy in its objects, themes, methods, researchers' disciplinary commitments and output.
Official term for policies in Xinjiang aimed at countering religious extremism. The article describes them as combining education, legal measures and mass work.

A term for policies and currents that roll back economic integration, such as trade barriers and protectionism. The article treats it as a stage beyond earlier 'anti-globalization' thought, now carried out by governments.
Hou's term for the tendency to strip Marxist philosophy of its class and worldview character. He describes it as depoliticizing and as a form of 'removing the firewood from under the pot'.
The author's label for parties abandoning Marxism as their guiding ideology or sole theoretical basis.
The author's phrase for Western parties' practice of sidelining popular interests while claiming to represent the people.
The campaign begun by Khrushchev's 1956 secret speech at the 20th CPSU Congress, criticizing Stalin's personality cult and abuses of power.

The process of dismantling the political and ideological system and the personality cult built under Stalin, beginning with Khrushchev's 1956 secret speech. The author treats it as a negation of Stalin and of Soviet history.

A theme in French structuralism and postmodern thought that the autonomous, rational human subject is dissolved by structures, language or power. The article traces its Marxist forms from the Second International to Althusser.

zh: 关于真理标准问题的讨论
en: the debate on the criterion of truth
q: debate on the criterion of truth
py: guānyú zhēnlǐ biāozhǔn wèntí de tǎolùn
ex: A 1978 nationwide discussion launched by an article arguing that practice is the sole criterion of truth. It is regarded in Party history as intellectual preparation for the reform turn.

zh: 真理标准问题的大讨论
en: debate on the criterion of truth
q: debate on the criterion of truth
py: zhēnlǐ biāozhǔn wèntí de dà tǎolùn
ex: A 1978 debate which held that practice is the sole criterion of truth. It helped to loosen dogmatic adherence to Mao-era positions and to prepare for reform and opening up.

en: the debate on the criterion of truth
q: debate on the criterion of truth
lit: great discussion on the criterion of truth
ex: A 1978 ideological debate asserting that practice is the sole criterion of truth, which loosened dogmatic constraints and prepared the ground for reform.

en: debate on the criterion of truth
q: debate on the criterion of truth
lit: discussion of the question of the criterion of truth
ex: A 1978 nationwide debate, begun by the article "Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth", which became the ideological basis for ending the Mao-era dogmatism and launching reform.
A scholarly controversy among Japanese Marxists in the late 1920s and early 1930s over how to analyse the character of Japanese capitalism and the appropriate revolutionary strategy.

A student-led anti-Japanese demonstration that began in Beiping on 9 December 1935, protesting Japanese pressure to detach North China. It is commemorated in Chinese historiography as a turning point in the national salvation movement.
A concept, also used by the International Labour Organization, covering adequate pay, good working conditions, social protection and sound labour relations.
A document signed in Washington on 1 January 1942 by 26 Allied states pledging joint war effort against the Axis powers.
The authors' term for questioning or mocking the accounts of revolutionary heroes. They treat it as a political attack, not as scholarship.
A Chinese phrase for the severing of economic, technological and supply-chain ties, mainly used to describe US and Western policy toward China. Official Chinese discourse opposes it.
An ecological philosophy associated with Arne Naess. It stresses ecocentric equality and a wider ecological self that is realised together with other beings.

zh: 实体经济和数字经济深度融合
en: deep integration of the real economy and the digital economy
q: deep integration of the real economy and the digital economy
py: shítǐ jīngjì hé shùzì jīngjì shēndù rónghé
ex: Official policy goal of applying digital technologies and data across production sectors, especially manufacturing. The article abbreviates it as "shi-shu ronghe" (实数融合).

zh: 学位授予和人才培养学科目录
py: Xuéwèi shòuyǔ hé réncái péiyǎng xuékē mùlù
lit: Catalogue of disciplines for degree conferral and talent training
ex: The catalogue issued by the Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council and the Ministry of Education, revised in 2011. Only disciplines listed in it can independently grant degrees, recruit and train graduate students.
A current of thought and movement that calls for reducing material and energy throughput in rich countries without lowering wellbeing. Albert distinguishes it from growth-oriented socialism.
The decline of manufacturing's share of output and employment in advanced economies. The authors link it to the export of low- and mid-range industry to developing countries.

lit: natural theology / theory of a natural God
ex: The view that God created a rationally ordered world but does not intervene in it; it was widespread among seventeenth- and eighteenth-century thinkers.

lit: landlords of the way of the gods
ex: Mao's term in the Xunwu Investigation for temples, monasteries, shrines and altars that owned land and collected rents. He classed them among 'public landlords'.
Amin's strategy for peripheral countries: breaking from the logic of the capitalist world market in order to pursue an autonomous, socialist development path.
A current of Italian Marxism that grew out of Galvano della Volpe's work. It stresses close, rigorous reading of Marx's texts and a scientific, anti-Hegelian approach.
Policy tools that expand and shape demand, especially domestic consumption and investment. Official texts pair it with supply-side reform as mutually complementary.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion with binding unity of action under higher bodies.

The organisational principle of Leninist parties and of the Chinese state, combining democratic discussion and election with binding central decisions. The article treats the Commune's centralisation dilemma as relevant to it.
A faction in the Russian Communist Party that criticised bureaucratic centralisation and called for broader internal democracy. It was also criticised at the Tenth Congress.
The gap between the promise of democracy and its performance in meeting citizens' demands. The article uses it for Latin America's 'limited democracy' after the end of military rule.

A coalition of smaller non-Communist political groups and intellectuals, founded in 1941 and 1944 in its later form. It sought a third path between the Kuomintang and the CPC and was close to the CPC on the coalition-government demand.
Regular Party branch meetings in which members review their conduct and engage in criticism and self-criticism.

Badiou's term, from Logics of Worlds, for the contemporary outlook that recognises only bodies and languages and denies truths and the infinite. The article treats it as one of the two enemies of the new materialist dialectic.
The eight non-Communist parties legally recognised in China, most founded before 1949. They accept Party leadership and take part in consultation and in the discussion of state affairs.
The campaigns of the early 1950s that abolished landlord and feudal privileges in minority areas. They included rent reduction, land reform and, later, reform of religious institutions.
A current that seeks socialism through elections and parliamentary means. The article applies it to the Philippine Democratic Socialist Party and the PLM.
The author's term for groups, such as the rural poor and the elderly, who are excluded from digital participation channels by unequal access to digital and intelligent resources.

A policy adopted at the Second Party Congress (1922) of cooperating with the Kuomintang and other democratic forces against imperialism and warlords while the Party kept its independence. It paved the way for the first Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.
The alliance policy adopted at the Second Congress in 1922. It proposed uniting workers, peasants, the petty bourgeoisie and the bourgeoisie against imperialism and warlords.
An official Chinese formulation calling for equality of all states, joint rule-making and opposition to hegemony in world affairs.
The body of ideas associated with Deng Xiaoping on reform and opening up and socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is written into the Party's guiding ideology.

A description of China's administrative structure, in which vertical lines of functional departments (tiao) intersect with territorial governments (kuai). Critics use the term for fragmentation and poor coordination.
A school, largely Latin American and Marxist-influenced, holding that underdevelopment in the periphery results from exploitation by core capitalist countries.

A body of theory, developed in Latin America from the mid-twentieth century, that explains underdevelopment through the dependence of 'peripheral' economies on 'central' ones. The article treats its Marxist strands as a Latin American contribution.
Chen's term for a capitalist path in which a country's economic policy serves external powers rather than national interests. The author equates it with Wallerstein's peripheral capitalism.
A term from dependency-style Marxist analysis for a capitalism whose economy and politics are subordinated to foreign powers. The article uses it to characterise Lebanon's social nature.
The rendering Xi proposes for xiejiao, borrowed from Western sociology of religion's term 'cult' (膜拜团体) with the qualifier 'destructive'.

en: developing morally, intellectually, physically, aesthetically and in labour
q: developing morally, intellectually, physically, aesthetically and in labour
py: dé zhì tǐ měi láo quánmiàn fāzhǎn
lit: all-round development of morality, intelligence, physique, aesthetics and labour
ex: A formula for the aims of education in China, stressing all-round development in five areas, with aesthetic education as one.
A line attributed to Deng Xiaoping during the reform era, used to stress that economic growth takes priority in solving China's problems.
The author's term for where the country stands in its developmental stage, contrasted with its "historical position" (历史方位) within the course of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Bai's phrase for Capital's method of 'discovering a new civilisation in criticising the old one'. It combines negation of capitalist civilisation with the creation of a new one.
Lukács's account of Marxism's essence as a method that grasps society as a whole in which the whole determines the parts. Chinese scholarship treats it as the foundation of Western Marxism.

The philosophical system of the Marxist tradition, developed by Engels, Lenin and Soviet and Chinese theorists, combining materialism with dialectics. Hou defends it against those who call it 'official philosophy'.
A Hegelian-Marxist notion in which a concept is negated by a deeper one while its valid content is retained. The author uses it to describe how Marx's categories develop through stages.
The authors' term for the Laozi's recognition that opposites transform into and unite with each other. They distinguish it from dialectics as a worked-out method.

zh: 辩证唯物主义一元史观
ex: The author's term for Marx's conception of history as a single, materially grounded and dialectically developing process. It is set against idealist or pluralist accounts.
The Marxist method of grasping things in their universal connection, change and development. Chen presents it as a guide to research that complements analytical tools.
An's name for the theoretical basis of the greater historical materialism: the mutual shaping of humans and their environment through labour.

zh: 中国特色的马克思主义辩证法
en: dialectics of Marxism with Chinese characteristics
q: dialectics of Marxism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The author's phrase for a Chinese-context development of Marxist dialectics, which the article says should draw on critical study of foreign interpretations.

Engels's term for the dialectical laws operating in nature. In China it also names an academic field, now called philosophy of science and technology, taught as a Marxist theory course to science graduate students.
A Marxist-Leninist term for bourgeois class rule over the state and society, whatever the formal political system. Deng uses it to characterise cognitive capitalism.
A Marxist term for working-class rule in the transition from capitalism to communism. In Chinese discourse it is linked to the formula of the people's democratic dictatorship.
Mao's term for the anti-Communist faction within the Nationalist camp that favoured attacking the Communists and resisting cooperation.
The essential feature that distinguishes a concept from other concepts under the same genus. The article analyses which elements, such as aim and means, serve as extremism's differentia.
Fei Xiaotong's concept of rural Chinese social relations as concentric circles radiating from the self, contrasted with Western group-based structures.
Lefebvre's term for an alternative space that resists the homogeneity of abstract space and is sought through differentiated everyday spatial practice.

lit: the difficult matter of material interests
ex: Marx's phrase, in the 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, for the embarrassment of having to pronounce on economic questions as editor of the Rheinische Zeitung. He presents it as the initial motive for his economic studies.

A term for the main form capital takes in the digital economy, centred on data and digital platforms. Cai notes that some scholars regard it as not strictly conforming to political-economy norms but uses it provisionally.
A term for capitalism in the era of digital platforms and data. The authors hold that it remains capitalism, still resting on exploitation of living labour.
A national strategy for building China's digital economy, digital government and digital society, promoted in official documents since the late 2010s.
A term used in Chinese official discourse, including in Xi Jinping's 2021 message to the World Internet Conference, for the material, spiritual and institutional achievements of the digital age.

en: digital community with a shared future
q: digital community with a shared future
ex: An extension of the official idea of a community with a shared future for mankind to the digital sphere, referring to international cooperation on digital development and governance.
The idea that information and communication technologies, especially the internet and social media, can strengthen political participation and deliberation.
The use of big data, AI and shared platforms by Party discipline inspection commissions and state supervisory commissions to detect and prevent corruption.
The gap between groups or regions in access to and ability to use digital technologies and infrastructure.
An analogy with the historical enclosure of common land. It refers to tech giants building ecosystems of software, hardware and network connections to appropriate data.
An extension of Marx's commodity fetishism to data and platforms, which are said to hide the social relations and real-economy basis of capital's control.

A term for formalism carried out through digital means, such as compulsory app check-ins, repeated data reporting and showy websites. It is criticised in Party discourse as adding to the burdens on grassroots cadres.
Workers such as ride-hailing drivers, couriers and content creators who depend on platforms for work without a formal employment relationship with them.
The use of digital technologies and data to reshape government administration and public services, a stated national construction goal in China.
A term used in Chinese writing for a state's use of cyberspace and network technology to extend dominance. Chen applies it mainly to the United States.
A shorthand for applying digital and intelligent technologies, such as big data and AI, to ideological and political education.
The control by advanced countries of data, digital infrastructure and digital culture to dominate less developed countries, as the article uses the term.

Spatial concentrations of interlinked firms, suppliers, research institutes, financial bodies and facilities engaged in digital products, services and technology. The article treats them as an organisational form of digital production.

A concept in critical digital studies covering paid and unpaid activity that produces value for digital platforms, including users' data-generating behaviour. The article uses it to describe life time being turned into production time.
The article's term for archival records of spoken testimony by participants or witnesses, generated and stored with digital equipment.

The authors' term for a stage of capitalism in which tech giants, financial oligarchs and politicians extract income through technology, platforms and data rather than production. It builds on earlier 'rentier capitalism' arguments such as Guy Standing's.
The digital strand of the Belt and Road Initiative, covering digital infrastructure and technology cooperation with partner countries.

A label for various proposals by Western left thinkers to achieve socialism through digital technologies such as platforms, big data and automation. Xu treats the term as an umbrella for four theoretical strands.
The authors' extension of Marx's surplus value to profit extracted from digital labour, paid and unpaid, and from digital infrastructure and data.
The authors' term for algorithm-driven standardisation and close monitoring of work, modelled on Taylor's scientific management.

The practice of requiring grassroots workers to document their activity online, through records, photos or logins, so that it can be inspected. Critics within the Party see it as a source of formalism.
Virtual replicas of physical systems or places, used here to test policy options in simulated environments before real-world implementation.
A policy programme to apply information and digital technology to rural production, governance and services. The 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–2025) calls for accelerating its construction.
China's central bank digital currency, in pilot use in a number of provinces. The article treats it as a tool of monetary sovereignty and public payment infrastructure.
A compound of 'digital' and 'intelligent' technologies, referring to big data and artificial intelligence used together.
A recent term combining digitalisation and intelligent (AI) technologies. It refers to organisations using these technologies to strengthen their own capacity.
A Chinese expression combining digital technology and artificial intelligence, used to describe the present stage of technological change.
A composite term for digital technologies combined with artificial intelligence, such as big data, algorithms and generative AI.

en: digital-intelligent development for the health of the whole population
q: digital-intelligent development for the health of the whole population
lit: digital-intelligent construction of health for all people
ex: A phrase from the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, referring to applying big data, AI and related technologies across the health system.
Shorthand for the deep integration of the digital economy with the real (physical, industrial) economy, as used in recent Party policy documents.
Foucault's term, central to Discipline and Punish, for power exercised through training, surveillance and norms in institutions such as prisons, schools and factories.

The independent identity and self-grounded character of an academic discipline, as distinct from borrowing from other fields. It is a theme in recent Chinese debates on building autonomous knowledge systems.
An academic classification of a field of research, listed in the state catalogue for postgraduate education and degree awarding.
The combined work of the Party's discipline inspection commissions and the state supervisory commissions, which oversee Party members and public officials.
A first-level academic discipline formally established in China in 2022. It studies the work of Party discipline inspection commissions and state supervisory commissions.
Party bodies that supervise members' compliance with Party rules and investigate violations. The Central Commission was founded in 1949 with Zhu De as secretary.

en: discipline is stricter than law and comes before it
q: discipline is stricter than law and comes before it
py: jì yán yú fǎ, jì zài fǎ qián
lit: discipline stricter than law, discipline ahead of law
ex: A principle that Party discipline sets a higher standard than state law and should be applied first, so that violations are caught before they become legal offences.

zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系
en: discipline system, academic system and discourse system
q: discipline system, academic system and discourse system
py: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
ex: Xi Jinping's formula for the three parts of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The article calls them the 'three major systems'.
The articulation of Party discipline with state law, through institutional design and procedures. It covers case transfer, evidence, responsibility and the boundaries between the two systems.
The renewal of theoretical and political language so that Marxism can address new problems and persuade audiences in China.
The capacity to shape how events and ideas are framed in international debate. It is a common concept in Chinese writing on international communication.
The capacity to set the terms, concepts and narratives in ideological and propaganda work. Party leaders have stressed since 2012 that it must remain under Party control.
The organised set of concepts, themes, expressions and narratives through which a party or state presents its ideas.
The author's term for narratives about China and the CPC that the US and the West are said to construct deliberately to stigmatise it and build a hostile consensus.

zh: 有鉴别的对待，有扬弃的继承
py: yǒu jiànbié de duìdài, yǒu yángqì de jìchéng
lit: treating with discrimination, inheriting with sublation
ex: Xi Jinping's formula for handling traditional culture: sort its essence from the outdated, discard the latter, and develop the former.
The dominance of one side's concepts and standards in setting the terms of debate. Chinese theorists use it to criticise the Western monopoly on defining 'democracy'.
A term in Chinese official and academic usage for strengthening China's ability to shape international narratives and theoretical debate.
Chinese rendering of Max Weber's Entzauberung der Welt, the process by which rational explanation displaces religious and magical worldviews in modern society.
Max Weber's term for the loss of magical and religious meaning in the modern, rationalised world.
Official phrase, used from around 2020–21, for curbing monopolistic and unregulated growth of large private capital, especially in platform companies.
An official phrase, prominent since about 2020, for unregulated growth of private capital, especially in platform and technology sectors. It is used to justify regulation and anti-monopoly measures.

en: dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western
q: dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western
py: gǔ jīn zhōng xī zhī zhēng
ex: A long-running debate in modern Chinese thought over how to relate tradition to modernity and Chinese culture to Western culture. Xi Jinping has said the present era is better placed to resolve it.
Mao Zedong's metaphor for studying a small number of representative cases in depth in order to understand wider conditions.

A computational approach to culture that analyses very large text and image corpora statistically rather than reading individual works closely. It echoes the 'distant reading' idea in digital humanities.

One of the 'six views' (world view, values, history, civilization, democracy, ecology) that Xi Jinping said are contained in Chinese modernization. This article treats the world view as the leading one.

The principle, taken from Marx's account of the first phase of communist society, that income is allocated according to the quantity and quality of labour contributed. Chinese texts treat it as the main distribution principle under socialist public ownership.
Marx's principle for the higher stage of communist society, summed up as "from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs".

A principle of China's income distribution system under which capital, technology, data and other production factors receive income according to their contribution. It operates alongside distribution according to work.

zh: 按劳分配为主体、多种分配方式并存
en: distribution by labour as the mainstay, with several modes coexisting
q: distribution by labour as the mainstay, with several modes coexisting
py: àn láo fēnpèi wéi zhǔtǐ, duōzhǒng fēnpèi fāngshì bìngcún
ex: Part of the basic socialist economic system as defined by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). It combines payment according to labour with payment to other production factors such as capital, land, technology and data.
Rancière's term for the way a social order divides what can be seen, said and heard, and by whom. It is the core of his political aesthetics oriented towards equality.

en: divergence between virtual and real sectors
q: divergence between virtual and real sectors
lit: leaving the real for the virtual
ex: A phrase describing capital and firms moving away from the real economy towards finance. The authors use it to describe both Western economies and an early tendency in China.
The idea that countries may reach and build socialism in different ways according to their conditions.

A formula for the Chinese nation as a single community made up of many ethnic groups, associated with Fei Xiaotong's 1988 account of the Chinese nation. It is now standard in official ethnic policy discourse.
A popular label for television dramas about the war with absurd plots and superhuman heroes. The authorities criticised and curbed them from 2013.

en: division of labour among the three powers
q: division of labour among the three powers
ex: Vietnam's official formula, written into the 2013 constitution, for how legislative, executive and judicial power are organised. It stresses unified state power with cooperation and supervision among organs, as opposed to separation of powers.
Part of a three-stage anti-corruption formula: officials should be unable to, dare not and not want to be corrupt. The third stage stresses moral and cultural self-discipline.
Foucault's phrase for bodies made useful and obedient through disciplinary techniques.
The 1982 Central Committee document on the basic viewpoint and policy on religious questions in the socialist period. It served as the main guideline for religious work in the following decades.
In Party history, the practice of applying doctrine or foreign models without regard to actual conditions. It is attributed to the "Left" leadership before Zunyi.

en: doing practical things for the people
q: doing practical things for the people
lit: I do practical things for the masses
ex: A practice campaign linked to the 2021 Party history education, in which Party members and cadres were asked to address concrete problems of ordinary people.
A traditional Party method of persuasion through personal conversation and attention to individuals' needs, which the author treats as a form of diffuse cultural power.
The idea that China's economy should rely mainly on internal production, distribution and consumption, with international trade complementing it.

A long-standing policy aim of raising household consumption and investment within China so that growth relies less on exports. The article treats it as the strategic base of the 'new development paradigm'.
The principle in China's basic economic system that public ownership remains the mainstay while multiple ownership forms develop alongside it.
A government programme, launched in 2015, to build world-class universities and disciplines in China.
Policy announced by Mao Zedong in 1956 encouraging "a hundred flowers blossoming" in the arts and "a hundred schools contending" in scholarship, under Party leadership.
Karl Polanyi's idea that market expansion provokes a counter-movement of social protection. The article uses it to explain alternating waves of nationalisation and privatisation.
A 2021 policy to reduce students' homework burden and off-campus tutoring, including tighter regulation of private tutoring companies.

lit: dual support (supporting the army and the people)
ex: A long-running campaign in which the army and government/people are to support each other: society honours soldiers and their families, and the military supports local communities.
The author's term for the spiritual drive needed to realize the Chinese Dream. The author says its content is still being formulated.
A cultural-policy formula requiring that social benefit and economic benefit be combined, with social benefit given priority.
China's twin goals of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060.
China's pledge to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and reach carbon neutrality before 2060.

In Marx's Capital the term refers to the concrete and abstract aspects of commodity-producing labour. Li uses it in a wider sense, for labour's natural aspect (people and nature) and its social aspect (people and people).
An economic strategy that stresses a domestic cycle of production and consumption as the mainstay, interacting with international trade and investment.
An economic strategy put forward in 2020. It takes the domestic cycle as the main body while the domestic and international cycles reinforce each other.
A Shandong campaign slogan: Party building should merge with economic development and with social governance, in order to create new economic space and a new governance pattern.
The author's own analytical term for the combination of economic and political power that decides which sovereign currency becomes world money.
A system under which Party members register both at their workplace Party branch and at the community where they live, to take part in local service work.
The arrangement since 1994 in which the Cuban peso and the convertible peso both circulated, with different exchange rates. The 2020–21 reform aims to abolish the convertible peso.
A term from Corden and Neary (1982) for the de-industrialisation of the Netherlands after its natural gas boom, used for how a resource export boom can undermine other sectors.
China's general policy from 2020 to late 2022 of rapidly suppressing every outbreak through testing, tracing, lockdowns and quarantine.
A national project that moves data-processing demand from the eastern coast to computing hubs in western China, where energy and land are more available.
A humanist current of Marxism in Eastern Europe, including the Czech Kosík and the Yugoslav Praxis group, critical of both capitalism and Soviet-style socialism.

en: the East rising and the West declining
q: East rising and the West declining
ex: A phrase in Chinese official and scholarly discourse describing a perceived shift of global power from the West towards China and other Eastern countries. The article treats it as a long-term historical trend.
A dispute around 1941 in which the Nationalist Fifth War Zone pressed the Hubei provincial government to hand over control of local administration in eastern Hubei.
The CCP's term for feared deals among Japan, Britain, the United States and the Kuomintang that would sacrifice China, by analogy with the 1938 Munich Agreement.

The Comintern's policy of supporting anti-imperialist national movements in Asia and creating communist parties there, as part of world revolution. The 1920 Baku congress was one of its main expressions.

en: eating from the same big pot
q: eating from the same big pot
ex: A colloquial term for egalitarian distribution regardless of effort or contribution, associated with the pre-reform economy and criticised in reform-era discourse.
Malm's proposal for a state-led, emergency-style response to ecological catastrophe, drawing on the Leninist and socialist tradition.
A current that uses Marxist theory to analyse ecological crisis as a product of capitalism. John Bellamy Foster is among its leading figures.
A strand of left thought holding that the ecological crisis cannot be solved under capitalism and requires a socialist reorganisation of production. The article discusses Western versions of it.

lit: ecological capitalisation / turning ecology into capital
ex: The article's term for converting natural resources and the goods and services they provide into capital that yields profit. It names the core method of neoliberal environmental governance as the authors describe it.
An official goal and framework in China that places environmental protection within the overall development strategy. It is also the title of the Xi Jinping selected works cited in the article.
An official policy goal, written into Party and state documents since the early 2010s, of integrating environmental protection into economic, political and social development.

A concept developed by the French Communist Party, which holds that ecology is a core element of communism and that communism is necessarily ecological. Pierre Laurent stated this at a 2018 conference.
In this article, a system in which dominant capitalist powers control the natural resources and ecological conditions of other regions to serve their own accumulation.
A strand of Western Marxism from the late twentieth century that combines Marxist critique of capitalism with ecological thought to explain environmental crisis.
Policy concept referring to converting ecosystem services such as clean air, water and carbon sinks into economic value through pricing, trading or compensation.
Boundaries drawn around ecologically important or fragile areas within which development is restricted or prohibited. They form part of China's land-space planning.

A concept developed from Emmanuel's unequal exchange. It holds that trade between core and periphery moves resources and environmental burdens asymmetrically, even when prices look fair in money terms.

The authors' term for a view of wealth that counts ecological resources and environment as social wealth alongside material and spiritual wealth. It builds on Xi Jinping's 2018 remark that green mountains are both ecological and economic wealth.

The author's label for the value-laden dimension of Marx's analysis of capital. It concerns the human meaning of labour, property and exchange, and what people ought to do, beyond the factual laws of economics.
The relations of production that, in the Marxist base–superstructure model, underlie a society's political and ideological superstructure.

A Marxist pair of categories: the economic base is the sum of relations of production, and the superstructure covers the political, legal and ideological forms resting on it. The superstructure is held to react back on the base.
The Party's basic line adopted after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, shifting priority from class struggle to developing the economy.

A set of ideas and models in which workers or citizens share in the ownership, management and investment decisions of firms, typically through cooperatives. The article treats it as a recurring project of the Western left.

The reading, attributed to Second International theorists such as Kautsky, that the economic base mechanically determines the superstructure and that socialism will arrive through natural development. Western Marxism's founders attacked it.
The authors' label for a reading of historical materialism that treats social development as dictated by economic conditions, leaving little room for human agency. They attribute it to Kautsky.
The classical political economy assumption of a rational individual maximising self-interest. Marx criticised it as an abstraction from capitalist relations.
In this article, the philosophical study of how capital and capitalist society arise and develop historically. It mediates between economics and anthropology.
In this article, the form of domination that capital exercises through market relations and wage labour. It replaces direct personal coercion with impersonal, "silent" compulsion.
The early-1960s period in which the Party scaled back the Great Leap Forward targets and restored balance among sectors.
A term drawn from Marx's 1859 Preface. Zhang uses it for the antagonistic stages (Asiatic, ancient, feudal, capitalist) in which the production of things dominates human beings.
The 1980 book by Hungarian economist János Kornai, which attributes chronic shortage in socialist economies to soft budget constraints. The authors reread it as applicable to capitalism too.
A trend in Russian Social-Democracy around 1900 that limited the workers' movement to economic struggles and downplayed political and theoretical work. Lenin criticised it.
A current in Russian Social-Democracy around 1900 that stressed economic struggle for workers' immediate demands over political struggle. Lenin attacked it in What Is to Be Done?
The deep integration of digital technologies into education systems, which official documents, including the 20th Party Congress report (2022), treat as a strategic task.

A strand of Party ideological and political education that aims to instil Marxist belief, the communist ideal and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, especially among Party members and young people.

zh: 教育强国建设规划纲要（2024—2035年）
py: Jiàoyù qiángguó jiànshè guīhuà gāngyào (2024–2035 nián)
lit: Outline of the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country
