ex: A planning document issued by the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the State Council in 2025. It sets goals for education development through 2035.
A metaphor for the overall environment of people, resources, institutions and atmosphere in which students are educated. The authors use it to stress coordination across all parts of a university.
A qualitative research method in education that interprets teachers' own accounts of their experience.
The people and institutions that carry out ideological and political education on behalf of the Party and state. The authors treat them as a collective, not individual teachers.
The Third Plenum's term for how well China's external communication achieves its aims. The authors read it as covering persuasiveness and cultural resonance as well as reach.

en: an efficient market and a capable government
q: efficient market and a capable government
ex: Official formula for the combined roles of market and state in the socialist market economy. It is used to argue that both should play active, complementary roles.

The practice or idea of equalising incomes regardless of work contribution. In Chinese and Cuban reform discourse it is criticised as distinct from socialist equality and as producing "eating from the same big pot".

Eight pairs of requirements for teaching the courses, set out by Xi Jinping at a 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses, such as political and academic character, and indoctrination and heuristic teaching.
A summary of the core theoretical propositions of Xi Jinping Thought, presented in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).
Xi Jinping's eight tests for judging whether a country's political system is democratic and effective, including orderly leadership succession and effective checks on power.
A code of socialist moral conduct promoted by Hu Jintao in March 2006. It pairs eight behaviours to be honoured with eight to be shunned.
A list of competences for cadres set out by Xi Jinping, such as learning, political leadership, reform and innovation, and risk prevention.

zh: 对外经济技术援助的八项原则
py: duìwài jīngjì jìshù yuánzhù de bā xiàng yuánzé
ex: Principles Zhou Enlai announced during his 1963–64 tour of Africa. They stress equality, mutual benefit and no political conditions on aid.
Xi Jinping's 2019 guidelines for running ideological and political theory courses. They pair elements such as political and academic nature, values and knowledge, and theory and practice.
Eight paired principles for reforming ideological and political courses, set out by Xi Jinping in 2019, such as unifying political and academic character or explicit and implicit education.
A set of eight strategic measures for Zhejiang's development, put forward in 2003 by Xi Jinping when he led the province.
Rules adopted by the Party leadership in December 2012 against extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism in officials' work and conduct.

A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee's Political Bureau in December 2012 on improving work style and keeping close to the masses. It restricts official banquets, travel, meetings and perks.
The Eighth National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in 1956, which assessed the completion of socialist transformation and the new tasks of construction.

The Eighth National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in September 1956. It judged that the main domestic contradiction was no longer between the proletariat and the bourgeoisie, but between the people's needs and backward production.

lit: Eighth Congress of the Cuban Communist Party
ex: The congress of the Communist Party of Cuba held in April 2021, which elected Díaz-Canel First Secretary in place of Raúl Castro.
Communist-led army formed in 1937 from the Red Army in the north under the united front with the Nationalists.

Wang's term for the capacity of the capitalist state, owing to the relative separation of economy and politics, to absorb part of the working class's economic demands without threatening capitalist relations of production. It builds on Poulantzas's remark on the "flexibility" of the capitalist state.
A slogan dating from the late 1970s urging Party members to break free of rigid dogma. It is usually paired with seeking truth from facts.
A Party slogan for breaking free of rigid thinking in order to deal with new conditions, closely associated with Deng Xiaoping and the late-1970s reform period.

en: emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts
q: emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts
ex: The Party's official ideological line, associated with Mao's phrase "seek truth from facts" and revived under Deng Xiaoping in 1978. It is used to justify rejecting dogma in favour of practice-based policy.

zh: 解放思想、实事求是、与时俱进
en: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times
q: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times
py: jiěfàng sīxiǎng, shíshì qiúshì, yǔ shí jùjìn
ex: A formula describing the Party's ideological approach, combining Deng Xiaoping-era slogans with a later addition. It is presented as the essence of Marxism in China.

zh: 解放思想、实事求是、与时俱进、求真务实
en: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, keeping pace with the times and being realistic and pragmatic
q: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, keeping pace with the times and being realistic and pragmatic
py: jiěfàng sīxiǎng, shíshì qiúshì, yǔshí jùjìn, qiúzhēn wùshí
ex: A four-part formula of ideological guidelines in Party discourse. It stresses breaking with outdated thinking while basing policy on practical reality.
A psychological idea, used here to mean that visitors learn by physically placing themselves in reconstructed historical scenes and immersive settings.
A mid-level analytical concept used by some Chinese historians for how the Party shapes, manages and channels emotions in governing and mobilising society.
The use of emotional appeals to rally people behind a political campaign, as in land reform or the Korean War.
The Japanese institution of the emperor as sacred head of state. The authors treat it as fundamentally opposed to Marxism; the 1946 constitution made the emperor a symbol of the state.
A strategy named in the Report to the 19th Party Congress that makes employment the top priority of macroeconomic policy.
An official approach that places employment at the centre of macroeconomic and social policy, so that fiscal, monetary and industrial policy are coordinated with job goals.
A policy stance, reaffirmed in the 20th Party Congress report, that treats employment as a priority in macroeconomic and social policy.

en: encircling the cities from the countryside
q: encircling the cities from the countryside
ex: The revolutionary strategy associated with Mao in which the Party built rural base areas before taking the cities.

lit: theory of the end of history
ex: Francis Fukuyama's thesis, after the Cold War, that liberal democracy is the final form of political order. Lan treats it as a myth that real events have refuted.

lit: theory of the end of ideology
ex: A thesis from Western social science holding that grand ideological conflict has ended. Hou treats it as the context for Fukuyama's 'end of history' and for 'de-ideologizing' Marxism.

lit: theory of the end of socialism
ex: The argument, widespread after the Soviet and East European upheavals, that socialism has failed historically. Chinese writers often link it to Fukuyama's "end of history".
A biological metaphor Lu uses for a close, mutually dependent human–AI system that adjusts dynamically, rather than a simple subject–object relation.

A slogan describing the Eighth Route Army's practice of sending forces into enemy-held areas when Japanese and puppet troops attacked its bases. It plays on the better-known guerrilla maxim of retreating when the enemy advances.

Provisions of the UN Charter (Articles 53, 107 and 77) that concern states that were enemies of the Allies in the Second World War. The article reads them as allowing action against such states without Security Council authorisation if they resume aggression.
The share of household spending devoted to food; a falling coefficient is used as an indicator of rising living standards.
A phrase associated with Stalin and widely used in Chinese discourse for writers who shape people's moral and ideological outlook.
A policy line promoting cultural activities and education to strengthen identification with Chinese culture and the Chinese nation among Xinjiang's population.
In the article, officials who held key posts and used them for private gain. The author argues they resisted reform until it let them legalise their wealth.
A term the Party leadership has promoted in recent years. It praises private entrepreneurs' patriotism, innovation, integrity, social responsibility and international vision.
Foster's term for a broad working class defined by its environmental as well as economic conditions, including ecological peasants and workers in the Global South.
Foucault's term (l'épistémè) for the underlying configuration of knowledge that governs how thought is possible in a given period. Yang uses it for the deep structure behind Marx's two texts.
Louis Althusser's thesis that Marx's thought divides around 1845 into an 'ideological' and a 'scientific' phase.

lit: opening up heaven and splitting earth
ex: An idiom drawn from creation myth, used in Party histories to describe the founding of the CPC as an unprecedented turning point.

zh: 平等有序的世界多极化
ex: A formula endorsed by the Central Conference on Work Relating to Foreign Affairs in 2023. It calls for a multipolar world in which states take part as equals and the process is orderly and constructive.
A policy goal of narrowing gaps in access to education, health care, social protection and similar services between regions, urban and rural areas, and social groups.
The Left Party's programme, adopted at its Erfurt congress in October 2011 and still in force. It sets out a 'democratic socialism of the 21st century' and a critique of capitalism.
A term used in the border region for idlers or loafers, often associated with gambling, vagrancy and petty theft. The Party ran campaigns to reform them through productive labour.

Official term for ideological currents such as liberalism, constitutional democracy and historical nihilism, which Party theorists regard as opposed to Marxism. It is used in discussions of ideological work.
The fundamental attribute that distinguishes socialism from other social systems. Deng Xiaoping gave it an explicit definition in 1992, and it has since become a standard theme of Party theory.

The author's own term for a method of seeing through appearances, especially illusory ones, to grasp essence, and then criticising appearances on that basis. The author presents it as the root method of Capital.

py: pò lì bìngjǔ, xiān lì hòu pò
lit: break and establish together, establish first and break later
ex: A reform principle stressed by Xi Jinping: build new arrangements before dismantling old ones, so that change is both rapid and steady. The article treats it as part of the dialectical unity of breaking and establishing.
A principle of building new institutions or practices while dismantling outdated ones.

en: establishing teaching through the Way of spirits
q: establishing teaching through the Way of spirits
lit: setting up instruction by the Way of spirits
ex: A phrase from the Book of Changes, meaning that sages use reverence for the spiritual to educate and transform the people.

en: establishing the new before breaking the old
q: establishing the new before breaking the old
ex: A policy principle for the energy transition: build reliable new energy capacity before phasing out existing fossil sources, so as to protect energy security.
A Confucian-derived notion that rule should be achieved through culture, ritual and education rather than coercion; Hong treats it as a distinctive trait of Chinese civilization.
The author's label for Hegel's response, in which the state is an ethical totality (Sittlichkeit) that unites universal and particular, going beyond subjective morality.

zh: 英国伦理社会主义传统
ex: A line of British anti-capitalist thought from Carlyle and Ruskin to William Morris that criticises capitalism on moral and aesthetic grounds. The article says Thompson largely "invented" it as a tradition in 1955.
Regions with autonomous governments for ethnic minorities, including autonomous regions, prefectures and counties, which hold special local legislative powers.
The Party and state's work on ethnic minority affairs, run partly by the united front system and the State Ethnic Affairs Commission.

zh: 欧洲中心主义单线史观
ex: Liang's term for a view that describes European history as an independent, necessary process running from ancient Greece to the modern West, which leads and defines world history. Liang treats it as largely synonymous with 'Western-centrism'.

A current in Western European communist parties from the 1970s that sought paths to socialism independent of the Soviet model. The article says it weakened the dictatorship of the proletariat and democratic centralism in the CPGB.
The Allied grand strategy of giving priority to defeating Germany before concentrating on Japan. The article argues that China's resistance made this strategy workable.
A grouping of communist parties formed in 2023 after a split in the Initiative of Communist and Workers' Parties of Europe. The article places it in opposition to the World Anti-Imperialist Platform.

lit: raise to the level of principle and the party line
ex: A phrase for inflating a minor issue into a grave political or ideological one. Du's opponent used it to accuse Du of this.
An education approach centred on preparing students for examinations, often contrasted in China with 'quality education' (suzhi jiaoyu).
Mao's image of 1949, when the Party moved to Beijing, of the Party sitting an examination whose judges are the people. Later leaders use it to frame ongoing governance tasks.
Mao's remark to Zhou Enlai in March 1949, as the leadership travelled to Beijing, that they were going to take an examination and must not be like Li Zicheng.
Ritual offerings beyond those prescribed by the state; from the Han onward they were treated as illegitimate and were targeted by officials and thinkers.

en: exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
q: exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
ex: A formula promoted by Xi Jinping and the Party leadership since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It calls for equal, open interaction among civilizations in which each learns from the others.

en: exchanges, interaction and integration among ethnic groups
q: exchanges, interaction and integration among ethnic groups
ex: An official formula for the processes by which ethnic groups are meant to come closer together, used as a policy aim in ethnic work.

en: exhausting the potential of the land
q: exhausting the potential of the land
lit: teaching to exhaust the strength of the land
ex: A policy associated with Li Kui of Wei in the Warring States period, promoting intensive cultivation, crop diversification and timely harvesting.
The term Hou uses for a shift in modern Western philosophy away from epistemology towards existence and lived practice. Hou reads it as a turn to subjective idealism.
Government efforts to guide and stabilise public and market expectations through policy explanation, information disclosure and press briefings. It is treated as part of macroeconomic governance.

Chinese shorthand for Engels's point, in his late letters on historical materialism, that actions have intended aims while their actual results are unintended. Chinese scholars treat it as a contradiction within history.

The core doctrine of Wang Yangming (1472–1529), a Ming-dynasty Neo-Confucian of the 'learning of the mind' school. It means bringing the innate moral sense in the mind to full realisation in thought and action.

en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
q: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
py: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
lit: jointly discuss, jointly build, jointly share
ex: A slogan that sums up the Chinese approach to global governance: decisions are made jointly, institutions are built jointly, and the results are shared by all.

en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
q: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
ex: The official formula (共商共建共享) for Xi Jinping's approach to global governance: decisions made through wide consultation, institutions built jointly, and benefits shared by all.

en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
q: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
py: gòng shāng, gòng jiàn, gòng xiǎng
lit: joint consultation, joint construction, joint sharing
ex: A Chinese formula for global governance and Belt and Road cooperation, stressing joint decision-making, joint building and shared results.
Fighting outside one's own base areas, in enemy-held territory, as opposed to inner-line operations within the base areas.
In this article, the foreign-facing activities of a party that does not yet hold state power. The authors set it against party diplomacy, which belongs to ruling parties.

The Party's own relations with foreign political parties and organisations, distinct from but coordinated with state diplomacy. It is also called 'external work' (对外工作) and is handled mainly by the International Department.

The Party-state's term for communication aimed at foreign audiences, often shortened to waixuan. It covers foreign-language media, press briefings, white papers and cultural exchange; the English equivalent 'propaganda' has a more neutral sense in Chinese.
Hegel's term for reasoning that applies general principles abstractly to any content without entering its substance. Wu equates it with dogmatism or formalism.

In the article's typology, parties that keep a traditional revolutionary stance, such as orthodox communist, Trotskyist, Maoist and anarchist groups. The article describes them as marginal in electoral politics.
The authors' label for expressions that attribute productive force to a single factor, such as knowledge, land or data. They argue these are not separate concepts in Marx.
The view, associated with Say and Smith, that value comes jointly from labour, capital and land. The article treats it as a defence of capitalism.
The view that land, capital, machinery and other non-labour factors also create value. Chinese Marxist writers typically present it as a bourgeois rival to the labour theory of value.
A review mechanism in which government policies and measures are checked for rules that exclude or restrict competition.
A paired value term in Party discourse covering equity in rights, opportunities, rules and distribution. It features prominently in speeches by Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping on social governance.
The article's term for US foreign policy that makes religious freedom central. Xi presents it as a successor to missionary diplomacy and human rights diplomacy.
Heidegger's Verfallen: Dasein's everyday absorption in the anonymous "they", through idle talk, curiosity and ambiguity, which is a mode of inauthentic existence.
A phrase from Engels's 1893 letter to Mehring. It describes thinking that treats ideas as self-generating and overlooks their material roots.
A qigong-based spiritual movement founded by Li Hongzhi in the early 1990s. It was banned in China in 1999 and is described by Chinese official sources as an evil cult.
The moral tone and customs handed down within a family, often expressed in family instructions (jiaxun). Official discourse has encouraged them as a basis for moral education.
A sentiment that links personal and family fate to the fate of the nation. Chinese official discourse presents it as a core trait of traditional Chinese culture.

lit: family and state share one structure
ex: A description of traditional Chinese political thought, especially Confucian, in which the state is seen as an enlarged family and the ruler as a household head.
A cover practice from 1927 in which Party members lived together as a 'family', large or small, to pass tenancy checks in the concessions.
The organised online fan communities around celebrities, known for defending idols collectively.

en: "fang de huo" (liberated and lively) and "guan de zhu" (properly regulated)
q: "fang de huo" (liberated and lively) and "guan de zhu" (properly regulated)
py: fàng de huó, guǎn de zhù
lit: loosened enough to be lively, controlled enough to hold
ex: A phrase from the 2024 Third Plenum describing an economy that gives market actors freedom while keeping effective oversight.
A term used by the CPC and the Comintern for a feared deal in which Britain would appease Japan at China's expense, as Czechoslovakia had been sacrificed at Munich in 1938.
A line of argument, associated with 1990s intellectual debates, that rejects revolution as a path for modern China. Zhu links it to historical nihilism.
Deng's term for a party that treats other communist parties as subordinates and issues orders to them, applied to the Soviet party.
The Vietnam Fatherland Front is the CPV-led umbrella organisation of mass and social organisations. The article describes it as carrying out non-binding external supervision of state organs.

A phrase associated with Mao Zedong and repeatedly used by Xi Jinping. It refers to cadres' anxiety that their abilities do not meet the demands of new tasks, and it is used to urge continuous learning.
A proposal put forward by Kim Il Sung at the Sixth Congress (1980) for unifying the Korean peninsula as a federation.
A model of resolving disputes locally, which originated in Zhuji, Zhejiang in the 1960s. It has been promoted as a template for grassroots conflict mediation.
A grassroots approach, named after a locality in Zhejiang, of resolving disputes at the local level through mediation rather than litigation.

A model from Fengqiao town in Zhejiang, dating from the 1960s, of resolving disputes at the grassroots through mobilizing local people. It is promoted by the Party as a template for community governance.
Marx's term for the way social relations between producers appear as natural properties of things, as with commodities and money.
The word used in the standard Chinese rendering of Marx's 1859 Preface, where relations of production turn from forms of development of the productive forces into their fetters.
A Chinese term for practices such as fortune-telling, geomancy and divination. The article, following Ya, treats them as distinct from religion and therefore outside the scope of religious freedom.
Marx's term for capital in financial form, such as stocks and bonds, that creates no value itself and claims a share of value produced in material production.

A term, building on Marx's notion of fictitious capital, for financial capital detached from production and generated through circulation, such as excess paper money and securities. The authors treat it as defining a new stage of capitalism since the 1980s.
Chen Yun's summary of a sound way of thinking: not bowing to superiors, books or anything but reality, plus "exchange, comparison, repetition".
Borrowed from the Spanish Civil War, it refers here to people inside a state or party who are said to work for hostile outside powers. The author applies it to senior Soviet leaders.

lit: battle to tackle the toughest problems of poverty alleviation
ex: The official name of the 2013–2020 campaign to eliminate extreme poverty by Chinese standards. Its completion was declared in February 2021.

A standard Party phrase for grassroots Party organisations as strongholds that lead and mobilise people and carry out tasks. It is often paired with the "vanguard and exemplary role" of individual members.
A Party term for readiness to confront difficulties and opponents directly. Xi Jinping has urged cadres to develop it as part of their ability to handle risks.
A strategy of seeking military advantage on the battlefield to strengthen the negotiating position. The author describes it as Mao's approach in the armistice talks.

en: fighting, stabilising and building at once
q: fighting, stabilising and building at once
py: biān kàng, biān wěn, biān jiàn
ex: A policy line of the early 1950s to advance the war effort, economic stability and reconstruction simultaneously.
A Marxist term for capitalism dominated by large financial and monopoly firms. The article uses it to describe the present Western system.
In Lenin's theory of imperialism, the fusion of bank and industrial capital under the dominance of finance. Cai uses it for the finance-led form of capital that he argues still dominates.
The author's term for systematic control and exploitation of other states through financial means, presented as a form of neo-colonialism after formal colonial empires ended.
As defined in the article, a dominant power structure in the global financial system based on control of the leading currency, financial institutions and rule-making.

A term for imperialism dominated by finance capital, following Lenin's thesis that finance capital rather than industrial capital characterises the imperialist stage. Chinese scholars use it to describe the present-day world order.
A Marxist-Leninist category for the fusion of bank and industrial capital in large financial groups. The author treats it as the real ruling force in the United States.
Lenin's term in Imperialism for the small group controlling finance capital and, through it, economic and political life.
An official goal, stressed since the Central Financial Work Conference of 2023, of building China into a country with strong, internationally competitive financial institutions and markets.
The growing weight of finance in capitalist production and politics. Zhou presents it as a central feature of the neoliberal stage of capitalism.
The growing weight of finance, financial assets and financial profits in an economy, including in non-financial firms. The article treats it as a defining feature of capitalism since the 1970s.
An official phrase for the parts of China's cultural heritage that the Party regards as worth drawing on. It is often paired with the idea of creative transformation and innovative development.

A Party rule that meetings of Party committees and groups open with study of Xi Jinping's thought and speeches before other business. The February 2024 opinion called for establishing and improving it at all levels.
The first classroom means formal teaching in the curriculum. The second classroom means extracurricular activities such as practice, culture and competitions.
The target of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021. The second centenary goal is a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.
China's first five-year plan for economic development, 1953–1957, which prioritised heavy industry.
The International Working Men's Association, founded in London in 1864 with Marx's involvement. It was dissolved in the 1870s.
A practice of placing study of Xi Jinping's latest speeches and instructions first on the agenda of meetings.

zh: 中国共产党第一次全国代表大会
py: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng Dì-yī Cì Quánguó Dàibiǎo Dàhuì
lit: First National Congress of the CPC
ex: The founding meeting of the CPC, which began in Shanghai on 23 July 1921 and ended on a boat on South Lake, Jiaxing. It adopted the Party's first programme and first resolution.
The top official of a Party committee or organisation, usually the secretary. The article treats this figure as the main bearer of responsibility for implementing democratic centralism.
The top tier of China's official academic classification, set by the Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council and the Ministry of Education. It is divided into second-level disciplines.

zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
ex: A discipline category established in China in 2005 under the law major group, with six second-level sub-fields. It underpins research and the teaching of ideological and political courses in schools.

A Party image, associated with Mao Zedong's wartime writings, saying that the army relates to the people as fish to water, depending on popular support. It is used in Party history to describe army–civilian solidarity.
Xi Jinping's summary of lessons from Five-Year Planning: Party leadership, proceeding from reality, a nationwide approach, democracy and collective wisdom, and statutory planning.
Official shorthand for five groups of researchers: universities, Party schools, military academies, research institutes and Party and government research bodies.
Five pairs of relationships that the Central Economic Work Conference at the end of 2024 said must be handled in a coordinated way in economic work.
A framework sorting poor people by remedy: development of production, relocation, ecological compensation, education, and social security as a basic safety net.
Official shorthand for material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization, whose coordinated development is presented as the aim of national construction.
The five core texts of the Confucian canon: the Book of Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites and Spring and Autumn Annals.
A formulation by Xi Jinping that the peoples of China jointly opened up the territory, founded the unified multi-ethnic state, wrote its history, created its culture and fostered its national spirit.
Innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward by the Party leadership in 2015 as the guiding framework for development.
Shorthand for five groups of retired people: veteran cadres, veteran soldiers, veteran experts, veteran teachers and model workers. They form the core volunteer force of the committees.

A name for five major debates in 1950s–60s Chinese Marxist historiography: periodisation of ancient history, feudal land ownership, peasant wars, sprouts of capitalism, and formation of the Han nation.

en: five great Party-building lines of the new era
q: five great Party-building lines of the new era
py: xīn shídài wǔ dà dǎngjiàn lùxiàn
ex: A formulation attributed to Kim Jong Un covering political, organisational, ideological, disciplinary and work-style building of the Party. The Ninth Congress wrote it into the WPK charter.

A rural support system, begun in 1956, under which the collective guarantees food, clothing, fuel, education (for children) and burial for childless, elderly, disabled or otherwise unsupported villagers.
Education in the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, of socialist development and of the Chinese nation.
A formula that groups the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, of socialist development and of the Chinese nation as the content of Party education.
Required identification with the motherland, the Chinese nation, Chinese culture, the Communist Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

py: wǔ jí shūji zhuā xiāngcūn zhènxīng
lit: five levels of secretaries take charge of revitalization
ex: A responsibility system under which Party secretaries at provincial, city, county, township and village levels are all held accountable for rural revitalization.
Five pairs of relationships that Xi Jinping told the September 2024 National Education Conference must be handled correctly in building a leading country in education.
A set of five principles on economic work set out at the Central Economic Work Conference in December 2023, summarising the Party's understanding of how to conduct economic work in the new era.

Five principles set out in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): Party leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, unity and struggle, the new development philosophy, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The report calls them essential insights drawn from long practice.
Xi Jinping's 2023 summary of Chinese civilization as marked by continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. It was given at a symposium on cultural inheritance and development.
Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression and non-interference, equality and peaceful coexistence, associated with Chinese foreign policy since the 1950s.
The five areas of rural revitalisation officially identified: industry, talent, culture, ecology and organisation.

zh: 中华文明五大突出特性
en: five salient characteristics of Chinese civilization
q: five salient characteristics of Chinese civilization
py: Zhōnghuá wénmíng wǔ dà tūchū tèxìng
ex: A formulation attributed to Xi Jinping (2023) describing Chinese civilization as marked by continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness.
The schema of primitive, slave, feudal, capitalist and socialist or communist society, a standard framework in Chinese Marxist historiography.
The five systems for building a high-quality cadre corps: training, judging people, selection and appointment, strict management, and positive incentives.

A formula for the basic requirements of the unified national market: unified basic institutions, infrastructure, information, standards and regulatory enforcement, plus opening to the outside world. The article treats unifying government conduct as part of it.

lit: five organs and six hollow organs
ex: A metaphor from the sociologist Fei Xiaotong, who used the body's organs to describe what a discipline needs to be established. The "five viscera" are society, institute, department, library centre and publishing outlet.
The principle of developing moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education together.

py: wǔ piān jìhuà yǔ liù cè jìhuà
ex: Marx's successive outlines for his critique of political economy, in the 1857 Introduction and the 1859 Preface. Both include a separate part on the state.
An early Republican slogan that the state was shared by the Han, Manchu, Mongol, Hui (Muslim) and Tibetan peoples. Sun Yat-sen later replaced it with the idea of a single Chinese nation.
The official framework, adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012), that places economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development within one overall plan.
The Party's overall plan, adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012), to advance economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress together.
Stalin's summary of historical development as primitive, slave, feudal, capitalist and communist society, widely adopted in Chinese historiography after the 1930s.
China's medium-term national economic and social development plan, issued every five years since 1953 (called a 'plan' until the 11th, then a 'programme/plan'). The 15th covers 2026–2030.

A principle that a government's powers should be granted to match the responsibilities listed for it, so that responsibility comes before power. The article sets it against the older model of the regulatory (管制型) government.

lit: flooding the field with a large volume of water
ex: A metaphor in Chinese policy discourse for broad, undifferentiated delivery. It is contrasted with "precise drip irrigation" (精准滴灌), which targets specific groups.

A model from development economics in which industries shift in sequence from more advanced to less advanced economies, like geese in formation. The article argues that Asia has moved from a Japan-led pattern to one with several lead economies.
A Chinese scholarly category covering popular, non-institutional beliefs and sects outside the officially recognised religions. In narrower usage it refers to secret sects suppressed by the state.
A legal concept for events that cannot be foreseen, avoided or overcome. Article 19 of the Regulations uses it as a ground for not pursuing disciplinary responsibility.
A term for willpower or mental energy, used in the title of Mao's 1917 essay "The Power of the Mind". The article treats it as his moral ontology.
The mass-production, mass-consumption regime of accumulation dominant from the Second World War to the mid-1970s, associated with Keynesian welfare states.
A certificate issued by the Bank of China from April 1980 for foreigners and overseas Chinese to use in place of foreign currency within China.
A broad Chinese academic category covering Marxist thought developed outside China, including Western Marxism, ecological Marxism and post-Marxism.
The general term for Marxism outside China. It is also the name of a second-level discipline within Marxist theory in Chinese universities, added in 2008.
A Chinese law adopted in 2023 that sets out principles and institutions for the country's foreign affairs. Cao treats it as a framework law with mainly declaratory provisions.
A journal of the Central Compilation and Translation Bureau that reports on theoretical developments outside China, including foreign Marxism.

A concept in Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law covering the parts of China's legal system that deal with foreign and international matters, and China's participation in international law. It is paired with domestic rule of law under the principle of coordinating the two.
A special fund drawn from timber sales costs and reserved for forest renewal, planting and tending. It was meant to let forestry finance itself.

zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
q: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
lit: firmly forging the consciousness of the Chinese national community
ex: A slogan designating the main thread of the Party's ethnic work since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It stresses national identity shared by all ethnic groups.
An official phrase describing the aim of education as shaping students' ideological convictions along with their knowledge.
Wu's name for Marx's method of starting from an abstract idea, examining its formal determinations, and uncovering the formal and historical preconditions that make it appear.

en: formal and real subordination of labour to capital
q: formal and real subordination of labour to capital
ex: Marx's distinction between capital taking over an existing labour process and capital transforming the labour process itself, used here to explain proletarianisation.
Marx's distinction between capital taking over an existing labour process (formal) and remaking the labour process on a capitalist basis (real).
Marx's term for capital's control of labour that has not yet been reorganised through machinery or a distinctly capitalist labour process.
In Party discourse, work done for show, such as excessive paperwork and reports. Reducing its burden on the grassroots is an official aim.
Party terms for officials who go through the motions, stage shows or pile up paperwork instead of solving problems. The Party treats them as obstacles to carrying out central policy.
Official terms for empty, show-oriented work and for officials detached from the people and practical conditions. The Party treats them as persistent faults in its working style.

zh: 形式主义、官僚主义、享乐主义和奢靡之风
py: xíngshì zhǔyì, guānliáo zhǔyì, xiǎnglè zhǔyì hé shēmí zhī fēng
ex: The four undesirable work styles, often abbreviated as the "four winds", which the Party has targeted since 2012.
Marx's term in The German Ideology for the social forms in which people produce and exchange. Liu reads it as the forerunner of "relations of production".
A traditional Party metaphor for primary-level organizations as strongholds that carry out the Party's line and mobilize the masses. It is used here in contrast to being only service providers.
A multilateral platform founded in 2000 that holds summits and ministerial meetings between China and African states.

A concept used by Western left-wing scholars, such as Andreas Malm and Ian Angus, for capitalism's dependence on fossil fuels. It links capital accumulation to climate change and ecological destruction.

In Huang's account, an escalated form of fossil capitalism in which powerful states seek to secure and monopolise fossil-fuel supplies abroad. They are also said to use those supplies to hold back other countries.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral character alongside knowledge, in line with Party policy.
A requirement for propaganda and media workers to strengthen their footwork, eyesight, brainpower and writing power (脚力、眼力、脑力、笔力). It is used as a framework for training journalists.
The four principles for practising multilateralism in Xi's January 2021 Davos address: openness and inclusiveness, international law, consultation and cooperation, and keeping up with the times.
An architectural metaphor for the main structural framework of a system. Here it refers to the core institutional pillars of the New Democratic system.

Deng Xiaoping's 1979 formulation: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought. They serve as a political bottom line.
An official formulation of the Chinese nation's history. It says that the territory, history, culture and spirit of China were jointly developed by all ethnic groups.

Xi Jinping's strategic framework, put forward in 2014–2015, covering a moderately prosperous society, deepening reform, governing by law and Party discipline. Its first element later became building a modern socialist country in all respects.
An official requirement that Party members maintain political awareness, a sense of the big picture, of the core, and of alignment with the Party centre.
The Party's formulation of four major dangers it faces: lack of drive, incompetence, detachment from the people, and passivity and corruption.

Official list of dangers facing the Party: mental laxity, inadequate capacity, detachment from the people, and passive corruption. It is paired with the "four tests" of long-term rule, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment.

py: sì zhǒng wēixiǎn, sì dà kǎoyàn
ex: Official formula: the dangers are lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people and corruption; the tests are governing, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment.
Official shorthand for the peace, development, security and governance deficits that Chinese leaders say the world faces.
The author's term for the framework set out in the 1951 Frankfurt Declaration: political, economic, social and international democracy.
Huayan's fourfold scheme of the realm of principle, the realm of phenomena, the unobstructed interpenetration of principle and phenomena, and of phenomena with phenomena.
A working system that sends officials to grassroots units to do research, handle petitions, promote policy and solve problems. It is associated with Xi Jinping's earlier work in Fujian.

A graded approach to handling rule violations, from criticism and warnings for minor problems up to expulsion and criminal referral for serious ones. It is applied by Party discipline inspection bodies.

lit: four forms of supervision and discipline enforcement
ex: A graded approach to handling violations: criticism and talks as the norm; light disciplinary sanctions or organisational adjustment; heavy sanctions; and criminal referral for serious cases. It is written into Party regulations.

zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议、全球治理倡议
py: quánqiú fāzhǎn chàngyì, quánqiú ānquán chàngyì, quánqiú wénmíng chàngyì, quánqiú zhìlǐ chàngyì
ex: Four proposals Xi Jinping advanced in 2021–2025 on development, security, civilization and governance. China presents them as public goods for international cooperation.
Four Chinese proposals on global development, security, civilisation and governance, presented by Xi Jinping as contributions to international cooperation.
Xi Jinping's formula of great struggle, great project (Party building), great cause (socialism with Chinese characteristics) and great dream (national rejuvenation).
A Party education theme covering the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development.

zh: 思想理论工作“四大平台”
lit: four major platforms of ideological and theoretical work
ex: Four institutional channels named by Xi Jinping in 2016 for Marxist theory research and publicity. They are the Marxist theory research and construction project, the research centres on the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, Schools of Marxism, and the press and online media.
Xi Jinping's formulation of priorities for Tibet work: stability, development, ecology and strengthening the border.
The post-1949 goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology. It was prominently revived by Zhou Enlai and Deng Xiaoping in the late 1970s.

Four requirements for religious work set out at the Central United Front Work Conference in May 2015. They are to adhere to the direction of sinicization, to raise the level of rule of law in religious work, to view the social role of religion dialectically, and to value the role of religious figures.
A method of unannounced inspection: no prior notice, no briefing, no reception arrangements and no accompanying officials. Inspectors go directly to the grassroots and directly to the problem site.
The requirement that when a county is removed from the poverty list, responsibility, policies, assistance and supervision are not withdrawn.
A critical shorthand for evaluating researchers only by papers, titles, academic degrees and awards. Official policy calls for eliminating this practice.
A guideline for science and technology work: facing the world's scientific frontiers, the main economic battlefield, major national needs, and people's lives and health.
The authors' label for Vietnam's division of the four top posts (Party general secretary, prime minister, state president, National Assembly chair) among different people.

Independence, complete equality, mutual respect and non-interference in each other's internal affairs. They were formally set out in the report to the 12th Party Congress in 1982 as the basis for the Party's relations with foreign parties.

py: sì gè gémìng, yí gè hézuò
ex: Xi Jinping's energy security strategy, first put forward in 2014. It calls for revolutions in energy consumption, supply, technology and institutions, plus comprehensive international cooperation.
A formula calling on the Party to purify, improve, reform and raise itself (自我净化、自我完善、自我革新、自我提高).

The official educational guideline that education should serve the people, the Party's governance of China, consolidating and developing the socialist system, and reform, opening up and socialist modernization.
Xi Jinping's 2016 requirement that higher education serve the people, the Party's governance, the consolidation of the socialist system, and reform, opening up and modernization.
Principle set out by Mao Zedong in 1938: the individual to the organisation, the minority to the majority, the lower level to the higher level, and the whole Party to the Central Committee.

py: sì dà kǎoyàn, sì zhǒng wēixiǎn
lit: four great tests and four dangers
ex: Xi Jinping's formula for the challenges facing the ruling Party: the tests of governing, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment, and the dangers of slackness, inadequate capacity, detachment from the people and corruption.

The tests the Party says it faces in governing: those of governing, of reform and opening up, of the market economy and of the external environment. They are paired with the "four dangers" of lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people, and corruption.

py: sì dà kǎoyàn hé sì zhǒng wēixiǎn
lit: four great tests and four kinds of danger
ex: Official list of challenges to the Party: the tests of governing, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment; and the dangers of slackness, inadequate capacity, detachment from the people, and passivity and corruption.

py: sì dà kǎoyàn hé sì dà fēngxiǎn
ex: Official shorthand for challenges to the Party's rule. The tests are governing, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment. The risks are lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people, and corruption.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. The Party has campaigned against them since 2012, starting with the Central Committee's eight-point regulation.
A formula for the kind of young person the education system is meant to cultivate: with ideals, moral integrity, knowledge and a strong sense of responsibility.
Hiromatsu's model of cognition, with four poles: the given, the meant, the knowing someone and the self/other-self. Zhang traces its origins in Mach, Husserl and others.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. A fourth, confidence in culture, was added later, and the article uses the earlier three-part form.

lit: synchronised development of the four modernizations
ex: The 18th Party Congress (2012) formula of developing industrialisation, informatisation, urbanisation and agricultural modernisation together.
Xi Jinping's formula that all ethnic groups should share weal and woe, honour and disgrace, life and death, and destiny. The article treats it as the ideological basis of the national community idea.
A list of fourteen principles summarising Xi Jinping's thinking on Party building, ranging from Party leadership to full and rigorous self-governance and the anti-corruption struggle.
A list of fourteen principles for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era, presented in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).

en: the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
q: Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
py: dǎng de èrshí jiè sì zhōngquánhuì
ex: A plenary session of the Party's 20th Central Committee, held in 2025, whose decisions are being studied nationwide according to the article.

lit: free and comprehensive development of the human being
ex: A Marxist ideal of a society in which individuals can develop their capacities fully. It is a stated goal of socialism in Chinese official theory.
A Marxist ideal of the full development of each individual's physical and intellectual capacities. Chinese Party texts link it to common prosperity.

py: rén de zìyóu ér quánmiàn fāzhǎn
ex: A Marxist ideal of individuals developing their capacities fully. Official Chinese discourse treats it as the ultimate aim of modernization.
Marx's term in the 1857–58 manuscripts for the third stage of human development, after personal dependence and independence based on dependence on things.
In the article, labour that goes beyond necessary labour and expresses human capacities as an end in itself, based on Marx's idea of the realm of freedom.

Marx's term for time beyond necessary labour, covering leisure and time for higher activity such as study, art and social life. In Marxist theory it is the measure of wealth and the basis of all-round human development.
Designated areas where China pilots reforms in trade, investment and regulation, with successful measures later spread nationwide.

lit: released so that it comes alive
ex: Shorthand for loosening controls so that market actors have vitality and room to innovate. It is paired with "managing well" in recent economic policy language.
A slogan Bernstein used to demand the right to criticise and revise Marxism. Lenin attacked it in What Is to Be Done? as a pretext for introducing bourgeois ideas into the workers' movement.

The constitutional and Party policy that citizens may believe or not believe in religion, and that normal religious activities are protected. The article reads it as covering the freedom to propagate atheism as well.
A constitutional principle in China that protects citizens' religious belief. Official doctrine holds that Party members, unlike ordinary citizens, must be atheists.
The principle that citizens may choose to believe or not believe in a religion. Li argues the Marxist party upholds it while pursuing the long-term aim of freeing belief from religion.
A concept drawn from the Marxist tradition: labour in which producers jointly own and control production. Cheng applies it to public enterprises, in varying degrees.
The CPC's term for armed and political clashes between KMT and communist forces during the war. Anti-communist surges are called 'anti-communist high tides'.

en: from a revolutionary party into a ruling party
q: from a revolutionary party into a ruling party
ex: A formula in Chinese debates holding that after taking power the Communist Party should shift from a revolutionary to a governing role. Zhu rejects it as a false opposition.

zh: 从具体到抽象再从抽象上升到具体
en: from the concrete to the abstract and back to the concrete
q: from the concrete to the abstract and back to the concrete
py: cóng jùtǐ dào chōuxiàng zài cóng chōuxiàng shàngshēng dào jùtǐ
ex: Marx's method of exposition, set out in the 1857 Introduction. Research moves from concrete material to abstract determinations and then rises again to a concrete totality.
The Party's front-line committee in the Red Fourth Army, the army's highest Party organ. Mao Zedong served as its secretary.
The conventional front where Kuomintang-commanded armies fought Japanese forces, as in the battles of Shanghai, Taierzhuang and Wuhan.
The administration and management of China's land and maritime border regions, treated in Chinese scholarship as an academic field and a policy area.
Marx's phrase, used in the article for the productive forces accumulated across stages, which later generations inherit.

en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
q: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
lit: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
ex: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
The phase of the war against Japan that began with the 7 July 1937 Marco Polo Bridge Incident, when Japan launched a full invasion of China.

Grassroots League units set up on the basis of student self-governing bodies, clubs or task groups, rather than formal departments or classes. They supplement the traditional organisation-based (entity-type) League branches.
A national land-use strategy that divides territory into optimized, prioritized, restricted and prohibited development zones according to ecological and economic function.
The Party's constitution describes wholehearted service to the people as its fundamental purpose. It is the basic standard against which Party work is meant to be judged.
In Party discourse, the top tier of the institutional hierarchy, above basic and important systems. It is meant to have top-level decisive, all-round and guiding effect on the socialist system.

zh: 根本制度、基本制度、重要制度
py: gēnběn zhìdù, jīběn zhìdù, zhòngyào zhìdù
ex: A three-tier classification of China's institutional system first set out at the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in 2019. It runs from the overarching political system down to specific institutional arrangements in particular fields.

A Chinese shorthand for the four stages of the venture and private-equity cycle: raising funds, investing, managing and exiting. Recent State Council documents use it to frame reform of the investment ecosystem.

The reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024. It builds on the comprehensively deepening reform launched in 2013 and sets a timetable of targets, with a main goal of perfecting socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance.
Emerging industries based on frontier technologies that are still at an early stage. Official documents list six fields: manufacturing, information, materials, energy, space and health.
A French tense for an action completed before another future action. Žižek uses it as a model of time in which a projected future retroactively determines present action.
The author's name for the present stage in which game production and play are fully integrated into capitalist relations of production.
Official term for four Party leaders, including Jiang Qing, blamed for ultra-leftist policies in the Cultural Revolution and arrested in 1976.
A Mencian expression that Wang equates with extending innate knowing: accumulating righteous acts and virtue over time.

The political line associated with Charles de Gaulle, stressing French independence, a strong state and resistance to US hegemony. The article treats it as the guiding tradition behind European unity and as now largely ended.
The author's coinage, modelled on Marx's 'production in general', for the abstract category of data that governs digital production, exchange and consumption.
A term from Marx's 1857–58 manuscripts for socially accumulated knowledge that becomes a direct force of production. Autonomist writers use it to ground their theories of immaterial labour.
A notion from Marx's Grundrisse for socially accumulated knowledge that becomes a direct productive force. Post-workerist authors use it to argue for a communist potential.

en: general keynote of making progress while maintaining stability
q: general keynote of making progress while maintaining stability
py: wěn zhōng qiú jìn gōngzuò zǒng jīdiào
lit: general keynote of seeking progress within stability
ex: The Party's guiding principle for economic work, repeated at each annual Central Economic Work Conference since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It requires stable growth, employment, prices and financial security alongside structural adjustment and reform.

A phrase from Lenin's texts (a 1920 text on the Proletkult and a 1922 Party congress resolution). The article takes it to mean supreme, overall leadership by the ruling party, exercised mainly indirectly through state organs.

en: general line for the transition period
q: general line for the transition period
ex: The Party line announced in 1953. It aimed to achieve industrialization and the socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and private industry and commerce over roughly three five-year plans.
The Chinese rendering of Althusser's concept of the problematic. It names the underlying framework of thought that determines which questions a theorist can pose and how.
Rousseau's volonté générale, the universal will of citizens aimed at the common good, distinguished from the mere sum of particular wills.
In classical definition theory, the higher-level category to which a defined term belongs. The article debates whether extremism belongs to conduct, ideology, belief or something else.
The tradition of Kant, Fichte, Schelling, Hegel and Feuerbach, which Marxist theory names as one of the direct sources of Marxism.

en: getting one's hands on the matter and doing it
q: getting one's hands on the matter and doing it
lit: to lay hands on it and actually do the thing
ex: Yan Yuan's slogan for learning through direct, practical engagement. He used it to reinterpret 'investigating things' (gewu) in the Great Learning as hands-on practice.

A term from the early Chinese reception of Buddhism, when Buddhist ideas were explained through native Daoist and Confucian concepts. Chen uses it for interpreting and judging one body of Marxism through the categories of another.
Gorbachev's policy of openness from the mid-1980s, loosening censorship and permitting public discussion of Soviet history.
Huang Zhixiong's image of states that depend heavily on networks. Each can throw stones at others' glass houses but fears the same in return.

zh: 全球人工智能治理倡议
ex: A 2023 Chinese proposal on international AI governance. The article cites it as China's contribution to global governance in this field.

An initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2023 that calls for respecting civilizational diversity, promoting common human values, valuing the inheritance and innovation of civilizations, and strengthening international cultural exchange.

zh: 全球发展和南南合作基金
en: Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund
q: Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund
py: Quánqiú fāzhǎn hé Nán-Nán hézuò jījīn
ex: A fund that China upgraded in 2022 from the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund set up in 2015. It is used to support cooperation under the Global Development Initiative.
A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 focusing on poverty reduction, food security, development financing and climate change, linked to the UN 2030 Agenda.

zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议
en: the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives
q: Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives
py: Quánqiú Fāzhǎn Chàngyì, Quánqiú Ānquán Chàngyì, Quánqiú Wénmíng Chàngyì
ex: Three initiatives proposed by Xi Jinping (2021, 2022 and 2023) as China's contributions to global governance and to dialogue among civilizations.
Chinese texts use this for the institutions and rules that manage international affairs. They often call for reforming it to give developing countries a larger voice.
The management of transnational problems and international rules through institutions such as the UN. Chinese official discourse calls for reforming it to give developing countries more voice.

A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in September 2025. It is presented as the fourth in a series of global initiatives, after those on development, security and civilisation, and stresses sovereign equality and a central role for the UN.

zh: 共商共建共享的全球治理观
en: global governance outlook of extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
q: global governance outlook of extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
py: gòngshāng gòngjiàn gòngxiǎng de quánqiú zhìlǐ guān
lit: global governance view of joint consultation, joint construction and joint sharing
ex: An official Chinese principle of global governance. It holds that all countries should take part equally in making and benefiting from international rules.
A proposal issued by China in September 2020 setting out principles for global data security governance. The article cites it as China's alternative to data monopoly and mass surveillance.

The practice of shifting production to low-wage countries so as to profit from the gap between wage differences and productivity differences. The authors link it to the exploitation of workers in the Global South.

Shorthand for wealthy, industrialised countries and poorer, formerly colonised or dependent countries. Ecosocialists in the article call for consumption contraction in the former and resource transfers to the latter.
The article's term for how states and the international community manage religious affairs, extremism and church–state relations.
A proposal introduced by Xi Jinping in 2022 advocating a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security concept and the political settlement of conflicts.

A term for developing and formerly colonised countries, widely used in Chinese official and academic discourse. Here it refers to the peripheral economies whose workers are said to bear super-exploitation.
Jin Yinan's popular 2009 history of the Communist Party's early decades, which stresses hardship, sacrifice and eventual victory. The title is a literal rendering and not an official English title.

A phrase from Lenin's 1918 text, which the author reads as keeping to the chosen revolutionary course while setting policy from actual conditions. The author notes it is distinct from the Chinese Communist Party's later use of the phrase.
A current among some Russian Marxists, including Lunacharsky and Gorky, after 1905. It proposed a humanist "religion of socialism", and Plekhanov and Lenin opposed it.
The religious-philosophical search for God among Russian intellectuals after 1905, often tied to idealist and mystical thought.
A label some historians and commentators give to the Nationalist government's 1927–1937 period of relative stability and development; the author rejects it.

en: good at both ends, poor in the middle
q: good at both ends, poor in the middle
ex: Zhou Enlai's summary evaluation of the Comintern, which the authors adopt: its early and late periods were good, its middle period poor but not without merit.
The criteria for cadres set out under Xi Jinping: loyalty, integrity and a willingness to take responsibility.
The authors use it for the highest state of national governance, an ideal balance between state and civil society.
A policy slogan, endorsed by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), for safe, comfortable, green and smart housing. It shifts housing policy from quantity to quality.
A phrase combining just laws with effective governance. It is used in contemporary Chinese legal discourse and traced by the author to classical Chinese political thought.
A term prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), which described the people's growing need for a better life as one side of the principal social contradiction.
An official ideal of effective, orderly rural governance that serves the public interest and involves villagers.
A phrase for the gap between the world's growing need for governance and the inadequate supply of rules, institutions and ideas.
A historical frontier governance approach of ruling different peoples in line with their own customs. The authors present it as an earlier stage of Chinese frontier policy.
The political, class, organizational and performance foundations on which the ruling party's authority is said to rest.
The language and concepts through which the ruling Party expresses why it governs, what it aims to do and how. The article treats it as a distinct object of academic study.
Principle that the Party must exercise its ruling position through the constitution, laws and Party regulations. It was made the Party's basic mode of governance in 2004.
The article's term for regulating and supervising the exercise of power, notably by binding it with institutions and popular oversight.
The official formula for rule of law in China, in which the state is governed according to the Constitution and statutes under Party leadership.
The author's term for a governance model in which medium- and long-term plans, above all the Five-Year Plan, guide national development under the Party.

lit: governing the Party according to rules
ex: The practice of managing the Communist Party through its own intra-Party regulations (党内法规), headed by the Party Constitution. It is presented as parallel to governing the state by law.
A concept in Party-building discourse that stresses managing the Party through formal intra-Party rules and regulations, alongside ideological and organisational Party building.
State-capitalised investment funds meant to draw in private capital to priority sectors such as technology.
The annual report delivered by the Premier to the National People's Congress. It sets the year's economic targets and tasks.

en: government, industry, academia, research and application
q: government, industry, academia, research and application
ex: An official model of collaborative innovation linking government bodies, enterprises, universities, research institutes and end users.
A model in which the government relies on social organisations and communities to share in governance and public services.
The author's term for a holistic, systems-based view that joins natural and social ecology. It extends ecological analysis beyond environmental protection.
A term used by some Chinese scholars for a broad reading of historical materialism that covers not only human–human and human–society relations but also the human–nature relation.
An overarching account that gives a society's or the world's history a single framework. Postmodern thought has criticised such accounts.
A methodological notion promoted by Xi Jinping: analysing change from the long course of history, the tide of the times and global developments.
A recent approach in Party historiography, derived from Xi Jinping's call for a "grand view of history", which examines Party history within long historical, epochal and global contexts.

en: grasping with both hands, both firmly
q: grasping with both hands, both firmly
py: liǎng shǒu zhuā, liǎng shǒu dōu yào yìng
lit: grasp with two hands, both hands must be firm
ex: A Deng-era formula calling for equal attention to material and spiritual civilization, or to development and legal order.
The lowest levels of the Party and government system, such as townships, subdistricts and villages or communities, where cadres deal directly with residents.
Party and government officials working at village, township, street and county levels, who deal directly with the public.
The Party's lowest-level units, such as village Party branches, which the article treats as the backbone of rural collective development.

The system of self-management through urban and rural community bodies such as villagers' and residents' committees. Officially it is described as the main form of direct democracy, under Party leadership.
The system of village committees and urban residents' committees through which residents manage local public affairs. Official texts count it among China's basic political institutions.

en: great change unseen in a century
q: great change unseen in a century
py: bǎi nián wèi yù zhī dà biànjú
ex: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse for a perceived deep shift in the global order, involving the rise of emerging economies and growing uncertainty.

zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
en: great changes unseen in a century
q: great changes unseen in a century
py: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
lit: great changes in the world not seen in a hundred years
ex: Phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe a period of rapid shifts in the global order, including technological change and the rebalancing of power.

en: great changes unseen in a century
q: great changes unseen in a century
py: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
lit: great changes not seen in a hundred years
ex: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse since about 2017 for the current shift in the global balance of power and in the international order.

en: the great debate on the criterion of truth
q: great debate on the criterion of truth
ex: A nationwide discussion beginning in 1978, sparked by the article "Practice Is the Sole Criterion for Testing Truth". It challenged dogmatic reliance on leaders' pronouncements and is widely seen as preparing the ideological ground for reform and opening up.
The debate on why Europe industrialised ahead of China and other regions. Kenneth Pomeranz's 2000 book and the California School gave it prominence.

en: great founding spirit of the Party
q: great founding spirit of the Party
ex: A formulation, set out by Xi Jinping in 2021, of the Party's founding values: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and true to the people.
A classical Confucian ideal of a harmonious world in which "the world is shared by all". Party writing uses it to describe a world of common good.
An ideal of a world in which 'all under heaven is shared' (天下为公), drawn from classical Confucian texts. The article, following Ai Siqi, links it to the reception of communism in China.
A Confucian ideal of a society in which the world is held in common, found in the Book of Rites. Early Chinese intellectuals often equated it with socialism and communism.
The 1958 campaign for rapid industrial and agricultural growth. The article mentions it only as the background to Mao's call to study political economy.
The spirit attributed to settlers who reclaimed the wilderness of Heilongjiang for farming from the 1950s onward.

lit: the great undertaking of Party building
ex: A phrase Mao Zedong introduced in 1939 to describe building the Party as a large, continuing task alongside revolution. Later leaders have described successive stages as a "new great project".
Marcuse's term for a radical rejection of the established one-dimensional society.
The 1924–1927 revolutionary movement of the First United Front between the Communists and the Guomindang. It ended with the Guomindang's 1927 purge of Communists.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party-led transformation of Chinese society, which in this usage includes reform and opening up and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

en: the great spirit of reform and opening up
q: great spirit of reform and opening up
ex: An official formulation for the values attributed to the reform era, such as daring to innovate, pragmatism and a sense of responsibility. It is used in Party education.

lit: great spirit of the War of Resistance
ex: An official formulation for the patriotism, heroism and endurance attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan. It is invoked in Party commemoration as a source of present-day motivation.

en: great spirit of the Chinese nation
q: great spirit of the Chinese nation
ex: A formulation in official discourse for the Chinese nation's enduring spiritual qualities. Xi Jinping has summarised them as the spirits of creativity, struggle, unity and dream.
A phrase used in Party discourse under Xi Jinping for the Party's struggle against major risks and challenges on the path to national rejuvenation.
An honorific for teachers who combine deep learning with moral example. It has been used in Xi Jinping's speeches on education.

en: great union of the popular masses
q: great union of the popular masses
ex: The title of an essay Mao Zedong published in the Xiang River Review in July 1919. It calls for ordinary people of all occupations to organise together against the powerful.

en: great union of the popular masses
q: great union of the popular masses
ex: A phrase from Mao Zedong's early writings (1919), calling for broad unity among the popular masses; the author treats it as the starting point of people's politics.
A traditional political idea, traced to early Confucian texts, of a unified realm under one order. Official discourse presents it as a source of the continuity of Chinese civilization.
A slogan describing the aim of united front work: uniting the widest possible range of social forces around the Party's goals.
Zhang Zai's term for the formless original state of qi and for the substance of Heaven, empty but not nothing.
A Maoist-era term for arrogant or condescending behaviour by a large country towards smaller ones. Mao used it to criticise Chinese personnel abroad.
The attitude of a large state or party that treats smaller ones as inferiors. Mao demanded that it be eliminated from China's international dealings.
A mathematical metaphor used by Xi Jinping for the widest shared ground among different social groups, used especially in united front work.

An official development approach that seeks to cut pollution and carbon emissions while sustaining economic growth. It is linked to China's "dual carbon" targets for peaking emissions and reaching carbon neutrality.
The strategy of addressing environmental crises through markets, technology and corporate action within capitalism. Eco-socialists criticise it as inadequate.
One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy announced in 2015. It stresses harmony between economic growth and the environment.
One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy announced in 2015, stressing harmony between development and the environment.

lit: green cultivation of people in universities
ex: A term for incorporating ecological values and ecological civilization education into university teaching and student development.
A term used by the Norwegian and Finnish parties for the claim that major capitalist powers use environmental protection as a pretext to sustain neo-colonial domination.
A family of state-led investment programmes for green technology and green jobs, ranging from centrist to radical left versions. The article treats it as a possible but unstable transition platform.

A term in official discourse for productive forces built on green innovation and environmental protection, treating ecology and resources as elements of production. It follows Xi's remark that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces.
The label for the environmental and low-carbon dimension of the Belt and Road Initiative, promoted in official documents since the mid-2010s.

en: green transformation of the development model
q: green transformation of the development model
lit: green transition of the mode of development
ex: A requirement set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and elaborated at the Third Plenum (2024) to shift economic and social development onto a low-carbon, resource-saving basis.
A grassroots governance method that divides a locality into small grid units, each with assigned staff responsible for services and problem-solving.

A system of grid-based management in which communities or villages are divided into small units, each with assigned workers responsible for monitoring, services and reporting. It is widely used in Chinese grassroots governance.
A practice that divides communities into small grids, each with assigned Party members and officials. It is used for service delivery, monitoring and risk screening.
A regional development cluster linking nine cities in Guangdong with Hong Kong and Macao, which the article notes operate under different legal, tax and currency systems.
The official concept that media should steer public opinion in a direction consistent with Party and state priorities. Official texts treat it as a core task of Party-led media.

zh: 积极引导宗教与社会主义社会相适应
en: guiding religion to adapt to socialist society
q: guiding religion to adapt to socialist society
py: jījí yǐndǎo zōngjiào yǔ shèhuì zhǔyì shèhuì xiāng shìyìng
ex: Long-standing Party policy line that religions should be actively guided to fit socialist society. The article treats sinicization as its concrete form.

zh: 引导宗教与社会主义社会相适应
en: guiding religion to adapt to socialist society
q: guiding religion to adapt to socialist society
py: yǐndǎo zōngjiào yǔ shèhuì zhǔyì shèhuì xiāng shìyìng
ex: A core principle of Party religious policy, stated in full in a 1992 central document. It was later written into the Party Constitution (2007) and treated as the basic direction of religious work.
The Yugoslav formula that replaced the Soviet-style 'leading role' of the Party. As Ma describes it, it meant the Party would coordinate rather than command state and self-management bodies.

zh: 意识形态领域指导地位
en: guiding role in the ideological field
q: guiding role in the ideological field
lit: guiding position in the ideological domain
ex: The Party's long-standing principle that Marxism is the guiding thought in ideology, culture and academia. The 2019 Decision restated it as a fundamental system.

lit: Guild socialism (also rendered 行会社会主义, 工行的社会主义)
ex: A British-originated current favouring worker-run guilds in industry. In China it was advocated in the early 1920s by Zhang Dongsun and others in opposition to Marxism.
A popular term for fashionable products and artworks that fuse traditional Chinese elements with contemporary style.

The Chinese name for Statistik/Statistique in its early modern sense: a state-oriented empirical discipline surveying population, economy, military and social organisation, which preceded modern statistics.
