The 1929 Party congress of the Fourth Red Army, held in Gutian. Its resolution established the Party's absolute leadership over the army and an early system of political work.
A resolution drafted by Mao for the Fourth Red Army's Party congress in December 1929. It sets out the principles of the Party's command over the army and ideological work in the Party and army.
A special economic zone on Hainan island, with policy plans announced by the central government in 2018 and 2020, that has liberalised trade and investment rules.
A Party term for attitudes in which the Han majority disregards or dominates minorities. It is usually paired with "local nationalism" as the two errors to be opposed.

zh: 为人民谋幸福、为民族谋复兴、为世界谋大同
en: the happiness of the people, the rejuvenation of the nation and the great harmony of the world
q: happiness of the people, the rejuvenation of the nation and the great harmony of the world
py: wèi rénmín móu xìngfú, wèi mínzú móu fùxīng, wèi shìjiè móu dàtóng
lit: seek happiness for the people, rejuvenation for the nation, great harmony for the world
ex: A formula used by Xi Jinping to summarise the Communist Party's aims. "Great harmony" (datong) draws on a classical Confucian ideal of a harmonious world.
A long-standing Party ethos of austerity, diligence and perseverance, associated with the revolutionary period and still promoted as a virtue of cadres.
A phrase popularised by Deng Xiaoping's 1992 Southern Tour remarks ("development is the hard truth"), meaning a principle that is non-negotiable. Xi Jinping applies it to high-quality development.

py: yìng liántōng, ruǎn liántōng, xīn liántōng
ex: Official shorthand for BRI cooperation in infrastructure, in rules and standards, and in people-to-people ties.
A term linked to the official goal of building a harmonious society, promoted from the mid-2000s, which stresses balance among social groups, regions and the economy and environment.
An official aim of cooperative relations between employers and employees, pursued through collective consultation, unions and legal protections; it derives from the 'harmonious society' idea.
A policy goal promoted by the Chinese leadership from the mid-2000s. Li invokes it when describing the social ideal he finds in Wang's doctrine.
A goal put forward in the 2000s under Hu Jintao, centred on social cohesion and the reduction of social conflict.
A vision of international order put forward by Hu Jintao in the mid-2000s, stressing multilateralism, dialogue and peaceful development.
A traditional Chinese idea of harmony and integration among differing elements, which Zhang Liwen has long developed as a philosophical concept.
An official formulation for China's state–religion relationship. It rests on the separation of state and religion but aims at positive interaction between them.

lit: harmonious coexistence of humans and nature
ex: An official formulation of ecological civilization. It treats humans and nature as a life community in which nature is to be respected, accommodated and protected.
A classical Chinese idea, now used in official discourse to express respect for the diversity of civilizations.
Diplomacy conducted personally by the head of state. Official discourse describes it as the highest form of Chinese diplomacy.
A principle that sectors such as industry, transport and education should assess the health effects of their policies, similar to the international 'Health in All Policies' approach.
A strand of China's poverty-alleviation campaign that targets illness-related poverty, through medical insurance, medical assistance and better rural health services.
A national strategy launched with the 2016 Healthy China 2030 Planning Outline, aiming to improve population health through policy across sectors. The article refers to a goal of building it by 2035.
A Confucian term for the people's support, trust and acceptance of a ruler. Confucian thinkers treated it as decisive for whether a regime keeps or loses power.
In early Chinese thought, a supreme power or realm that could confer rule and send blessings or disasters. It could also mean nature or moral order.
A term used in Chinese official and academic discourse for a stronger state's use of military, economic or other power to dominate others and shape the international order.
Gramsci's concept of leadership that combines political, economic and cultural dimensions. Yang argues it is often wrongly reduced to cultural hegemony.

zh: 海德格尔式马克思主义
ex: A label for thinkers who combine Heidegger's philosophy with Marxism. Traditionally it meant Marcuse's early work; the article proposes a wider use.
An anarchist periodical started in 1908 by the same circle, which continued Tianyi's work after it was forced to stop.
A 2018 Chinese law that protects the names, reputations and honour of heroes and martyrs and penalises defaming or insulting them.

A conception that history is driven chiefly by great individuals such as rulers and generals. Marxist historiography, as presented in the article, opposes it with the view that the masses make history.
The body of values, stories, commemorations and symbols that honour heroes and martyrs. In Party and military discourse it is used for ideological education and morale-building.
The Indian Buddhist tradition of logic and debate, transmitted to China; the article counts it as one of the three source traditions of world logic.
Wang's alternative to "being and non-being". Things appear or vanish to human sight as qi gathers or disperses, while qi itself always exists.

lit: hide one's brightness and nourish obscurity
ex: A foreign-policy maxim associated with Deng Xiaoping, advising a low profile and avoiding open displays of strength.
A policy announced by the Nationalists in 1945 for Tibet and Outer Mongolia. The article says it later shrank into ordinary local autonomy.

A term popularised in Xi Jinping's recent speeches, referring to a governance system that effectively turns institutional strengths into results. The article treats it as an original concept drawn from Chinese practice.

lit: high-level science and technology standing on its own feet and strengthening itself
ex: A Party slogan for securing independent control of key and core technologies, used especially in response to foreign technology restrictions.
A policy goal in recent government work reports that stresses both the number of jobs and their quality.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
The official policy of widening China's openness to the world through better rules, institutions and platforms, as part of reform and opening up.

zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
py: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
ex: A formulation first introduced at the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) and made a reform priority at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It denotes a more advanced stage of the socialist market economy system.
The article's term for the loss of the general ability to reproduce basic living conditions in areas left behind by cities. It shows up in rising suicide, addiction and falling life expectancy.

An official periodisation in which Mao Zedong Thought is the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to China, and later theoretical achievements are further leaps. The 2021 resolution speaks of a first leap and two 'new' leaps.
In Chen's definition, the confidence and conviction of the agents of history in the history of their nation, state or party.
A term in Chinese Party discourse for a conscious grasp of historical laws and of one's place in historical development. The article treats it as the core attribute of Mao Zedong Thought.
The pattern in which regimes rise, decay and collapse in repeated cycles. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in Yan'an in 1945, in the exchange known as the 'cave dialogue'.

The idea, raised in the 1945 Yan'an "cave dwelling conversation" between Huang Yanpei and Mao Zedong, that regimes tend to rise and then decline. Party writers present supervision by the people and the Party's self-reform as ways to escape it.

en: historical cycle of rise and decline
q: historical cycle of rise and decline
py: zhì luàn xīng shuāi lìshǐ zhōuqīlǜ
lit: historical cycle of order and chaos, rise and decline
ex: A phrase from the 1945 Yan'an conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei. It names the pattern of dynasties flourishing and then falling, which the Party says it has escaped.

en: historical cycle of rise and fall
q: historical cycle of rise and fall
ex: Refers to the 1945 'cave dialogue' between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how to avoid the pattern of dynastic rise and decline. Mao answered 'democracy'. Xi Jinping later added self-reform as a 'second answer'.
The view that history develops according to objective laws. Critics read it as mechanistic or fatalist; the article defends a non-fatalist reading.
The author's name for Marx's method of explaining social forms through the contradictions that arise in their historical development.

lit: historical initiative / taking the initiative in history
ex: In Chen's definition, the spirit and ability to grasp the broad trend of history on the basis of its laws and to drive historical change consciously.
A concept from traditional Chinese historiography, ranked by Liu Zhiji alongside talent and learning. It means the ability to grasp the meaning and larger significance of historical events.
A concept used in Chinese official discourse for upholding accurate historical facts and narratives, here applied to the Second World War and its outcomes.
In Marxist usage, the objective regularities governing social development, grounded in the production and reproduction of real life.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations drive historical development.

The Marxist theory that social and cultural phenomena are explained by material conditions and the development of productive forces. Here it is used to explain the origin and function of fortune-telling.
The author's term for Hegel's system, in which history is treated as the unfolding of pure concepts such as spirit. Marx is said to have criticised and overcome it.
In Party usage, a label for views seen as denying or belittling the Party's revolutionary and socialist history, often by stressing its errors.
A concept associated with Xi Jinping, who used it in 2013 on urbanisation. It stresses long-term, gradual progress towards strategic goals and resistance to haste.
A phrase Xi Jinping has used since the 18th Party Congress (2012), urging steady, gradual progress on long-term tasks such as modernization instead of hasty, short-term results.

A term used in Party discourse for where the Party and country stand in the course of history. The 19th Party Congress (2017) used it in declaring that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era.

The idea, which Marx puts forward in The Poverty of Philosophy, that every category and principle belongs to a particular historical period. The article treats it as one of two turning points in Marx's development.
Three authoritative Central Committee resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021) that set the Party's official assessment of its history.

A concept in recent Party discourse for steady strategic determination grounded in an understanding of historical laws and trends. The authors present it as an original category of new-era Party theory.
In this context, efforts to deny or play down Japan's wartime aggression and war responsibility.
The agent understood to make or change history. In classical Marxism this is chiefly the working class; the article traces how Western Marxists have redefined or dissolved it.
The view that history as a whole moves towards a predetermined end or purpose, as in Hegel's unfolding of Absolute Spirit. The article treats it as idealist and opposed to historical materialism.
Yu's term for a widely influential current of ideas, often with a world-historical theme, that reflects social conditions and serves as a form of social consciousness.
A school associated with Lefebvre, Harvey and Soja that analyses capitalism through the production of space and uneven geographical development.

A term Wang uses for Marx's mature worldview, combining historical materialism with attention to the geography of capital. It echoes the 'historical-geographical materialism' associated with David Harvey.

lit: narrative of the materialist conception of history
ex: The author's term for historical narration grounded in historical materialism and in non-fictional facts, which seeks to reveal the underlying laws of social change.
The article's label for Hegel's principle that history, both of philosophy and of the world, is an unfolding of the logical determinations of the Idea or Absolute Spirit.
The branch of history that studies how history-writing has developed, including its methods, genres and thinkers.

lit: history of the development of Marxism
ex: A sub-discipline within Marxist theory studies in China that examines how Marxism emerged and developed historically and the laws governing that process.
The history of the People's Republic of China since 1949, treated as a distinct field of research, publicity and education alongside Party history.
The ideological legacy of Ho Chi Minh, adopted by the Communist Party of Vietnam, alongside Marxism-Leninism, as its guiding ideology.
A network of secret supply routes, partly through Laos and Cambodia, used from 1959 to supply forces in South Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
Xi Jinping's 2014 concept of national security covering political, economic, ecological and other fields together.
The authors' term for the internal coherence and staying power of Marx's theoretical language, which they say rests on its form, content and significance.
Yan's term for a life in which material, social and spiritual needs are met together. Yan treats it as the ultimate good that economy and politics serve.

A public-administration approach (known in the West as holistic or joined-up governance) that seeks to overcome fragmented, siloed management by coordinating actors and policies around problem-solving.
An approach that places a topic within wider international, social and cultural contexts rather than treating it as only political or military history.
The Party's term, associated with Xi Jinping's holistic approach to national security, for treating security as covering many fields, from political and economic to cyber and social.

The author's own formulation, derived from the holistic view of national security. It treats ideological security as a broad, systemic and long-term matter that combines the state of security with the capacity to maintain it.
The label the authors give to the 1980s cooperation between the US government and the Vatican against communism in Eastern Europe.
Diplomatic activity that China hosts on its own territory, such as summits, forums and large international events. Official commentary treats it as a way to set agendas and present China's positions.
An idiom for one's core, decisive competence. Xi Jinping applies it to mastering Marxism as the basic skill for Party cadres and teachers.

The author's term for Party-history research that picks its subject because it is the researcher's home area or easily accessible. It is modelled on the author's earlier criticism of "hometown sociology".

en: honours system of a large Party and country
q: honours system of a large Party and country
py: dà dǎng dà guó róngdiǎn zhìdù
lit: honours-and-ceremonies system of a great Party and great country
ex: A phrase for the system of state and Party honours and ceremonies. The authors treat the oath ceremony as one of its foundations.
An official term for foreign or domestic actors presented as seeking to undermine the Party and the socialist system, usually without naming them.
Protestant congregations that meet outside the officially registered "Three-Self" churches. The authors treat their unregistered status as a governance problem.
The rural reform of the late 1970s and 1980s that let farm households contract land and output from collectives. It is widely seen as a landmark of reform and opening up.

en: housing is for living in, not for speculation
q: housing is for living in, not for speculation
lit: houses are for living, not for speculating
ex: A housing policy principle announced at the 2016 Central Economic Work Conference. It stresses housing's residential function and aims to curb speculation.

en: Hua and Yi as one family
q: Hua and Yi as one family
ex: A traditional idea that Han (Huaxia) and non-Han peoples belong to one community under the ruler. The article presents it as a mainstream view across dynasties.
Japan's 1935 pressure to extend its control over north China, which the article treats as making north China the anti-Japanese front line.
A Chinese Buddhist school based on the Avatamsaka (Huayan) Sutra, formalised in the Tang dynasty and known for its doctrine of mutual interpenetration of all phenomena.
The traditional distinction between the civilised Huaxia and surrounding peoples. The authors argue it was defined by ritual and culture and not by descent.
A Communist-held revolutionary base area on the borders of Hubei, Henan and Anhui in the late 1920s and early 1930s. The article calls it the second largest Soviet area after the Central Soviet Area.
China's household registration system, which ties access to public services to place of registration and affects labour mobility between city and countryside.

Marx's term in the 1844 Introduction and "On the Jewish Question" for emancipation from private property and alienated labour. He contrasts it with merely political emancipation, which leaves civil society's inequalities intact.
Marx's goal of emancipating all humanity, distinguished from merely political emancipation; the authors treat it as the core of his whole theory.
Liu's own term for the "environment" in Marx's thesis: social environment plus humanised nature, as distinct from nature-in-itself.

py: rén wéi běn, mín wéi guì
lit: humans as the root, the people as most precious
ex: Du's shorthand for Chinese humanism. The second half echoes Mencius's idea that the people rank above the ruler.
The author's term for the world Marx envisages after alienation is overcome, in which people produce and enjoy as human beings and own their social essence.

zh: 人道的民主的社会主义
py: réndào de mínzhǔ de shèhuì zhǔyì
ex: Gorbachev's formula for his reform programme, adopted in the CPSU's 1990 28th Congress document. The authors treat it as a shift from scientific socialism to social democracy.

zh: 人道的、民主的社会主义
py: réndào de, mínzhǔ de shèhuì zhǔyì
ex: Gorbachev's formula for the Soviet Party's aims from 1988–90. The author treats it as a form of social democracy that served to introduce capitalism.
A concept drawn from Marx's early writings: nature as it is shaped by human labour and practice. Chinese Marxist writing uses it to argue there is no nature wholly independent of humanity.
The tradition reading Marx through alienation, the subject and early works such as the Paris Manuscripts, opposed to scientistic interpretations.
The mid-twentieth-century current that read Marx through the early, humanist writings, such as the 1844 Manuscripts. In this article Sartre and Merleau-Ponty are its leading figures.
Label for the theoretical project of East European neo-Marxists who sought a socialism centred on the human being and practice, in contrast to Soviet orthodoxy.

A term Chinese scholars use for Marx's theory of the human being, covering human essence, subjectivity and all-round development. In this article it is used to ground policy in a concern for the concrete person.
A theoretical proposition tied to Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on culturally developed regions with strong economies. It concerns the mutual reinforcement of culture and economic development.

A concept the author develops, rather than a fixed official term. It is read here as an economy in which human beings, their culture and their wellbeing are the starting point and purpose of economic activity.
A cultural orientation that stresses human value, dignity and development. In Chinese debate since the 1990s it has been a key term for discussing the spiritual consequences of marketisation.
The doctrine that outside powers may use force in another state to prevent mass atrocities. The article treats it as a pretext for pursuing interests and for violating sovereignty.
A term the author uses for labour in which people and AI systems work together as partners. It extends the official phrase "human–machine collaboration".
An ecological-civilisation concept holding that humans and nature form an integrated whole, so harming nature harms humanity.
A 1920–21 movement for provincial autonomy in Hunan, in which Mao took part and which sought to build a Hunan republic.

The regional culture of Hunan province, associated with practical statecraft learning, patriotism and a reformist, perseverant temperament. Thinkers such as Wang Fuzhi and Zeng Guofan are treated as its representatives.

lit: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools contend
ex: A policy Mao announced in 1956 to encourage diversity in the arts and scholarly debate under Party leadership. The article contrasts it with Soviet cultural policy.

lit: Let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools contend
ex: A policy announced in 1956 encouraging diversity in the arts and academic debate under socialism. Tian notes that its implementation was later set back.
A large Eighth Route Army campaign in North China in 1940, centred on the Zhengtai railway, against Japanese railway lines and strongpoints.

zh: 百县千镇万村高质量发展工程
en: Hundred-County, Thousand-Town, Ten-Thousand-Village High-Quality Development Project
q: Hundred-County, Thousand-Town, Ten-Thousand-Village High-Quality Development Project
py: Bǎi xiàn qiān zhèn wàn cūn gāozhìliàng fāzhǎn gōngchéng
ex: A Guangdong provincial programme, abbreviated as the "Hundred-Thousand-Ten Thousand Project", aimed at narrowing urban–rural and regional gaps by developing counties, towns and villages. It was modelled on Zhejiang's "Ten Million Project".

A term associated with Gilles Lipovetsky for a stage in which modernity is pushed to excess rather than replaced by postmodernity. The article uses it for the age of accelerated, urgent abstract time.
A Chinese scholarly idiom for faithful commentary on canonical texts. The article uses it for text-centred Marxology, in contrast to the opposite mode of 'the Classics annotate me'.
A counterfactual setting in which all participants have equal opportunity to speak and no coercion or manipulation intervenes.
The Chinese term for philosophical idealism, here covering German idealism and its Cartesian precursors.
A standard Party term for cadres' commitment to communism and socialism with Chinese characteristics, treated as their spiritual pillar.
Political mobilisation organised around group identities such as race, gender and sexual orientation rather than class. The article treats it as a strategy of the post-industrial Western left.

lit: ideological-political courses and ideological-political education within courses
ex: Refers to dedicated ideological and political courses and to the embedding of ideological content in other subjects. Xi Jinping has called for the two to work in the same direction.
The system of courses and activities in Chinese schools and universities that teaches Marxism, Party theory and patriotic values.

A Chinese academic discipline, within the field of Marxist theory, that studies how the Party and state shape the ideas, political views and morals of citizens, especially students. It also covers the related teaching practice.
The authors' term for a large AI model built specifically for ideological and political education, trained on that field's data and aligned with mainstream ideology.
Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and political education taught from primary school through university in China. They are meant to build students' worldview and political convictions.

Compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses taught at all levels of Chinese schooling, abbreviated sizheng ke. They are treated as the main channel for teaching Marxism and the Party's theories.
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and official ideology taught in all Chinese universities. They are often abbreviated as sizheng ke.
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and political education taught in Chinese universities. They are treated officially as central to moral and political education.
The Party's work of shaping the beliefs, values and political outlook of its members and the public through education, persuasion and communication. It is often described as the Party's "lifeline".
The Party's work of political education, value guidance and mobilisation of the public, carried out in schools, workplaces and the media.
The author's label for the contest over ideas, discipline, identification and morale within and between armies. It is the author's analytical construct, not a term Engels used explicitly.
One of the Party's core areas of self-construction. It covers theoretical study and education in ideals and convictions for members and cadres.

The deep conviction and identification of a party, state, nation or people with its own ideology. In Chinese Party discourse it is linked to the 'confidence' formulas and to the Party's emphasis on ideological work.
A concept prominent in Chinese Party discourse since the 2010s. It refers to the capacity to shape public narratives and have one's ideological account accepted, domestically and internationally.

lit: nurture the root and forge the soul
ex: A Party slogan for building firm ideological and spiritual foundations, here through the spread of Marxism.
A common Party-Marxist term for the domain of ideas to be held and expanded against rival worldviews. Here it refers to the reach of Marxist atheism.

The article defines it as governing actors aligned with the ruling class using formal and informal institutions to integrate resources in the ideological sphere. It is presented as part of the modernization of national governance.
A common term in Party youth work for shaping the political beliefs and values of young people.
A concept from Gramsci. It refers to the leadership that a ruling group exercises by winning consent through ideas and culture rather than by force alone.
A term in Chinese security discourse for the alleged use of culture, media and values by foreign states to reshape another society's thinking. The author treats it as a form of cultural colonisation.

One of four capacities (political leadership, ideological leadership, mass organisation, social mobilisation) that the Party's 15th Five-Year Plan proposals say should be strengthened. It refers to the Party's ability to win acceptance for its guiding ideas.

The Party's claim to lead and control ideological and cultural work, including education, media and publishing. It draws on Lenin's Party principle and is often discussed in Gramscian terms of hegemony.
The Party's claim to direct ideological and cultural work, drawing on Gramscian-influenced Chinese Marxist discourse; the article pairs it with discourse power (huàyǔquán).
The Party's basic approach to knowing and handling reality. Official history treats it as the foundation for its political and organisational lines.
The Party tradition of strengthening the Party through ideological education and struggle over its members' thinking, stressed by Mao Zedong in the 1940s.
A term in Chinese Party discourse for establishing and managing the institutions and spaces (media, universities, the internet) through which the Party's dominant ideology is spread and defended.
A term in Chinese ideological education for people's actual state of thought, attitudes and values, which educators are expected to understand and shape.
A campaign in 1951–52 requiring intellectuals and educators to study Marxism and criticise their previous outlook.
The idea that a state's dominant ideology and historical narrative need protection from hostile external influence, in the same way as territory or cyberspace.
The field of ideas, culture, media and theory that the Party treats as an arena of political struggle and leadership.
Althusser's term for institutions such as schools, family, churches and media that function mainly through ideology and help reproduce the relations of production.

The article's term for the professional group that produces, spreads and practises ideology for a ruling class. It is built from Marx's references to 'ideological' strata such as officials, clergy, lawyers and officers.
Official term for the contest over ideas and public opinion, which Party documents say includes the internet as a major arena.

The author's term for the ideas, values, beliefs and customs of a society, as distinct from the political superstructure of formal institutions. Yang derives it from Marx's wider uses of "superstructure".

In Chinese Marxist usage, the part of the superstructure made up of ideas, such as law, morality, art, philosophy and religion, as distinct from the political superstructure of institutions. It is held to be determined by the economic base.
The Party's work of shaping thought, culture and public opinion, including media management and ideological education. It is treated as a core responsibility of Party organisations.

Dedicated ideological and political theory courses that all Chinese university students take, such as courses on Marxism and Party doctrine. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
In this article, the core category of ideological and political education. Zhong treats it as a form of knowledge and a state-linked force, following Marx and Engels.

The authors' term for the capitalist notion that labour defines human essence and that personhood is secured through property earned by labour. They argue that Marx's critique of alienated labour exposes it as historically specific.

en: Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law
q: Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law
lit: Thought, morality and the rule of law
ex: A compulsory ideological and political theory course, usually the first one taken by Chinese university students. It covers outlook on life, values, morality and the rule of law from a Marxist standpoint.
In the article's definition, religious activity that violates the constitution, laws, regulations and policies, including unauthorised gatherings and temple building.
A phrase from The German Ideology describing the state as a seemingly common interest that in fact serves the ruling class.
Maurizio Lazzarato's term for labour that produces the informational and cultural content of commodities. The article treats it as the typical labour form of cognitive capitalism.
A long-standing Chinese policy principle of tailoring development approaches to the specific conditions of each region.
Engels's qualification of the economic factor as determining history only 'in the last instance'. Tang reads it as implying necessity, mediation and non-exclusivity.
An official regulatory approach that tolerates experimentation with new technologies and business models while monitoring risks.
Financial services aimed at widening access for ordinary people, small firms and rural areas.
Lenin's thesis that socialist consciousness does not arise spontaneously from workers' struggles but is brought to the working class from outside by the party.

The principle that Chinese religious bodies and affairs should be run by Chinese believers without control by foreign forces. It grew out of the anti-imperialist religious movements of the early 1950s.
The principle that Chinese religious bodies run their own affairs without control by foreign religious organisations. Official texts link it to resisting foreign 'infiltration'.
A long-standing principle of Chinese Communist Party policy, stressing that development should rest on the country's own strength and decisions rather than on dependence on outside powers.

lit: independence and autonomy, self-reliance and self-strengthening
ex: A long-standing Party principle that China decides its own path and depends mainly on its own strength. Under Xi it is applied in particular to science and technology.

zh: 独立的比较完整的工业体系和国民经济体系
en: independent and relatively complete industrial system and national economic system
q: independent and relatively complete industrial system and national economic system
py: dúlì de bǐjiào wánzhěng de gōngyè tǐxì hé guómín jīngjì tǐxì
ex: A goal set out at the Third National People's Congress (1964–65). It refers to the capacity to produce key materials, machinery and defence goods domestically, together with agriculture and other sectors.
The practice of the Party opening and running real shops and firms as cover, as opposed to merely borrowing or pretending to be a business.

A phrase used by Xi Jinping in 2022 for scholarship that rests on Chinese practice rather than Western frameworks. It is presented as the ultimate aim of building the three systems (discipline, academic, discourse).

zh: 建构中国自主的知识体系
py: jiàngòu Zhōngguó zìzhǔ de zhīshi tǐxì
ex: A slogan prominent after Xi Jinping's 25 April 2022 speech at Renmin University of China. It calls for philosophy and social sciences grounded in Chinese experience rather than borrowed from the West.

A principle proposed by patriotic Christian and Catholic figures in the 1950s and backed by the Party and government. It holds that Chinese religious bodies must be free of foreign control, and the Constitution says religious bodies are not subject to foreign domination.

The article's term for the path Lenin adopted after the failure of war communism. It leads to socialism through intermediate steps (associated with the New Economic Policy) rather than by direct measures.
Marx's phrase in Capital for the property form that replaces capitalist private property, based on cooperation and common possession of the means of production.
The idea that aggression in one region threatens security everywhere. In the article it is tied to collective security and to China's wartime appeals to the international community.

The mode of development based on large-scale industrial production and consumption. Chinese writers on ecological civilisation often contrast it with a proposed post-industrial or ecological paradigm.
The decline of a country's manufacturing base as firms relocate production abroad or shift towards services and finance.

A term Marx used in Capital for the study of diseases linked to industrial work, drawing on physicians' reports. Li argues Marx turned it from description into a critique of capitalist relations of production.
Marx's term for the unemployed and underemployed surplus population that capital accumulation produces and draws on.
Policy of tying universities and vocational education closely to industry, including joint labs, research institutes and technology transfer.
Official shorthand for cooperation among enterprises, universities and research institutes in developing and commercialising technology.
A term for the narrowing of a person's information intake when algorithms feed them only content that matches their existing preferences.
A term from Mencius for what people can do without learning; Zhang Zai makes it a feature of Heaven's own nature.
A term from Mencius that Wang Yangming made central: the inborn moral awareness that judges right and wrong without study or deliberation.
A phrase the article attributes to Western public opinion, describing sharp ideological confrontation inside Western societies. It is used alongside "culture war".
Qian's term for the enduring structure of Chinese civilization: the pairing of Confucian doctrine as spiritual carrier with a unified state as political carrier.
A classical Confucian ideal in which inner moral cultivation grounds effective public governance. The article recasts it as wholehearted service to the people.

A concept first put forward at the Sixth Plenum of the 16th Central Committee (2006). It stresses unity, and resolving inner-Party contradictions without escalating them, as a basis for social harmony.
The Party's internal practices of meetings, criticism and self-criticism, study and discipline, regulated by norms such as the 2016 guidelines mentioned in the article.

zh: 创新是引领发展的第一动力
en: innovation as the primary driving force of development
q: innovation as the primary driving force of development
py: chuàngxīn shì yǐnlǐng fāzhǎn de dì-yī dònglì
lit: innovation is the first driving force leading development
ex: A formulation in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), tied to the innovation-driven development strategy.
Cooperative bodies of firms, universities and research institutes organised around a shared research task. The article proposes that leading firms head them.
A form of cooperative organisation led by leading enterprises together with universities and research institutes to tackle key technologies.
A term used in Party documents, including the 20th Party Congress report, for the values, norms and atmosphere that encourage scientific and technological innovation.

A policy term for real-world settings, such as city districts, buildings and public services, where new technologies and products are trialled and applied. Local governments publish lists of such opportunities.
A national strategy that makes scientific and technological innovation the main engine of economic growth, promoted in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
An official goal of making innovation the main driver of national development, with strong independent innovation capacity.
In Chinese discourse on tradition, extending and enriching inherited ideas with new content. It is usually paired with creative transformation.
Marx's image in the 1844 Manuscripts for nature as the extension of the human body, on which human life depends.
A Party system in which central inspection teams visit regions and departments to examine discipline and corruption; resident supervision (派驻) places supervisory bodies inside agencies.
A system in which inspection teams sent by higher authorities review local bodies. In the Party today it is a central supervision tool, and the article traces its historical forerunners.
A research institute of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences that publishes Contemporary China History Studies. The article abbreviates it as 当代所.
A research institute of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, founded in the 1960s following a proposal by Mao Zedong. Ren Jiyu was its first director.

lit: taking institution-building as the main line
ex: A principle added to the reform principles in the 2024 Third Plenum Decision. It makes building and refining institutional systems the organising line of reform.
One of four scholarly models. It explains corruption by gaps in, or breaches of, institutions and rules, and stresses building a sound anti-corruption system and rule of law.
The ability of a state to shape international institutions and global governance by setting agendas, making rules and spreading institutional ideas. The term appears in Party documents from 2015.
The term, used in the article for the post-2012 approach of coordinating reforms into a coherent, complete and effective system.
Official term for opening that stresses alignment and shaping of rules, regulations and standards, going beyond trade and investment flows.

The authors' term for poverty caused by injustice in a society's or state's institutions, as opposed to the individual differences between people. They use it to interpret Marx's account of proletarian poverty.

The author's proposed analytical concept: the practice of an institution seen as a closed five-link cycle from design to evaluation. It is offered as a new framework, not an established official term.
A pair of concepts derived from Max Weber. Instrumental rationality seeks efficient means, while value rationality concerns ends such as human freedom.
Living cultural practices such as opera, crafts, festivals and folk performance, protected through national and UNESCO listings.

zh: 大中小学思政课一体化建设
en: integrated development of ideological and political courses
q: integrated development of ideological and political courses
py: dà zhōng xiǎo xué sīzhèngkè yītǐhuà jiànshè
lit: integrated construction of university, secondary and primary school ideological-political courses
ex: A policy push, stressed by Xi Jinping in 2019, to link the content, teaching and teacher training of these courses across school stages in a progressive, spiral sequence rather than treating each stage separately.
A policy aim of coordinating moral, political and ideological education across primary, secondary and university stages, mainly through ideological and political theory courses (思政课).

zh: 新闻宣传和网络舆论一体化管理
en: integrated management of news and publicity and online public opinion
q: integrated management of news and publicity and online public opinion
py: xīnwén xuānchuán hé wǎngluò yúlùn yītǐhuà guǎnlǐ
ex: A policy direction stressed at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to coordinate traditional publicity work with the governance of online discourse.

zh: 山水林田湖草沙一体化保护和系统治理
en: integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert
q: integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert
py: shān shuǐ lín tián hú cǎo shā yītǐhuà bǎohù hé xìtǒng zhìlǐ
ex: An official policy principle treating land and water ecosystems as one interconnected whole to be protected and restored together rather than separately by sector.
Legal exclusive rights over knowledge products such as patents and trademarks. The author treats them as the legal form of private appropriation of knowledge and as a tool of monopoly.

A guiding idea in recent Chinese AI policy discourse that AI development should be oriented towards human wellbeing and ethical values. It appears in the 2025 State Council opinion and in the SCO Tianjin Declaration.
Computing based on big data, artificial intelligence and large language models, used here as a research method for the humanities and social sciences.
A Chinese term for the media environment shaped by AI, in which algorithms and generative AI take part in producing and distributing content.

The author's term for a productive-force system using data, algorithms and computing power as means of production and AI systems and robots as tools. The author presents it as a form of 'new quality productive forces'.
A term for the social transformation driven by artificial intelligence, big data and digital technologies.
A term for the spread of AI-based systems through production, organisation and management. The article contrasts capitalist and socialist forms of it.
Relations among political parties across borders. The article treats Marx and Engels's views on this as the theoretical basis of socialist parties' external exchanges.
The author's key concept for a relation in which each party is treated as a subject rather than an object. The author contrasts it with a 'single-subject' Western mode of thought.

en: interaction, exchange and integration among ethnic groups
q: interaction, exchange and integration among ethnic groups
ex: A Party term for the deepening mixing of ethnic groups in social, economic and cultural life. Official usage distinguishes it from forced assimilation.

The authors' term for the relationship between youth and the Party, in which the two share common features and flourish together. It is used by the authors as an analytical frame rather than as an official slogan.
The authors' term for a relation in which individuals recognise one another's freedom as an end, which they identify with communism. It is their reading of Marx, not a phrase from Marx's own texts.
A group pursuing its own sectional advantage. Party leaders use the term, including for groups inside the Party, to describe a threat to the Party's nature and political integrity.
The author's term for an arrangement that links the differing interests of several parties so that they act together toward a common goal.

A term the article takes from the Japanese scholar Watanabe Masao. It describes a system in which big capital wins the middle class's loyalty through laws, institutions and subsidies, so that workers cannot ally with it.
Engels's idea that legal and political ideologies mediate between the economic base and more distant ideologies such as philosophy and religion.
A concept Mao Zedong set out in 1946 to describe the territories lying between the United States and the Soviet Union. In the 1960s it was revised into 'two intermediate zones'.
Zhang's term for the strain that arises when an ideology lags behind practice. He treats it as a driver of innovation if addressed and a source of risk if neglected.
The Chinese term for external communication aimed at foreign audiences, covering media, diplomacy and cultural outreach. It is often discussed as a way to "tell China's story well".
A Maoist international organisation founded on 26 December 2022 with 15 member parties and organisations, mainly in Europe and Latin America.

The worldwide network of communist parties and organisations, historically centred on the Comintern and later the Soviet party. Chinese scholars use it for both the history and the present state of these parties.
The Chinese state agency, established in 2018, that manages foreign aid and development cooperation.
The capacity to shape agendas, narratives and concepts in international public debate, a key term in Chinese discussions of international communication.
The authors' term, drawing on Lenin's finance capital, for large globally operating banks and multinational firms that exert major influence on the world economy.

zh: 国际金融垄断资本主义
ex: A Chinese Marxist characterisation of the current stage of capitalism, marked by globalised financial monopoly capital, transnational corporate alliances and financial dominance.
The Party body, founded in 1950, that manages relations with foreign parties. It is now usually called the International Department of the CPC Central Committee.

zh: 共产党和工人党国际会议
en: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
q: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
lit: International Conference of Communist and Workers' Parties
ex: An annual multilateral forum of communist and workers' parties, running since 1998. It has no standing leadership or binding programme.

zh: 世界共产党和工人党国际会议
en: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
q: International Meeting of Communist and Workers' Parties
py: shìjiè gòngchǎndǎng hé gōngréndǎng guójì huìyì
ex: An annual international forum of communist and workers' parties on a shared Marxist basis. The article says the Belgian party attends every year.
The article's term for transnational capital, mainly finance capital, that it says leads globalization and sometimes conflicts with national industrial capital.
Mao-era idea of uniting all countries willing to resist hegemony and war, regardless of social system.
US law that created an ambassador-at-large and an annual State Department report on religious freedom worldwide. It also provides for designating 'countries of particular concern'.

en: international science and technology innovation centres
q: international science and technology innovation centres
ex: City or regional hubs designated by the Chinese state to lead in research, technological innovation and industrial upgrading. Three have been designated: Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area.
The English School's core concept: states bound by shared rules and institutions such as sovereignty, diplomacy and international law, not just by power.
Mao's concept of building broad alliances abroad, in particular an anti-fascist coalition during the Second World War, to support China's struggle.
The Chinese name for International Women's Day on 8 March. Communist-led women's groups observed it in China from the 1920s, and it is marked in Yan'an in this speech.
The Marxist principle of solidarity among workers and nations across borders. Here the article cites Mao's claim that it is consistent with revolutionary patriotism.
A national strategy launched in 2015 to integrate internet technologies with traditional sectors such as manufacturing, finance, agriculture and retail.

zh: 互联网+无神论宣传教育
ex: The authors' term for integrating atheist education with internet platforms and new media, modelled on the official "Internet Plus" slogan.
Government administration of individuals and organisations involved in religious activity online. The author treats it as part of religious work and of national security work.
A term Žižek uses for activity done in order to prevent anything from really happening. The article applies it to left activism that stays inside the capitalist framework.
Louis Althusser's concept (Chinese translation of interpellation) for how ideology addresses individuals and turns them into subjects.

lit: interpreting the world and changing the world
ex: An allusion to Marx's eleventh thesis on Feuerbach, used here to describe the unity of scientific theory and transformative practice.

lit: using the West to explain China
ex: The practice of explaining Chinese thought with Western concepts and frameworks, which the authors caution against when it is done uncritically.

lit: using the West to interpret Marxism
ex: A critical label for the tendency to treat Western Marxist readings as the model for reforming Chinese Marxist philosophy.
A concept from Western philosophy, widely used in Chinese education theory, describing education as a relation between two subjects, not between a subject and an object.
The problem that resource-exporting governments cannot credibly promise investors that policies will stay unchanged after investments are sunk, which raises investors' transaction costs.
The practice of broadening member participation in discussion, selection and decision-making within the Party, which official discourse treats as a basis for wider democracy.
The shared beliefs, values, norms and habits of conduct within the Communist Party, which official texts treat as shaping its political ecology.
A term popularised under Xi Jinping for the overall environment, atmosphere, habits and conduct within the Party. It is used to discuss Party discipline, culture and anti-corruption work.
In the article, the authority that Party organisations hold over lower organisations and members, defined as a form of organisational public power.
Formal rules issued by the Party's own organs, including organisational, leadership, self-building and oversight regulations, which are distinct from state law.
The system by which the Communist Party oversees its own organisations and members, led by Party committees and discipline inspection bodies.
A concept from industrial safety engineering. It aims to build safety into the design and operation of facilities so they remain functional under shocks.

A long-standing Party method of fact-finding through fieldwork and analysis before making and implementing policy. It is associated with Mao Zedong's 'no investigation, no right to speak' and has been repeatedly stressed by Xi Jinping.
A policy slogan that treats spending on education, skills, health and livelihoods as investment in human capital, not as consumption or welfare.
Policy term for investment in physical production capacity such as infrastructure, equipment and technology.
A mechanism that combines bank lending with equity investment in the same firm, so that banks share in the firm's growth.
A popular term for intense, zero-sum competition that consumes effort without raising overall welfare. The authors use it for overwork and pointless competitive pressure.
Destructive, low-return competition such as price wars, which official policy since 2024–25 has said should be curbed.
A phrase from Lenin's writings, used in Party rhetoric for strict, binding discipline within the Party.
Commercial and price-management maxims attributed to Ji Ran, recorded in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian and said to have been used by Fan Li.
The label later given to Mao's 1944 exchange with Guo Moruo and his use of Guo's essay on the fall of Li Zicheng's regime in 1644, as a warning against complacency.

The Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei border region, one of the main anti-Japanese base areas led by the Communist Party behind Japanese lines during the War of Resistance (1937–1945). The article uses its name for the region and its newspaper.

The Party's name for the values attributed to the Jinggangshan base area struggle of 1927–1929, summarised by Xi Jinping as firm conviction, hard struggle, seeking truth from facts, daring to blaze new trails, and reliance on the people.

A Confucian-derived tradition, associated with Ming-Qing thinkers such as Wang Fuzhi, holding that learning should serve practical governance and social needs. Wu uses it to define the purpose of scientific research.

A summary of the development path of Jinjiang, a county-level city in Fujian, which Xi Jinping distilled in the early 2000s. It stresses the market, local strengths, integrity and a service-oriented government.
An academy in the state of Qi in the Warring States period that gathered scholars of many schools and is associated with the "hundred schools of thought" debates.

lit: joining the Party on the firing line
ex: An exceptional admission, in war or disaster, in which the usual procedure is shortened for someone who has shown courage or merit.

en: joint investigation and joint handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption
q: joint investigation and joint handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption
py: fēng fǔ tóng chá tóng zhì
lit: investigate and handle work style and corruption together
ex: A Party discipline principle that treats unhealthy work styles and corruption as linked problems to be investigated and addressed together. It was written into the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

en: joint investigation of misconduct and corruption
q: joint investigation of misconduct and corruption
ex: A principle that treats breaches of conduct rules and corruption as linked and investigates them together.

en: joint rule of virtue and law
q: joint rule of virtue and law
ex: The idea, drawn from traditional Chinese political thought, that moral education and legal norms should work together in governing society.
The idea that reporting and propaganda were themselves a form of resistance to Japan, alongside military struggle.
North Korea's official ideology of self-reliance and of the masses as masters of their own destiny, associated with Kim Il Sung.
A central Confucian term for the morally exemplary person. It originally denoted aristocratic status and was recast by Confucius as a moral ideal.
A production model that keeps inventories to a minimum by producing parts only when needed.
Short name for the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University, the Communist-led military and political academy founded in 1936 and based mainly in Yan'an and the base areas.
The guiding ideology of the LPRP alongside Marxism-Leninism, named after the Party's founding leader and first head of the Lao state.

en: keeping the whole world in mind
q: keeping the whole world in mind
lit: holding the world in one's heart
ex: A phrase from traditional Chinese thought, used in Party discourse for a global outlook; it is listed among the Party's historical experiences.
Technologies seen as critical to industrial security and competitiveness, often those where China depends on foreign supply. Breakthroughs here are a stated priority of national policy.
A term for leading cadres, whose conduct and study are held to set an example for the wider Party and society.
The CPV's phrase for the central importance of cadre work in party building, used in Thirteenth Congress documents.
The economic school following John Maynard Keynes that advocates government demand management and intervention. Liu treats it as the theoretical basis of state monopoly capitalism.
The Cambodian communist movement led by Pol Pot, which ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. The review notes the attention given to its mass killings.
The ideological formula, in the Workers' Party of Korea's usage, for the ideas of its two late leaders. The report calls for remoulding all of society according to it.
The official guiding ideology of the Workers' Party of Korea, built on the Juche idea. The revised Party rules of 2021 describe it as the Party's permanent guiding thought.

en: knowing the person and the age
q: knowing the person and the age
lit: know the person, discuss the age
ex: A classical Chinese critical method that calls for understanding an author's life and historical setting before judging a work.
The cognitive, emotional and volitional aspects of personality. Chinese moral philosophy uses the triad to describe a well-rounded ideal character.
A framework from Chinese moral and ideological education describing four stages in forming belief and conduct: cognition, emotion, will and practice.
The article's term for the dominance of imperialist countries over knowledge and technology production. Intellectual property rules and academic dependence maintain it.

The article's term for monopoly capital's control of the conditions of knowledge production, such as intellectual property and specialised personnel, in order to command global production and profits.

In current Chinese policy discourse, the 'autonomous knowledge system' is the goal of building Chinese-developed theories and concepts. The author treats it as the combined expression of the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems.
The first united front (1924–27) between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party. Communists joined the Kuomintang as individuals and worked within its institutions.
The Japanese army stationed in the Kwantung Leased Territory and along the South Manchuria Railway zone, which carried out the 1931 invasion of Manchuria.
The movement founded by Jean-Luc Mélenchon in 2016–2017 to contest the presidential election, which the PCF backed in 2017.

A concept from Engels, developed by Lenin, for a better-paid stratum of workers in imperialist countries said to be bought off by imperialist super-profits. Rockhill applies it to Western Marxist intellectuals.
An area of Chinese schooling, strengthened by a 2020 Party and State Council opinion, that aims to cultivate respect for labour and practical labour skills among students at all levels.
A concept developed by the authors from Marx's view of labour as human species-essence. It denotes the deep satisfaction people gain when labour confirms their essence.
Model workers and peasants publicly honoured in the border region for outstanding output and exemplary conduct. The Party used them as examples for others to follow.

The early PRC system of workers' benefits covering injury, illness, maternity, old age and death, set out in the 1951 Labour Insurance Regulations. It was financed by enterprises and administered by trade unions.
A concept the authors attribute to Marx: the evaluation of labour activity, labour relations and labour methods by the standard of justice, centred on who owns and enjoys the products of labour.
Peasant associations for exchanging labour, building on traditional seasonal labour exchange; work was recorded in work points and settled at year-end.
The view that labour is the foundational category of human social being. Lukács adopts it in his late work, and Yang traces it to Hegel and the 1844 and 1857–58 manuscripts.

The Lockean idea that a person's labour, mixed with natural things, makes them that person's property. The article treats it as a category that Marx's critique shows turning into its opposite under capitalism.
The guiding ideology the Brazilian Workers' Party adopted in 1990. The article presents it as a moderate, pluralist left outlook that opposes capitalist exploitation but seeks gradual reform.

The theory, developed in classical political economy and by Marx, that the value of commodities is determined by the socially necessary labour time needed to produce them. The article debates how far it applies to artificial intelligence.

In Marx's usage, the worker's capacity to work, which is what the capitalist buys, as distinct from labour itself, the activity. In ordinary Chinese economic writing the same word can also mean the workforce.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's idea (Bildung through work) in the master–slave dialectic, that the labouring slave gains independent consciousness by shaping things.
The redistribution of land from landlords to peasants carried out in newly liberated areas from 1950 to 1952, accompanied by class classification.
The redistribution of land from landlords to peasants carried out in Communist-held areas before and after 1949.
The Party's programme of redistributing land from landlords to peasants. It gave its name to the 'agrarian revolutionary war' period of 1927–1937.
The phase of the revolution (roughly 1927–1937) when the Party built rural base areas such as the Central Soviet Area and redistributed land.
Official term for a mass relapse of lifted households into poverty. Preventing it is set as a bottom line of rural policy.
A common metaphor for the final stage at which central policies are implemented at the local level.
Foster's term for the present phase of imperialism, marked by monopoly-finance capital and transnational commodity chains linking developing and developed countries.
The view, criticised by the authors, that Marxism is a European product unsuited to Latin America.

A label used by some Chinese scholars for the varieties of socialism proclaimed by left-wing governments in Latin America since the late 1990s, such as Venezuela's "21st-century socialism". It is not the European fascist usage.

The process of adapting Marxism to Latin American conditions, analogous to the Russianisation and Sinicisation of Marxism. The article dates it from Mariátegui's call for a Marxism rooted in the region.

en: the law of the mutual transformation of quantity and quality
q: law of the mutual transformation of quantity and quality
ex: One of the basic laws of materialist dialectics: gradual quantitative change reaches a limit and produces qualitative change, and vice versa.

en: law of the negation of the negation
q: law of the negation of the negation
ex: One of the three basic laws of materialist dialectics as formulated by Engels in Dialectics of Nature, alongside quantity–quality transformation and the unity of opposites. It describes development as a spiral in which a thing negates itself and is then negated again.

zh: 《中华人民共和国英雄烈士保护法》
en: Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs
q: Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs
py: Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó Yīngxióng Lièshì Bǎohù Fǎ
ex: A law adopted by the NPC Standing Committee on 27 April 2018 and in force from 1 May 2018. It protects the names, reputations and honour of heroes and martyrs.
A concept in Xi Jinping's economic and legal thought holding that market economic activity must be governed by law. Xi has stated that the socialist market economy is in essence a law-based economy.
A metaphor for leading cadres setting an example, as the lead goose guides the flock. It is used in Party discourse to stress that officials must model good conduct.

A term in Chinese Party discourse for the central leadership body or figure around which the Party is to be united. The article applies it both to Lenin's centralised organisation and to the present Central Committee.
A Party term for the paramount leader around whom the collective leadership is said to unite; applied to Mao, Deng and, since 2016, Xi.
The authority to guide the dominant thinking in a society. Chinese Party-state writing treats it as a key part of political rule, and it is often compared with Gramsci's hegemony.
The Party's authority to direct propaganda, theory, education, culture and media. The Party has stressed it since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and reaffirmed it in the 2021 historical resolution.
Officials holding leadership posts in the Party, government and state institutions in China.
Party and state officials who hold leadership posts, together with civil servants governed by the Civil Servants Law. The review treats them as decision-makers who also set an example for the public.

en: leading force of ideological and political education
q: leading force of ideological and political education
ex: A term Xi Jinping used at the National Education Conference in September 2024. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer the direction, development and talent training of education.
A strategic goal, which the article dates to 2035, of making China a world leader in science and technology.
An official goal of making China a world leader in sport. It is linked in Party discourse to the slogan "when sport is strong, China is strong".

A policy category for large, technologically advanced firms expected to lead national innovation efforts. Official documents treat them as part of the national strategic science and technology forces.
Mao Zedong's 1949 formula for aligning the new People's Republic with the Soviet Union and the socialist camp rather than with the imperialist powers.

The idea, from late Marx and Engels on Russia, that some societies might bypass the capitalist stage (the "Caudine Forks"). Chinese scholars treat it as a theoretical basis for socialist modernization in the East.

A nationwide campaign launched in 1963 urging people to emulate Lei Feng, a soldier who died on duty in 1962 and was presented as a model of selfless service. It is still promoted each March, often through volunteer service.
A phrase for the early twentieth-century turn of Chinese radicals from imitating Western Europe and the United States to taking the Russian Revolution as a model.
A Party self-description stressing continuous theoretical study as a defining trait of the Communist Party of China.
A Party-run mobile learning platform launched in 2019 that carries Party theory, news and study content.
The label the article, citing other scholars, gives to a mix of left-wing economic and welfare policies with culturally conservative and nationalist stances, especially on migration.
An electoral and political alliance formed around 2009 by the PCF and the Left Party of Jean-Luc Mélenchon and others. The article reports that it split after Mélenchon founded La France Insoumise.
The author's label for the period of about 2015–2018 when left governments lost power or elections across Latin America and right-wing forces gained.

The official Party label for the ultra-radical political and military line that dominated the Central Committee in the early 1930s. Party histories associate it with Wang Ming and, in military matters, with Bo Gu and Otto Braun.

In Chinese Party vocabulary, an ultra-radical line that overestimates revolutionary conditions and refuses alliances with other forces. The article applies it to the CPUSA's early united-front policy.

The Party's official label for the line of Wang Ming and the Bo Gu leadership. It is said to have mechanically applied Soviet experience and Comintern instructions without regard to Chinese conditions.
The Party's official label for ultra-radical lines in the late 1920s and early 1930s, such as putschism and adventurism, which later Party history judges to have caused serious losses.

The label official Party history gives to the leadership line of Wang Ming and others before Zunyi, criticised as dogmatist and adventurist. The article associates it with positional defence in the fifth anti-encirclement campaign.
Lenin's label for Struve and others who used Marxist arguments in tsarist-approved publications to defend capitalism's necessity and permanence.
The author's term for local lawmaking that favours appearance over substance, such as omnibus laws that copy other regions' texts.
The author's preferred Chinese rendering of the English "legitimacy". It denotes moral and social acceptance of authority, which the article distinguishes from legality (hefaxing).

The set of virtues associated with Lei Feng (1940–1962), a soldier held up since 1963 as a model of selflessness, hard work and service to the people. Official campaigns to 'learn from Lei Feng' have recurred for decades.

Lenin's account of imperialism as the monopoly stage of capitalism, set out in Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism (1917). Chinese Marxist writers often treat it as the basic framework for analysing modern capitalism.

en: let a hundred flowers bloom, weed through the old to bring forth the new
q: let a hundred flowers bloom, weed through the old to bring forth the new
lit: a hundred flowers bloom together; push out the old to bring forth the new
ex: Mao's 1951 inscription for the Chinese Opera Research Institute, which became a guiding line for the arts. It is related to the 'Double Hundred' policy of the 1950s.

A slogan associated with Mao Zedong's 1956 policy of encouraging varied artistic and scholarly expression, together with "a hundred schools of thought contend". The authors accept it within limits set by the Party's guiding ideology.

en: letting a hundred schools of thought contend
q: letting a hundred schools of thought contend
ex: A slogan from the Warring States period, revived by Mao Zedong in the 1950s as a policy for academic and cultural debate, often paired with "letting a hundred flowers bloom".

lit: the first to get rich lead the later ones
ex: Deng Xiaoping's formula from the reform era that some people and regions would prosper first and then help others to prosper.

A current of Russian populist thinkers, including Danielson and Vorontsov, who saw the peasant commune as a way to avoid capitalism. Lenin criticised them as representing the interests of small producers.
The term the CPC used for the base areas it governed behind Japanese lines and elsewhere during the war.

zh: 解放生产力,发展生产力,消灭剥削,消除两极分化
en: liberating productive forces, eliminating exploitation and polarisation
q: liberating productive forces, eliminating exploitation and polarisation
py: jiěfàng shēngchǎnlì, fāzhǎn shēngchǎnlì, xiāomiè bōxuē, xiāochú liǎngjí fēnhuà
ex: Part of Deng Xiaoping's definition of the essence of socialism, from his 1992 southern tour. The article reads its later clauses as concerned with justice.
Deng's formula that reform, like revolution, frees the productive forces by removing institutional obstacles to growth.
The Communist Party's main newspaper in Yan'an, founded in 1941 and used for propaganda and policy guidance.

A concept associated with Xi Jinping, notably in the phrase that mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts form a life community. It treats ecosystems as interdependent wholes.
A concept proposed in 2018 by the Party committee of the Zhejiang Wanli Education Group. It aims to embed ideological and political education in students' daily lives on and off campus.
A phrase in Party discourse describing ideological and political work as the lifeline of economic work and all other work. The author cites Hu Jintao's formulation.
A concept from Husserl and Schütz taken up by Habermas. It is the taken-for-granted background of shared knowledge in which everyday communicative action takes place.
A group of mainly right-leaning Latin American governments and Canada, formed in 2017 to press the Maduro government in Venezuela.
The doctrine, associated with the Brezhnev Doctrine, that a threat to socialism in one country concerns all socialist states and justifies intervention. It was invoked in 1968 against Czechoslovakia.
In Party usage, the overall strategic, political and organisational orientation of the Party. Disputes over the 'correct line' are treated as the central questions of Party history.
The Communist Party's wartime line of mobilising the whole population to fight, as opposed to the Kuomintang's reliance on government and regular armies.
The patrilineal kin group that formed the basis of social organisation and rule in traditional Yi society.

lit: culture south of the mountain ridges
ex: The regional culture of the area south of the Five Ridges, centred on Guangdong and neighbouring areas. It includes Cantonese opera, Chaozhou traditions and a long record of maritime trade and overseas migration.
A principle central to Mao's thought that Marxist theory must be applied to concrete Chinese conditions. It is closely tied to seeking truth from facts.

In this article, a Korean left current that rejects Soviet socialism and the theory of permanent revolution and draws on post-Marxism and postmodernism. The author distinguishes it from the broader Korean political practice of 'settling accounts' with opponents.
The most basic and widespread form of popular schooling in the base areas, including people's schools, night schools and anti-illiteracy classes.
A term for writers and artists who, in the Party's view, put their work at the service of the revolutionary struggle and the masses. It is used here in contrast to the independent "artist".

py: zhuān jīng tè xīn “xiǎo jùrén” qǐyè
lit: specialised, refined, distinctive and innovative 'little giant' enterprises
ex: A government-designated category of small and medium-sized firms that specialise in niche products, with strong technology and market positions. It is used in industrial policy to support manufacturing and supply-chain security.

lit: take the lead in living tight days
ex: A slogan calling on Party and government bodies to cut spending and practise frugality, so that public funds go to priority and livelihood areas.
A broad term for people's everyday well-being, covering education, health care, employment, housing, pensions and social security. It is a recurring priority in Party and government policy language.
One of the six attributes of a leading education country listed by Xi. It refers to education's ability to meet people's everyday needs and ensure fair access.
Marx's term (lebendige Arbeit) for labour actually being performed, as against the “dead labour” stored in machines and materials. For Marx it is the only source of surplus value.
Mao Zedong's term for Marxism combined with Chinese realities and expressed in a Chinese style, as opposed to dogmatic repetition of texts.

The 1981 historical resolution's term for the standpoint, viewpoint and method running through Mao Zedong Thought. It is usually listed as seeking truth from facts, the mass line, and independence and self-reliance.

en: the living soul of Mao Zedong Thought
q: living soul of Mao Zedong Thought
py: Máo Zédōng sīxiǎng huó de línghún
ex: Phrase from the 1981 Party resolution on history, naming three basic aspects of Mao Zedong Thought: seeking truth from facts, the mass line, and independence and self-reliance.

zh: 毛泽东思想的活的灵魂
en: living soul of Mao Zedong Thought
q: living soul of Mao Zedong Thought
py: Máo Zédōng sīxiǎng de huó de línghún
ex: A formula from the 1981 Party resolution naming three core elements of Mao Zedong Thought: seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence.
The author's term for the success of socialism with Chinese characteristics, set against an "overall ebb" of the international communist movement.
A Party term for minority-group nationalism seen as placing local ethnic interests above national unity. It is the counterpart of "Han chauvinism" in official ethnic-policy discourse.
Practices by local governments that favour local firms or restrict outside ones, which fragment the national market.
A term some scholars use for the ordinary, lawful, locally rooted form of folk belief, to distinguish it from secret sects.
The idea that a general theory such as socialism must be adapted to a country's own conditions. It is related to Chinese discussions of adapting Marxism to the national context.
The process of adapting Marxist theory to a country's own culture, history and conditions. In Chinese scholarship it parallels the idea of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.

en: locking power in an institutional cage
q: locking power in an institutional cage
py: bǎ quánlì guān jìn zhìdù lóngzi
lit: lock power into the cage of institutions
ex: A phrase used by Xi Jinping for restraining officials' power through rules, procedures and supervision.

Official Party phrase for communism as the Party's ultimate goal, contrasted with the "common ideal" of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In this article it refers to Marx and Engels's prediction of the future society's basic features.
A Marxist expression for capital's inherent drive to self-expand through surplus value, which shapes social life. Chinese writers often contrast it with the "logic of the people".
A phrase from Lenin's Philosophical Notebooks. He wrote that Marx left no 'Logic' but did leave the logic of Capital, in which dialectics, logic and theory of knowledge coincide.

en: the logic of capital and the logic of power
q: logic of capital and the logic of power
ex: A frame in Chinese Marxist writing that treats the drive of capital for valorisation and the operation of state power as intertwined. The authors use it to explain how biotechnology comes to serve capital accumulation.
The author's counterpart to "the logic of capital": a development logic oriented to the public interest, common prosperity and the all-round development of the person.
The first, most basic category from which a theoretical system is developed, as commodity is in Marx's Capital.

Marx's 24 notebooks of extracts and notes on economics, history and colonialism, made in London in 1850–1853. They are published in MEGA2 Division IV, volumes 7–9, and the later notebooks remain incomplete.
Michael Roberts's term for the prolonged period of weak growth after the 2008 financial crisis, which the article's scholars say has not ended.
The strategic retreat of the Chinese Red Army from 1934 to 1936. The Central Red Army began it from Jiangxi in October 1934.

A state-planned heritage zone linking relics and cultural resources along the Red Army's Long March route across 15 provincial-level units. It is one of five national cultural parks, and its plan was issued in 2021.
The official name for the values attributed to the Red Army's 1934–36 Long March, such as endurance, loyalty and unity, invoked in Party education.

A set of values the Party associates with the Red Army's Long March of 1934–36. Xi Jinping defined it in 2016 as putting the people's interests first, firm revolutionary ideals, self-reliance, discipline and unity, and reliance on the masses.
Braudel's concept (longue durée) of very slow historical rhythms such as geography and deep structures, set against the shorter time of conjunctures and events.
A theme in Party discourse about how the CPC can remain the ruling party over the long run. Xi Jinping has called it a fundamental question the Party must answer.
Mao's phrase from the 1942 essay Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing. It means propaganda should be adapted to its audience, as an archer looks at the target.
