Economic activity based on low-altitude flight by crewed and uncrewed aircraft, including drones and eVTOL vehicles.
A US military doctrine of long, combined military, political, economic and psychological warfare. Wang says it was used against guerrilla movements in the Third World.

zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
q: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
lit: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
ex: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing.
A strand of egalitarian theory holding that inequalities caused by luck or involuntary circumstances are unjust and should be compensated, while inequalities from choice may be acceptable.

Zhang Yibing's recurring metaphor for a shift that moves the essence of a thing from external objects to human subjective activity, as Luther moved faith inward. Zhang applies it to both Marx's ontology and Lefebvre's view of space.
A colloquial term for deliberately minimising work and ambition. The authors cite it as an attitude that university labour education should counter.
A style of judging associated with the Border Region judge Ma Xiwu. It involved going to the locality, investigating on site, relying on local people and avoiding rigid formality.
The philosophical current based on Ernst Mach's empirio-criticism, which Lenin attacked in 1908–09 as disguised subjective idealism. In Russia some Bolsheviks, such as Bogdanov, had adopted it.
The long-standing Chinese term for state management of the overall economy, mainly through fiscal and monetary policy to smooth cycles.
An official term that places macroeconomic regulation within the broader system of national governance, using fiscal, monetary, industrial, regional and structural tools together.
The September 1948 revolt by the Indonesian Communist Party, put down by the Indonesian Republic's government. The review counts it as the party's second devastating blow.
The official Chinese description of China's battlefield in the Second World War, used to stress its central place in the global anti-fascist war.
A cultural-policy term for works that promote mainstream official values and a positive image of national development.
An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in a crisis. Mao Zedong used it in 1941 of the Communist-led forces, and the Party now uses it for its role in the War of Resistance.
In Chinese official discourse, the dominant body of ideas led by Marxism and Party theory, which the state seeks to keep in the leading position in public opinion.
Official term for the dominant, Party-endorsed ideas and public discourse, as distinct from "negative" or "erroneous" opinion.
In Chinese usage, chiefly Party and state-run news organisations regarded as authoritative channels for official information and publicity.
Xi Jinping's phrase at the April 2016 National Conference on Religious Work, used to stress that upholding Marxist atheism is a basic requirement across all areas of work.

en: major reforms must have a legal basis
q: major reforms must have a legal basis
py: zhòngdà gǎigé yú fǎ yǒu jù
lit: major reforms are grounded in law
ex: A principle stated by Xi Jinping in 2013 that significant reforms should rest on legal authority. It is part of Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law.
A term for the developing regions where most of the world's population lives and works, used as an alternative to "Global South" or "developing countries".

en: making the past serve the present
q: making the past serve the present
lit: let the ancient serve the present
ex: A cultural-policy principle of using the heritage of the past for present needs. Mao stated it explicitly only after 1949.

en: making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China
q: making the past serve the present and foreign things serve China
py: gǔ wéi jīn yòng, yáng wéi Zhōng yòng
lit: let the ancient serve the present, let the foreign serve China
ex: A slogan associated with Mao Zedong from the 1950s, calling for critical use of both the Chinese heritage and foreign culture in building a new socialist culture.

en: the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall
q: man of Qi who feared the sky would fall
lit: the man of Qi worries about the sky
ex: A Chinese idiom from the Daoist text Liezi, for groundless anxiety. The story is used in the article as a contrast to Western doomsday belief.

en: management of religious affairs according to law
q: management of religious affairs according to law
ex: The principle that religious activities, venues and organisations are regulated by law, notably the 2004 Regulations on Religious Affairs, while personal belief remains free.

A reform approach proposed in 2013 in which state asset regulators supervise state capital as value-form assets, for example through investment and operating companies, instead of directly managing enterprises.
Phrase from the Party's 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations (2025), replacing the earlier "guandezhu" (managing tightly). It stresses precise, law-based and forward-looking regulation.
An idea dating from the early Zhou dynasty that Heaven grants rulers the right to govern and can withdraw it from unvirtuous ones.

en: Manifesto of the Fourth Red Army
q: Manifesto of the Fourth Red Army
ex: A proclamation issued in early 1929 by the Party organisation of the Red Fourth Army in the Soviet areas. The article reads it as applying the Manifesto's revolutionary tasks to China.

One of the named spirits in the Party's official 'spiritual lineage', summed up as being especially able to endure hardship, fight, tackle key problems and dedicate oneself. It is associated with the Chinese manned space programme.
The article's term for building aesthetic perception, cultural symbols and emotional experience into design, craft, production and products. It is presented as China's soft power in industry.
Official goal of moving China from being the world's largest manufacturer to a leader in technology, quality and brands.
Marx's category for capital as it exists in the plural and in competition. In the author's reading, it is the concrete unfolding of capital in general.
The Party's official term for the sinified Marxism developed by Mao and his colleagues. It was written into the Party constitution at the 7th Party Congress in 1945.

The label used by overseas parties for Mao Zedong's contribution to Marxism, which they treat as a 'third stage' after Marxism and Leninism. In China the standard term is Mao Zedong Thought, and the article describes these parties from an external standpoint.

A Chinese policy and media phrase for replacing workers with automated equipment. Several provinces and cities issued dedicated implementation plans for it. (In the summary, the related state survey step is called "mapping".)
The clash near Beijing on 7 July 1937 that marked the start of full-scale war between Japan and China. Chinese historiography treats it as the start of the nationwide war of resistance.
A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops near Beiping on 7 July 1937, which marked the start of full-scale war.
A national goal, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), of developing China's marine economy, naval strength, technology and maritime rights.
A legal and policy category covering enterprises, individual businesses and farmers' cooperatives, all of which are registered and take part in market activity.
A strand of Western socialist thought that holds that markets and competition can operate under social or public ownership. Schweickart and Lane are among its advocates in the article.

A trade-law designation affecting how anti-dumping cases are assessed. Under China's WTO accession protocol, China expected to receive it after 15 years, but the United States, the EU and Japan have not granted it.
The ideas of José Martí, the nineteenth-century Cuban independence leader. The article says the Party wrote them into its statutes alongside Marxism-Leninism.
The term Unit 731 staff used for the prisoners subjected to experiments, treating them as materials rather than people.

zh: 中国化时代化的马克思主义
en: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
q: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
ex: The official description of the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to contemporary developments. It is often rendered in short as the 'sinicisation and contemporisation' of Marxism.

en: Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western learning for application
q: Marxism as soul, Chinese culture as substance, Western learning for application
py: Mǎ hún Zhōng tǐ Xī yòng
lit: Marxism the soul, Chinese the substance, Western the function
ex: Fang Keli's formula, which adds Marxism as the guiding "soul" to the older "Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application" scheme. It is not an official Party term.
A top-level academic discipline category for Marxist theory in China's university system, established in 2004. It groups the study of Marxist theory under Marxism schools.

A phrase from the 20th Party Congress report (2022), which says that the Party's success and the merits of socialism with Chinese characteristics ultimately rest on the efficacy of Marxism. The article treats it as a historical conclusion.

zh: 马克思主义在意识形态领域的指导地位
en: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
q: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
py: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì zài yìshí xíngtài lǐngyù de zhǐdǎo dìwèi
ex: A principle of Party rule, listed as a fundamental system at the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in 2019. It requires Marxism to be the guiding thought across ideology, education and culture.

zh: 意识形态领域的指导地位
en: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
q: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
py: yìshí xíngtài lǐngyù de zhǐdǎo dìwèi
ex: The principle that Marxism provides the guiding thought in culture, media, education and scholarship. The 4th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) named it a fundamental system.

The term was first used by the Comintern's Fifth Congress in 1924, after Lenin's death, for Marxism as developed by Lenin. In China it became the Party's foundational doctrine, and the article traces its adoption in Party documents from 1925.
A doctrine adopted by many foreign Maoist parties, notably Peru's Shining Path, which treats Maoism as the third stage of Marxism. It differs from the official Chinese term 'Mao Zedong Thought'.

The Marxist approach to religion taught and researched in Chinese academic institutions, which treats religion as a product of social conditions and as an ideological force. The journal Science and Atheism publishes work in this field.
A term in Chinese theory for the concepts, categories and modes of expression through which Marxist theory is presented and spread. Building it is treated as a task of Chinese social science.

zh: 提高全党马克思主义水平和现代化建设能力
en: Marxist level and capacity for modernization
q: Marxist level and capacity for modernization
py: tígāo quándǎng Mǎkèsīzhǔyì shuǐpíng hé xiàndàihuà jiànshè nénglì
lit: raise the whole Party's Marxist level and modernization-building capacity
ex: A requirement in the communiqué of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It concerns Party members' theoretical grounding and practical ability to carry out modernization.
Study of religion grounded in Marxist theory, promoted by Xi Jinping at the 2021 national religious work conference as a discipline to be built.

zh: 马克思主义科学无神论
ex: Atheism grounded in dialectical and historical materialism, which explains religion as a product of social conditions and human alienation. In Chinese Party-academic usage it is a field of study and an element of ideological education.

The teaching of Marxist theory to Party members, officials and students, including ideological and political courses in schools and universities. It is treated in China as a means of upholding Marxism's leading position in ideology.
A first-level discipline established in China in 2006 under the law category. Ideological and political education is one of its second-level disciplines.

A first-level academic discipline in China's university system, set up in the 2000s. It includes sub-fields such as basic principles of Marxism, the adaptation of Marxism to China, ideological and political education, and foreign Marxism.
The body of Marxist thought on religion that Chinese official scholarship treats as the basic framework for understanding religious questions in a socialist state.

en: Marxist theory of the human being (renxue)
q: Marxist theory of the human being (renxue)
ex: A field of Chinese Marxist philosophy that studies the nature, existence and development of the human being, often drawing on Marx's early writings.

en: Marxist theory research and construction project
q: Marxist theory research and construction project
ex: A national project, launched in the early 2000s, to compile standard textbooks and research on Marxist theory for use in Chinese universities. Its textbooks are regarded as authoritative.

zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
en: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
q: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
py: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
ex: A national project launched in 2004 to compile textbooks and promote research and teaching in Marxist theory.
The Marxist view that capitalist production and exchange break down national isolation and turn separate national histories into a single world history.
The reading of Marx and Engels on nature, labour and capitalism that the authors use as the standard for judging Western ecologism.
The official body of principles on the nature and role of news work, centred on the Party-led press. It is taught as a core subject in Chinese journalism schools.
The Marxist-Leninist framework that treats religion as an ideological form tied to class society and promotes atheism. It underpins official religious policy in China.
Parties that take Marxism-Leninism as their guiding ideology and keep the Soviet communist tradition, such as the CPRF and the All-Union Communist Party of Bolsheviks.
A Western philological and historical approach to Marx's texts, often presented as free of ideology. The article criticises it for hiding its own ideological standpoint.

A research tradition devoted to Marx's life, texts, editions and intellectual development, and to the differences among Marxist schools. Wang describes it as interdisciplinary, non-ideological and purely scholarly.
A line of interpretation, common in Western scholarship, that separates Marx's own thought from Engels's later 'Marxism' and holds that the two men's worldviews diverged seriously.
A slogan from the 2014–15 period, promoted by Premier Li Keqiang, encouraging start-ups and innovation among the general public.
The Party's working method of gathering ideas from the masses, refining them and returning them as policy. It is described as the Party's fundamental working line.

zh: 从群众中来，到群众中去
py: cóng qúnzhòng zhōng lái, dào qúnzhòng zhōng qù
lit: from the masses, to the masses
ex: Mao Zedong's leadership method of gathering the views of the masses, concentrating them into policy, and returning to the masses to implement and test it. The article cites Mao's wording on correct leadership.

zh: 从群众中来、到群众中去
py: cóng qúnzhòng zhōng lái, dào qúnzhòng zhōng qù
lit: from the masses, to the masses
ex: The Party's basic working method, formulated by Mao Zedong. Leaders gather the views of ordinary people, refine them into policy and then take that policy back to the people to be tested in practice.

zh: 党的群众路线教育实践活动
py: dǎng de qúnzhòng lùxiàn jiàoyù shíjiàn huódòng
lit: Party's mass line education and practice activity
ex: A Party-wide rectification campaign of 2013–2014 aimed at combating formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance among officials.
Work with Party-led mass organizations such as the Youth League, trade unions and women's federations, which link the Party to specific social groups.
The SACP's post-1990 self-definition: a party with a broad popular base that remains the political vanguard of the working class.

lit: view of history of the masses
ex: The Marxist-Leninist claim that the people are the creators of history and decide its course. Chinese authors use it as part of historical materialism.
The Party doctrine that the masses are the makers of history and that Party work must rely on and serve them; it is closely tied to the "mass line".
The everyday work of Party members and cadres in communicating with, serving and mobilising ordinary people, including mediating disputes and responding to concerns.
A term used in 1920s Party documents for turning the Party from a small body of intellectuals into one with a broad base among workers and peasants.
A metaphor used by Xi Jinping for the three outlooks, which are said to govern a person's other choices and judgments.

The "two civilizations" paired in official discourse since Deng's era: economic and material progress on one side, and cultural, ideological and moral progress on the other. Their coordinated development is a recurring policy aim.

zh: 物质文明和精神文明相协调
py: wùzhì wénmíng hé jīngshén wénmíng xiāngxiétiáo
lit: material civilization and spiritual civilization coordinated
ex: A long-standing official pairing, in which economic prosperity and cultural-ethical development are meant to advance together.

A paired concept in Party discourse: material civilization covers economic and material progress, spiritual civilization covers ideology, ethics, education and culture. The Party has stressed developing both together since the 1980s.

A phrase from Marx's account of historical materialism for the relations people enter into in producing their material means of life. The article treats it as the constant basis of history and the source of social progress.

zh: 物质文明、政治文明、精神文明、社会文明、生态文明
en: material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization
q: material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization
py: wùzhì wénmíng, zhèngzhì wénmíng, jīngshén wénmíng, shèhuì wénmíng, shēngtài wénmíng
ex: The five-sphere framework of civilization used in official Chinese discourse, which grew from earlier material/spiritual and later political, social and ecological additions. Sun uses it to structure both the critique and the alternative.
A late concept of Louis Althusser, who read history as an open process shaped by contingent meetings of elements rather than a predetermined course.
The Chinese term for historical materialism, Marx's theory that material production and its social relations shape the course of history. It is also commonly shortened to 唯物史观.

The Marxist philosophical method that treats nature, society and thought as developing through contradiction and the unity of opposites. It is a core component of the dialectical materialism taught in Chinese Marxist philosophy.

lit: the big things of the country
ex: A phrase used by Xi Jinping asking officials to keep the Party and state's most important interests and priorities in view in their work.
The wave of student and worker protests and strikes in France in May 1968. It strongly shaped Badiou's turn to Maoism and event philosophy.
The large Japanese offensive against the Central Hebei base area from 1 May to 20 June 1942, which the article describes as severely damaging the base.

Slogans issued by the Party Central Committee in April 1948 that called for a democratic coalition government. Non-Communist figures responded positively, and official histories treat the exchange as a milestone for the system.
The 1919 student and intellectual movement for national renewal. Party historiography treats it as the point at which Marxism entered China and new culture became proletarian-led.
The official summary of the legacy of the 1919 May Fourth Movement, defined as patriotism, progress, democracy and science.

The 1925 anti-imperialist movement of strikes and protests that began in Shanghai after British-led police shot demonstrators on 30 May. The article presents it as a turning point for Party expansion.
The anti-communist political campaign of the early 1950s in the United States, named after Senator Joseph McCarthy. The article treats it as the ideological basis of the traditional school.
A Confucian ideal of moderation and balance, avoiding extremes. The authors treat it as a practical method for handling opposing forces, summed up in 'grasping the two ends and using the mean'.
A Hegelian-Marxist category for the unity of quality and quantity. It marks the range within which a thing keeps its quality, and quantitative change beyond it brings qualitative change.

zh: 互联网宗教信息服务管理办法
en: Measures for the Administration of Internet Religious Information Services
q: Measures for the Administration of Internet Religious Information Services
py: hùliánwǎng zōngjiào xìnxī fúwù guǎnlǐ bànfǎ
ex: A departmental rule issued jointly by several agencies in 2021. It sets licensing requirements and content boundaries for online religious information.

The author's own category, which applies social-mechanism analysis to the Marxist thesis that the people make history. It names the internal structure and modes of operation of the people's historical activity.

zh: 生态产品价值实现机制
en: mechanisms to realise the value of ecological products
q: mechanisms to realise the value of ecological products
ex: Policies that turn ecological resources, such as clean air, water and forests, into measurable and tradable economic value through surveys, property rights, accounting and compensation.
Official policy of integrating traditional and new media and technologies, promoted under Xi Jinping to build new mainstream media and expand the reach of the Party's messaging.

The manner in which Party meetings are conducted, including preparation, speech, discussion and decision-making. In Party discourse it is treated as part of the broader 'work style' (zuofeng) of cadres.
The second Marx-Engels Gesamtausgabe, the historical-critical complete edition of Marx and Engels. Its Part II, completed in 2012, publishes Capital and its preparatory materials.

zh: 马克思恩格斯全集历史考证版
lit: Historical-critical edition of the Complete Works of Marx and Engels
ex: The second Marx-Engels-Gesamtausgabe, a historical-critical edition begun in 1975. The article calls its Capital section, completed in 2012, the most authoritative and complete edition.
The second Marx-Engels-Gesamtausgabe, the historical-critical complete edition of the writings of Marx and Engels, used as the textual basis for newer translations.
Labour carried out chiefly by the brain; the author treats it as the process of 'conceptual construction' inherent in all human labour.
Marx's term for the production of ideas, consciousness and cultural products such as law, religion, philosophy, science and art. Chinese scholarship often renders it as 'spiritual production'.
Zhang Shenfu's 1930s idea of uniting Confucius, Russell and Lenin, meaning Chinese philosophy, Western analytic philosophy and Marxism, into one new philosophy.

lit: politics of the virtuous and capable
ex: A term for a system in which officials rise by ability and experience through a professional civil service. It is often traced to Confucian tradition.
A label for readings that combine Marxism with Jewish-Christian messianic and eschatological themes, associated here with Benjamin, Derrida and others. The article uses it as an object of critique.
The branch of ethics that examines the nature, presuppositions and justification of moral claims, as distinct from prescribing particular norms.
A concept from governance studies meaning the governance of governance, here used for the Party's role in coordinating other actors.
Reflection on a theory's own concepts, objects and assumptions. In this review it means scholars examining the methodology of the discipline itself.

A concept drawn from Marx's remarks on soil fertility and capitalist agriculture, developed by Foster and Burkett. It describes the breakdown of the exchange of matter between society and nature under capitalist production.
Marx's idea, developed by Foster, of a rupture in the metabolic exchange between human society and nature under capitalist production.
Marx's idea, developed by Foster, that capitalist production breaks the natural cycle of nutrients and matter between society and nature. Foster uses it as the basis of ecological Marxism.
John Bellamy Foster's concept, derived from Marx, of a breakdown in the metabolic exchange between human society and nature under capitalism.
The standard Chinese rendering of Marx's term Stoffwechsel, the exchange of matter between humans and nature that labour mediates.
Aron's term for the analysis of science itself, including whether a single model of science exists. He argued that the rival readings of Marx depend on the metascience each interpreter holds.

In Marx's Afterword to the second edition of Capital, the stage of mastering material, analysing its forms and tracing their inner connections. The article ties it to the path from the sensuous concrete to abstract determinations.

Marx's term (Darstellungsweise) from the Afterword to Capital Volume I, for the way research findings are set out, as distinct from the method of research. The authors treat it as a method for building narrative systems.

The view that all social phenomena can in principle be explained by the properties, goals, beliefs and actions of individuals. The article presents it as the narrow methodological stance that APE rejects as an exclusive requirement.
Official term for petty corruption at the grassroots, such as that of low-level officials who affect ordinary people directly.
The authors' term for light, everyday superstitious behaviours that give psychological comfort without amounting to full devotion. Examples include praying for exam luck or online fortune-telling.

In the article's Marxist usage, the petty bourgeoisie: owners with some means of production who work mainly by their own or family labour. It is distinguished from the broad 'middle class' (中产阶级) of Western sociology.
In Mao's analysis, groups such as the middle bourgeoisie, enlightened gentry and regional power-holders, standing between the Communists and the diehards and open to being won over.
A term from development economics for countries whose growth stalls after reaching middle-income levels. The article applies it to Brazil.

A term from Western social science for theories that sit between grand theory and empirical description. The author treats it as producing fragmented theory that handles historical complexity crudely.
A label applied to the openly materialist, anti-clerical atheism of the French Enlightenment, which attacked theology and the church directly.
A phrase from Lenin's 1922 article "On the Significance of Militant Materialism", which called for a materialist and atheist struggle against idealist worldviews.
A compulsory course on military theory and training for Chinese university students, the main vehicle of national defence education in higher education.

The basic political method of the North Korean party from 2010, which gave priority to the military. The Eighth Congress in 2021 replaced it with people-masses-first politics, according to the article.
Joint bodies of army and local Party and government leaders set up in many CPC base areas from 1938, often chaired by the commanding officer, until replaced by Party committees.
Marx's 1844 excerpts from and comments on James Mill's work, part of the Paris Notes. They contain his discussion of money and alienated exchange.

Term for socialist participation in a bourgeois government, named after Alexandre Millerand, who joined a French cabinet in 1899. It set off a major dispute in the Second International between Marxists and revisionists.

lit: the people are the foundation of the state
ex: A classical Chinese political idea, from the Book of Documents, that the people are the root of the state. The Party cites it as a traditional source for its people-centred stance.
A traditional Chinese political idea, 'the people are the root of the state', which the article says must be creatively transformed under Marxism.
Yang's term for Lukács's reading of Marx, which he says puts Marx's concepts and texts in the wrong logical and textual place.
The historical task the Party sets itself, here defined by the author as reaching socialism and then communism.

A concept in Chinese political science describing the CPC as a party driven by a historical mission, such as national rejuvenation, rather than by vote-maximising. The article notes it resembles Nanni's "missionary party" category.

zh: 国有企业混合所有制改革
ex: A reform policy that brings non-state capital into state-owned enterprises while keeping them under state control or influence.
A term in Chinese economic policy for enterprises or arrangements combining public and private capital. Chen mentions it only in the conclusion.

An economic arrangement in which state, collective and private capital hold cross-shares in the same enterprises. The Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) described it as an important way of realising the basic economic system.
Policy of bringing private and other non-state capital into state-owned enterprises, and state capital into private firms, so that different ownership forms share one enterprise.
A concept the author proposes to describe the form and path by which integration takes place. It is modelled on the Marxist category of the mode of production.
In Marxist theory, the unity of productive forces and relations of production that shapes the material basis of a society.
Cases selected, edited and published by the Supreme People's Court or Procuratorate to illustrate how the law and policy goals, here the core socialist values, should be applied.

Cuba's official term for its economic and social reform process, launched under Raúl Castro and formalised at the 6th Party Congress (2011). It aims to adjust the socialist model while keeping its basic principles.
The ideal of dedication, striving for excellence and selfless contribution, associated with the national model workers honoured by the state since 1950.

zh: 劳模精神、劳动精神、工匠精神
py: láomó jīngshén, láodòng jīngshén, gōngjiàng jīngshén
lit: model-worker spirit, labour spirit, craftsman spirit
ex: A trio of values promoted officially to encourage diligence, honest labour and pursuit of skill, modelled on national model workers.
A drafting approach, used for the Code, that extracts common rules into a general part while leaving room for separate laws and for later adaptation.
A long-standing Party goal of broad, modest prosperity. Officials declared it built in all respects in 2021.
The goal of a moderately prosperous society in all respects, declared achieved by the Party in 2021. The word xiaokang also appears in classical Chinese texts.
A development goal set by the Party around the turn of the century, aiming at a comparatively comfortable standard of living for all.

en: a moderately prosperous society in all respects
q: moderately prosperous society in all respects
ex: A Party development goal, announced at the 16th Party Congress in 2002 and declared achieved in 2021. It is the first of the "Two Centenary Goals".

en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
q: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
lit: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
ex: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 as part of a new cultural mission. Official discourse presents it as a civilization that combines socialism, Chinese tradition and modernity.

A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 19th Party Congress (2017), describing an integrated economy of industrial, market, distribution, green and open sub-systems. The article reads it as comprising six systems and one mechanism.

zh: 中国特色现代企业制度
en: modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics
q: modern enterprise system with Chinese characteristics
ex: The modern corporate system as adapted to China's basic economic system. It combines Party leadership of state-owned enterprises with corporate governance structures.

An official goal of an industrial structure that is technologically advanced, integrated and anchored in the real economy, and that includes manufacturing, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
Another label for Marx's philosophy, used here for a materialism that works within the relations of subject and object, spirit and matter, idea and reality.

A concept from the Central Urban Work Conference of July 2025, building on Xi Jinping's phrase that cities are built by the people and for the people. It sets out six dimensions of urban development, with innovation listed first.
The goal set at the 19th Party Congress (2017) of making China a prosperous, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist country by the middle of the 21st century.

The mode of production, life and thought that took shape with capitalist modernization since the European Renaissance. The authors use it to ask what kind of modern order China's modernization builds.
A term used in Chinese Marxist scholarship for modernity as shaped by the logic of capital, which Marx's critique is read as targeting.
Here it refers to the Soviet-era drive for industrialisation and state-planned development, which the article says Russian historians now treat as a path of modernization.

zh: 人与自然和谐共生的现代化
en: modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony
q: modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony
py: rén yǔ zìrán héxié gòngshēng de xiàndàihuà
ex: One of the stated features of Chinese modernization, which stresses ecological protection alongside economic development.
A policy goal of upgrading industrial chains to be more advanced, secure and controllable, widely used in official economic discourse.
An official goal of improving China's system and capacity for governance, usually linked to the Party's reform agenda.

zh: 人与自然和谐共生现代化
en: modernization of harmony between humanity and nature
q: modernization of harmony between humanity and nature
py: rén yǔ zìrán héxié gòngshēng xiàndàihuà
ex: A formulation, presented in official discourse as one of the defining features of Chinese modernization, that stresses ecological civilization and development in harmony with nature.
A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to modernizing the country's system and capacity for governance.
A policy goal of upgrading how villages are administered, as part of modernizing the national governance system and capacity. It is linked to the rural revitalization strategy.
The idea in Chinese official and academic discourse that modernization is essentially about transforming people's qualities, capacities and ways of living, not only the economy.

zh: 国家安全体系和能力现代化
en: modernization of the national security system and capabilities
q: modernization of the national security system and capabilities
py: guójiā ānquán tǐxì hé nénglì xiàndàihuà
ex: A policy goal in Party documents of upgrading China's security institutions and capacities to meet new risks.

en: modernization of the system and capacity of state governance
q: modernization of the system and capacity of state governance
lit: modernisation of the state governance system
ex: A goal set out in the Party's 2013 Third Plenum decision, referring to improving institutions and the ability to govern.

An approach that organises modern Chinese history around the pursuit of modernization, often identified with Western models. The authors present it as a rival to the revolutionary-history framework based on historical materialism.
Post-1945 Western social-science theory holding that societies develop along a path similar to that of the earlier industrialised West; world-systems theory was formed in opposition to it.

zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
en: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance
q: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance
py: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
lit: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
ex: A goal set by the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), alongside improving socialist institutions with Chinese characteristics. It is treated as the overall objective of 'comprehensively deepening reform'.
Marx's concept of how money conceals social relations of labour and makes them appear as natural properties of things.

lit: politics of the golden master / financial backers
ex: A Chinese critical label for a political system in which wealthy donors hold decisive influence over candidates and policy. The article applies it to the United States.
The Nationalist Government's central body for Mongolian and Tibetan affairs, which drafted policy for the region.

en: monistic view of living labour as the source of value
q: monistic view of living labour as the source of value
ex: The position that living labour alone creates value and surplus value, so that machines, knowledge or data cannot do so independently. The article defends it against pluralist theories of value.

The stage of capitalism dominated by a few large firms, analysed by Paul Baran and Paul Sweezy in Monopoly Capital (1966). The authors build on this theory to argue that stagnation is its normal state.
The stage of capitalism analysed by Lenin, in which monopolies and finance capital dominate. The author sees financialization as its latest development.

lit: monotheism (as doctrine or mode of thought)
ex: In the review, a term for an exclusive and dogmatic habit of thought derived from monotheistic religion (yishenjiao). It is said to survive in secular political and cultural forms.
Massive open online courses. The Chinese term is a phonetic and semantic rendering of the English abbreviation.
Education in morals, values and ideology in Chinese schools. It is often tied to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (立德树人).
The author's term for Rousseau's project of grounding the political order in moral principles, above all the general will, against the modern separation of morality and politics.

en: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education
q: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education
py: dé zhì tǐ měi láo wǔ yù bìngjǔ
lit: five educations pursued together: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic, labour
ex: An education policy line stated by Xi Jinping at the 2018 National Education Conference. It adds labour education to the four earlier components of Chinese schooling.
A term for factionalism rooted in the separate revolutionary base areas, where groups put local or group loyalties above Party unity.
Bolivia's ruling left-wing party (MAS-IPSP), led by Evo Morales and rooted in coca growers' and peasant unions. It governed from 2006 to 2019 and returned to office in 2020.
The Material Product System, the national accounting method used in the Soviet bloc and in China before reform. It counted only material production sectors in output.
The staged explosion on the South Manchuria Railway near Mukden (Shenyang) on 18 September 1931, used by the Japanese Kwantung Army as a pretext to occupy north-east China.
The authors' proposed ownership model, in which collective force is publicly owned at levels from workshop to world, alongside private ownership of individual contributions.

The official description of relations between the Communist Party and the eight non-communist "democratic parties" in China. The Communist Party leads, and the other parties take part in consultation and government.

zh: 多党合作和政治协商制度
py: duōdǎng hézuò hé zhèngzhì xiéshāng zhìdù
ex: The formal name of the basic political institution under which the CPC rules and the democratic parties take part in consultation and advisory roles. It is written into the Constitution.
In Chinese official usage, the principle that international affairs should be decided by all countries through consultation rather than by one or a few powers.

zh: 中国共产党领导的多党合作和政治协商制度
py: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng lǐngdǎo de duōdǎng hézuò hé zhèngzhì xiéshāng zhìdù
lit: multiparty cooperation and political consultation system led by the Communist Party of China
ex: A basic political institution of China in which the eight non-communist 'democratic parties' and non-party figures take part in consultation under Communist Party leadership.
The idea that world power should be spread among several centres rather than dominated by one state. Official texts qualify it as 'equal and orderly'.
A concept in Negri, Hardt and Virno for a plural, self-organising collective subject of post-Fordist, immaterial labour, in contrast to a unified 'people' or class.
Hardt and Negri's term for the new form of the proletariat under immaterial labour. The authors criticise its use as a replacement for the proletariat.
Mao's colloquial term for wearing a strong enemy down through patience and manoeuvre before destroying it.
Yang's term for two-way explanation, in which each tradition is read in the other's terms and gains new self-understanding.
A phrase in official Chinese diplomacy and theory, associated with Xi Jinping's Global Civilization Initiative. It stresses exchange and learning between civilizations rather than clash or hierarchy.
Yang's term for using Chinese and Western ideas as reference points for each other in dialogue, so that each is illuminated by difference.
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for patient, repeated and thorough implementation of policy, likening it to hammering a nail until it holds. It is often invoked in campaigns against formalism.
The label for pre-scientific-revolution atheist thought. In this account it criticised particular beliefs in ghosts and gods but could not deny their existence at root.

A Party-defined set of values drawn from the 359th Brigade's land reclamation at Nanniwan near Yan'an in the early 1940s. It stresses self-reliance and hard work and is part of the Yan'an spirit tradition.
Russian populist revolutionaries of the 19th century who saw the peasant commune as the basis of a socialist path that would avoid capitalism.
The authors' term, glossed with the English word Narrative, for the function by which relics tell stories and convey values in political education.
The language, concepts and modes of expression through which a theory or national story is told. In current Chinese usage it is linked to the effort to build China's own 'discourse power' abroad.
In Mao's class analysis, the Chinese capitalists not tied to imperialism or the state. He saw them as having both revolutionary and compromising tendencies.
The psychological traits shared by members of a nation or state, also called national disposition (国民性). The authors treat it as shaped by historical and material conditions.

A Party meeting of delegates convened between congresses when necessary to decide major issues promptly. It is provided for in the Party Constitution and is smaller in standing than the national congress.
A periodic high-level Party meeting setting policy on religious affairs. The 2021 meeting called for strengthening Marxist religious studies.

The Party's highest organ under its constitution, which is convened periodically to set the line, amend the constitution and elect the Central Committee. The article treats the rules governing it as a basic Party institution.
The Party's supreme body, held every five years, which elects the Central Committee and approves the political report.

A state-led initiative begun around 2017 to protect and showcase major cultural heritage routes, including the Great Wall, the Grand Canal, the Yellow River and the Long March. The parks combine heritage protection, education, tourism and research.
The attractiveness and influence of a country's culture and values, an idea adapted from Joseph Nye's concept and a stated policy goal in China.
A Chinese state body established in October 2023 to coordinate data infrastructure, data property rights, circulation and digital planning.
The official programme of modernizing the armed forces, which the article describes as comprising four elements: military theory, organisational forms, military personnel and weaponry.
The knowledge, attitudes and skills regarding national defence that official education policy aims to cultivate in citizens.

A Marxist-Leninist concept for a revolution in a dependent or colonial country that combines national liberation from imperialism with democratic transformation of domestic political and social structures, often seen as a step toward socialism.

zh: 国家发展和改革委员会
ex: A State Council body responsible for macroeconomic planning, major projects and coordinating development policy.
The central medium- and long-term plan, in practice the Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development, which sets strategic goals for the country and guides lower-level plans.

Provincial-level pilot areas (starting with Fujian in 2016, later Jiangxi, Guizhou and Hainan) where the central government tests institutional reforms in environmental governance before wider rollout.
The Chinese rendering of the early Marx's term for political economy (Nationalökonomie). Yan uses it for classical political economy from Smith onward.
A major national meeting on education policy, held in September 2024. Xi Jinping gave a keynote speech there.
In this usage, the history of the People's Republic of China since 1949, treated as a discipline that grew out of Party history research.
A early twentieth-century label for China's traditional scholarship as a whole. The article says it was better known than 'classical studies' in the 1920s.
Chinese-language opera drawing on folk music and traditional theatre, usually dated from The White-Haired Girl (1945).
China's national legislature and, constitutionally, its highest organ of state power. Its deputies and Standing Committee have supervisory functions over the government, courts and procuratorates.
The idea of restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'. Today it appears as 'the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation' in Party discourse.
A central theme of Party discourse, presenting modern Chinese history since the Opium War as a path from decline to renewal of the Chinese nation.
The 1920s movement, led by the Kuomintang with Communist participation, against imperialism and warlord rule.

en: National Social Science Fund of China
q: National Social Science Fund of China
ex: The main state funding body for humanities and social science research in China. It supports projects including special programmes on the War of Resistance against Japan.

en: national strategic science and technology forces
q: national strategic science and technology forces
ex: A term for the core state-backed research bodies, such as national laboratories, national research institutes, leading research universities and leading technology firms.
A popular revival of interest in traditional Chinese learning and culture from the 2000s, seen in television lectures, Confucius Institutes and private academies.

The state anti-corruption and supervision body created in 2018 under the national supervision reform. It supervises all public officials and works closely with the Party's discipline inspection organs.

A planned integrated system of natural rivers and lakes, water-diversion channels, storage works and smart controls. It is meant to allocate water, control floods and protect water ecosystems across basins.

A national policy to promote mass participation in sport and exercise. It was raised to a national strategy after the 18th Party Congress, and it is governed by the National Fitness Regulations and successive five-year National Fitness Plans.
An approach that values natural resources as productive inputs and holds that environmental protection and profit can be compatible. Cai treats it as an application of the utility theory of value.

Marx's phrase in the preface to Capital for the development of the economic formation of society as a process governed by laws independent of human will. The article uses it as the second logic of his theory of progress.
A label Chinese scholars give to Engels's warning, in Dialectics of Nature, that every human victory over nature brings unforeseen adverse consequences.

The label the article gives to Western ecological currents such as environmental ethics, wilderness philosophy and deep ecology. It treats nature as having intrinsic value and rights, in opposition to anthropocentrism.
Labour required to sustain life and production, performed under external purposes and the division of labour. The article treats it as the basis on which free time is created.

en: the need for a better life
ex: The term used in the Party's post-2017 formulation of the principal social contradiction. Scholars use it to reframe the aims of ideological and political education.
The question, associated with Joseph Needham, of why modern science did not originate in China despite its earlier technological advances.
The question, posed by the British scholar Joseph Needham, of why modern science and industrial capitalism arose in Europe rather than in China despite China's earlier technological achievements.
In this Marxist usage, needs are the underlying drives behind people's thoughts and actions. The authors place the principal contradiction at this level, not at the level of ideas.
A Hegelian dialectical law that Marx and Engels use for historical development. For example, capitalist private property negates small-scale individual property and is in turn negated.
Here the Hegelian method in which each category is negated and passes into a more concrete one. Sun says Marx followed this method in his critique of Hegel while inverting its idealist basis.
A list of sectors closed or restricted to foreign investment; everything not listed is in principle open.
A list of sectors closed or restricted to investors; anything not listed is open to them ("what is not prohibited is permitted").

Negative figures, incidents, failures and lessons used for education by showing what not to do. In Party usage it includes 'negative teachers' (fanmian jiaoyuan), people whose errors serve as a warning.
Indirect control of formally independent states through economic, political and ideological means. Chinese Marxist writing, drawing on 1960s Party polemics, uses it mainly to describe US policy.
The Song-Ming revival of Confucian thought centred on "principle" (li), human nature and cosmology. Shao Yong is counted among its early figures.

Dean's name for a possible successor to capitalism, in which accumulation runs through rent, debt and political power rather than profit from production. It is marked by fragmented sovereignty, steep hierarchy and territorial exclusion.
A broad label for non-orthodox Marxist currents. The authors use it for the Frankfurt School and for post-1970s schools such as analytical, post-modern and post-Marxism.
The authors' term for the shift since the 1970s toward deregulation, tax cuts for the rich, attacks on unions and a closer fusion of state and capital.
The market-oriented policy regime of deregulation, tax cuts and weakened unions since the 1980s. The authors treat it as capital's response to falling profit rates.

A label for the militant, publicly outspoken atheism associated with Harris, Dawkins, Dennett and Hitchens from the mid-2000s. Chinese scholarship on atheism treats it as a contemporary Western trend.
A label used in Chinese and foreign commentary for deepening US–China rivalry. Zhang rejects it as analytically misleading.
The label the PCF applies to its twenty-first-century theoretical orientation. The article describes it as broad but lacking a core idea.

py: xīn shídài xīn de wénhuà shǐmìng
lit: new cultural mission of the new era
ex: Xi Jinping's 2023 formulation: to promote cultural prosperity, build a culturally strong country and build a modern Chinese civilization.
Xi Jinping's formulation of 2023: advancing cultural prosperity, building a strong socialist culture and building a modern Chinese civilisation.
A phrase Xi Jinping used in 2023 for the product of the Second Integration, described as an organically unified whole of Marxism and traditional culture.
An intellectual movement from about 1915 that criticised Confucian tradition and promoted science and democracy. Its main journal was Chen Duxiu's New Youth.
Mao Zedong's theory, set out around 1940, of a stage of anti-imperialist, anti-feudal revolution led by the proletariat, preceding the transition to socialism.
Mao Zedong's theory, developed around 1939–40, of a transitional stage of Chinese revolution led by the proletariat before the move to socialism.
Mao Zedong's theory of a revolution led by the proletariat through a broad class alliance. It was adopted as the Party's strategy in place of the Soviet-period model.

The state form Mao outlined in On New Democracy (1940): a joint dictatorship of all anti-imperialist, anti-feudal classes under proletarian leadership, with democratic centralism as its political system.
Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution from 1919 to 1949, led by the proletariat and aimed at overthrowing imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism as a step toward socialism.

The set of political, economic and cultural institutions Mao Zedong designed for the stage between the Chinese revolution's democratic phase and socialism. It rested on a joint dictatorship of revolutionary classes under Communist leadership, and was in place from about 1949 until the mid-1950s.
A strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other ('dual circulation').
A framework put forward in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

The Party's designation, since 2021, for the period after the completion of a moderately prosperous society, running to the middle of the 21st century. It is defined as a stage within the primary stage of socialism.
A current in Western Marxism, represented in the article by Ian Hunt, that defends and reconstructs Marx's dialectic against its dismissal by analytical Marxism.
An Anglophone and German current (including Christopher Arthur) that reads Capital as a systematic dialectic of categories, in which the exposition proceeds logically rather than historically.

lit: two kinds of enterprise and three new
ex: Shorthand for private and foreign-invested enterprises plus new economic organizations, new social organizations and new employment groups, where Party organizations are being extended.
Official shorthand for new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups. Party-building and ideological work is considered weak in these areas.

zh: 新经济组织、新社会组织、新就业群体
en: new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups
q: new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups
py: xīn jīngjì zǔzhī、xīn shèhuì zǔzhī、xīn jiùyè qúntǐ
lit: new economic organisations, new social organisations, new employment groups
ex: Official shorthand ("two news" plus new workers) for private and platform firms, newer non-state organisations, and flexible workers such as couriers and drivers. The Party has made building organisations among them a priority.
Non-public-sector economic entities such as private and foreign-invested enterprises and self-employed businesses.

The policy Lenin introduced in Soviet Russia in 1921, replacing grain requisitioning with a tax in kind and allowing limited market activity. Chinese official discourse often cites it as a precedent for reform.

An official term for workers in new platform-based and flexible forms of employment, such as couriers, delivery riders and ride-hailing drivers. It has appeared in recent Party documents and speeches.
A mid-1930s intellectual movement led by Communist-aligned intellectuals, which continued the May Fourth spirit of 'science and democracy' and opposed cultural revivalism.
The term used since the 19th Party Congress (2017) for the current period of Chinese development under Xi Jinping's leadership.

zh: 中国特色社会主义新时代
lit: new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The official name for the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), marked by Xi Jinping's leadership and presented as a new historical stage.

zh: 中国特色社会主义进入新时代
py: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì jìnrù xīn shídài
ex: The Party's description, since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and especially the 19th (2017), of the present stage of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Grassroots centres, set up across urban and rural areas, that organise volunteer services, education and cultural activities promoting official values.

zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义思想
en: new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics
py: xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
ex: The 19th Party Congress (2017) declared socialism with Chinese characteristics to have entered a new era. The article uses it to mark a new stage and a changed principal contradiction.

en: a new form of human civilization
ex: A phrase used in official discourse, notably since 2021, for the civilizational form that Chinese modernization is said to create, distinct from capitalist modernization.

Official term for work organised through internet platforms, such as delivery, ride-hailing and livestream marketing. It is characterised by flexible labour relations and often unclear employment status.
Communist-led army formed in 1937 in south-central China, also under the united front.

zh: 党的建设新的伟大工程
en: new great project of Party building
q: new great project of Party building
py: dǎng de jiànshè xīn de wěidà gōngchéng
ex: A formulation, in use since the 19th Party Congress (2017), for strengthening the Party's organisation, ideology and conduct in the new era.
A policy term for emerging sources of economic growth based on innovation, such as new industries, business forms and models, replacing older investment- and factor-driven sources.
In the article, the post-Cold War stage of monopoly capitalism, marked by non-military control through transnational corporations, finance capital and technology rather than colonial conquest.

The author's term for the wave of technological change since about 2008, covering re-industrialization with new energy, biotechnology and health, intelligent manufacturing, and the digital 'smart society'.
An official term for industrial development built on digital, networked and intelligent technologies and innovation. The 20th Party Congress set the aim of basically achieving it by 2035.

lit: new road of sitting an exam
ex: A metaphor from Mao Zedong in 1949, revived by Xi Jinping, presenting governing as an ongoing exam taken before the people.
A term for the post-1950s currents of the left that departed from traditional communist and social-democratic parties, often rooted in students and new social movements.
The post-1956 British left movement and intellectual milieu, including figures around New Left Review, which broke with Stalinism and Soviet-style orthodoxy.

A non-Communist left movement that emerged in Britain after 1956, following the Hungarian events and Khrushchev's secret speech. Its journals included The New Reasoner and Universities and Left Review.
British left-wing journal founded in 1960 and edited for many years by Perry Anderson. The article treats it as a key forum and barometer of Western left theory.
An Education Ministry initiative to reform humanities and social science education through interdisciplinary programmes and integration with technology.
A metaphor used by Party leaders, notably since 1978, to describe the current task of national development as a continuation of the Long March.
The idea of a person with socialist consciousness who rejects private-ownership attitudes. It is associated with Cuban revolutionary thought, including Che Guevara and Castro.

A term for popular creative forms in the internet age, such as amateur writing, short video, micro-dramas and stand-up comedy. It was written into the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, as the article notes.
A name Marx used for his own philosophical position, distinguishing it from earlier idealism and from older, contemplative materialism. Chinese scholarship often pairs it with "modern materialism".
Xi Jinping's 2014 term for China's economy shifting from high-speed to medium-high-speed growth and to structural upgrading.
A study society founded by Mao Zedong and others in Changsha in April 1918. Several members later became prominent in the communist movement.
In Marxist terms, the social relations (ownership, labour, distribution) that the authors say must be rebuilt to fit digital productive forces.

A label the article attributes to Western left thinkers for a revised revolutionary subject, defined by radicalism, political exclusion and shared values rather than by ownership of the means of production.

A school of Western-based scholarship that stresses the Manchu and Inner Asian character of the Qing empire. Chinese official commentary often criticises it for questioning the continuity between the Qing and China.
A phrase modelled on "new quality productive forces". Here it refers to the enhanced operational capacity of the state security organs.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.

A West German current from the 1960s (Backhaus, Reichelt) that reads Marx's critique of political economy as a theory of value and social form. It stresses the value-form and exchange over a production-centred reading.
A neutral scholarly label in the sociology of religion for recently emerged religious groups, used as an alternative to the term "cult".
Miliband's 1985 label for Hobsbawm, Laclau and Mouffe, and Hall. He accused them of rejecting class politics and relying on new social movements instead of the working class.
A recent trend in studies of modern Chinese history that revises the older revolutionary-history approach. Chen cites it as a model for a revised history of Marxist historiography.

lit: new road of sitting an examination
ex: An image drawn from Mao Zedong's remark in 1949 that the Party was going to Beijing to "take the exam". It is now used to describe the Party's governing challenges, with the people as examiners.

A policy term for village-level collective economic organisations that own collective resources and assets and operate in the market, as distinct from the older, administratively run collective economy. It follows the reform of collective property rights.
An official formulation for a national security system that guarantees the new development pattern, linked to the holistic approach to national security.

A term from Western social theory for movements since the 1960s (peace, ecology, feminism, identity politics) that are organised around non-material values rather than class and the workplace. The article contrasts them with the traditional workers' movement.
A term used by Russian parties such as A Just Russia and by scholars for post-Soviet interpretations of socialism. The article treats it as a social trend.
A rural development programme announced in the mid-2000s, aiming to improve rural production, living conditions, governance and culture.

The author's label for organised belief in spirits or deities that arose after reform and opening up outside officially recognised religions, including qigong groups, "extraordinary powers" and Falun Gong.
Zhao Tingyang's proposal for a world order, adapting the ancient concept of tianxia. It is based on relational rationality and aims to minimise conflict rather than maximise interest.

A concept Xi Jinping first presented in a March 2013 speech in Moscow, centred on win-win cooperation. The 19th Party Congress formulated it as mutual respect, fairness and justice, and win-win cooperation.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2017. It calls for inter-party ties based on seeking common ground while shelving differences, mutual respect and mutual learning.

The official description of China's multi-party cooperation system under Communist Party leadership, in which the democratic parties participate in consultation and supervision rather than compete for power.
The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Chinese Communist Party leadership, involving the eight democratic parties.
A term for China's socialist state institutions, described as guaranteeing that the people are masters of the country and as distinct from both capitalist and traditional Soviet-style systems.

lit: new-type think tanks with Chinese characteristics
ex: A think-tank system promoted by the Party since 2013. It is led by designated national high-end think tanks and is meant to support policy advice and theoretical innovation.
Engels's term for the outlook he and Marx developed in the 1840s, namely historical materialism and scientific socialism.
The journal founded by Chen Duxiu in 1915 that became the main platform of the New Culture Movement. It later carried the first major introductions of Marxism in China.
A journal founded by Chen Duxiu in 1915 (first titled Youth Magazine) that became the main platform of the New Culture Movement and later of early Chinese communists.
Mao Zedong's 1940 concept of a national, scientific and mass culture suited to the stage of New Democracy, the Party's programme for the pre-socialist revolution.
The Party's official periodisation for 1919–1949, from the May Fourth Movement to the founding of the People's Republic. The Chronicle covers 1921–1949.
A nationwide programme, begun around 2018, that uses local centres, stations and volunteers to carry Party theory, moral education and public services to the grassroots.

lit: civilization outlook of the new era
ex: The body of ideas on civilization associated with Xi Jinping since the 2010s: civilizations are diverse, equal and learn from each other. Liang uses it as the guiding principle for reading world history.
A phrase in Party discourse for young people expected to be politically loyal, patriotic and capable of taking part in national rejuvenation.
A Yan'an-era formulation for regular, systematic education that remains tied to Chinese revolutionary conditions, as opposed to copying existing university models.

zh: 新型城市基础设施建设
ex: Urban infrastructure that fuses new-generation information technology with urban construction and governance, such as data platforms, sensing networks and building information models.

A Chinese policy strategy, prominent since the early 2010s, that stresses quality, integration with the countryside and the settlement of rural migrants as urban residents, rather than simple expansion of urban land and population.
A policy concept for mobilising state and market resources across the country towards major science and technology goals. It updates the earlier 'whole-nation system' of centrally organised effort.
A Party term for the management of news media and the guidance of public opinion. It treats journalism as part of the Party's wider propaganda and ideological work.
Modern Chinese rendering of Nihilism, built on the older Daoist word xuwu. In early twentieth-century China it also overlapped with anarchism and populism.
A Japanese-derived translation of Nihilist, applied in China to Russian revolutionaries, especially the assassins of the Narodnaya Volya. It was often equated with anarchists.

Nine principles drawn from Xi Jinping's 2018 speech, covering Party leadership over ideology, core socialist values, media influence, the online space and telling China's story. The article treats them as the basic guide for propaganda work.
Nine points of historical experience set out by Xi Jinping in his speech at the Party's centenary on 1 July 2021, which the ten upholds build on.
The nine pairs of relationships the 12th CPV Congress said must be handled in future renewal, including those between stability and development and between the state and the market.
Nine practical requirements for the Party's self-reform, each beginning with 以, from centralised leadership to combining self-supervision with public supervision.

en: no crime without explicit legal provision
q: no crime without explicit legal provision
lit: crimes and punishments fixed by law
ex: The criminal-law principle that conduct is a crime, and punishable, only if the law expressly says so (nullum crimen sine lege). It is set out in Article 3 of China's Criminal Law.

en: no forbidden zones in academic research
q: no forbidden zones in academic research
lit: academic research has no forbidden zones
ex: A slogan from the reform era that research topics should not be placed off limits. The authors invoke it to defend open scholarly debate in Party history.
The first policy document the Party Central Committee and State Council issue each year. Since 2004 it has been devoted to agriculture, rural areas and farmers.
The Laozi's ideal of governing without coercive, wilful interference, letting things follow their own nature. It is not simple inaction.
Measures such as criticism, talks, public notification, suspension or job adjustment. The article says they are not primarily punitive and sit alongside formal Party sanctions.

zh: 关于新形势下党内政治生活的若干准则
py: guānyú xīn xíngshì xià dǎngnèi zhèngzhì shēnghuó de ruògān zhǔnzé
lit: Several Norms on Intra-Party Political Life under the New Situation
ex: A Party document adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2016. It sets rules on supervision, discipline and leaders' conduct.

Communist-led guerrilla forces that fought Japanese occupation in Northeast China from the early 1930s to the early 1940s. Yang Jingyu and Zhao Yiman are among its best-known figures in Chinese official memory.
The military campaign launched from Guangdong in 1926 by the National Revolutionary Army to defeat northern warlords and unify China.

en: not believing in evil, not fearing ghosts, not fearing pressure
q: not believing in evil, not fearing ghosts, not fearing pressure
py: bù xìn xié, bù pà guǐ, bù pà yā
ex: A formula expressing the Party's fighting spirit. Mao Zedong used "not believing in evil" and "not fearing ghosts", and Xi Jinping added "not fearing pressure" in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

en: not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality
q: not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality
py: bù wéi shàng, bù wéi shū, zhǐ wéi shí
lit: not defer to superiors, not defer to books, defer only to reality
ex: The first nine characters of Chen Yun's "fifteen-character formula", formulated in Yan'an. It urges cadres to base decisions on actual conditions rather than on instructions or texts alone.

en: not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt
q: not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt
py: bù gǎn fǔ bù néng fǔ bù xiǎng fǔ
lit: dare not be corrupt, cannot be corrupt, do not want to be corrupt
ex: A formula used in Party anti-corruption discourse since the 18th Party Congress. It combines deterrence through punishment, institutional constraints and ideological cultivation.
A tradition of interpreting the Book of Changes through numerical and symbolic patterns. Shao's version is the one the article says could slide toward theism.
The article's term for conveying stories and values through material or intangible objects rather than words alone.
Feuerbach's term (Vergegenständlichung) for humans making their own essence into an object, here God. The article treats it as the positive side of religion.
Labour embodied in a product or in capital, as opposed to living labour in action. In this article it also serves as the central concept of Marx's critique of political economy.
A term from Marx's early philosophy (gegenständliche Tätigkeit) for sensuous, practical activity directed at real objects. The article contrasts it with capitalist objectified labour.
Marx's notion that beings exist and confirm their essence only through objects they act upon. Luo uses it to describe humans and nature as mutual objects.
A protest movement begun in New York in September 2011 against financial power and economic inequality. The author contrasts it with the Tea Party.

lit: the road of the October Revolution
ex: In Zhou's usage, the path of establishing socialism on the basic principles of scientific socialism, first taken in Russia in 1917. He presents it as universally valid.

en: an old country with a new mission
q: old country with a new mission
ex: A phrase from the Classic of Poetry. Chen used it to describe socialist China as the contemporary form of an ancient country.

Regions that served as bases of the Communist-led revolution before 1949, such as the Dabie Mountains. They receive special policy support, and their history is part of the Party's legitimating narrative.
An income pattern with a large middle-income group and small low- and high-income groups, presented as a policy goal.
Mao Zedong's 1937 essay on the universality and particularity of contradiction, central to his version of materialist dialectics.

Mao Zedong's January 1940 essay setting out the political, economic and cultural programme for the stage between the old order and socialism. It defines the "national, scientific and mass" culture that Wu treats as the guiding line.
Mao Zedong's 1937 essay on the relation of knowledge and practice, which the article treats as a core Chinese Marxist statement on epistemology.
Two philosophical essays by Mao Zedong (1937) on the theory of knowledge and dialectics, treated in Chinese Marxism as core texts of Mao Zedong Thought.
Mao Zedong's 1938 work, which set out three stages of the war (strategic defence, stalemate, counter-offensive). It is presented in Party history as the strategic guide to resistance.

Mao Zedong's report to the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee in October 1938. It addressed the anti-Japanese war and the united front, and the call for the "Sinification of Marxism" appears in it.
Staying for an extended period at a chosen village, factory or unit to study it in detail, usually while living with the local people.

en: one blueprint followed through to the end
q: one blueprint followed through to the end
lit: draw one blueprint to the end
ex: A slogan stressing continuity of strategy across successive leaderships and plan periods.
The authors' image for the three systems: the disciplinary system is the body, and the academic and discourse systems are the wings.

en: one central task, two basic points
q: one central task, two basic points
py: yí gè zhōngxīn, liǎng gè jīběndiǎn
ex: The Party's basic line: economic development as the central task, with adherence to the Four Cardinal Principles and to reform and opening up as the two basic points.

py: yí gè zhōngxīn, liǎng gè jīběndiǎn
ex: The Party's basic line for the primary stage of socialism, formalised at the 13th Party Congress (1987). The centre is economic development, and the two basic points are the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up.
A governance formula in which Party organisations form the leading core while governments, enterprises and social organisations take part.
The policy under which Hong Kong, Macao and, in intention, Taiwan keep their own systems within China. Some Japanese scholars cited in the article link it historically to the United Front.
A formula associated with Mao Zedong's account of dialectics, stressing division and struggle of opposites rather than their merging into a unity (合二为一). Badiou took it up as a core principle.
A formula in which Marxism holds the guiding position in ideology while other thought currents coexist beneath it.

lit: the whole country as one chessboard
ex: A Party slogan for coordinating all regions and departments under a unified national plan, subordinating local interests to the overall situation.

zh: 一引领五认同三爱四史教育
en: one guidance, five identifications, three loves and four histories
q: one guidance, five identifications, three loves and four histories
py: yī yǐnlǐng wǔ rèntóng sān ài sì shǐ jiàoyù
ex: A summary of Xi Jinping's 2021 directives on religious work. Religious circles are to be guided by socialist core values, identify with the country, nation, culture, Party and socialism, and study patriotism, collectivism and socialism along with the history of the Party, New China, reform and opening up, and socialism.
The general line for the transition period (1953–56): industrialisation, plus socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce.
The rule that every Party leader is responsible both for their own professional or administrative work and for Party conduct and discipline in their area.

A summary by Zhou Enlai of Mao's instructions on Taiwan: Taiwan must be unified with China, with specified autonomy arrangements afterwards. The article treats it as a forerunner of "one country, two systems".
The Centre's stated positioning: a general China studies repository plus academic research, decision-reference and cultural exchange centres.

en: one set of staff, two nameplates
q: one set of staff, two nameplates
lit: joint office work (一套人马、两块牌子)
ex: An arrangement in which two institutions share the same personnel and premises. Here it refers to the supervisory commission and the Party discipline inspection commission at the same level.
Wang's phrase for the view that Marxist philosophy, rooted in Marx and Engels, develops into many forms and schools in different national conditions.
The author's shorthand for the basic knowledge framework of a discipline: general principles, the world history of the field's theory, and its history in China.
The Soviet-era reading, traced to Lenin, which treats Marx's turn to materialism and communism as a single shift in the early 1840s.
The author's shorthand for three methods Mao used: writing, running newspapers and running schools. The label is the article's own, not a standard Party formula.
The political arrangement in which the Communist Party is the only legal party. Raúl Castro defended it in 2012 as a strategic safeguard of national unity and sovereignty.
A Chinese university initiative that brings services, Party-building and ideological work into student residential areas, so that these activities reach students where they live.
The capacity to shape agendas, narratives and public opinion online. The term is used to frame competition between states and actors in cyberspace.
The use of internet platforms and online space to shape students' values and character, as a complement to classroom teaching.

The application of Party-led ideological and political education, a core activity of Chinese universities, to the internet and digital platforms. It has developed since the mid-1990s as a sub-field of the ideological and political education discipline.
Ideological and political education carried out through internet platforms and social media, mainly aimed at university students.
