A security concept in Chinese Party discourse, referring to protecting the dominance of mainstream (Marxist, Party-led) ideology in cyberspace. Xi Jinping has linked it to state sovereignty and political power.
The term for Cuban efforts to counter what the authors describe as hostile ideological infiltration through social media, and to promote socialist values online.
An extension of the Party's traditional 'mass line' (going among the people and responding to their needs) to digital platforms. It is used to justify user-oriented services and online participation.
Views, attitudes and opinions that internet users form about specific events and about governing bodies. Monitoring and guiding it is a task of Chinese internet governance.

The article's term for the use of the internet by overseas religious organisations and individuals to spread religious content in China, which it presents as aimed at interfering in internal affairs and undermining the political system.

zh: 唯一正确的思想发展形式
en: only correct form of intellectual development
q: only correct form of intellectual development
py: wéiyī zhèngquè de sīxiǎng fāzhǎn xíngshì
ex: Engels's phrase, in his review of Marx's 1859 Contribution, for Marx's dialectical method stripped of Hegel's idealism.
Used by the author for a Europe made ethnically plural by migration, which the article says is divided between accepting diversity and returning to a closed society.

en: opening the door to run newspapers
q: opening the door to run newspapers
ex: A Maoist approach in which newspapers draw contributions from many cadres, workers and ordinary people, not only professional journalists.
The policy begun in 1978 of engaging with foreign trade, capital and technology, designated a basic national policy.
An Italian current of Marxism, prominent from the 1960s, that centres on the working class's autonomous struggles. Antonio Negri is its best-known representative.
A long-standing Party-state concept of shaping public discourse through media and publicity so that it aligns with mainstream values and official priorities.
Influential online figures whose posts shape public discussion; the author treats them as able to dominate opinion.

Marx's description of religion as the "opium of the people", which Lenin called the cornerstone of the Marxist outlook on religion. The article treats it as one of three Marxist definitions of religion's essence.
Traditional Marxist-Leninist labels for tendencies seen as abandoning revolutionary principles in favour of reform or compromise. Many of the parties cited use them against other left currents.

A 1930 essay by Mao Zedong attacking dogmatic reliance on texts and directives instead of investigating actual conditions. Its slogan "no investigation, no right to speak" is widely cited in Party discourse.
A Chinese dialectical formula, cited here from Mao Zedong. It holds that contradictory aspects both struggle against each other and, under conditions, become unified.

lit: joint struggle of parties out of power
ex: The JCP's term for cooperation among Japan's opposition parties, based on agreements on policy, election candidates or government. Li treats it as the main form of the JCP's united front.
Derived from Debord's 'society of the spectacle'. It names a social order in which images and representations mediate and conceal capital's domination.
Hess's term for a rational, organised and diverse human society in which labour and enjoyment are united and each person develops freely.

A Gramscian term for intellectuals who emerge from and articulate the worldview of a particular class. Here it covers media workers, public-relations staff and youth leaders who produce symbolic meanings.

A term in Party-building discourse for the Party's ability to lead, unite, fight and mobilise through its organisations. The article breaks it into leading capacity, cohesion, combat effectiveness and mobilising appeal.
A policy phrase for basic research planned and coordinated around national strategic needs, rather than left to individual researchers' free exploration.
A policy approach in which universities direct research towards national strategic needs through coordinated teams and platforms, rather than relying mainly on individual free exploration.
Mao Zedong's slogan, associated with his 1943 Yan'an speech, for gathering scattered smallholders into mutual-aid and cooperative bodies.
The Party central organ responsible for membership, cadre appointments and Party organisation. Chen Yun headed it from December 1937.

The Party's guiding principles for organizational work, covering structures, cadres and talent. The term first appeared in a 1928 Party Congress resolution; Xi Jinping gave it a formal definition in 2018.
Zhang's term for a movement's capacity to organize and unite its forces, above all through the party and the socialist state.

A concept from European Enlightenment thought, associated with Montesquieu, describing Asian states as ruled by arbitrary monarchs and prone to stagnation. Liang criticises it as a support of Eurocentrism.
A Party slogan, "staying true to the original aspiration and keeping our mission firmly in mind". It calls on Party members to remain faithful to the founding purpose of serving the people.
A slogan of Xi Jinping-era Party building. It refers to the Party's founding purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the nation.

lit: never forget the original heart, keep the mission firmly in mind
ex: A Party slogan, prominent from 2017 onwards, calling on members to remember why the Party was founded: to seek the people's wellbeing and national rejuvenation.
A Party formulation, stressed in the 2019 campaign, that the Party's aim is to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

lit: do not forget the original heart, keep the mission firmly in mind
ex: A slogan emphasised at the 19th Party Congress (2017) calling on Party members to remember their founding purpose of serving the people and pursuing communism.
A Party slogan, stressed under Xi Jinping, for the Party's founding purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
The review's term for the field's theory as it first appears in the classic Marxist texts, before later interpretation.
In Wang's usage, the line from Engels and the Second International through Lenin and the Third International to the Soviet-bloc textbook system, plus present-day orthodox currents.
A Neo-Confucian notion of an authoritative line of transmission of the true Way from the sage kings onward. The author warns against tying Xi's cultural thought to it.

A document proposed by Cuba and adopted at the São Paulo Forum in 2017 as the left's answer to the neoliberal Washington Consensus. The article says it sets out shared values and aims without prescribing action plans for individual countries.

zh: 新时代公民道德建设实施纲要
en: Outline for Implementing Citizen Moral Development in the New Era
q: Outline for Implementing Citizen Moral Development in the New Era
py: Xīn shídài gōngmín dàodé jiànshè shíshī gāngyào
ex: A policy document issued by the Central Committee and State Council in October 2019. It updates the 2001 Outline and sets tasks for moral education and conduct.

zh: 全民科学素质行动计划纲要
en: Outline of the National Scientific Literacy Action Plan
q: Outline of the National Scientific Literacy Action Plan
py: Quánmín kēxué sùzhì xíngdòng jìhuà gāngyào
ex: A State Council programme issued in February 2006 to raise public scientific literacy by 2010 and 2020. It named leading cadres and civil servants as a key target group.

en: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy
q: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy
ex: Engels's 1843–44 essay critiquing classical political economy and private property. Marx drew on it in his own early economic studies.
Xi Jinping's term, used in his 2023 speech on cultural inheritance and development, for the five features of Chinese civilization: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness.
Five features (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness, peacefulness) that Xi Jinping set out in 2023 as marking Chinese civilization.
Qian's term for the capacity of Chinese civilization to absorb and merge with outside cultures while keeping its core.

lit: taking overall charge of the situation and coordinating all parties
ex: A formula describing the Party's leading role over state organs, the legislature, the government, enterprises and other bodies.

zh: 生态文明体制改革总体方案
en: Overall Plan for Reforming the Ecological Civilization System
q: Overall Plan for Reforming the Ecological Civilization System
py: Shēngtài wénmíng tǐzhì gǎigé zǒngtǐ fāng'àn
ex: A 2015 Party and State Council document setting out eight institutional systems for ecological civilization.
Althusser's idea that a social contradiction is determined by many interacting contradictions, not by the economy alone.
Althusser's concept that a social contradiction is determined by many interacting contradictions, not by the economy alone. The article says he drew on "On Contradiction" for it.

lit: religious infiltration from outside the borders
ex: An official term for activities by foreign groups or individuals using religion in ways that violate Chinese law and policy. In the article it covers illegal proselytising and is framed as a contest over ideology.
A slogan in Chinese industrial and science policy meaning to surpass competitors by entering new fields or technological paths rather than following established ones.
The official description of the anti-corruption results since 2012. The article stresses that it does not mean a thorough or final victory.

The term means establishing or confirming legal and economic rights over a thing. The article uses it for the question of who holds rights over products made with AI. The summary renders it as 'ownership'.

In Chinese Marxist usage, the social form in which the means of production are held and controlled, as distinct from legal property rights. It is treated as the basis of the relations of production and of a society's character.
The constitutional name for state ownership, one of the two forms of socialist public ownership alongside collective ownership by the working masses.
The set of additional economic support measures announced in late 2024 to stabilise growth, the property market and capital markets and to boost domestic demand.
A Chinese policy practice in which designated developed regions provide financial, personnel and technical support to less developed or disaster-hit regions.
A movement for African unity, self-determination and solidarity that grew from anti-colonial and anti-racist struggles. It underlies the Organisation of African Unity and the African Union.
A term for personalised communication that is centred on each individual yet reaches everyone, presented as the step beyond mass and niche-audience communication.
A term Chinese scholars use for contemporary Western Marxism's cross-disciplinary approach to economics, which extends it to topics such as gender and minorities and mixes in other disciplines.
A term describing the spread of entertainment content into every area of public life, which critics say dilutes serious public and political discussion.
A broad alliance of working-class organisations and other progressive or oppressed groups against capitalism. The article proposes it as the strategy for the Western left.
A term the author says was proposed in a research report, holding that all currents calling themselves socialist belong to one family. The author rejects it.
A partyless system of councils introduced by King Mahendra of Nepal in 1960, which banned open political party activity. It was abolished in 1990.
The doctrine that God is identical with nature or the universe. The article treats Spinoza as its highest representative.

The author's term for a stage of research following studies of Marxist philosophical paradigms and of Chinese Marxist philosophical paradigms. It concerns building a distinctive paradigm of Chinese Marxist philosophy.
A paradigm centred on real problems in history's "original" rather than on texts or ideas. The authors treat it as the third and decisive axial paradigm in Marx's development.
Xi Jinping's term for China's industrialisation, informatisation, urbanisation and agricultural modernization proceeding together, in contrast to the sequential ("series") path of Western countries.

lit: line of advancing both at once
ex: The strategy announced in 2013 of pursuing economic construction and nuclear weapons development together. It was declared complete in 2018.
The revolutionary municipal government that ruled Paris in March–May 1871. Marx defended it in The Civil War in France as a new political form.
Marx's excerpt notebooks on political economy from 1844, covering authors such as Say, Smith and Ricardo.
A pejorative label in the Marxist tradition for parties that treat parliamentary struggle as the only road to change. Guo warns left parties against this attitude.

en: part of those who have no part
q: part of those who have no part
lit: the share of those without share
ex: Rancière's term for those counted as having no standing in the community, such as the poor or the proletariat, whose appearance as political subjects interrupts the existing order.
Staff with other main jobs, such as counsellors, administrators, industry experts or teachers of other subjects, who are recruited to teach part of these courses.
The official designation of the democratic parties. It distinguishes them from both ruling and opposition parties.
A model in which citizens take part directly in government decisions, to supplement or partly replace representative institutions. The article treats it as the central goal of the radical left.
The official framework of Party, supervisory, state, democratic, public and media oversight, in which Party oversight is said to be primary.
Work to establish and strengthen Party organisations and their influence, here extended to platform-economy workers and enterprises.
The Communist Party's work of strengthening its organisations, discipline, ideology and membership, here applied inside business parks.
The Party's work on its own ideology, organisation, conduct and discipline. The article pairs it with national construction as the two main forms of jianshe.
A formula meaning that Party organisations at the grassroots take the lead in governance and in coordinating other actors.

zh: 党建引领基层治理现代化
en: Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance
q: Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance
lit: Party building guiding grassroots governance modernization
ex: A formula first put in a central document in 2021. It holds that strengthening Party organizations should guide and improve governance in villages, neighbourhoods and other grassroots units.
A principle of Chinese Communist Party doctrine that the armed forces are under the Party's absolute leadership. It is often traced to Mao Zedong.
The Communist Party of China's basic internal rulebook, covering its guiding ideology, aims, membership, organisation and discipline. It is revised at National Party Congresses.
A formal channel through which the Communist Party consults the democratic parties and non-Party figures on major policies before decisions are made.

A term in Chinese scholarship for the international exchanges and cooperation conducted by ruling and other legitimate parties alongside state diplomacy. It came into use in China from the 1970s and drew academic attention in the early 1990s.

The binding code of conduct for Party organisations and members. It includes political, organisational, integrity, mass-line, work and lifestyle discipline, set out in the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions.
The responsibility a Party organisation or member bears for a violation of Party discipline. The article treats it as a distinct element between the violation and the sanction.
A Party-wide campaign in 2024 centred on study of the revised Regulations on Disciplinary Actions.
Groups of Communist members organised inside other bodies, such as the Kuomintang or strike committees, to coordinate the Party's line within them.
Party bodies set up inside non-Party state or social institutions, such as government departments, to ensure the Party's leadership there.
Party bodies set up inside government, legislative and state-enterprise organs to play a decision-making role in major matters.
A Party-wide campaign to study the Party's history, launched in 2021. The article says the archives can help make it routine and long-term.
The author's proposed concept: the ruling party's integration of the state apparatus, its own organisations and society, offered as a fourth type of social integration.

zh: 党领导、国家管理、人民当家作主
en: the Party leads, the state manages, the people are masters
q: Party leads, the state manages, the people are masters
py: dǎng lǐngdǎo, guójiā guǎnlǐ, rénmín dāngjiā zuòzhǔ
ex: The CPV's formula for the overall operating model of Vietnam's political system. The article says the 13th Congress added the Fatherland Front and other social organisations as pillars of popular mastery.
A principle that the Communist Party leads and controls work in the ideological field, including media and online opinion.
The principle that the Party directs propaganda, media and ideological work; it is often paired with "the Party manages ideology".
A Party principle that the Party leads talent selection, training and deployment through its organisation departments.
A principle of Party leadership over internet governance, listed first among the 'ten adherences' for cyberspace and informatisation work set out in 2023.
Party members who hold official or leadership posts, the main audience of Party discipline and integrity education.

en: Party members may not hold religious beliefs
q: Party members may not hold religious beliefs
lit: Party members cannot believe in religion
ex: A long-standing Party principle, treated as political discipline, that Communist Party members must not hold religious beliefs. The article defends it against proposals to relax it.

lit: Party members' making and fulfilling of pledges
ex: A grassroots Party-building practice in which members publicly commit to concrete tasks or self-improvement goals and are then checked on fulfilling them.
A pan-European alliance of communist, socialist and other radical left parties, founded in 2004. It acts as a loose, decentralised association of autonomous member parties.
A thesis put forward at the 22nd Soviet Party Congress (1961) that the Party no longer represented one class. The author treats it as a revisionist abandonment of Marxism-Leninism.
A newspaper run by a Party committee at a given level that serves as its official voice, such as the New Hunan Daily for the Hunan provincial committee.
The requirement that media and journalists uphold Party leadership and policy. Official texts present it as consistent with serving the people.
Mass campaigns to re-educate members and purge those deemed unqualified or corrupt, a method inherited from the Leninist and Chinese communist tradition.
Institutions run by Party committees at each level to train cadres and Party members in Party theory, policy and discipline. The Central Party School is the national flagship.

A concept the author develops from the Daodejing's idea of self-knowledge. It covers a party's clear grasp of its mission, strengths, flaws and historical conditions, and it combines confidence, awareness, introspection and discipline.

The qualities of political standpoint, loyalty, discipline and commitment expected of Communist Party members. In Chinese Party discourse it covers both the Party's essential character and each member's personal cultivation.
A formula holding that loyalty to the Party and service to the people are identical in the Party's work. It is often applied to the media and ideological work.

en: Party spirit and the people's character
q: Party spirit and the people's character
ex: A pairing in Chinese Party ideology: the Party's class-based loyalty and discipline, and its orientation towards the interests of the broad masses. Official discourse holds that the two must be unified.
The Party's conduct and image in thought, work and life, as seen by the public. The term is traced to Mao Zedong's 1942 essay on rectifying the Party's style.

zh: 中共中央关于党的百年奋斗重大成就和历史经验的决议
py: Zhōnggòng Zhōngyāng guānyú dǎng de bǎinián fèndòu zhòngdà chéngjiù hé lìshǐ jīngyàn de juéyì
lit: Resolution of the CPC Central Committee on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party over the Past Century
ex: A document adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in November 2021, giving the Party's authoritative assessment of its first hundred years.

en: the Party's absolute leadership over the military
q: Party's absolute leadership over the military
py: dǎng duì jūnduì de juéduì lǐngdǎo
ex: An official principle that the armed forces are under the direct command of the Communist Party of China, and not of the state or other bodies.

zh: 党的宗教工作基本方针
en: the Party's basic policy on religious work
q: Party's basic policy on religious work
py: dǎng de zōngjiào gōngzuò jīběn fāngzhēn
ex: The official four-part guideline: fully implement the policy of religious freedom, manage religious affairs according to law, uphold independence and self-administration, and actively guide religion to adapt to socialist society.

en: the Party's basic principles and policies on religious work
q: Party's basic principles and policies on religious work
ex: The Party's official guidelines on religion, including freedom of religious belief, management of religious affairs according to law, independent self-run religious bodies, and guiding religion to adapt to socialist society.

en: the Party's command over the army
ex: The principle that the armed forces obey the Communist Party's leadership, the first of the stated requirements for the PLA.

The Party's authority over ideological, propaganda and cultural work, which the article defines as leadership, management and discourse power in this field. The wording echoes Gramscian hegemony but is used here in a Party-leadership sense.
Official phrase for the Party's latest theoretical achievements, centred today on Xi Jinping Thought. Study and propagation of it is a standing task of Party education.
A Party working method, dating to the Mao era, of drawing on the views of the masses and then returning to them in policy and practice.

zh: 新时代党的建设新的伟大工程
en: the Party's new great project of Party building
q: Party's new great project of Party building
py: xīn shídài dǎng de jiànshè xīn de wěidà gōngchéng
ex: An official formulation for Party building since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers political, ideological, organisational, stylistic and disciplinary building and anti-corruption work.
The principle that the Communist Party leads all sectors of work, including education. In universities it is exercised through Party committees.

A strand of Party building concerned with political direction, loyalty to the central leadership and political discipline. The 19th Party Congress in 2017 placed it first among the Party's building tasks.
The Party's fundamental guiding direction and tasks, which the article treats as the reference point for all policy and for checking deviations.
A formula in Party discourse since the 2010s for the Party reforming itself through discipline, criticism and anti-corruption work; officially presented as the key to its long-term rule.

zh: 中国共产党人的精神谱系
lit: the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
ex: An official series of named 'spirits' (such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits) traced back to the 'founding spirit' of the Party. Xi Jinping highlighted it in 2021.

en: the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era
q: Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era
py: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Zàng fānglüè
ex: The official framework for Tibet policy, consolidated at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work (2020) and summarised in ten "musts". It combines Party leadership, regional ethnic autonomy, stability, development, ecology and border security.

en: the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
q: Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
py: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Jiāng fānglüè
lit: the Party's Xinjiang-governing strategy of the new era
ex: The official name for the Party's policy framework on Xinjiang since the 18th Party Congress (2012), associated with Xi Jinping. It combines a general goal, eight principles and five guiding lines of work.

lit: cooperatives initiated and run by the Party branch
ex: A model developed in Yantai, Shandong, from 2017, in which village Party branches register and lead farmers' cooperatives that pool land, funds and labour.
The practice of writing the role of the Party organisation into a company's articles of association.
Officials sent to firms, especially non-public ones, to help set up and run Party organisations.
Service and governance platforms, increasingly digital, set up by Party organisations to share information and integrate resources for Party work and ideological-political work.
A system that makes Party committees and officials accountable for Party-building tasks. It is assessed through annual agenda-setting and evaluation.

The habits and practices the Party says it has formed and consistently kept in leading the revolution, construction and reform and in building itself. The article treats them as expressing the Party's stance, principles, values and spirit.
The long-term effort by members to raise their political awareness, theoretical level, discipline and morality. It is a standard theme of Party education in China.

The various forms of education the CPC gives its members, especially leading cadres, on ideals, discipline, work style and loyalty. It is delivered through Party schools, cadre academies and campaigns.
The relationship between the Communist Party and ordinary people, which the Party describes as its lifeline and often compares to fish in water.
Leisure modelled on rest and compensation for tiring labour, which the author says can slide into consumerism and hedonism.

zh: 中国特色金融发展之路
en: the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics
q: path of financial development with Chinese characteristics
py: Zhōngguó tèsè jīnróng fāzhǎn zhī lù
ex: A formulation set out by Xi Jinping at the Central Financial Work Conference in October 2023. It describes a financial model stressing Party leadership, serving the real economy and risk prevention.
The official line that China pursues development without seeking expansion or hegemony. The editorial pairs it with a firm defence of China's core interests.

zh: 中国特色社会主义道路
en: the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: path of socialism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The official name for China's development route since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and a market economy. The article treats it as the specific meaning of "the Chinese path".

zh: 中国特色社会主义法治道路
en: the path of the rule of law of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: path of the rule of law of socialism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The official name for China's model of legal development, which is presented as distinct from Western models and as rooted in national conditions and Party leadership.
The Lao communist-led movement that fought for power in Laos and took control in 1975. It worked in close alliance with Vietnamese communists.
Capital that accepts medium- and long-term returns rather than short-term profit. It is used in current Chinese economic policy discourse as a way to channel investment into technological innovation.
Federici's term for the system in which men's waged labour gives them power over women, whose unpaid reproductive work is made dependent and invisible.

zh: 爱国主义教育示范基地
ex: An official designation for museums and memorial sites that are used for patriotic education programmes in China.

A law adopted by the National People's Congress Standing Committee in October 2023 and in force from 1 January 2024. It sets out requirements for patriotic education across schools, society, culture and the internet.
A mass sanitation and hygiene mobilisation begun in the early 1950s, which the article treats as a lasting Chinese method of public health work.
The Party-led alliance of non-Party groups, parties, ethnic and religious groups and overseas Chinese. Official discourse describes it as a means of building broad support.
A relationship in which a lay patron supports a religious teacher. Tibetan authorities used it to describe ties with the central government as purely religious, denying political subordination.
A formulation associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong, describing the Chinese nation as a unified whole made up of many ethnic groups.
Deng Xiaoping's assessment that peace and development, not war and revolution, are the main themes of the age. It underpins reform-era foreign policy.
An official initiative aiming at social stability and public security, covering crime prevention, dispute resolution and risk control.
Common name for Japan's 1947 constitution, whose Article 9 renounces war and the maintenance of war potential. The article presents it as a constraint imposed on a defeated state.

A term associated in Chinese discourse with John Foster Dulles's idea of undermining communist states by non-military means. Chinese writers use it for perceived Western efforts at ideological and political subversion.
The strategy of the Italian Communist Party under Togliatti after the Second World War. It aimed at socialism through parliamentary politics and broad alliances, not violent seizure of power.
The strategy of reaching socialism through parliamentary and democratic means rather than armed revolution. Many Western communist parties adopted it after the Second World War.
The idea in the Communist Party's 1951 programme, The British Road to Socialism, that Britain could reach socialism through parliamentary democracy and mass struggle rather than armed revolution.
A short-term school set up in Guangzhou in 1924 under Kuomintang–Communist cooperation to train peasant-movement organisers. Peng Pai directed its first class.

The set of theoretical and practical problems about the peasantry's role in revolution and socialism. Engels used the term in 1894, and Lenin and Mao later gave it a different content centred on land and struggle against landlords.
The tendency, described by the author for Latin America, of governments to swing between left and right in successive elections.
The authors' term for the recurring swing of power between left and right in Latin America, driven by electoral alternation and shifting public moods.
Term used in Xi Jinping's remarks to the 2026 CCDI plenum. It refers to supervision's ability to see through the appearance of power and reach its structure and hidden risks.

en: the people are most important and the ruler least
q: people are most important and the ruler least
py: mín wéi guì, jūn wéi qīng
lit: the people are precious, the ruler is light
ex: Mencius's formula that the people rank above the state altars and the ruler. Later writers cited it in support of the idea of people-centred government.

en: the people as masters of the country
q: people as masters of the country
lit: the people being masters of the house
ex: An official formulation for the essence of socialist democracy, meaning that the people hold state power. It is usually paired with Party leadership and law-based governance.

en: the people as the foundation of the state
q: people as the foundation of the state
ex: A traditional Chinese political idea, found in the Book of Documents, that the people are the root of the state. Official discourse often cites it as a precedent for people-centred governance.

zh: 民知、民议、民为、民检、民监、民享
en: people know, discuss, do, inspect, supervise and enjoy
q: people know, discuss, do, inspect, supervise and enjoy
py: mín zhī, mín yì, mín wéi, mín jiǎn, mín jiān, mín xiǎng
ex: The CPV's formula for popular participation. It started as 'people know, discuss, do, inspect' in 1986, and the Thirteenth Congress (2021) added supervision and enjoyment.
A concept of urban development, promoted by Xi Jinping, holding that cities are built by the people and for the people.

lit: important concept of the people's city
ex: A concept associated with Xi Jinping's 2019 Shanghai visit, summed up as "the people's city is built by the people and for the people". It is presented as the guiding principle of urban work in the new era.

A principle associated with Xi Jinping, first stated in 2019 in Shanghai, that cities should be built and governed by the people and for the people. The article presents it as the guiding idea of urban work.
The central executive body of the Chinese Soviet Republic, formed under the Central Executive Committee to handle routine government affairs and issue decrees.
The 1958 drive to merge agricultural cooperatives into large rural communes combining economic and administrative functions.
Large rural units set up in 1958 that combined economic management and local government and ran farming, industry, commerce, education and militia. They were dissolved after the reform period began.
China's fundamental political institution, in which congresses at each level are said to exercise state power on behalf of the people.
Mao Zedong's idea, first put forward in the 1920s Hunan self-government movement, that the people elect representatives to a constitutional assembly that drafts the constitution.

The official term for China's democratic principle, under which the people are said to be masters of the country under Party leadership. Lin treats it as the theoretical core of the institutional system.

Mao Zedong's 1949 formulation, in which democracy for the people is combined with dictatorship over reactionaries. It was later written into the Party constitution and the state constitution as one of the Four Cardinal Principles.

The CPI(M)'s programmatic strategic goal: completing the unfinished tasks of India's democratic revolution through land revolution and curbs on monopoly and foreign capital, as a stage preparing the transition to socialism.
The broad alliance of classes and groups, including religious circles, that the Party sought to organise against the Nationalists and imperialism in the late 1940s.
Wu's ideal for economists who take the standpoint of working people and serve their interests, as the article presents it.
A national honorary title awarded to outstanding educators. In 2024 it went to Zhang Jinfan and Huang Danian.

en: the people's hearts are the greatest politics
q: people's hearts are the greatest politics
lit: popular support is the greatest politics
ex: A slogan of Xi Jinping's era holding that popular support determines the Party's survival. It is used to justify a people-centred approach to governance.
A phrase used in Party discourse for the claim that ordinary people originate new practices, such as rural reforms, which the Party later adopts and generalises.
The model of literature and art serving workers, peasants and soldiers, associated with Mao Zedong's 1942 Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art.

The political programme adopted by the CPN (UML) at its fifth congress in 1993. It accepts multi-party politics and a peaceful, gradual transition to socialism, and in the authors' view it laid the theoretical ground for the parliamentary path.

en: the people's need for a better life
q: people's need for a better life
ex: A formulation introduced by Xi Jinping at the 19th Party Congress (2017). It replaced the earlier reference to "material and cultural needs" and covers areas such as democracy, rule of law, fairness, security and the environment.
The author's term for the political form created by the Communist Party in China, which he contrasts with Western multiparty "party politics".
A Party principle that the people are the main actors and ultimate beneficiaries of development and governance.
The author's own term for a socialist form of social relations. It is presented as a transitional form between capitalist reified relations and communist human relations.

A term in Chinese Party theory for taking the fundamental interests of the broad masses as the starting point of theory and policy. The article treats it as continuous with the proletarian standpoint.
The idea that the people are the principal agent and beneficiary of historical development. Official discourse presents it as a Sinicization of the Marxist view of history centred on the masses.
A system in which citizens chosen from various backgrounds observe and give opinions on procuratorial case handling. The Supreme People's Procuratorate began trialling it in 2003.

zh: 政务院人民监察委员会
lit: People's Supervisory Committee of the Government Administration Council
ex: The central administrative supervision body of 1949–1954, set up under the Government Administration Council. It oversaw state organs and officials and handled public complaints, until replaced by the Ministry of Supervision in 1954.
The process by which rural migrants gain full urban residency rights and public services, beyond merely moving to cities. The article contrasts it with "land urbanization".
Mao Zedong's strategy of fighting by mobilising the whole population alongside regular and irregular forces. The article treats it as a continuing basis for modern warfare.

lit: people's livelihood is the greatest matter
ex: A phrase from Xi Jinping stressing that livelihood protection is central to Chinese modernization. 'Minsheng' covers jobs, income, education, health, housing and social security.
Classical Chinese political idea that the people are the foundation of the state and that rulers must nurture them. Contemporary Party writers link it to the people-centred approach.

lit: taking the people as the centre
ex: A guiding principle of Party discourse under Xi Jinping holding that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by the people. The article contrasts it with the "capital-centred" Western model.
A core principle in Chinese Party cultural policy holding that literature and art should come from, serve and reflect the people. It draws on Mao Zedong's 1942 Yan'an talks.

lit: taking the people as the foundation
ex: The core principle of the Scientific Outlook on Development, meaning that development should serve people's interests and all-round development.

zh: 以人民为中心的发展理念
py: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn lǐniàn
ex: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era holding that development should serve the people's interests and wellbeing. Here the authors apply it to atheist propaganda work.

zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
py: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
ex: An official formulation holding that development should aim at the well-being of the people. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 2010s.

py: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn
ex: An official principle holding that development should serve the people's needs and interests. The authors treat it as a law of socialist development.
The view, emphasised in Chinese Marxist writing, that the people are the decisive force in historical development.

py: yǐ rén wéi běn, zhìnéng xiàng shàn
ex: A formula attributed to Xi Jinping on AI development and governance. It also appears in China's Global AI Governance Initiative.
A political principle of the Workers' Party of Korea, presented at the Eighth Congress as the Party's basic political method, with the slogan 'the people are heaven'.
A key Huayan idea that all things interpenetrate without obstruction. The author treats it as a basis for harmony among differing peoples and teachings.

Ceballos's own label for a cadre system in which officials are promoted on the basis of demonstrated results and experience across several posts. He links it to the traditional idea of appointing the capable.
Party judgement, first made at the 16th Party Congress (2002), that the international environment allows China to make significant progress. It was restated in later congress reports.

A Party assessment, first formally stated at the 16th Party Congress (2002), that the first two decades of the 21st century offered China favourable conditions for development. Later documents have kept the term while adjusting its content.

lit: the world has entered a period of turbulence and transformation
ex: A judgement Xi Jinping put forward in 2020, presented as a further stage of the "changes unseen in a century" assessment, stressing growing instability and uncertainty.

Trotsky's theory that backward countries could move directly from a democratic revolution to a socialist one, and that socialism needs world revolution. Chinese scholars disagree on whether it is dogmatic or a sound strategy.
The title of a talk Mao gave to model youth in Yan'an in May 1939. It means continuing the struggle for life and across generations.
A deity conceived as having personality and will, who rules over humans. The article says Shao's cosmology denied this traditional notion.
The deification of an individual leader above the masses, class and Party. The authors treat it as a product of an idealist view of history and as opposed to honouring heroes.

lit: composite right of personality and property
ex: The author's proposed right form that treats data as a unity of personality and property elements, rather than as either a thing or information.
In Marxist usage, the class of small independent producers and owners, such as artisans and small farmers. The article applies the label to Proudhon's outlook.
A term popularised by The Economist in 2006 and by Bishop and Green's book. It refers to wealthy donors applying business and investment methods to philanthropy.
The author's term for the highest level of Marx's reasoning, where communism is conceived as the human being's return to its social essence.
A label applied to Marx's communism in 1843–44, said to rest on abstract philosophical reasoning rather than scientific analysis of political economy.
The Marxist claim that Marx broke with earlier philosophy by basing it on practice and changing the world rather than only interpreting it.
The standard Chinese official category covering the humanities and social sciences. Party documents set it as a field to be guided by Marxism and to serve national development.

zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学
en: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
q: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
ex: An official goal, stressed by Xi Jinping from 2016, of building a Chinese system of disciplines, scholarship and discourse guided by Marxism.
Hess's programme of turning speculative philosophy into a guide for revolutionary practice, centred on free, self-determining activity.
A branch of philosophy that studies culture and its relation to human existence. In the article it is traced to Ernst Cassirer.
The philosophical study of the overall direction, laws and meaning of historical development, the perspective the reviewed book adopts.
A Latin American philosophical current from the 1970s, associated with Leopoldo Zea and Enrique Dussel, that seeks a philosophy of the 'Third World' free from European dependence.
Gramsci's term in the Prison Notebooks for Marxism, partly a code word to avoid prison censors. Chinese scholars debate whether it is identical to Marxism or an original development.
The Chinese rendering of the German Rechtsphilosophie, as in Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right. It covers questions of the legitimacy and rational basis of law, property and the state.
A Hegelian-derived current developed by the Young Hegelians, which treats human self-consciousness as the highest standard of judgement, including of religion.

Badiou's philosophy holds that truths arise from rare, contingent events, and that subjects are constituted by fidelity to them. He identifies four domains of truth: poetry, mathematics, politics and love.
A phrase from Marx and Engels's polemics against the Young Hegelians, meaning radical rhetoric that does not engage with material conditions.
Xu's label for an urban planning approach that stresses controlled physical form, order and the aerial view. The English rendering here is a gloss, not an established term.
Popper's term for cautious, partial and revisable social reform, which he contrasts with holistic social planning.
A 17th–18th-century revivalist movement within German Lutheranism that stressed inner devotion and Bible reading. Engels grew up in a strongly Pietist milieu and criticised it in his early writings.
A reform approach in which measures are first tested in selected localities or zones before being extended nationally.
A common term for the wave of left and centre-left governments elected in Latin America from the late 1990s and 2000s.

A common name for the wave of left and centre-left election victories in Latin America from the late 1990s onwards. The article uses it for the first wave and treats the post-2018 wave as a new round.
A common term for the wave of left and centre-left election victories across Latin America from the late 1990s. The article treats it as having receded after 2015.
A CASS programme that funds selected disciplines, including 'special' and endangered ones, to raise their standing.
Sun's term for the earlier tendency in socialist countries to apply Marx's general sketch of a future economy directly, treating central planning as inseparable from socialism.

A traditional Chinese practice in which participants hold a stick or planchette that writes characters said to be messages from spirits. Spiritualist societies used it as supposed experimental proof of souls.

Marx and Engels's idea that in a future society associated producers organise production consciously according to need, in contrast to capitalism's anarchy of production. The article distinguishes it from Soviet-style state planning.
Term associated with Nick Srnicek for a capitalism organised around data-extracting platform firms. Lan treats it as the monopoly stage of digital capitalism.
The authors' shorthand for cloud rent on e-commerce platforms, analysed by analogy with Marx's differential, absolute and monopoly ground rent.

The author's label for views holding that digital platforms profit mainly from rent (data rent, cloud rent and so on) rather than from producing surplus value. It covers ideas such as techno-feudalism and data colonialism.
A proposal, associated here with James Muldoon, to turn large digital platforms into publicly owned or cooperative infrastructure under democratic control.
Cooperatives in which peasants pooled funds or draught animals so that members could share ploughing oxen, which were scarce in the base areas.
The 1997–2002 government led by Socialist prime minister Lionel Jospin, which included the PCF, the Greens and other left parties.

lit: pattern of pluralism and unity of the nation
ex: A formulation associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong. It describes the Chinese nation as one entity made up of many ethnic groups.

zh: 中华民族多元一体格局
lit: pattern of plurality within unity of the Chinese nation
ex: A concept from the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong (1988). It holds that the Chinese nation is a single entity formed historically from many ethnic groups.
A formula, associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong, holding that the 56 ethnic groups form one Chinese nation. Official discourse presents it as a dialectical unity of the one and the many.
A left-populist Spanish party that grew out of the 2011 protest movement and rose sharply from 2014. The article presents it as a main rival to the PCE.
The Chinese rendering of Rancière's 'la police': not law-enforcement officers but the order that allocates social places, roles and the right to speak.
The author's term for tracing one policy across a long time span, to see continuities and breaks between earlier and later decisions.
The author's term for the set of related policies issued together in the same period, which should be studied in relation to one another.
A principle of Party doctrine that the armed forces must be built first on political loyalty and Party leadership. It is traced to the 1929 Gutian Conference and revived under Xi Jinping.
A Party-building practice, named by Xi Jinping in 2018, in which members and organisations regularly examine their political stance and conduct. It was written into Party regulations in 2019.
A system in which Party-appointed officers sit alongside military commanders and countersign orders. It serves to ensure Party control of the armed forces.

A term in Party discourse for conscious, self-directed alignment of one's thinking and actions with the Party's political goals. Xi Jinping often pairs it with 'ideological consciousness' and 'action consciousness'.

The system of consultation between the Communist Party, other parties and social groups, institutionalised through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, first convened in September 1949.
The American norm of avoiding language and practices seen as offensive to minority groups. The authors treat it as the cultural expression of pluralism that Trump opposes.
In this article, the process by which Party members and cadres train themselves to raise their political awareness and the quality of their political thinking.

A strand of Party-building that stresses political direction, loyalty to the Central Committee and political discipline. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) official texts have placed it first among the Party's various forms of building.
The category of Party discipline concerning loyalty to the Party line and the Central Committee. Official texts rank it first among the Party's disciplines.

zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学
en: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
py: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zhèngzhì jīngjìxué
ex: The official name for the theoretical system that generalises China's reform-era economic practice within a Marxist framework. Xi Jinping promoted the term after 2012.
An official metaphor for the overall political climate within the Party, including its culture, norms, and the state of discipline and corruption.
In Marx's early writings, the formal, legal emancipation achieved by bourgeois revolutions such as the French Revolution of 1789. In his view it leaves private property and class oppression in place.
A term from comparative politics for the deliberate design of political institutions. The author recasts it as a Party-centred framework for explaining how the CPC carries out construction.

A concept in Chinese political science and Party-building writing for citizens' sense of belonging to, and support for, a political system or ruling party. The article treats it as a source of the Party's legitimacy.
Inspection teams sent by higher Party bodies to examine lower-level Party organisations for political and disciplinary problems.
Movements and parties that seek to organise state and society on Islamic principles. The article treats them as the main rival of the Arab left.

zh: 政治判断力、政治领悟力、政治执行力
py: zhèngzhì pànduànlì, zhèngzhì lǐngwùlì, zhèngzhì zhíxínglì
ex: Three abilities that Party leaders have required of cadres since the 2019 education campaign. They cover assessing the political situation, grasping the leadership's intentions, and carrying out decisions.

One of four 'capacities' (with ideological guidance, mass organizing and social mobilizing) the Party aims to strengthen. It refers to the Party's ability to set political direction and make major decisions.
An Anglo-American current associated with Robert Brenner and Ellen Meiksins Wood. It stresses social property relations and class struggle in explaining the origins and development of capitalism.
A metaphor for the alternation in power between left and right in Latin American politics. The author treats it as a regular pattern of the region's political life.
A concept borrowed from physics and used by Chinese political scientists. It refers to the stored authority of the Party that can be converted into governance effectiveness.

en: political responsibility for governing the Party
q: political responsibility for governing the Party
lit: political responsibility for managing and governing the Party
ex: The duty of Party organisations and officials at each level to manage and discipline the Party, with accountability if they fail.
A term Xi Jinping emphasised from 2015 for the informal and formal norms of conduct expected inside the Party, used alongside political discipline.
In official usage, the security of state power, the political system and ideology, treated as the foundation of national security.
The capacity of officials to detect early signs of political problems and risks and to judge them from a political standpoint.
The primary duty of discipline inspection and supervision bodies in Party usage: checking that Party organisations and officials carry out the Central Committee's line, policies and decisions.
The moral character expected of those who hold public office. Xi Jinping has urged leading cadres to "speak of political virtue", and the term draws on Confucian ideas of rule by moral example.
The authors' own label for Lenin's post-1917 approach, in which politics is the pivot that moves the other elements of society and aligns the superstructure with the economic base.
The term the article uses for the theoretical system built by Brenner and Wood. It treats historical materialism first as a critique of capitalism rather than a general law of history.
Hu's label for the Marxian perspective, in which technology is a productive force whose liberating potential is realised by transforming relations of production.

Hu's label for contemporary radical technology critique, which rejects industrial civilisation but offers no practical political programme. The term draws on Daoist wuwei and the Western notion of quietism.
The article's term for a system in which representatives act as agents bound by mandates and recall, as opposed to the largely unconstrained representatives of 'representative government'.
The Comintern line adopted at its Seventh Congress in 1935, calling on communist parties to ally with all democratic forces, including the national bourgeoisie, against fascism.
Here, the strategy of alliance among the proletariat, peasants and petty bourgeoisie against fascism, which the article attributes to Gramsci and the Comintern's later line.
Ai Siqi's widely read introduction to Marxist philosophy. It began as lectures titled Philosophical Talks (Zhéxué jiǎnghuà) and was renamed in 1936 to avoid Nationalist censorship.
The idea that supreme political authority belongs to the people. In the article it marks the shift from dynastic rule to the modern nation-state.
The principle, associated with Rousseau, that political authority derives from the people. The authors distinguish its bourgeois form from what they call genuine popular sovereignty.
A Confucian-derived idea that the people are the foundation of the state, so that rulers should govern for their welfare.
The effort to make Marxist and Party theory understandable and acceptable to ordinary people, often by using plain, familiar language. It is a long-standing theme in Chinese Marxist discourse.

The effort to make Marxist theory understandable and persuasive to ordinary people through plain language and familiar forms. It is a recurring theme in Chinese Party theory, going back to the Yan'an period.
Efforts to spread social science and humanities knowledge to the general public, organised in China by bodies such as the federations of social science circles.
A political current that pits 'the people' against establishment elites. The article treats its 21st-century Western form as increasingly right-wing and nationalist.
Parties that appeal to ordinary voters against established elites. The article treats their rise as squeezing the space for communist parties.
A phrase Xi Jinping used at the 2013 national conference on propaganda and ideological work. It calls on cadres to recognise that ideological spaces not held by the Party will be taken by others.
A military-derived term for ideological and media outlets (press, schools, online platforms) which the Party says it must occupy and hold.
A popular term, taken up in official discourse, for upbeat, constructive content and attitudes. In internet governance it means content that supports mainstream values.

zh: 人的积极本质与积极存在
py: rén de jījí běnzhì yǔ jījí cúnzài
ex: Categories the author draws from Marx's reading of Hegel. Positive essence refers to human material desire; positive existence refers to the free and all-round development of the person.
The dominant Republican-era school, associated with Hu Shi, Gu Jiegang, Fu Sinian and Wang Guowei, which stressed evidence, textual criticism and new source materials.

zh: 后资本逻辑的哲学形态
py: hòu zīběn luójí de zhéxué xíngtài
ex: The author's term for a philosophy that sublates capital logic by using and governing capital under socialism so that it serves human development.
Rancière's term for a consensus-based order in which democratic forms persist but real dispute and popular politics have been removed.
The regime following the crisis of Fordism, marked by flexible production, globalisation, financialisation and neoliberal policy.
The period in advanced capitalist societies after industrial manufacturing declined, which the article links to the weakening of working-class revolutionary dynamism.
A current associated with Laclau and Mouffe that rejects essentialism and the primacy of class. It stresses discourse and the linking of heterogeneous subjects.
Xu's term for the period since reform and opening up, in which foreign missionaries are barred from China. Religious exchange continues through other channels.
A period in which, as the author describes it, narratives about facts carry more weight than the facts themselves.
A label used in Chinese scholarship for left theorists after the classic Western Marxist tradition, such as Poulantzas, Laclau and Mouffe, Hardt and Negri. It is often linked with post-Marxism.
The Party's practice of granting membership after death to a person who died for its cause and had asked to join. Party regulations set the approval procedure.
The system of institutions and norms built after 1945, centred on the United Nations and the UN Charter.
The campaign launched in 2015 to eliminate absolute rural poverty by 2020. It was officially declared successful in 2021.
The authors' term for power that actors use to resist, block or punish domination by others. They contrast it with domination-type power, which they see as the form power takes in corruption.
Power understood as the ability to impose one's will on others. The authors treat it as the form into which corrupt officials convert their public authority.

Marx's phrase in the Preface to Capital, where it replaces the microscope and chemical reagents in analysing economic forms. The authors read it as a dialectical force that grasps social relations behind things.
A term in Party discourse for the motivating force of members' commitment to Marxism and communist ideals. The article treats it as a source of the Party's cohesion and strength.
A Chinese political term for the practice of powerful states imposing their will on weaker ones, often under the maxim that "might makes right".
A basic principle of Chinese public administration that an organ's authority should correspond to its duties, so that it neither fails to act nor oversteps.

A term in Chinese Marxist writing for Marxism's orientation towards practice, summed up in the formula of both interpreting and changing the world. It is often attributed to Xi Jinping's formulations.

Sun's term for Marx's mature method, which analyses the contradictory movement of real social practice, chiefly production, instead of movement from concept to concept. Sun treats it as equivalent to the historical dialectic.
In the article, knowledge teachers form by reflecting on and refining their own teaching and work experience, as distinct from systematic theoretical knowledge.
A reading of Marx's "new materialism" that stresses practice (praxis) and human subjectivity, in contrast to Feuerbach's contemplative "old" materialism.

Li Da's term for Marxist philosophy, which puts practice (centred on labour) at the core of materialism. It is close to the 'practical materialism' (实践唯物主义) discussed in Chinese philosophy in the 1980s.
The out-of-classroom component of ideological and political courses, including social surveys, site visits, volunteering and online activities.

lit: ideological and political course practical teaching base
ex: Sites such as museums, memorials, enterprises or communities where students take part in practice-based ideological and political education outside the classroom.
A concept close to Aristotle's phronesis: the capacity to judge and act well in concrete situations. The author uses it to join theoretical reason and practical reason.
A core category of Marxist philosophy in China, understood following Marx's Theses on Feuerbach as sensuous human activity that changes the world.

zh: 实践是检验真理的唯一标准
en: practice as the criterion of truth
q: practice as the criterion of truth
py: shíjiàn shì jiǎnyàn zhēnlǐ de wéiyī biāozhǔn
lit: practice is the sole criterion for testing truth
ex: A philosophical debate launched in 1978 that challenged dogmatic adherence to Mao-era orthodoxy. It gave ideological support to the reform and opening up policy.
The view that practice is the ground of being, so that the world is understood as the product of human practical activity. Hou argues that it denies the priority of external nature.
A critical label, attributed by Guo to the philosopher Zhao Jiaxiang, for the tendency to treat practice as the sole or supreme standpoint of Marxism and downplay theory.
Liu's interpretive formula: practice itself educates the agent, awakening self-consciousness, which in turn guides further action.
The 1968 reform movement in Czechoslovakia, ended by a Soviet-led military intervention. Wang treats it as the decisive event in the CPN's turn away from the Soviet model.
A group of Yugoslav Marxist philosophers active from the 1960s, associated with the journal Praxis and the Korčula Summer School, known for humanist critiques of both Stalinism and capitalism.
Chinese rendering of Guy Standing's coinage (precarious + proletariat) for workers in unstable, casual, unprotected employment. Lan uses it for the new proletariat of digital capitalism.
An approach that uses data and technology to tailor political education to individual students. It was called for at the 2019 national education work conference.
An approach, borrowed from the language of targeted policy, that matches educational content and methods to specific groups or individuals rather than applying uniform measures.
Australia's system in which voters rank candidates and lower preferences are transferred, which the article says favours the two traditional major parties.

The view, associated with Kautsky, that socialism in Russia came before the material conditions were ripe. Critics of the Soviet experience have used it, and Chinese Marxist authors such as Yu Bin rebut it.
Zhao's proposed alternative to the doctrine of innate human rights. Rights are enjoyed only by those who fulfil their obligations to others and respect others' rights.
A meeting held before a congress opens to exchange views, settle delegates and discuss draft documents. The article says the Third Congress began this practice.

en: preparing for war and natural disasters, and doing everything for the people
q: preparing for war and natural disasters, and doing everything for the people
ex: A slogan of the mid-1960s based on Mao Zedong's instruction and summarised by Zhou Enlai, guiding planning with attention to war readiness and disaster relief.

en: preserving heavenly principle and eliminating human desires
q: preserving heavenly principle and eliminating human desires
ex: A Neo-Confucian maxim urging moral cultivation by keeping to cosmic principle and suppressing selfish desires. Yan Yuan and later critics attacked it as denying real human needs.

zh: 党委领导下的校长负责制
en: president responsibility system under the Party committee
q: president responsibility system under the Party committee
py: dǎngwěi lǐngdǎo xià de xiàozhǎng fùzé zhì
lit: president-responsibility system under Party committee leadership
ex: The university governance arrangement in China's public universities, in which the president manages the institution under the leadership of the university Party committee.
The term Chinese translations use for what is original or primary in Engels's question 'spirit or nature?'. Jie reads it as the ground or source of the world and its creator.
The first round of income distribution among factors of production, mainly wages and returns on capital, before redistribution by taxes and transfers.
Deng Xiaoping's 1988 formulation that science and technology is the foremost productive force, going beyond Marx's statement that science is a productive force.
The duty of Party committees and their leaders to run Party discipline in their own jurisdiction, distinct from the supervisory responsibility of discipline inspection commissions.
The Chinese Communist Party's official characterisation of China's present stage, in which markets, foreign investment and technology are used to develop the productive forces.

The work of building and running Party organisations at the lowest levels, such as villages, neighbourhoods, enterprises and schools. It is treated as the foundation of the Party's organisational system.
Marx's term for the violent separation of producers from the means of production, through enclosures, colonial plunder and similar processes. It created the preconditions for capitalist production.
Marx's term for the violent, non-market separation of producers from the means of production, especially land, that preceded capitalist production.
A Party concept for the main social contradiction at a given time, which shapes strategy. The article says the Sino-Japanese national contradiction replaced the class contradiction in this role.

A concept developed in Mao Zedong's On Contradiction: among many contradictions in a process, one plays the leading, decisive role. Party documents also use it to define the central problem of each historical stage.

en: principal contradiction of the new era
q: principal contradiction of the new era
lit: main social contradiction of the new era
ex: The Party's 19th Congress (2017) formulation: the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
In Neo-Confucianism, the principle or pattern governing things. Wang treats it as arising from qi, not as a transcendent source.

en: the principle that the Party manages youth affairs
q: principle that the Party manages youth affairs
lit: principle of the Party managing youth
ex: A principle stressed under Xi Jinping that Party organisations hold leadership over youth work and the cultivation of young people.

Major judgements within a theoretical system that are foundational, essential and an origin for other claims. Xi Jinping called for research on them in 2023 as part of systematizing the Party's theory.

zh: 原则性与灵活性相结合
ex: The Workers' Party of Belgium's strategic formula from its 2008 congress: firm adherence to Marxism and socialism together with tactical adaptability. The article treats it as the party's defining strategy.
The Uno School's term for the purified, abstract theory of a pure capitalist economy, which it distinguishes from stage theory and analysis of present conditions.

lit: Law on Promoting the Private Economy
ex: A law that took effect in May 2025. According to the article, it first defines the legal status of the private economy and protects private firms' rights in market access, innovation and financing.
A social layer enjoying special rights or advantages through position or power. In Party discourse it is linked to the warning drawn from the fall of the Soviet Communist Party.
The label the article gives to Aron's view that historical conclusions reached through understanding and explanation remain uncertain and cannot be strictly necessary.

lit: the difficult problem of material interests
ex: The puzzle Marx met in 1842 when he found that real material interests, not rational principles, determined law and the state. Chinese scholars commonly treat it as the practical spur to his turn to materialism.
A working principle emphasised by Xi Jinping: policy and work should start from identifying and solving real problems.
A method stressed in Xi Jinping's discourse: policy should start from identifying and solving real problems. The 20th Party Congress report listed it among the "six musts" of theoretical innovation.

The translator's rendering of Althusser's French term problématique, which Gu Liang's Chinese edition of For Marx translates as 'general problematic' (总问题). It names the underlying framework of questions that structures a body of thought.
Chinese rendering of Althusser's concept of the 'problematic', the underlying framework that governs a text's questions. Zhang uses it to dispute Althusser's dating of Marx's break with Feuerbach.

lit: the dispute over problems and isms
ex: A 1919 exchange between Hu Shi and Li Dazhao over whether to concentrate on concrete social problems or on doctrines such as socialism.
Zhou's term for Marx's examination of capital through its whole movement of formation, growth and extinction.
The view that Mao's turn was a gradual process that cannot be tied to one date; Wu's own position is closest to it.
A trade mode in which imported materials or components are assembled or processed in China and the finished goods are re-exported.
Services that support production, such as R&D and design, logistics and finance, as distinct from services consumed directly by households.
A state-run organisation in Xinjiang established in 1954 from demobilised army units. It combines farming, economic development and border-defence functions.
A campaign launched in the base areas in the early 1940s in which troops, officials and peasants raised output to ease economic hardship.

Yang's name for an anthropological logic in which production serves the satisfaction of human needs. He says it is shared with classical political economy and with the viewpoint of The German Ideology.
Lefebvre's concept, from his 1974 book The Production of Space, holding that capitalism reproduces itself by producing space itself, not just things within space.
In Marx's usage, labour that produces surplus value for capital. Chinese economists debated in the 1960s and 1980s whether commercial and service labour counts as such.
The principle that the development of productive forces is the basic measure of social progress. It was prominent in Deng-era arguments for reform.

The view that productive forces ultimately determine relations of production and, through them, wider social change. In Chinese debates it is often defended against charges of mechanical or one-factor determinism.
A category of study set up by a university to train people in a particular line of work, with its own courses and degrees.

A network of centre-left parties founded on 22 May 2013, led by Western European social-democratic parties, including Germany's SPD. Many of them left or downgraded their membership of the Socialist International.

en: Project to Trace the Origins of Chinese Civilization
q: Project to Trace the Origins of Chinese Civilization
ex: A long-running state-backed interdisciplinary research programme that uses archaeology to study the origins and early development of Chinese civilization.
The idea that the working class, not the bourgeoisie, should lead a revolution that is bourgeois-democratic in character. Lenin developed it in 1905 in his polemics with the Mensheviks.

The Marxist-Leninist principle that workers and communist parties of all nations should act in solidarity across national lines. The Comintern used it to demand that national parties follow a common line.

zh: 无产阶级的革命的功利主义
py: wúchǎn jiējí de gémìng de gōnglìzhǔyì
ex: Mao's phrase from the 1942 Yan'an talks. It means judging action by the combined present and future interests of the great majority of the people, as opposed to the narrow utilitarianism of exploiting classes or individuals.
The process by which small owners lose their independent means of livelihood and become wage labourers.

A Russian movement of the revolutionary years, centred on the Proletarian Culture organisations (Proletkult) and led by Alexander Bogdanov, which sought to create a distinctly working-class culture independent of the past and of the Party. Lenin criticised it in 1920 and after.
A Russian organisation founded around 1917 that sought a new proletarian culture independent of the Party and of older culture. Lenin criticised it.
The first of the five science and technology ethics principles in the 2022 Opinions. The article presents it as a value shared with international ethics and development frameworks.

A formulation in the policy keynote of the 2023 and 2024 Central Economic Work Conferences. It adds an emphasis on proactive action to the older principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability.
Propaganda and presentation of a decision through proclamations, media and cultural forms. The article treats it as the second stage, which turns reception into active participation.

lit: able to go up, able to go down
ex: A principle that officials should be promoted or removed according to performance, rather than holding posts indefinitely.
A scholarly model in which local officials compete on measurable performance indicators for promotion by their superiors.
The Party's term for its work on theory, media, culture and ideology. The article notes it replaced the narrower phrase "propaganda work" in official usage from the 1990s.
The Party's portfolio covering publicity, ideology, media and cultural affairs. The Chinese term for propaganda (xuānchuán) is used officially and is not pejorative in Chinese.
The article's term for the capitalist relation in which owners of capital take possession of others' labour and its products. It is contrasted with "property ownership" (财产所有).
The principle that the severity of a sanction should match the fault. The article notes it appears in both the Regulations and the Accountability Regulations.
The strategic line, advanced by Communist leaders from 1937, that China should prepare for a long war against Japan instead of seeking a quick decisive battle or a negotiated peace.

Mao Zedong's 1938 theory that China would defeat Japan through a long war in three stages: defence, stalemate and counter-offensive. The article treats tunnel warfare as a product of the stalemate stage.
Kosík's term for the familiar world of everyday appearances and manipulation, which hides the essence of things. Yan treats it as a key obstacle to grasping reality.
Rifaat al-Said's 1996 thesis (al-Ta'aslim), which the author describes as rejecting the legitimacy of political Islam and as targeting the Muslim Brotherhood and religious extremism.
Beliefs or practices that claim scientific status without meeting scientific standards. The article uses it for fortune-telling that presents itself as a science.

py: míng dàdé, shǒu gōngdé, yán sīdé
lit: understand great virtue, observe public virtue, be strict in private virtue
ex: A formula from Xi Jinping asking citizens to grasp major virtue (loyalty to country and Party), observe public morality and keep strict private morality. The article uses it as the basic framework for youth moral education.
Capital owned by the state or collectives under public ownership. The authors treat it as the leading capital form in a socialist market economy.

A mechanism in which government-held public data is made available under authorisation to enterprises and institutions for use, under security controls. Local governments in China have piloted various forms.
Cai's proposed category of publicly owned digital capital, such as state-built public data platforms and computing infrastructure, which would take the leading position in the digital economy.
The author's term for a system of universal principles and rules underlying knowledge classification, meant to be shared across civilizations.

In Chinese debate, the term (often shortened to 'gongzhi') refers to independent commentators who criticise public affairs. Official-leaning writers often criticise them as carriers of Western values.
Ownership of the means of production by the whole people or collectives. In China's socialist market economy it is described as the main body of the system, with the state sector in the leading role.

zh: 公有制为主体、国有制为主导
en: public ownership as the mainstay with the state sector in the leading role
q: public ownership as the mainstay with the state sector in the leading role
py: gōngyǒuzhì wéi zhǔtǐ, guóyǒuzhì wéi zhǔdǎo
lit: public ownership as the main body, state ownership as the leading force
ex: An official formula for China's ownership structure. Public ownership predominates, state-owned enterprises guide the economy, and private enterprise is allowed as a supplement.

en: public ownership of the means of production
q: public ownership of the means of production
ex: The ownership basis that Marxist theory takes to define a socialist economic system. The article uses it as its main test of whether a state is socialist.
The author's term for individuals who understand public affairs, take public responsibility and take part actively in governance through institutions and digital platforms.
One of Burawoy's four types of sociology. It aims to widen public debate on moral and political issues and to link sociology with civil society.
The sphere of social life outside the family and the market where public norms operate. The article treats it as the practical basis of social morality.
Cheng's own concept: surplus value produced by freely associated labourers in publicly owned enterprises, which he distinguishes from private surplus value.

zh: 基本医疗卫生事业的公益性
en: public-interest character of basic medical and health services
q: public-interest character of basic medical and health services
py: jīběn yīliáo wèishēng shìyè de gōngyìxìng
ex: A principle that basic health care is a public good rather than a profit-making service. Reform of public hospitals is meant to reduce profit-seeking incentives.
A wartime guideline for external work: spreading the Party's views abroad and winning foreign sympathy and support.
A regional coordination body of left-wing politicians and parties from about 14 Latin American countries, which the article presents as a counterweight to right-wing groupings.

en: punishing past errors to prevent future ones and curing the sickness to save the patient
q: punishing past errors to prevent future ones and curing the sickness to save the patient
py: chéng qián bì hòu, zhì bìng jiù rén
