lit: punish the past to guard the future; cure the illness to save the person
ex: A principle associated with Mao Zedong from the Yan'an rectification period, under which discipline aims to reform offenders as well as punish them.

zh: 把权力关进制度的笼子
en: putting power into the cage of institutions
q: putting power into the cage of institutions
py: bǎ quánlì guānjìn zhìdù de lóngzi
lit: lock power in the cage of institutions
ex: A phrase associated with Xi Jinping, meaning that power should be constrained by rules and institutions.

en: putting stability first and seeking progress within stability
q: putting stability first and seeking progress within stability
py: wěn zì dāngtóu, wěn zhōng qiú jìn
ex: The general principle of China's economic work, which prioritises stability while pursuing progress. Official documents repeated it as the keynote for 2022.
A principle in Party discourse that the people's interests rank above all else. It is closely linked to the 'people-centred' approach.
The basic stuff of the cosmos in much Chinese philosophy. Gao reads Wang's qi as a material substrate from which all things and mental phenomena arise.
A strand of Chinese philosophy that takes qi, a material-energetic substance, as the basis of all things. The article treats it as the theoretical base of ancient Chinese atheism.

lit: theory of qi as the root
ex: The view that qi, the material-energetic stuff of the cosmos, is the origin of all things. Chinese Marxist scholars often present it as a materialist strand in Chinese philosophy opposed to the primacy of li (principle).
A question posed by the scientist Qian Xuesen: why Chinese universities do not produce outstanding, innovative talent.
A Communist base area in eastern Guizhou (around Tongren), set up in 1934 by He Long's Red Army units.
A set of breathing and meditation exercises with roots in Daoist and other traditions. A qigong boom in the 1980s and 1990s was later linked by critics to mystical movements.
Internet slang for young university teachers, a pun on 青年教师, used for their heavy workload and precarious position.
The name of a series of annual special campaigns run by China's cyberspace authorities to clean up online content and behaviour deemed harmful.
A series of special campaigns run by Chinese internet regulators, led by the Cyberspace Administration of China, to clean up online content and platform conduct.
The Chinese Communist Party Central Committee's flagship theoretical journal, published twice a month.
The authors' term for the structural character of productive forces at a given stage, which they analyse through substantive elements, science and technology, and modes of organisation.
An education approach promoted since the 1990s that stresses all-round development rather than exam results alone.
The authors' label for the core socialist values' intermediate status in adjudication. They are not binding rules or principles, but they may be cited to support legal reasoning.
The author's term for AI as an entity that is not a living, conscious subject but behaves in subject-like ways, such as learning, adapting and generating content.

In Lin's usage, parties to the left of social democracy but distinct from the far left, mostly successors of former communist parties, together with newer left groups. Lin treats the term as vague and internally diverse.

In the article's typology, left parties between moderate social democracy and the extreme left, such as Syriza and Die Linke. They combine social justice with ecological and feminist aims and have given up revolutionary overthrow of capitalism.
The author's label for the Soviet-style model adopted by left parties in power, marked by comprehensive state intervention and priority for state-owned enterprises.
A phrase used in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan for higher education, meaning enlarging places in good institutions while improving standards.

zh: 举旗帜、聚民心、育新人、兴文化、展形象
en: raising the banner, rallying the people, nurturing new people, reviving culture and projecting the country's image
q: raising the banner, rallying the people, nurturing new people, reviving culture and projecting the country's image
py: jǔ qízhì, jù mínxīn, yù xīnrén, xīng wénhuà, zhǎn xíngxiàng
lit: raise the banner, gather popular hearts, foster new people, revive culture, display image
ex: A five-part statement of the mission of propaganda and ideological work, set out in Xi Jinping's 2018 speech.

The strand of Analytical Marxism associated with Elster and Roemer that insists on rational-choice theory and methodological individualism. The article blames it for the decline of the school's economics.
Marx's phrase for the valuable core of Hegel's dialectic, which he held could be extracted from Hegel's idealist system. Zhang Shiying's essay on it is the main text Badiou discusses.
A phrase from Capital, volume 1. It refers to restoring individual property on the basis of cooperation and common possession of the means of production, after the expropriation of the expropriators.
The claim that economic crisis pushes middle-class people into the position of wage-dependent workers, enlarging the proletariat.
An idiom for judging people's moods from their speech and expressions. Mao used it to mean observing how ordinary people eat, dress and feel as a first step in understanding their lives.

An abstraction that arises from the practice and exchange relations of people in society, not from thought alone or from the intuition of things. The article contrasts it with the intuitive abstraction of classical political economy and the speculative abstraction of Hegel.
A notion Liu takes from Albritton: abstractions such as value and abstract labour are produced by capital's own operation, not just by thought.
Counterpart of the "illusory community" in Marx's thought, a community in which individuals develop together. Sun links it to people's democracy.
The part of the economy that produces goods and services, such as manufacturing, as distinct from finance and speculative activity.

The label Marx and Engels gave their own position in The Holy Family (1844–45), drawing on Feuerbach's humanism while turning towards real human beings and their material conditions. Chinese scholars treat it as a transitional stage towards historical materialism.
Marx's starting point in The German Ideology: living people in definite social relations, as opposed to abstract notions of humanity.
A concept from Marx and Engels's The German Ideology. It names the concrete, historically situated people whose material activity is taken as the premise of history.
Marx and Engels's phrase in The German Ideology for communism as an actual historical movement rather than an ideal. It is the central concept of the article.
Marx's notion of the concrete, historically existing subject (living individuals in society) set against the speculative subject of idealist philosophy.
Marx's term for the stage in which labour is wholly subordinated to capital through machinery and relative surplus value. Hardt and Negri use the Chinese rendering "absorption".
An approach, associated in the article with Erik Olin Wright and Sam Gindin, that combines utopian imagination with rigorous analysis of constraints, trade-offs and paths of transition.
The author's term for a practice-orientation grounded in real individuals and concrete social practice, as opposed to idealist or dogmatic versions of practicality.
Marx's term for the sphere beginning beyond necessary material production, where human powers develop as an end in themselves.
Marx's term in Capital, volume 3, for the sphere of material production, where labour is determined by necessity and external purposes.

en: realm of necessity to the realm of freedom
q: realm of necessity to the realm of freedom
lit: kingdom of necessity and kingdom of freedom
ex: Marx's distinction in Capital Volume III between labour imposed by material necessity and the free development of human capacities beyond it. The article treats it as the shape of the transition from capitalism to communism.
The wartime territory in south-west and north-west China under Nationalist control, away from the front, where the CPC also conducted work.
Xi Jinping said in 2022 that the essence of ideological and political courses is to 'reason' with students. The article reads this as a method of persuasion.

en: recognition of data assets on balance sheets
q: recognition of data assets on balance sheets
ex: The accounting practice of recording data resources as assets in company financial statements. Chinese regulators began to allow this in 2024.
The author's key notion: neither a natural unity nor an absolute opposition of body and mind, but a dialectical unity of opposites achieved in practice.
A Party-wide campaign of study, criticism and self-criticism meant to correct ideological errors and bad work styles. The best-known one was launched by Mao in Yan'an in 1942.
A campaign in Cuba in the mid-1980s to correct perceived flaws of the institutionalised system set up in the 1970s.
The Party-wide ideological campaign launched in Yan'an in the early 1940s against subjectivism, sectarianism and Party formalism.
A compiled collection of study texts for Party cadres, first published in 1942 and later expanded, used as the standard reading in the rectification campaign.
The authors' proposed reasoning model. It replaces the minor premise of the classic judicial syllogism with a recursive premise and adds a second minor premise based on a value keyword.
A system of keeping records on puppet officials, awarding red or black points for their conduct. The article describes it as a tool of psychological and political pressure.
A phrase for the revolutionary heritage and political character that the Party says it inherits from its history. It is used in Party education to stress continuity with the revolutionary past.
Named after the boat on Nanhu Lake in Jiaxing, where the First Party Congress's final session was held in 1921. It stands for the Party's founding period.
The official newspaper of the provisional central government of the Chinese Soviet Republic, founded in December 1931 and used here as the main source.
A term for literary and documentary works about the Chinese revolution that are treated as canonical and used in political education.
The sites, documents, stories and spirit associated with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history, used in patriotic and political education.
The heritage of the Chinese revolution under the Communist Party, including sites, documents and the spirit associated with them. It is used in patriotic and ideological education.
Education that uses revolutionary history, sites and memorials to instil Party ideals and patriotic values.

A Party-promoted ethos drawn from the building of the Red Flag Canal in Lin County, Henan (1960–1969). It is summarised as self-reliance, hard struggle, solidarity and cooperation, and selfless dedication.
A Party-theory journal published under the Qiushi Journal group, carrying commentary on policy and ideology.
A metaphor in Party discourse for the revolutionary ideals, values and traditions of the Communist Party, said to be passed down across generations.
A phrase in Chinese official discourse for the revolutionary heritage of the Communist Party, presented as something to be passed on across generations.
A figure for the limits of conduct set by Party rules and discipline, which members must not cross.
Literary and artistic works that depict the revolutionary history, spirit and achievements of the Communist Party and the People's Republic. The category includes films, songs, novels and operas.
Press organs published by the Communist Party during the revolutionary era, such as Red China, used for propaganda and mobilisation.
Sites, relics, stories and spirit linked to the Party's revolutionary and socialist history, used in education and cultural work.
The Red Army's main newspaper during the Long March, used to publish discipline rules, model examples and warnings about violations.

A label for the investigation and statistics work led by the Communist Party in the revolutionary base areas, especially the Central Soviet Area in the 1930s. Present-day official writing presents it as the root of the PRC's statistical system.
Educational trips, often for young people, to revolutionary sites that combine tourism with patriotic and ideological education.
Tourism to sites linked to the Chinese revolution and Party history. The state promotes it for both economic and ideological education purposes.
Museums, memorial halls, former revolutionary sites and similar places that preserve and present the history of the Communist Party and the revolution, used for patriotic education.
The wing of the green movement that aims to replace the capitalist economic and political system. The article contrasts it with "green-green" currents focused on ecological values or technical fixes.
A political coalition of labour or socialist forces (red) and environmental movements (green). The article calls for a stronger and more coherent one.
Trade between the Communist-held 'red' Soviet areas and the Guomindang-held 'white' areas, used to obtain scarce goods and funds.

lit: lighten the load for the grassroots
ex: A policy aimed at cutting excessive meetings, paperwork, assessments and tasks imposed on township, village and community-level officials.
A phrase used in Chinese debate for calculating, well-presented individuals who pursue self-interest while appearing cultivated.
In the Guanzi, a fine, subtle form of qi regarded as the origin of all things and the basis of life and intelligence.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

en: reform of the national supervisory system
q: reform of the national supervisory system
ex: Reform begun around 2016 that created supervisory commissions covering all public officials. They work closely with the Party's discipline inspection bodies.
A 1941 report by Mao Zedong to Yan'an cadres criticising subjectivism and dogmatism in Party study. It was an early text of the Yan'an rectification movement.

zh: 区域全面经济伙伴关系协定
py: Qūyù Quánmiàn Jīngjì Huǒbàn Guānxì Xiédìng
ex: A free trade agreement among Asia-Pacific countries, including China and ASEAN members, with a chapter on e-commerce.

The constitutional system under which areas with concentrated minority populations set up autonomous organs of self-government within the unitary state. It is presented officially as a basic political institution.

The system by which areas where minorities live in compact communities set up organs of self-government within the unitary state. It was set out in the 1949 Common Programme and written into the 1954 constitution.

A heterodox school of political economy that emerged in France in the 1970s, associated with Michel Aglietta and Alain Lipietz. It analyses capitalism through accumulation regimes and modes of regulation.
A school of political economy, originating in France in the 1970s, that explains capitalism's historical stability through regimes of accumulation and the institutions and norms that regulate them.

zh: 中国共产党纪律处分条例
en: Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China
q: Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China
ex: The Party's main internal code setting out violations and sanctions. The article says it was revised in 2015 and twice more since.

zh: 中国共产党思想政治工作条例
en: Regulations on Ideological and Political Work of the Communist Party of China
q: Regulations on Ideological and Political Work of the Communist Party of China
py: Zhōngguó Gòngchǎndǎng sīxiǎng zhèngzhì gōngzuò tiáolì
ex: An intra-Party regulation issued by the Central Committee in September 2025. It sets out the system, duties, content and goals of ideological and political work.

zh: 中国共产党宣传工作条例
en: Regulations on Propaganda Work of the CPC
q: Regulations on Propaganda Work of the CPC
ex: Intra-Party regulations on propaganda, which the article calls the first basic and principal regulation of its kind.
The State Council regulations governing religious bodies, venues, clergy and activities in China. Wang says detailed rules should be built on them.
A controlled setting in which new technologies or policies can be tested under regulatory supervision before wider adoption.
A regulatory approach in which new technologies are tested in a controlled, limited setting under supervisors' watch before wider rules are fixed.
The official reversal of a wrongful verdict or political judgement against a person, often after death, restoring their reputation.

Lukács's term for the process by which social relations under capitalism take on the appearance of things governed by rational calculation. The article treats it as a product of the opposition between spirit and body and between subject and object.
The process by which relations between people appear as relations between things. Chinese scholars use this term for Marx's analysis of commodity and capital fetishism.

en: rejuvenating the country through science and education
q: rejuvenating the country through science and education
lit: revitalise the nation through science and education
ex: A national strategy adopted in the mid-1990s that gives priority to science, technology and education in economic and social development. The article presents it as part of Deng Xiaoping Theory.

en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
lit: great revival of the Chinese nation
ex: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

A research framework the author proposes for studying the War of Resistance. It combines historical materialism, Chinese historiographical traditions and the narrative of national rejuvenation under Communist Party leadership.
The author's proposed concept: the positive results of efforts to make human relations coordinated, balanced and harmonious. It is not an established official term.
In Marxist theory, the social relations people enter into in producing their means of life, above all relations of ownership and of control over production.
Engels's idea, developed in his 1890s letters, that ideology and the state develop by their own logic and react on the economic base while still being determined by it ultimately.
Marx's term in Capital for the workers made redundant by rising capital intensity. They form an 'industrial reserve army' that holds down wages and compels workers to accept exploitation.

en: relaxing the first line and controlling the second line
q: relaxing the first line and controlling the second line
lit: loosen the first line, control the second line
ex: The principle of freer movement across the border between the zone and Hong Kong (the first line), with strict controls on the boundary between the zone and the mainland interior (the second line).
A view, criticised here as Western in origin, that treats religion as a form or the essence of culture.
The author's term for university courses in philosophy, history, literature, traditional culture and similar fields that necessarily include religious knowledge, as distinct from preaching.
Feuerbach's idea that humans project their own essence onto God, and that this projected God then dominates them. The article contrasts it with religious objectification.

Refers to privileges that foreign missionaries and Chinese converts held under nineteenth-century unequal treaties, placing them partly outside Chinese jurisdiction. The author applies it to the US International Religious Freedom Act as a "new" form.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for violent or radical religious movements, which the article treats as a threat to national security.
Term used by Chinese atheism scholars for a perceived rise in religious interest and activity in society.
The management of religious affairs by the Party and state, which the author says Marxist religious studies should support with research and policy proposals.

An official term for activities by foreign forces that use religion, in the author's definition, to undermine the state and socialist system. It is applied here to campus proselytising and "cultural preaching".
A sociology-of-religion approach that treats religion as a market. The author understands it as a call to open China to religion and to resist state regulation.
The expectation that religious bodies manage and restrain themselves in line with law and Party policy. It is one of the four elements of the framework the author describes.

The academic study of religion as a discipline. In the article, the term is contested between a Western tradition associated with Max Müller and a Marxist tradition that the author wants to establish as orthodox.
The view that nature and the world are directed by a divine purpose or design. Marx, following Epicurus, rejected this in his dissertation.
The term used in China for the Party and state's management of and policy towards religious affairs and believers.

zh: “不忘初心、牢记使命”主题教育
en: "Remain true to the original aspiration" campaign
q: "Remain true to the original aspiration" campaign
py: “bú wàng chūxīn, láojì shǐmìng” zhǔtí jiàoyù
lit: Do not forget the original aspiration, keep the mission firmly in mind thematic education
ex: A Party-wide education campaign proposed in the 19th Party Congress report and later carried out in 2019.
A concept from Mao Zedong's writings on intellectuals, meaning their conscious change of outlook through study of Marxism and contact with the masses.
Benevolence or humaneness, the supreme Confucian virtue, centred on caring for others by extending one's own feelings to them.
The national currency issued by the People's Bank of China from 1 December 1948, before the People's Republic was founded.

The policy of increasing the use of China's currency in cross-border trade, finance and reserves. It began in 2009 and was restated at the 20th Party Congress as something to be advanced in an orderly way.
Vietnam's Doi Moi reform programme, launched at the Sixth Party Congress in 1986, moving the country towards a market-based economy under Communist Party rule.
The Chinese rendering of Vietnam's Đổi Mới policy, launched at the CPV's 6th Congress in 1986. It moved Vietnam from a planned, closed economy towards a market-oriented, open one.
The wartime land policy that capped landlords' rents and loan interest rather than confiscating land, in order to sustain the united front against Japan.

A wartime base-area agrarian policy lowering rents and interest while requiring tenants to pay the reduced amounts. It replaced land confiscation in order to keep landlords within the anti-Japanese united front.
Efforts to gain income by influencing government regulation, licences or quotas rather than by producing wealth; a standard concept in political economy.
A concept coined by Hussein Mahdavy in 1970 for states that regularly receive large external rents, such as oil revenues, and so depend little on taxing their own society.

lit: system of requesting instructions and reporting
ex: A Party discipline system, set out by Mao in 1948, under which subordinate bodies seek instructions beforehand and report afterwards to the centre.
Lefebvre's lived space: the imagined and bodily experience of space through symbols, art and everyday life.
Lefebvre's conceived space: plans, knowledge, codes and blueprints that order social relations and are tied to those who design space.
Rule through elected representatives. The article presents its "governance deficit" as an opening for populists.
The processes, including household work, childbearing and consumption of means of subsistence, by which the working population is renewed from day to day and across generations.

An approach that treats the Republic of China period (1911–1949) as an era of modern nation-state building and stresses empirical research. The article says it influenced Japanese scholarship in the 1980s and 1990s.
Yang Geng's signature scholarly proposal from the 1990s. It calls for returning to Marx's texts and historical context while starting from present-day practice.
Teams of cadres sent by higher-level organisations to live and work in villages, used in poverty alleviation and rural revitalisation.
Cities able to withstand, adapt to and recover from disasters, accidents and other shocks. The term appears in recent central policy documents on urban safety.

lit: Resist America and aid Korea movement
ex: The mass political campaign launched in China from late October 1950 to support the Chinese People's Volunteers in the Korean War through propaganda, donations, enlistment and production drives.

py: wěidà Kàng Měi Yuán Cháo jīngshén
lit: great spirit of resisting America and aiding Korea
ex: A set of values, summarised by Xi Jinping in 2020, comprising patriotism, revolutionary heroism, optimism, loyalty and internationalism.

zh: 关于若干历史问题的决议
en: Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party
q: Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party
py: guānyú ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
ex: A resolution approved in principle at the Seventh Plenum in 1945 and formally adopted in 1945. It assessed the Party's past line struggles, especially the 'Left' errors of the early 1930s.

zh: 党的十九届六中全会决议
en: the Resolution on the Party's century of struggle
q: Resolution on the Party's century of struggle
py: Dǎng de shíjiǔ jiè liù zhōngquánhuì juéyì
lit: Resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's century of struggle
ex: The third historical resolution of the Communist Party, adopted in November 2021, which sums up the Party's history and affirms Xi Jinping Thought.

zh: 党的百年奋斗重大成就和历史经验的决议
en: Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century
q: Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century
py: dǎng de bǎinián fèndòu zhòngdà chéngjiù hé lìshǐ jīngyàn de juéyì
ex: The third historical resolution of the Communist Party of China, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in November 2021. It sums up the Party's first century and lists ten lessons of historical experience.
Rosa's term for a responsive, non-alienated relationship between people and the world. The article presents it as a way to counter alienation caused by acceleration.
The author's own concept for an influence that rests on historical links and emotional and selective affinity rather than on direct textual citation or systematic study.
A traditional Chinese social norm of honouring teachers and treating education as important. Official discourse presents it as a virtue to be revived.
A concept in the ethics of technology. It refers to the difficulty of assigning moral responsibility when an autonomous system causes harm and no human clearly controlled the outcome.
A Party mechanism, formalised in 2015, that makes Party committees and leading cadres accountable for ideological and propaganda work in their areas.

An international norm, first proposed by the ICISS, holding that the international community may act when a state fails to protect its civilians from mass atrocities. The article presents it critically, as a vehicle for Western intervention.
Ordinarily a religious notion of karmic payback. The article argues that Marx used it in a materialist sense, for the objective causal consequences of colonial oppression.
A research trend in Chinese Marxist philosophy around the turn of the century, calling for rereading Marx's original texts rather than later interpretations.
Lü's term for popular historical writing that revises established judgements on the Soviet Union, the Comintern and the Chinese revolution, which Lü treats as a form of historical nihilism.
The author's method of finding a scientific form for Marx's philosophy by examining the internal limits of the natural and social sciences in turn.
Chen's term for the process, in 1987–89, of using Western Marxism to re-examine and criticise Soviet-textbook Marxism.
Mei's proposal that recommendation algorithms also show users content outside or opposed to their preferences, to widen the range of information they receive.
In communist usage, a charge against those accused of abandoning or diluting the core principles of Marxism-Leninism. Traditional parties apply it to deviations from the Soviet standard.

A phrase used in Chinese scholarship on world socialism for a hoped-for recovery of socialist movements after the setbacks of the early 1990s. The article presents communist-party cooperation as helping this process.
Phrase drawn from Engels's preface to the English edition of Capital, Volume I. The article uses it to argue that new scientific insights transform a discipline's technical vocabulary.
Engels's phrase in the preface to the English edition of Capital: every new scientific insight brings a revolution in the terms of that science. The authors use it to call for new Chinese concepts.
Mao's 1919 term for a non-violent, "bloodless" form of change. The masses press the powerful with persistent appeals for bread, freedom and equality.
An approach that equates modern Chinese history with the history of the revolution and of the Chinese Communist Party. The article says Japanese scholars began to question it in the 1970s.

Objects and sites associated with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history, such as former headquarters, documents and personal items, protected as state heritage and used in patriotic education.

The official term for the culture formed during the Party-led revolution, including the spirits of Jinggangshan, the Long March and Yan'an. It is one of three cultural sources, with fine traditional culture and advanced socialist culture, that Party discourse emphasises.
The phrase Lenin used for what he saw as the decisive element of Marxism: flexible tactics suited to changing conditions, instead of repeating a fixed model.

The set of concepts, categories and ways of speaking about revolution that express and shape a body of revolutionary thought. The article treats it as the outward form of Marxist revolutionary theory.
A Party term for courage and readiness for self-sacrifice in the revolutionary cause. It is one of the five components of the Korean War spirit.
An approach that periodises and judges historical scholarship by the stages and values of the revolutionary movement. Chen says it long shaped studies of Marxist historiography.

en: revolutionary ideals are higher than the heavens
q: revolutionary ideals are higher than the heavens
ex: A phrase Xi Jinping has repeated since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to stress that communist ideals take priority for Party members.
The Party's officially shaped account of the revolution and its history, used to convey values and legitimacy.
A Party term for steadfast confidence in the eventual victory of a just cause, even in severe hardship.
A phrase from Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, denoting the unity of changing circumstances and human self-change; the authors treat it as the only real way of transforming the world.
The set of values attributed to the Party's revolutionary history, such as struggle, sacrifice and service to the people, which official discourse promotes as a heritage.

The authors define it as a spiritual quality of the party and masses in a revolution: firm confidence in the revolutionary cause that can become a driving force. It is narrower than class consciousness because it concerns the process of overthrowing the old society and building a new one.
The author's term, citing Luo Rongqu, for a path in which China reaches modernity through social revolution rather than gradual reform.
Henri Lefebvre's late method for studying how cyclical and linear rhythms of body, nature and society interact in everyday life. It treats the control of time as a mechanism of capitalist domination.
The author's phrase for combining military training (the rifle) with political and cultural education (the pen).
A concept drawn from Marx's idea of the metabolism between humans and nature, developed by Foster to describe how capitalist production disrupts natural cycles.
A label the Party's official history applies to Chen Duxiu's line in the late 1920s. It means yielding to the Nationalists and the bourgeoisie, and he was removed as leader in 1927.
Parties such as France's National Rally, Italy's Brothers of Italy and Germany's AfD. They combine nationalism, anti-establishment rhetoric and opposition to immigration and to EU authority.

A Confucian way of weighing moral principle (yi) against material benefit (li). Xi Jinping invoked a 'correct view' of it in 2013 as a guide for China's dealings with developing and neighbouring countries.

lit: strict in scholarship, lofty in conduct
ex: An eight-character motto Fang proposed in 1998 for the CASS Graduate School. It is presented as the school's tradition and scholarly ethos.
In Confucian thought, the paired systems of ceremonial propriety and music that are meant to order society and cultivate harmony.
A system in which local Party and government officials are made personally responsible for the management and protection of particular rivers. A parallel lake chief system also exists.

lit: the road of going to sit the examination
ex: A metaphor drawn from Mao Zedong's remark in 1949, as the Party moved to Beijing, that it was "going to sit an exam". Xi Jinping has revived it to describe the Party's continuing task of proving itself to the people.

A method of ideological and political education that promotes exemplary individuals or collectives for the public to emulate. It has been prominent in Chinese Communist Party practice since the Yan'an period.
Xi's term for China's fine traditional culture as the nation's cultural roots, paired with the soul-line.
The principle of governing according to law. In Chinese official discourse it is usually discussed as 'socialist rule of law', distinct from Western liberal models.

A concept in Chinese legal and political writing referring to the values, beliefs and habits through which a society accepts and practises the rule of law. It is treated as the cultural basis of legal institutions.
Concept from the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014). It covers legal norms, enforcement, supervision, safeguards and Party regulations.
A phrase in Party discourse asking officials to handle reform, development and disputes according to law. Xi Jinping has stressed that major reforms should have a legal basis.
A traditional teacher's ruler used to discipline pupils. Xi Jinping uses it as a metaphor for Party discipline as a standard that restrains and corrects members.
The view, associated with Althusser, that Marx's thought divides into an early humanist phase and a later scientific one separated by an epistemological break.
Region-based economic bodies that exercise ownership of collectively owned rural land on behalf of their members. The 2024 law recognises them at township, village and group levels.
A national programme, with an Implementation Plan issued in 2022, to improve rural infrastructure, public services and living conditions.
The author's term for the overall management of agriculture, villages and peasants, extending beyond farm production to peasants' livelihoods and ways of life.

Movements and projects to rebuild rural society, historically associated with 1930s figures such as Liang Shuming and revived since the 2000s. Zhao criticises some versions as populist and silent on socialism.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to promote overall development of rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress in 2017 to modernise agriculture and the countryside. It covers industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A slogan from a November 1918 speech by Cai Yuanpei, which became a current of thought in the May Fourth era valuing workers and labour.
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for features said to distinguish the Communist Party of China from other parties, such as self-reform and the people's standpoint.
Oversight carried out by a unit within the organisation being overseen, such as administrative supervision bureaus inside governments. Chinese commentators criticise it as weak.
The nationalist, anti-imperialist ideas associated with Augusto César Sandino, which the FSLN combined with Marxism-Leninism.
Health system reforms from Sanming city in Fujian, covering hospital finance, drug procurement and staff pay. The Party has promoted them as a model for other regions.
The reorganisation of Mao's remaining troops at Sanwan village, Jiangxi, in late September 1927. Party histories credit it with establishing Party leadership over the army and internal democracy.

A reformist idea popular in early twentieth-century China that national salvation lay in industrial development and learning foreign technology. The article presents it as Deng's first form of patriotism.
A 1930s idea that the press could contribute directly to national survival in the face of Japanese aggression. It echoes wider slogans of "national salvation" (jiuwang) in that period.
Here a technical concept borrowed from media and internet studies, combining a relational 'field' (场) with a 'scene' (景). The authors treat it as the basic unit through which education is delivered.
Policy usage for creating real-world application settings in which new technologies and products can be demonstrated, tested and scaled.
The effort to give Party theory a rigorous academic and logical grounding. It is often paired with systematization (体系化) in official discussions of ideological work.
Academic elaboration of Party theory in disciplinary terms, so that official ideas become systematic scholarship.
A slogan for a society with a strong reading culture, used in national reading campaigns.
Training schools set up within or alongside army units to train lower-level political and military cadres quickly.
University units responsible for teaching the ideological and political theory courses and for the Marxist theory discipline.
A Chinese academic journal on atheism, science and religion studies, in which this article appeared in 2022.

zh: 科学技术是第一生产力
en: science and technology are the primary productive force
q: science and technology are the primary productive force
lit: science and technology are the first productive force
ex: A thesis associated with Deng Xiaoping in the post-1978 reform period, stressing the role of science and technology in economic development.
The management of ethical issues in research and technology through institutionalised norms, values and rules, a policy area stressed in China's 2022 official document.
Financial services and institutional arrangements designed to fund technological innovation across its life cycle. It is the first of the 'five major articles' of finance named in Party policy.
A term used by Marx and Engels in The German Ideology and later works. Its exact meaning is disputed in the scholarship the article discusses.
State-promoted dissemination of scientific knowledge to the general public, treated in China as a policy task.
Public education in science and scientific thinking, known in China as kepu. It is governed by the Law on Science and Technology Popularization, revised in December 2024.
Marx's method of moving from the chaotic surface of phenomena through successive abstractions to grasp their essential nature.

lit: science and technology standing on its own and strengthening itself
ex: An official goal of reducing dependence on foreign technology and building indigenous innovation capacity. The 19th Party Central Committee's Fifth Plenum (2020) made it a strategic pillar of national development.
The Marxist-based atheist worldview and the academic discipline devoted to it, covering theory, propaganda and education, and research on religion and cults.
The term for the communist theory Marx and Engels grounded in historical materialism and the analysis of capitalism, as distinct from utopian socialism.
Drawn from the Scientific Outlook on Development, a Party guideline that stresses comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable growth.
A term the article attributes to Lenin for Marxism as a class-based but scientific worldview. It is meant to guide the workers' movement against bourgeois and petty-bourgeois ideas.
An official principle holding that lawmaking should respect objective laws of social development. It is usually listed with democratic legislation and legislation in accordance with law.
The author's term for dialectical and historical materialism, the philosophical basis of Marxism as taught in China.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
The term for the socialism of Marx and Engels, based on historical materialism and the critique of political economy, as opposed to utopian socialism.
The view that the methods of natural science should govern all fields of knowledge. The author criticises its extension to ideological and political education.
In Chinese discussions of Italian Marxism, the reading associated with Della Volpe and Colletti that treats Marx's work as a science of society, in contrast to humanist and Hegelian readings.
Efforts to simplify Chinese characters and introduce alphabetic writing, which led to the Scheme for Simplifying Chinese Characters and the Hanyu Pinyin scheme in the PRC.
An image from the novel Journey to the West (the Monkey King's staff). It is used here to mean a steadying anchor of the whole enterprise.
The goal of building a modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced and harmonious by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.
Two goals set by the Party: building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021), and building a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).
Extracurricular activities such as social practice, volunteering and campus events. They are meant to complement formal classroom teaching (the first classroom).
A university record that logs and scores students' extracurricular activities, such as social practice and volunteering, alongside their academic grades.

Xi Jinping's formulation, stressed since 2021–23, that the basic tenets of Marxism must be combined with fine traditional Chinese culture. It complements the first combination, with China's concrete realities.
Mao's phrase from the 1950s for a second effort to combine Marxism with Chinese conditions, this time in socialist construction. It is the Party's term for the search for a Chinese path to socialism.
The international federation of socialist parties founded in 1889, whose leading theorists are often criticised in this literature for economic determinism.
The world of human creations, nature as transformed by human activity and society. The article links Žižek's use of it to Marx's view of nature as a product of industry and history.

en: Second Plenum of the Seventh Central Committee
q: Second Plenum of the Seventh Central Committee
ex: A meeting held at Xibaipo in March 1949. Mao warned there of the dangers of complacency and set out the tasks of shifting the Party's work to cities.

en: Second Plenum of the Seventh Party Central Committee
q: Second Plenum of the Seventh Party Central Committee
py: Dǎng de qī jiè èr zhōngquánhuì
ex: A plenary meeting held at Xibaipo in March 1949, shortly before the founding of the People's Republic. It shifted the Party's work focus from countryside to city.
A record of a student's activities outside formal teaching, such as volunteering and social practice, used in evaluating overall quality.
The Party's clandestine network of couriers, liaison stations and routes. It carried documents, intelligence, supplies and personnel between the Party Centre, white-area organisations and base areas.
A collective term for folk sects and secret societies such as the Yiguandao, which the Party classed as reactionary and banned.
In Party discourse, putting the interests of a faction or "mountain stronghold" above those of the whole Party. Mao treated it as subjectivism in organisational form.
Non-religious groups, such as ICSA, that warn the public about cults and help people harmed by them, as distinct from evangelical Christian counter-cult groups.

en: seeking common ground while shelving differences
q: seeking common ground while shelving differences
ex: A approach associated with Zhou Enlai at Bandung: cooperating on shared aims while setting aside disagreements.
The general tone set for economic work in Party and government planning. It treats stability as the basis and progress as the direction and driving force.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, made central to the Party's ideological line by Mao in the Yan'an period and by Deng Xiaoping later.
A Party watchword for a practical, evidence-based work style, closely linked to investigation and research.

en: seeking truth from facts and emancipating the mind
q: seeking truth from facts and emancipating the mind
ex: Two slogans associated with Mao Zedong and, from 1978, with Deng Xiaoping's ideological line at the start of reform and opening up. They are used here as a summary of Marxist philosophical method.
Luxemburg's term for the workers' movement unifying itself from below through experience and correction of errors, as against the centralism imposed by a party's central committee.
A principle highlighted in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), stressing confidence in China's own path and independent development rather than reliance on external models.
A central concept of Hegel and of Bruno Bauer's philosophy. Wang says the young Marx used it to defend Epicurus' atomic swerve and to place reason above religion.

Education that the learner carries out on themselves through reflection and practice, as distinct from being taught by others. The article treats it as a core topic in ideological and political education.
CPV terms for officials' internal political and ideological degeneration, paired with the 'peaceful evolution' it attributes to Western pressure.

en: self-governance, rule of law and rule of virtue
q: self-governance, rule of law and rule of virtue
ex: An official formula for grassroots governance that combines residents' self-governance, legal regulation and moral guidance.

zh: 社会主义制度的自我完善
py: shèhuì zhǔyì zhìdù de zìwǒ wánshàn
ex: Deng Xiaoping's description of reform as the way socialism improves itself rather than being replaced. Later Party documents repeat it.
The authors' term for the inner layer of the process: explicit, relatively bounded education activities in which the system's own elements interact to form order.

zh: 自我净化、自我完善、自我革新、自我提高
py: zìwǒ jìnghuà, zìwǒ wánshàn, zìwǒ géxīn, zìwǒ tígāo
ex: The 'four selfs' that Party documents name as the aims of the Party's self-reform. The article structures its argument around them.

Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continuous effort to purify, improve and renew itself. Official texts present it as the Party's second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.
Refers to the Party's self-revolution (self-reform), a theme in recent Party discourse that the book treats as a method of ideological education.
A phrase from Chinese Party discourse, used since the 2010s for a party's ability to confront its own problems and correct them. Here the author applies it to the PCE.
A long-standing Party principle of relying mainly on one's own strength, with outside assistance as a supplement. Mao used it in the anti-Japanese war and in the early People's Republic.
A contrast used in Chinese communication discourse between China presenting its own image and having it defined by foreign media.
The late Qing effort, from the 1860s, to adopt Western military and industrial technology.

The standard Chinese Marxist characterisation of Chinese society from 1840 to 1949, under imperialist pressure while retaining feudal social relations. It underpins the claim that the revolution had to be anti-imperialist and anti-feudal.
The Marxist characterisation of modern China, formalised in 1930s debates, as nominally independent but dominated by imperialist powers and retaining feudal relations.
A description used in the Central Committee's August 1944 directive on diplomatic work. It referred to the Party's external contacts, conducted while it was not yet a national government.
A traditional Chinese outlook, found in classical texts, of staying alert to danger in times of peace. Party writers present it as part of traditional culture that the Party has inherited.

en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
q: sense of community of the Chinese nation
lit: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
ex: A key concept in Party ethnic policy, which stresses that all ethnic groups belong to one national community. Official texts speak of 'forging a strong sense' (铸牢) of it.
A term popularised under Xi Jinping from 2015. It refers to the tangible benefits people feel they receive from development and reform, and is used as a criterion for judging reform.

The Chinese term for what is often rendered in Marx translations as sensuousness or the sensuous. It covers perception, bodily experience and practical, object-related human activity, not mere passive sense data.

lit: educated youth going up to the mountains and down to the villages
ex: The movement, strongest from the 1950s to the 1970s, in which urban educated young people were sent to the countryside and border regions. Its assessment is still disputed in China.

A formulation from Marx and Braverman on the split between mental and manual labour under capitalism. The article extends it to a global division of labour between countries holding core knowledge and those doing manufacturing.
A principle written into China's constitution and education law, barring religion from the state education system. The report cites it against campus evangelism.
A mechanism under which judicial administrative bodies select and manage the supervisors, while procuratorates only arrange their participation in cases. It is meant to keep supervision neutral.
The principle that religious institutions and the state should be kept apart, which Chen used against making Confucianism the state religion.

en: separation of religion and state, with religion subordinate to political authority
q: separation of religion and state, with religion subordinate to political authority
py: zhèngjiào fēnlí, zhèng zhǔ jiào cóng
lit: politics and religion separate, politics leads and religion follows
ex: The author's description of China's traditional relationship between religion and government, in which religion obeys and serves state power.
The claim, associated with Perry Anderson's account of Western Marxism, that Marxist theory in the West became detached from the workers' movement. Colletti endorsed it in a 1974 interview.
A group of scholars, including Cohen, Roemer and Elster, who began meeting in 1981 and are regarded as the formal founding of Analytical Marxism.
Kornai's term for the input needs that production plans rest on. The authors generalise it as expectations formed by experience and institutional constraints.
The title of Mao Zedong's 1944 speech at Zhang Sude's memorial meeting. It became the Party's stated fundamental purpose and was written into the Party constitution in 1945.
An official reform aim of shifting government functions toward public services, regulation and macro-control, and away from direct management of the economy.

A model in which manufacturers raise the share of services in their business, moving from selling goods to offering bundled products and services across the value chain. It is promoted in Chinese industrial policy.

lit: serve the people with one heart and one mind
ex: The Party's stated fundamental purpose, a slogan associated with Mao Zedong and written into the Party constitution.

A formulation in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) naming seven priority areas for further reform, such as the economic system, democracy, culture, people's livelihood, ecological civilization, national security and Party building.

Seven priority areas set out by Xi in October 2023 for propaganda, ideological and cultural work. They cover Party leadership, ideology, core values, news and public opinion, traditional culture, the cultural sector and international communication.
The bureau's own framework of seven requirements for managing the pledge process, from specific items to safeguard mechanisms.
A list Xi Jinping used in 2015 of seven political problems among officials. They include opposing the Central Committee's policies and engaging in cliques and factions.

Xi Jinping's extension of the "four histories" (Party, New China, reform and opening up, socialist development) to include 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, 170-plus years of national rejuvenation and the new era.

en: seven parts economics, three parts politics
q: seven parts economics, three parts politics
py: qī fēn jīngjì, sān fēn zhèngzhì
lit: seven parts economy, three parts politics
ex: Chen Yun's formula for the work of finance and economic cadres. It holds that economic work should be central but must be accompanied by political and ideological education.
An enlarged Central Committee work conference held in 1962 that reviewed the Great Leap Forward and the ensuing famine years.

The Seventh National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in Yan'an from April to June 1945. It adopted a new Party constitution and wrote Mao Zedong Thought into it as the guiding ideology.
Mao Zedong's rough verdict on Stalin: seventy per cent achievements and thirty per cent errors. Later Party leaders repeated it as "merits outweigh faults".
The Communist-led base area in northwest China, with Yan'an as its capital, that existed from the 1930s to 1950 and served as the Party's wartime centre.
The name given to the reorganised northward-marching force of the First Front Army after the Eljie meeting. Its formal establishment was announced at Hadapu on 22 September 1935.
Folk ritual healers who claimed to cure illness through spirits. The article treats them as fraudsters opposed to scientific medicine.
A Eurasian political, security and economic organisation founded in 2001, with China, Russia and Central Asian states among its members.
A term for the mixed, cosmopolitan culture that developed in Shanghai through contact between Chinese and foreign influences. The article presents it as open and inclusive.
A Communist-led anti-Japanese base area established behind Japanese lines in North China from 1937, covering parts of Shanxi, Chahar and Hebei. Mao Zedong called it a model base area.
Li's own term for the condition of people living together in society, of which common prosperity is presented as one special, ideal form.

One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy, put forward at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2015. It stresses that all people should share in the results of reform and development, with a focus on social justice.
One of the five development concepts adopted at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2015), holding that the fruits of development should be shared by all.
A phrase for the common cultural and ideological bonds among China's ethnic groups. Official texts pair it with a shared material home, meaning narrowing economic gaps.

zh: 中华民族共有精神家园
en: shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
q: shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
lit: common spiritual homeland of the Chinese nation
ex: A Party formulation for the common culture and values meant to unite all ethnic groups in China, linked to building a sense of community of the Chinese nation.
Singapore's official set of five values, set out in a 1991 White Paper, which stress community over the individual, consensus, racial and religious harmony, and the family as the basis of society.
Zhao's formula for studying Marxism: the history of Marxism, its basic principles, and the classic texts, studied together.
A package of rapid free-market reforms, such as spending cuts, privatisation and removal of subsidies. The authors use it to describe Milei's economic programme from December 2023.

en: shooting the arrow at the target
q: shooting the arrow at the target
lit: to shoot the arrow with a target in view
ex: Mao's image in "Reform Our Study" for linking theory to practice: the target is the Chinese revolution and the arrow is Marxism-Leninism.

lit: big economic provinces carry the main beam
ex: A phrase used by Xi Jinping from 2022 onward, calling on the wealthiest provinces to take the lead in stabilising and driving the national economy.
Baudrillard's idea that in consumer society the object of worship is the sign value of goods rather than the goods themselves. The authors present it as a rival to Marx's theory.
A term in Xi Jinping's discourse on building China's knowledge system. It refers to core concepts that mark a discipline's original theory and are meant to be recognisable internationally.
Netizens who read online content but rarely post; the author sees them as the key group to be mobilised.
Simulated respondents created by prompting a large language model to act as people with specified social attributes. They are used for pre-testing, experiment design and effect testing.

A formula used in official discourse since Xi Jinping's speeches of 2013–2017. It summarises the ancient Silk Road's legacy as peace and cooperation, openness and inclusiveness, mutual learning and mutual benefit, and it is linked to the Belt and Road Initiative.
The market for products and services serving older people.
A phrase for the contribution of older people to social and national development. It is used in Xi Jinping's encouragement of elderly volunteers.
A term from communication studies (Lippmann's "pseudo-environment") for a media-constructed picture of reality. Here it means immersive online settings built to deliver atheist messages.

A collection of Party documents from 1928 to 1941, edited in Yan'an under Mao Zedong's direction and published in 1941 as an internal document. It was a main source for the 1945 resolution on historical questions.
A Confucian virtue of inner authenticity, which Neo-Confucians turned into the principle by which humans and spirits respond to each other.

lit: Chinese-isation of religion in our country
ex: An official policy requiring religions in China to adapt to Chinese culture and socialist society, under Party leadership.

zh: 中国化的马克思主义宗教学
ex: A call to develop the Marxist study of religion in a form adapted to Chinese conditions, in line with the broader project of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.

In official discourse on religion, the process by which religions adapt to Chinese society, culture and political leadership. The article presents it as a long historical pattern, and current policy promotes it under Xi Jinping.
The effort to apply and adapt the materialist conception of history to Chinese conditions. It belongs to the broader tradition of 'sinicizing Marxism'.
The official policy of making Islam adapt to Chinese culture, society and socialism. The article treats it as the core issue of religious work in Xinjiang.

zh: 马克思主义无神论中国化
ex: The process of applying and adapting Marxist atheism to Chinese conditions, as part of the wider adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context.

zh: 马克思主义哲学中国化
ex: The process by which Marxist philosophy is adapted to Chinese conditions, culture and philosophical traditions. It belongs to the wider official programme of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.

Official policy line, stated by Xi Jinping in 2015 and 2016, that religions in China should adapt to Chinese culture and society. Critics abroad often read it as forced assimilation, while Chinese officials present it as guidance.
Marxism applied and developed according to China's concrete conditions, a project associated with Mao Zedong and later Party theory.
Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions, as developed in Chinese Party theory since Mao Zedong.

zh: 中国化马克思主义宗教心理学
ex: The authors' term for a psychology of religion guided by Marxism and adapted to Chinese conditions. They present it as a distinct field within Chinese scholarship on religion and scientific atheism.
Formula Mao Zedong put forward at the Sixth Plenum of the 6th Central Committee in 1938. It calls for applying Marxism according to Chinese particularities and against dogmatism.
A late-1930s intellectual movement, led largely by Communist or left-wing scholars, that sought scholarship rooted in Chinese realities. It followed Mao's call for the sinification of Marxism.
The Western academic study of traditional Chinese civilisation, begun in Europe in the 16th century and based on philology and classical texts.
A required ideological and political course in Chinese universities that explains current domestic and international developments and Party and state policy to students.

The principles for further deepening reform set out at the 2024 plenum: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, institution-building, law-based governance and a systems approach.
The six Confucian classics (Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites, Music, Spring and Autumn Annals), which the author treats as the base of a full cultural system.

Priorities set out in April 2020 in response to the epidemic: ensuring employment, basic living needs, market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and grassroots operations.
Yibin's resource-coordination method: integrating plans, balancing industries, layering policies, diversifying investment, running multiple models and coordinating forces.

lit: six things that must be upheld
ex: A set of principles in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) that summarise the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought. They are: put the people first; be self-confident and independent; uphold fundamental principles and break new ground; adopt a problem-oriented approach; apply systems thinking; and have a global vision.

The article's term for the worldview, values, view of history, view of civilization, view of democracy and view of ecology that it says Chinese modernization embodies. It draws on Xi Jinping's phrasing about the "unique worldview, values, view of history…" of Chinese modernization.

Requirements for targeted poverty alleviation, as the article lists them: precise targeting of recipients, project arrangement, use of funds, household-level measures, assignment of officials by village, and assessment of results.

A formula for teachers of ideological and political theory courses, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019: strong politics, deep feelings, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character.
Xi Jinping's 2019 criteria for ideological and political theory teachers: strong politics, deep feeling, new thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright personality.

Economic policy slogans introduced in 2018 and 2020. They call for stability in areas such as employment, finance, foreign trade and investment, and guarantees for areas such as jobs, basic living needs and supply chains.
A set of economic policy priorities introduced in 2018: stable employment, finance, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment and expectations.
The plan in the 1859 Preface covering capital, landed property, wage-labour, the state, foreign trade and the world market. Capital realised only the first part.

lit: cadres who dare in six ways
ex: A CPV ideal of officials who dare to think, speak, act, take responsibility, innovate and face difficulty for the public good.
A formula agreed by Chinese and Vietnamese Party leaders in 1999: long-term stability, future orientation, good-neighbourliness and comprehensive cooperation.
Xi Jinping's 2014 formulation for children practising core socialist values: 记住要求、心有榜样、从小做起、接受帮助. It is now widely cited in school moral education.
A Red Army force from the Hunan–Jiangxi base area. It set out westward in August 1934 under Ren Bishi, Xiao Ke and Wang Zhen to link up with the Second Army Corps.

The April 2011 congress of the Cuban Communist Party, which adopted the Guidelines of the Economic and Social Policy of the Party and the Revolution. The preface treats it as the foundation of the model update.

en: Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee
q: Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee
py: dǎng de shíbā jiè liù zhōngquánhuì
ex: The October 2016 meeting of the Party Central Committee that adopted guidelines on political life in the Party and regulations on intra-Party supervision.

en: Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee
q: Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee
ex: The November 2021 meeting of the Party's Central Committee, which adopted a resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over its first century.
Provisional regulations for universities directly under the Ministry of Education, adopted in 1961. They set out the Party committee's leading role and the place of political work in universities.
Marx's phrase in his late writings on Russia, referring to the possibility that a society might bypass the capitalist stage and its sufferings. It alludes to the Roman defeat at the Caudine Forks.
Small-scale BRI projects in areas such as health, education and training that aim at visible local benefits, as opposed to large landmark infrastructure.
A term used in early Party documents for the group of activists around Zhang Guotao after the Second Congress (1922). It had a factional sense, unlike the earlier generic meaning of "small group".
A phrase (originally from US policy discourse) for restricting a narrow set of sensitive technologies with strong barriers. The article treats it as a form of deglobalization.

A city that uses digital technologies such as sensors, big data and artificial intelligence in planning, public services and governance. China has run national pilot programmes for such cities since around 2012.
The Chinese rendering of the US foreign-policy concept of combining hard and soft power, associated with the Obama administration.
Economic growth driven by the division of labour, trade and market expansion, without major technological change. Some historians use it for both early modern Europe and Jiangnan.

A concept associated with Hartmut Rosa and with debates on accelerationism, describing the speeding up of technology, social change and the pace of life in modernity. The article adapts it to a historical-materialist framework.
Marx's term for the totality of human social life, formed through production and social relations. It is the basis that determines social consciousness.

A Marxist pair of concepts: social being is society's material life, and social consciousness is its ideas and culture. The authors treat their relation as the basic question of historical materialism.
In cultural policy, the principle that the social and ideological effects of cultural products take priority over economic returns.
A group-level psychological trait pattern and the behavioural pattern it produces. The term comes from Erich Fromm, and the authors trace its roots to Marx and Engels.
The level of civilizational progress of society. Party documents use it mainly for spiritual and ideological-moral progress and for citizens' civilized conduct.
The article's category for groups of people bound by ties such as kinship, class, nation or state. The author derives it from Marx and Engels's writings on forms of association.
A category of historical materialism covering the spiritual side of social life, from everyday social psychology to systematic forms such as morality, religion and philosophy.
A broad set of official mechanisms that record and reward or sanction conduct. Here it means local point schemes giving rewards for volunteer activity.
The view that human societies, nations and races are governed by competition and the survival of the fittest. The article criticises it as a misapplication of natural law to society.

A reformist current that seeks to move towards socialism by parliamentary means and welfare policy. In Chinese Marxist scholarship it is usually distinguished from scientific socialism and assessed critically.
A Party-state term for building the social sphere: livelihoods, public services, social governance and social organisations. It stands alongside economic, political and cultural development.
The idea that knowledge is produced, acquired and passed on through social interaction rather than by isolated individuals. The article treats it as the central theme of the field.

Yuan's own label for Marx's problem of how objective knowledge of historically specific, reified bourgeois social relations is possible. Yuan presents it as the route by which historical materialism becomes concrete.
A notion from Italian operaismo that capitalist production relations extend into every sphere of society, such as the home, school and consumption.
A term the article uses for the social setting in which practice takes place and which, in turn, is shaped by practice. Here it is used within a Marxist account of practice.
The overall structure of a society defined by its mode of production, such as feudal or capitalist society. Changes of social formation are treated as the content of historical development.
The official term that replaced "social management" (社会管理) in Party documents, stressing multiple participants rather than top-down administration.
An official formula for a governance arrangement in which Party, government, social organisations and citizens share responsibility and benefits.
A broad controversy of the late 1920s and 1930s over the nature and stages of Chinese society, linked to disputes over the character of the Chinese revolution.

A Chinese rendering of Marx's idea of a post-capitalist form of ownership. The article reads it as uniting common appropriation of the means of production with individual ownership of what labour produces.
Zhang's own term for the materialist view of social life that Marx reached through classical political economy in 1844, before historical materialism.
Mészáros's term for the way a society organises production, exchange and control; he treats capital as a total mode of such control.
The Party's work of rallying peasants and other groups to join peasant associations, the army and revolutionary campaigns.
A concept in Chinese sociology and Marxist theory describing society as a living organic whole that moves, changes and develops through interaction among its parts.
A Marxist notion of ownership of the means of production by society as a whole, which the author asks whether the digital economy might make achievable.
Brenner's key concept for the rules governing access to the means of production and the surplus. He uses it to explain why capitalism arose in England and not elsewhere in Europe.

The author's term for a new social reality in which virtual and physical spaces interweave in everyday life and social relations. The author distinguishes it from deliberately built VR/AR simulations.
The wider set of relations among people, including political, ideological and cultural ones. Yu holds that relations of production form their core but are not identical with them.
A Marxist-feminist current, associated with Tithi Bhattacharya and others, that analyses how labour-power is reproduced through households and public institutions under capitalism.

A slogan of radicals in the 1848 revolutions, short for the 'democratic and social republic', which sought universal male suffrage plus solutions to the social question. Marx used it for the republic form pursued by the working class, in contrast to the 'bourgeois republic'.
Used here for the broad transformation of society and the building of socialism under Party leadership, rather than an overthrow of the existing order.
Government-linked associations of scholars at national, provincial, city and county levels. They supervise academic societies and connect the Party and government with researchers.
The set of institutions covering social insurance, social assistance, social welfare and special care for veterans and their families.
The author's concept of society acting as both subject and object of critique, derived from Marx's phrase "self-criticism of bourgeois society".

en: social stability and lasting peace and order
q: social stability and lasting peace and order
lit: social stability and long-term order and peace
ex: The overall goal officially set for Xinjiang work. It pairs present-day stability with long-term security.
A radical US school of the 1980s (Gordon, Edwards, Reich, Kotz) that explains long economic cycles through institutional structures that support profitable accumulation, and their breakdown.

The article renders Marx's Gesellschaftskörper / gesellschaftliches Subjekt as the social body or organism, the whole of society's productive sectors. It serves here as the starting point of social-scientific method.
Time as organised and measured by human activity and social relations, as distinct from natural time. The article treats it as an abstract, quantified standard tied to capital.
Broad ideological tendencies circulating in society, such as neoliberalism or democratic socialism. In Chinese academic and Party discourse they are a field of study and of ideological management.

In this usage, a broad Party-led field covering grassroots governance, mass organizations, social organizations and services, not only professional casework. Party committees now have dedicated social work departments.
The author's term for the principle that universities should first serve national strategy and economic and social needs, contrasted with a 'disciplinary logic' centred on scholarly output.
A Marxist category for the growing division of labour and interdependence among producers in large-scale production. The author treats its degree as a marker of the level of productive forces.

zh: 奥地利色彩的社会主义
ex: A slogan of the Communist Party of Austria in the 1980s calling for a socialism fitted to Austrian conditions. The authors see the PdA's theory as its creative continuation.

lit: theory of victory in one country
ex: The thesis that socialist revolution can first triumph in a single country. The article attributes it to Lenin and notes the later Soviet shift to the 'socialism in one country' line.
The guiding principle of Ecuador's 2008 constitution under Correa, linked to the Andean idea of buen vivir. It was presented as an alternative to neoliberalism rooted in local history and culture.
The label for German professors such as Schmoller and Wagner who advocated state-led social reform to reconcile classes. Engels and others used the term critically (Kathedersozialismus).
A strategy proclaimed by Hugo Chávez and taken up by other left governments in Latin America in the 2000s. It stresses national and Indigenous identity and rejects a fixed Soviet-style model.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.
The official name for China's current political and economic system and its guiding theory.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's governing doctrine and system since the reform period. It is presented as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

zh: 建设有中国特色的社会主义
py: jiànshè yǒu Zhōngguó tèsè de shèhuìzhǔyì
ex: The formula Deng Xiaoping announced at the 12th Party Congress (1982) for the Party's line of building socialism suited to Chinese conditions. It remains the Party's central label for its path.
The official name for China's current political and economic system, used since the 1980s. Xi Jinping's formulation refers to a "new era" of it.

zh: 有古巴特色的社会主义
ex: Cuba's slogan, adopted after 1990, for building socialism suited to its own conditions. It echoes the Chinese phrase "socialism with Chinese characteristics".

zh: 社会主义建设者和接班人
ex: The official description of the goal of Chinese education: people who will carry forward the socialist cause.

en: socialist concept of honour and disgrace
q: socialist concept of honour and disgrace
lit: socialist view of honour and disgrace
ex: A moral code of 'eight honours and eight disgraces', promoted from 2006 under Hu Jintao as the basic moral standard of socialist society.

zh: 社会主义核心价值体系
ex: The Party's formulation of the central values that society is expected to uphold, later condensed into the socialist core values.
An official set of values promoted by the Chinese Party-state as the shared ideological basis of society. Shen describes them here as fairness, justice, equality and inclusiveness.
A national goal set out at the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) and in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), aiming to build a strong culture by 2035.

zh: 中国特色社会主义文化
ex: The official term for the culture the Party promotes as part of socialism with Chinese characteristics, combining Marxism, Chinese traditional culture and revolutionary culture.

zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义文化
en: socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era
q: socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era
py: xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì wénhuà
ex: A formulation Xi Jinping first used in 2023 and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) adopted as a core concept. The article presents it as bringing earlier cultural terms together.

zh: 社会主义生态文明建设
ex: A Chinese policy and theoretical framework, prominent since the early 2010s, that links environmental protection to socialist development and treats ecology as part of national construction.

zh: 社会主义生态文明思想
ex: The article's label for Xi Jinping's ideas on ecological civilization, which stress harmony between humanity and nature and link social justice with ecological sustainability.
A term the authors use for labour oriented towards a benign material exchange between humans and nature, as opposed to alienated labour under capital.
A campaign of the early 1960s, launched first in the countryside, aimed at ideological education and class-struggle awareness. It later drew in university staff and students.
A current in the mid-1950s that sought to ground Marxism in human agency and moral values, partly as a response to Stalinism. Thompson's 1957 essay made it the centre of the British New Left debate.

The worldwide association of social-democratic, socialist and labour parties, re-founded in 1951 at Frankfurt. Since the 2013 split its membership has been dominated by parties from developing countries.
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership.

zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
ex: The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.
The author's proposed research topic, set against capitalist modernity, which the author says Western Marxist critiques of modernity left unexamined.
