A question about whether a policy is socialist or capitalist in character. Deng Xiaoping criticised it as an obstacle to reform and proposed judging policies by their effect on productive forces, national strength and living standards.
A creative method, associated with the Soviet Union and adopted in China, that portrays social life realistically while serving socialist aims.

zh: 中国特色社会主义宗教理论
en: socialist religious theory with Chinese characteristics
q: socialist religious theory with Chinese characteristics
py: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì zōngjiào lǐlùn
ex: The Party's official body of thought on religion. It rests on freedom of religious belief, independent self-run religious bodies, and guiding religion to adapt to socialist society.
The LPRP's term for its reform line, launched in 1986 and combining market-oriented reform with continued one-party rule. It is comparable to Vietnam's Đổi Mới and to China's reform and opening up.

zh: 社会主义革命和建设时期
py: shèhuì zhǔyì gémìng hé jiànshè shíqī
ex: The official periodisation label for the years from 1949 to 1978, before reform and opening up.
A goal in the Vietnamese and Lao constitutions and Party documents. It places the Party's leadership within a constitutional and legal framework.

zh: 中国特色社会主义法治体系
en: socialist rule-of-law system with Chinese characteristics
q: socialist rule-of-law system with Chinese characteristics
ex: The official overall framework for law-based governance. It covers legal norms, implementation, supervision, safeguards and Party regulations.
A Party goal, developed from 1979 onward, of cultivating ideals, morality, discipline and culture alongside material development.

zh: 社会主义精神文明建设
ex: A Party policy line, prominent since the early 1980s, to cultivate morality, ideals and culture alongside material development.
The 1950s process of converting private ownership in agriculture, handicrafts and industry and commerce into collective or public ownership. It was declared basically complete in 1956.

In the Marxist-Leninist account, the long period between capitalism and a fully developed socialism. The CPV holds that Vietnam, which moved from small-scale production without a capitalist stage, is within this period.

zh: 中国农村的社会主义高潮
en: The Socialist Upsurge in China's Countryside
ex: A collection of 176 reports on agricultural cooperatives, compiled under Mao Zedong's direction in 1955 and published in 1956. Mao wrote editorial notes for 104 of the pieces.
The Communist youth organisation founded in 1920–22, a predecessor of the Communist Youth League. The article calls it the Party's reserve force and preparatory school.
The CPV's formula that industrialization and modernization must keep a socialist direction. The authors treat it as the principle separating Vietnam's path from Westernization.

zh: 社会主义定向的市场经济
py: shèhuì zhǔyì dìngxiàng de shìchǎng jīngjì
ex: The Lao Party's official description of its economic system, with a leading state sector and several forms of ownership and distribution. It is comparable to the Chinese term 'socialist market economy'.

zh: 社会主义定向市场经济
ex: The CPV's term for Vietnam's market economy under Party leadership, with the stated aim of advancing towards socialism. The article says it was set as the general model for the transition period at the 9th Congress.
Marx's concept of the labour time needed to produce a use-value under average social conditions. It determines the magnitude of a commodity's value.
Marx's term for the higher stage of communist society, free of alienation and compulsory division of labour.
Guy Debord's concept of a society in which social relations are mediated by images. The article treats it as a development of Marx's commodity fetishism.

A term in Chinese Marxist textbooks for the contradictions between the forces and relations of production and between the economic base and the superstructure. They are held to drive historical development.

en: sociology of ideological and political education
q: sociology of ideological and political education
ex: A proposed sub-discipline that applies sociological perspectives and methods to ideological and political education. The article assesses its aims and difficulties.
Kornai's term for a situation where firms expect state rescue and so are not limited by their own solvency. The authors argue the tendency also appears in modern capitalism.
The authors' label for a supposedly more covert, entertainment-oriented and implicit form of historical nihilism, spread through insinuation, parody and online media rather than open denunciation.
The author's term for indirect, entertaining, everyday-style ways of conveying a message, as opposed to openly argued "hard" ones.
Borrowed from Joseph Nye, the term is used in Chinese official discourse for the influence of culture, values and image, in contrast to "hard power" of economic and military strength.
The Han dynasty policy, associated with Emperor Wu, of making Confucian learning the state ideology.
The North Korean principle that the Party, state and society follow a single leader and the Party centre without deviation. The article treats its strengthening as a central result of the Congress.
A principle that all state and social work is organised under the Party's sole leadership. It was codified in the revised Ten Principles of 2013.
The independent Polish trade union founded in 1980. It became the main opposition to Poland's communist government.

py: xiān fù – hòu fù – gòng fù
lit: first rich – later rich – common prosperity
ex: Deng Xiaoping's reform-era formula that some people and regions may prosper first and then help others, leading to common prosperity.
Xi Jinping's formulation that Marxism is the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture the "roots" of theoretical innovation.
Xi's term for Marxism as the spiritual lifeline of the Party's theory, which he says must never be abandoned.

The January 1941 clash in which Nationalist forces attacked the headquarters units of the New Fourth Army in southern Anhui. Afterwards the Nationalist government stopped funding Communist forces, according to the article.

lit: Southern Bureau of the CPC Central Committee
ex: The Party's secret organ stationed in Chongqing, the Nationalist wartime capital, led by Zhou Enlai, which handled contacts with foreign diplomats and journalists.
Cooperation among developing countries in economic, technical, cultural and other fields, associated with the Bandung Conference of 1955.
The rural base areas, spread over more than ten provinces, where the Party set up Soviet governments. The best known are Jinggangshan and the Central Soviet Area.
A slogan the author attributes to critics who hold that Soviet-era Marxism, especially under Stalin, departed from Marx's thought and misled the Chinese revolution.

The system of centralised command planning, dominant public ownership and concentrated Party-state power that took shape under Stalin. It was later transplanted to Eastern Europe after the Second World War.
The Party's term for its 1927–1937 revolutionary stage, when it built Soviet-style governments in rural base areas. It is also called the Agrarian (Land) Revolution.
The codified, orthodox presentation of Marxist philosophy and political economy of Soviet manuals, which dominated Chinese Marxist research before 1978.
Treating space as a thing in itself, in analogy with Marx's commodity fetishism. It overlooks the social relations embedded in space.
Edward Soja's concept holding that justice and injustice are produced in and through geography. It was developed against universalist theories of justice such as Rawls's.
Lefebvre's term (pratique spatiale) for the everyday activities that produce and reproduce social relations within a given space. It is the first moment of his three-part spatial dialectic.
A shift in Western humanities and social theory, including Western Marxism, towards treating space as a central analytical category alongside time and history.

zh: 资本空间化与空间资本化
en: spatialization of capital and capitalization of space
q: spatialization of capital and capitalization of space
ex: A reading of Marx in Chinese scholarship: capital expands into and reshapes space, while space becomes a form of capital, and the two convert into each other.
A concept associated with David Harvey: capital relieves overaccumulation crises by expanding geographically and deferring returns over time. The article applies it to digital capital.
A land-reform-era practice in which peasants publicly recounted past suffering to build class consciousness and legitimise class struggle.
The Central Committee's intelligence and security organ, set up in Shanghai in 1927 under Zhou Enlai. It protected leaders, chose and guarded safe houses and gathered intelligence.
A provision in the Party's election rules, amended in 2014, that lets candidates beyond the age limit stay in office if the Politburo nominates them and the Central Committee approves.
Areas such as Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen given special policies from 1979–80 to attract foreign investment and test market-oriented measures. They were first called "export special zones".

lit: special abilities of the human body
ex: Claimed paranormal abilities such as reading with the ears or moving objects by thought, widely promoted in China from about 1979. They were debated by scientists and officials through the 1980s and 1990s.
A category in China's Civil Code that includes rural collective economic organisations, giving them legal standing to hold assets and conduct business.
The severe economic crisis in Cuba after the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern European socialist states in the early 1990s.
A proposed locally issued, freely convertible currency for Shenzhen. It was designed and sample notes were printed, but it was never issued.
A national programme, begun about 20 years before 2025, that recruits teachers for rural schools in central and western China.

en: specialised and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises
q: specialised and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises
ex: An official category of small and medium-sized firms that focus on niche markets with advanced technology. They receive policy support as potential leaders in key industrial links.
A government programme label for small and medium-sized enterprises that specialise in niche markets and show innovation capacity; such firms receive policy support.

A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2023, describing the ideal qualities of teachers: ideals and convictions, moral sentiment, wisdom in teaching, dedication, benevolence and the pursuit of promoting the Way.

A concept in Xi Jinping's discourse, used from 2013 and especially after 2021. It refers to the Party actively grasping historical laws, opportunities and responsibilities rather than reacting passively.
Jiao Yulu was a county Party secretary in Henan in the 1960s, held up by the Party as a model of selfless, frugal public service. His 'spirit' is used in Party education as an ideal for officials.
An officially promoted set of values for scientists, including patriotism, dedication, innovation and seeking truth. It is treated as part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage.

zh: 中国共产党的奋斗精神
lit: the Chinese Communist Party's spirit of struggle
ex: A component of the Party's 'spiritual lineage' (党的精神谱系), a canon of named spirits such as the Long March spirit. It stresses perseverance, hard work and pursuit of national goals.

en: the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
q: spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
ex: A Party-defined body of values drawn from the Communist-led guerrilla resistance to Japan in Manchuria, 1931–45. It is one of the officially recognised spirits of the Party's revolutionary history.
A Hegelian-Marxist notion, here used to mean grasping the essential concerns of the present age in theory.

en: spirit of the War of Resistance
q: spirit of the War of Resistance
lit: anti-war spirit; spirit of the War of Resistance against Japan
ex: The official name for the values attributed to the Chinese people's resistance to Japan (1931–1945). It is presented as including patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory.
A term in current Party discourse for fulfilment of people's cultural and spiritual life. It is paired with material sufficiency as a requirement of socialist modernization.
Official term for the ethical, cultural and ideological dimension of development, paired with material civilisation in Party policy since the 1980s.
The official term for building morality, culture and ideology alongside material development. It is often paired with "material civilization".
The article's key term for the subjective drive, confidence and initiative of a people and a Party. It is stressed in the 20th Party Congress report as a complement to material strength.
The author's term for a core value belief on which a person's or a civilisation's inner world is said to rest.

zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
ex: An official list of named "great spirits" (for example the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) said to have arisen in the Party's revolutionary, construction and reform practice. The first batch was published by the Central Publicity Department in September 2021.
The article's term for ideological and religious penetration of other countries, in the author's account carried out increasingly through religious bodies and NGOs.

lit: independence and autonomy in the spiritual sphere
ex: A formulation Xi Jinping used in his June 2023 speech on cultural inheritance and development. It refers to China relying on its own ideas, theory and culture rather than following foreign models.
A positive, proactive mental state in practical activity, treated in Chinese Marxism as part of subjective initiative. It is linked to Xi Jinping's call for "historical initiative".
The article's key notion: a state of mind in which the people are self-aware, confident and self-driven rather than subordinated to others, linked to the idea of 'seizing the initiative' in history.
A concept derived from Marx and Engels's idea of intercourse (Verkehr), referring to the exchange of ideas, emotions and values between people and peoples.
The author's name for the deep logic of cultural imperialism, which pursues strategic interests through ideological and intellectual control rather than direct trade profit.

The official term for the series of named 'spirits' the Party says it formed in successive periods, such as the Jinggangshan spirit and the Yan'an spirit. Official accounts treat the founding spirit as their source.
The official term for a series of named revolutionary "spirits" (such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits) that the Party presents as its spiritual heritage.

The authors' term for a social-wide deficit in mental and cultural life, such as weakened creativity, morality and aesthetic sense. They treat capitalist spiritual poverty as relative poverty, an imbalance between material and spiritual development.
The authors' term for culture that is widely shared and deeply recognised worldwide, by analogy with public goods in economics.
A spirit-communication current of the 1910s–20s. The article says it claimed to be "super-science" and was backed by the Beiyang government.
The belief that the spirits of the dead can be contacted through mediums. The author uses the term, and links it to the New Age, for belief in psychic and spirit phenomena.

The thesis that capitalist elements were emerging within late imperial Chinese society, notably Ming–Qing handicrafts, before Western intrusion. Mao Zedong's 1939 remark helped set the tone for the debate.
The idea, associated with Hegel and later Western sinologists, that China had no internal impetus for change and required external impact to modernize.
A term for the Soviet model of centralised state planning and one-party rule associated with Stalin. Anderson applies it to Mao-era China, which the article disputes.
A standard Party formula for the Marxist stance, way of seeing and way of working that leaders are expected to apply. The 20th Party Congress report stressed it as running through Xi Jinping Thought.

A formula in Chinese Marxist discourse for the class standpoint, worldview and analytical method underlying a theory. Wang takes it from Mao's wording and treats it as the core of Marxism's universal truth.

lit: state common spoken and written language
ex: The official term for standard Mandarin and the Chinese characters. Its promotion in minority areas is a stated policy priority.

lit: standing meetings of the People's Committee
ex: Regular sessions of the People's Committee, abbreviated changhui, at which the central government discussed and decided routine and major affairs.
The government body responsible for administering religious affairs in China, headed by Wang at the time of the interview.
In Lenin's NEP-era usage, capitalism operating under proletarian state control, seen as an intermediate link between small production and socialism.
Official term for the system of state institutions and the capacity to run them. It was foregrounded in the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013).

lit: the idea of the state and the spirit of the nation
ex: The author's rendering of Hegelian categories of the state and the substantial spirit of a people. The author treats them as the core of Hegel's 'totality' category.
A stage in which, as several parties argue, the state increasingly intervenes directly in the economy on behalf of monopoly capital and fuses with it.
A policy introduced in 1953 under which the state purchased key farm products, such as grain, at fixed prices and quantities and controlled their distribution.

A concept from Carl Schmitt, developed by Giorgio Agamben, for situations in which normal law is suspended and sovereign power is exercised. Here it is the frame through which several Western thinkers read the pandemic.
The central state body responsible for drafting economic plans and approving major investment projects.
The class nature of state power, in Chinese constitutional theory; for China, the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance.
The author's term for church bodies that would operate outside the control of the Chinese government.
Firms owned by the central or local state, treated in Party doctrine as the material foundation of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

A political grouping around the Young China Party (founded 1923) and the weekly Xingshi (Awakened Lion), which preached 'statism' and an all-class revolution and opposed communism and the Soviet Union.

en: step up in dimension and level
q: step up in dimension and level
ex: The author's phrase for a qualitative advance in how something is understood or organised. It is used here for civilization, the concept of modernization and human thinking.
A phrase in the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan describing modernization as a sequence of linked stages, each building on the last.
Mao's term for empty, formulaic and jargon-filled Party writing and speech, likened to the old imperial eight-legged examination essay.
A Chinese idiom meaning that outside experience can help one improve one's own work. The author uses it to describe the value of Russian rethinking for China.

en: storing grain in the land and in technology
q: storing grain in the land and in technology
py: cáng liáng yú dì, cáng liáng yú jì
lit: store grain in land, store grain in technology
ex: An official food-security strategy that stresses protecting farmland and advancing agricultural technology to secure long-term grain production capacity.
A traditional principle that national wealth rests on popular wealth, so the state should let the people prosper rather than accumulate in the treasury.
Popular belief in perceptible, supernatural apparitions, which Neo-Confucians such as Zhang Zai distinguished from the 'spirits' they themselves accepted.
A top-level, state-planned framework for international communication, which Xi Jinping has called on China to build with distinctive Chinese features.
A policy category of industries such as new-generation information technology, biotechnology, new energy and new materials, designated as drivers of long-term economic growth.
Holding the lead in shaping events rather than reacting to them. The authors derive it from Mao's military writings and extend it to political and economic work.
In Mao's military writings, the stage at which the PLA moved from defence to a general offensive, which Chinese historiography dates to mid-1947.

A concept Xi Jinping introduced in late 2012, meaning the capacity to hold to long-term strategic goals without being swayed by short-term shifts. It is usually paired with strategic confidence and strategic patience.
A category of top scientists emphasised in Party talent policy. They combine frontier expertise, strategic vision and the ability to organise large-scale research on national priorities.

One of the modes of thinking the Party encourages cadres to cultivate: far-sighted, big-picture judgement of overall trends and direction. The article treats it as the first of nine philosophical methods.

A long-standing Chinese economic policy that seeks to make growth rely more on domestic consumption and investment than on exports. The Party's 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations call it the strategic foundation of economic work.

en: strategy of invigorating China through science and education
q: strategy of invigorating China through science and education
lit: strategy of reviving the country through science and education
ex: A national strategy announced in the mid-1990s that makes science, technology and education central to national development.

en: the strategy of strengthening the country through talent
q: strategy of strengthening the country through talent
ex: A national strategy, reaffirmed in the new era, to cultivate, attract and make use of skilled personnel as a basis for national strength.

en: streamline administration, delegate power, improve regulation and services
q: streamline administration, delegate power, improve regulation and services
ex: A reform programme, launched in the 2010s, that reduces administrative approvals and improves oversight and public services.
Mass demonstrations, rallies, strikes and occupations of public space used to pressure a government. The article treats it as the final step of a colour revolution.

en: strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers
q: strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers
py: qiáng nóng huì nóng fù nóng
lit: strengthen agriculture, benefit farmers, enrich farmers
ex: A formula for rural support policy: building a strong agricultural sector, delivering benefits to farmers and raising their incomes. The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for improving the supporting system.

en: strict management with care for cadres
q: strict management with care for cadres
ex: A Party formula for managing officials. It pairs strict discipline and supervision with support, encouragement and protection.
The Party's policy of tightening discipline and internal management, stressed especially after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

lit: strive to create the first rank
ex: A slogan of striving for excellence in work, here traced by the author to the Soviet Areas period.
An official goal of building China into a country strong in agricultural supply, technology, equipment and industry, emphasised in Party documents since 2022.

A phrase used in Chinese Party scholarship for the present balance of forces between the capitalist and socialist systems. It is often paired with 'capital on the offensive, socialism on the defensive'.
A policy goal, set out in the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plan documents, of expanding domestic demand and supply so that the economy relies mainly on internal circulation.
A national goal of building China into a leading country in education, set out in official plans and stressed at the 2024 National Education Conference.
The Central Economic Work Conference's description of the main contradiction in current macroeconomic operation: a strong production capacity set against insufficient effective demand.
A goal named in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It refers to a country whose trade has strong competitiveness, influence and security, not only large volume.
An approach that builds on the mainstream "One Health" model but grounds disease emergence in historical materialism and circuits of capital.
A current that combines structuralism with Marxism, chiefly associated with Louis Althusser. It treats concepts such as mode of production and class as structural categories.
The author's term for a field that takes the costs paid for development as its object. It covers a theory of the existence of costs and a theory of managing them.
Organised educational trips or courses combining travel with inquiry-based learning, widely promoted for young people in China.

A formula derived from Mao Zedong's 1964 instruction to strengthen research on religion, as summarised by Ren Jiyu. Authors in the text treat it as the basic paradigm of Chinese Marxist religious studies.
A school of South Asian historiography that began with studies of peasant movements. Wang argues that its second generation turned to postcolonial questions and away from Maoist-style movements.
The authors' own coinage for the third general feature of capital: material means of production take on a social power that dominates and enslaves wage workers.
In Party usage, an attitude that acts on assumptions, book knowledge or enthusiasm rather than on investigation of actual conditions. Mao treated it as covering dogmatism and empiricism.
A concept Xi Jinping formally put forward in 2023, meaning that Chinese culture must have its own distinct identity and agency. It is presented as the basis of cultural confidence.

lit: method of inverting subject and predicate
ex: A critical procedure, associated with Feuerbach's critique of speculative philosophy, that treats what Hegel makes a predicate (such as thought) as dependent on its real subject (being). Marx used it against Hegel's philosophy of the state.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: a process that negates something while retaining and elevating its positive elements.
A traditional Chinese philosophical pair, in which "ti" is the fundamental essence and "yong" its practical application. The author uses it to describe how research questions and sources relate.

A pair of categories from Chinese philosophy, used since the late Qing in debates on Chinese versus Western learning. The formula "Chinese learning for substance, Western learning for application" made Confucian values the core and Western technology the tool.

lit: those who take over the shift
ex: The generation trained to take over leadership of the Party and state. Mao made it a major concern in the 1960s as a safeguard against revisionism.
Mao's phrase from 1949 for bourgeois flattery, comforts and temptations that could corrupt Communists who had never been defeated by armed enemies.
The view, based on Mao's 1936 account to Edgar Snow, that Mao became a Marxist in summer 1920.
Adapted from Zarach and Stucke's "super platforms": large internet platform firms that use network effects to control a whole ecosystem. The author treats them as a form of finance capital.
The article's term for the claim that Marx's economic works are critiques of economics whose real concern is the human being. They are not treated as pure economic science.
The claim that workers in the Global South are exploited above the global average, with wages pushed below the cost of subsistence. The idea comes from dependency theory.
An official term for China's huge domestic market, of over 1.4 billion people, treated in Party documents as a strategic economic advantage.
In Marxist theory, the political, legal and ideological forms that rest on the economic base of society.
The power to oversee and discipline public officials. In the contemporary system it refers to the state supervision bodies created by the 2018 Supervision Law.
The 2018 law of the People's Republic of China that sets out the powers and procedures of supervisory commissions, which investigate public officials. It was revised in 2024.
New state anti-corruption bodies created from 2016 and given constitutional status in 2018. They cover all public officials and work jointly with Party discipline inspection organs.
A nationwide cooperative network, set up in 1949, that handles the circulation of farm goods and farm inputs and is promoted as a link between the Party and peasants.
A policy line introduced around 2015 that aims to improve the quality and structure of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity and upgrading industry.

en: support the government and cherish the people, support the army and give preferential treatment to military families
q: support the government and cherish the people, support the army and give preferential treatment to military families
ex: A CPC campaign launched in the base areas after 1942 to improve relations between armed forces, local governments and civilians.
An umbrella term in the article for transnational and global democracy, meaning democratic governance extended beyond the borders of the nation-state.
A term from the Book of Changes, taken up by Zhang Zai. Wang Fuzhi makes it his single cosmic substance: the unity of material qi and its principle in the experienced world.

zh: 党是最高政治领导力量
py: dǎng shì zuìgāo zhèngzhì lǐngdǎo lìliàng
ex: A formulation from the report to the 20th Party Congress, written into the revised Party Constitution. It asserts that the Party's leadership extends over all state organs, the military, and social organisations.
The author's term for workers made redundant by AI-driven automation, linked to Marx's idea of the relative surplus population.
The wartime Soviet practice of taking peasants' surplus grain, and part of their basic ration, for the state. It was replaced by the tax in kind in 1921.
A term describing Party organizations that lose real contact with grassroots society and float above it.
A value outlook that the author builds on the idea of coexistence and mutual benefit. The author offers it in place of egocentrism as the ideological basis of relational civilization.
In Lacan, the realm of language, law and social norms that structures the subject after the imaginary stage of the mirror.

en: the symposium on cultural inheritance and development
q: symposium on cultural inheritance and development
ex: A meeting held in Beijing in June 2023 at which Xi Jinping gave a major speech on culture. It set out the "new cultural mission" including building the modern civilisation of the Chinese nation.

zh: 哲学社会科学工作座谈会
en: symposium on philosophy and social sciences
q: symposium on philosophy and social sciences
ex: A meeting held by Xi Jinping in May 2016 that set out tasks for building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.
Shorthand for Xi Jinping's 2024 instruction to advance ideological and political course construction in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory.

en: system of identifiers of Chinese civilization
q: system of identifiers of Chinese civilization
ex: A concept in the Fourth Plenum's decision (2025), meaning a structured set of symbols, relics and ideas taken to represent Chinese civilization. The article treats it as an organic whole with internal logic and levels.

en: system of ideological and political work
q: system of ideological and political work
ex: The integrated set of links, elements and institutions through which universities carry out ideological and political work. It was the subject of the 2020 guideline from eight central departments.
The body of formal rules governing the Communist Party's own organisation and conduct. It is defined as organised around the Party constitution, with democratic centralism at its core.

zh: 中国特色社会主义制度
en: the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
ex: The set of fundamental, basic and important institutions that Party documents associate with China's socialist path. The Third Plenum (2024) set the aim of continuing to improve and develop it.
Arthur's approach, drawn from Hegel's Logic, which reads Capital as a closed conceptual system unfolding from the value form rather than as a historical sequence.
A slogan in Party documents calling for a comprehensive restructuring of mainstream media institutions, going beyond media convergence.
Xi Jinping's formulation for the task of exposing the structure of the Party's theory and explaining its content with academic concepts and methods.
The authors' term for a state in which the various strong-country fields support one another so the national development system can run independently, without closing itself off.
A crisis seen as affecting the economic, social and political structure of capitalism as a whole, not only its financial sector.
A label for China in the EU's March 2019 strategic outlook on EU–China relations. Zheng reads it as stressing the contrast between the EU's social market economy and a state-led Chinese model.
One of the "six musts" of Xi Jinping Thought. It calls for seeing things as interconnected wholes and balancing the overall and the partial, the short and long term, and so on.

A reform method stressed by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It means organising reforms across economic, political, cultural, social and ecological fields so that they reinforce one another.
A method stressed in Xi Jinping-era Party theory that calls for treating problems as interlinked wholes and planning them comprehensively.
A method stressing development, comprehensiveness, interconnection and the handling of major relationships, which Xi Jinping presents as part of the Party's dialectical method.
A grouping of Latin American left-wing parties and organisations. It first met in São Paulo in July 1990, and the article says it has grown to 110 members.
A term for the loss of public trust in authorities: once a government loses credibility, whatever it says or does is distrusted. It is named after the Roman historian Tacitus.
A term in Party language for trailing behind the masses' spontaneous demands instead of leading them. It is criticised as abandoning the Party's leadership role.

en: take the essence and discard the dross
q: take the essence and discard the dross
py: qǔ qí jīnghuá, qù qí zāopò
lit: take its essence, remove its dregs
ex: A principle for treating cultural heritage, associated with Mao Zedong. It calls for keeping what is judged beneficial and rejecting what is judged feudal or backward.

en: taking class struggle as the key link
q: taking class struggle as the key link
lit: take class struggle as the guiding principle
ex: A slogan associated with Mao's later years. Post-1978 Party documents criticise it as a mistaken line.

lit: to shoulder responsibility and take action
ex: A cadre-management term for readiness to shoulder responsibility and act proactively, including in the face of risk and difficulty. Xi Jinping has made it a key criterion for assessing officials.
The idea that each link of the innovation and industrial chains needs matching types of personnel, so that talent policy should be organised along those chains.
A Party expression for keeping political awareness, loyalty to the Party line and discipline at the forefront of work. Here it is rendered as standing firm on political principle.

zh: 在延安文艺座谈会上的讲话
en: Talks at the Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art
q: Talks at the Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art
py: Zài Yán'ān wényì zuòtánhuì shàng de jiǎnghuà
lit: Speech at the Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art
ex: Mao Zedong's 1942 speeches setting out the Communist Party's line that literature and art should serve workers, peasants and soldiers and the revolution. It remains a foundational text of Party cultural policy.
The label Yibin gave its campaign, borrowing the idea of precision (as in targeted poverty alleviation) to direct Party-building work at specific problems and points.
A policy approach associated with Xi Jinping from 2013. Poor households are identified individually and given tailored support rather than general aid.
The policy, promoted by Xi Jinping, of tailoring poverty relief to specific households and villages rather than broad regional aid.

en: The Tasks of the Youth Leagues
lit: The tasks of the youth league
ex: Lenin's speech to the Third All-Russian Congress of the Russian Young Communist League in October 1920. In China it is treated as a classic text on education and communist morality.
A system of scientific management devised by the American engineer Frederick Taylor, which standardised workers' movements and output. Lenin judged it harsh but scientifically advanced.
A US right-wing populist movement that emerged around 2009–2011, opposing government spending, taxation and welfare. The article treats it as funded by billionaires and as a base of Trump's support.
Official term for the moral standards and professional behaviour expected of teachers, which are assessed and promoted through regulations and campaigns.
A traditional Chinese pedagogical principle of adapting teaching to each learner's abilities and characteristics.
Simondon's concept of the machine as an entity that exists only in relation to its human operators and milieu. Later thinkers extended it to the digital object.
A concept from Carlota Perez for the best-practice model through which a technological revolution is put to use. The article applies it to energy, technology, organisation and institutions.
A thesis, associated with Wark and Varoufakis, that digital platform owners now extract rent from "cloud fiefs" and that society is regressing beyond capitalism.
A reading of historical materialism in which material productive forces alone drive social development, leaving little room for moral values or human agency.
An extension of Marx's idea of fetishism to technology, meaning the worship of technology as autonomous and the obscuring of the social relations behind it.
The claim that digital platform firms act like feudal lords who collect rents from dependent users and workers. It is used by some Western critics of rent-seeking digital capital.
The author's term for the dominant form of contemporary monopoly capitalism, in which market power rests on patents, standards and technical barriers rather than on sheer scale.
The mode of thought in which reason takes the form of efficiency-oriented technique and permeates social life. Chinese discussion draws on the Frankfurt School's critique of instrumental reason.

A way of periodising history by the technological level of the productive forces (fishing and hunting, agricultural, industrial, intelligent), set alongside the Marxist classification by ownership relations.
Mei's proposal that the state publish regularly updated assessments of what current AI can and cannot do, and of how it is likely to develop.
Professionals who evaluate, market and broker technologies between research institutions, enterprises and investors.
A term for the view that technology alone can solve problems, so that other factors are neglected. The author uses it as a mistake to be avoided.
A phrase from Xi Jinping, who has called for "telling China's story well and spreading China's voice well". It is the standard formula for guiding China's external communication.
A ten-point summary of the core tenets of Xi Jinping Thought, adopted at the 19th Party Congress (2017) and later revised.

A 1956 speech by Mao Zedong on balancing relations such as those between industry and agriculture, coastal and inland regions, and the state and the individual. It is regarded in official accounts as an early attempt at a China-specific path of socialist construction.
A summary of the People's Liberation Army's operational principles, which Mao drew up in late 1947 from a year of fighting.
Xi Jinping's summary of the Party's Tibet strategy at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work (2020), a set of ten principles.

The ten items of historical experience listed in the November 2021 Party resolution, including upholding Party leadership, putting the people first, theoretical innovation, self-reform and the united front.
The 1940 policy programme of the Border Region, formally issued by the North China Bureau of the Party, setting out ten tasks in government and ten in other fields.

The standardised, codified presentation of Marxism in Soviet manuals that took shape in the 1930s, such as the 1954 Political Economy textbook. Chinese scholars often criticise it as dogmatic and one-sided.
The study of manuscripts and editions, here the editing and dating of Marx's works in MEGA and similar collections.
The free-market policy programme of British prime minister Margaret Thatcher. The article treats Brexit as its last struggle.
A Party-wide, time-limited study and rectification campaign on a set theme. The 2023 campaign focused on Xi Jinping Thought.
A form of National Assembly oversight that examines how a particular policy or law has been implemented. It is carried out by dedicated teams through report review, field visits and seminars.

In Chinese Party discourse, the main issue or struggle that defines a given period within a larger historical epoch. Since the 1980s official documents have named 'peace and development' as the present theme.

en: theme, main thread and mainstream essence
q: theme, main thread and mainstream essence
ex: A framework from Xi Jinping's letter for interpreting the history of the People's Republic. It is meant to direct historians to the dominant direction of that history rather than to its setbacks.
Mao's term in the 1927 Report for the hierarchy of gods, spirits and ghosts, which he counted among the four authorities (political, clan, theocratic, patriarchal) binding the peasantry.

lit: theory of the justice of God
ex: Originally the theological defence of divine justice despite evil. Chen uses it for the ultimate justification of the whole course of history through an eschatological or messianic frame.
A term of criticism for research on religion that adopts the standpoint or methods of theology instead of scientific, materialist analysis.
The opponent's term for theology done outside the official Chinese churches. Du takes it to mean outside the officially recognised two Christian bodies.
The Party's term for systematic education that equips members and the public with its official theory.
Confidence in the correctness of the Party's theoretical system, part of the official 'Four-sphere Confidence'.
A Party term for deliberate, continuous attention to theory and its innovation as a guide to practice.
A method, traced to Lenin's view that socialist consciousness is brought to workers from outside. It is controversial because critics see it as coercive.
Organised lectures and talks that explain Party theory and policy to Party members and the public. It is a standard part of the Party's ideological and propaganda work.
Study bodies in Party committees and Party leadership groups, made up of leading members and heads of departments, which meet to study Party theory and policy collectively.

zh: 中国特色社会主义理论体系
en: the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
q: theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics
py: Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì lǐlùn tǐxì
ex: The official name for the body of Party theory from Deng Xiaoping Theory onwards, presented as the latest stage of the sinification of Marxism.
The authors' term for the central questions a body of theory sets out to answer. They distinguish it from the theme of the times, the theme of practice and the theme of a Party congress.
The author's term for foreign readings that, in his view, go beyond the historical context and content of Mao's text and impose external frameworks on it.
Based on Engels's 1890 letter to Joseph Bloch, which says historical outcomes result from many intersecting individual wills. It is used here to treat the upheaval as the product of many forces.

A strand of Chinese Marxist scholarship that systematises Marx's and Engels's remarks on the free and all-round development of the individual into a theory. It is treated as part of Marxist philosophy and related fields.

A principle drawn from Lenin, who held that socialist consciousness must be brought to the working class from outside. Chinese scholars treat it as the starting point of ideological and political education.
The view, held by Plato, Descartes and others, that some principles are present in the mind before experience. Locke attacked it in Book I of his Essay.
The defeatist view in the early war that China could not resist Japan and would inevitably be conquered. Mao's work rebuts it.
A label for Engels's argument that nature reacts against human conquest of it, drawn mainly from "The Part Played by Labour in the Transition from Ape to Man" and Dialectics of Nature.
Dühring's view, criticised by Engels in Anti-Dühring, that political force is the primary determinant of economic life and property relations.
The opposite view that China could defeat Japan rapidly. Mao criticised it as underestimating the enemy.
Marx's analysis, in volume 2 of Capital, of how the total social capital is reproduced and its products sold. Lenin used it against Narodnik and bourgeois market theories.

The Marxist-Leninist view that human cognition reflects an objective, material reality existing independently of consciousness. Wang discusses it in an 'active' (能动的) form, stressing the subject's activity.
The authors' label for Marx's epistemology, which they distinguish from simple mirroring (reflection theory). On this view the mind creatively reworks reflected objects to grasp their essence.

en: theory of skipping a social formation
q: theory of skipping a social formation
lit: theory of leaping across social formations
ex: The idea, drawn from Marx's late writings on Russia, that a country with surviving communal landownership might reach socialism without passing through full capitalist development. Chinese scholars use it to discuss the possibility of 'skipping' stages in backward countries.

en: theory of the articulation of modes of production
q: theory of the articulation of modes of production
lit: theory of the connection of modes of production
ex: A 1970s Marxist approach, associated with Laclau, Rey and Taylor, that explains underdevelopment through the coexistence and interaction of capitalist and non-capitalist modes of production.
The author's term for Althusser's focus on the conjuncture (conjoncture), the concrete convergence of forces from which events arise.

A strand of historical materialism that treats society as an interrelated, evolving whole rather than a fixed structure. Marx's image of society as 'an organism capable of change' is the usual reference point.

lit: theory of dividing the three worlds
ex: Mao Zedong's early-1970s scheme placing the United States and the Soviet Union in the first world, other developed countries in the second, and developing countries in the third. China counted itself in the third.

Marx's analysis, in the first chapter of Capital, of how the value of a commodity must be expressed in another commodity and finally in money. It is central to the New Reading of Marx and related schools.

In Marxist usage, the account that capital's expansion and the world market turn local histories into one interconnected global history. Chinese scholars treat it as a core part of historical materialism.

en: the thesis that Confucianism is a religion
q: thesis that Confucianism is a religion
lit: the theory that Confucianism is a religion
ex: Ren Jiyu's view, put forward in the early 1980s, that Confucianism developed into a religion with a distinctive form suited to feudal China. It was debated widely in Chinese scholarship.

en: thesis that the spirit perishes with the body
q: thesis that the spirit perishes with the body
lit: theory of the extinction of spirit
ex: Fan Zhen's fifth-to-sixth-century argument against the Buddhist doctrine of an immortal soul.

lit: Third Bureau of the Military Commission
ex: The Communications Bureau of the Central Military Commission, which managed radio and telephone communications for the Party and the Communist-led armies during the war.

zh: 第三次中央新疆工作座谈会
py: dì-sān cì zhōngyāng Xīnjiāng gōngzuò zuòtánhuì
ex: A high-level Party meeting on Xinjiang policy held in 2020, at which Xi Jinping spoke. The article cites his call to uphold the Sinicization of Islam in Xinjiang.
Distribution through voluntary donations and charity, following primary distribution (market) and redistribution (state taxes and transfers).
Voluntary redistribution of wealth through charity and donations, treated in official discourse as a supplement to market distribution (first) and government redistribution (second).
A programme from the mid-1960s to the 1970s that built industrial and defence facilities in China's interior for war preparedness.
The 2021 Central Committee resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over its first century. It follows the resolutions of 1945 and 1981.
The 1923 Congress held in Guangzhou, which endorsed cooperation between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang. It also revised the Party constitution for the first time.
A Comintern doctrine adopted around its Sixth Congress (1928). It held that capitalism was entering a final crisis, and it called for a sharp turn to the left.

en: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978)
q: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978)
py: Dǎng de shíyī jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
ex: The December 1978 meeting of the Communist Party's Central Committee, regarded as the starting point of reform and opening up and of the move away from "Left" policies.

en: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978)
q: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978)
ex: The December 1978 meeting that marked the start of reform and opening up and shifted Party work towards economic modernisation.

en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
q: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
py: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
ex: The plenary session of July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively.

en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
q: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
ex: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization.

en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
q: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
py: Zhōnggòng Èrshí Jiè Sān Zhōng Quánhuì
ex: The July 2024 plenary meeting of the Party's Central Committee, which adopted a decision on deepening reform comprehensively.

en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
q: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
ex: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform.

A centre-left political approach of the 1990s, associated with Tony Blair's Labour Party, that accepted market-oriented policies while claiming to go beyond both old social democracy and neoliberalism. The article treats Australian Labor's adoption of it as a compromise with neoliberalism.
A Cold War term for countries outside the capitalist and socialist blocs. Mao Zedong's 1974 'three worlds' formulation placed China among the Third World.
The list of thirteen principles adopted at the 2023 National Organization Work Conference to summarise the core content of Xi's thinking on Party building.
A mode of thinking rooted in the Book of Changes, in which opposite pairs such as yin and yang generate change through interaction. Tian Chenshan treats it as the base of "Chinese dialectics".

lit: thought on governing the country and managing state affairs
ex: A label for Xi Jinping's speeches and ideas on state governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In 2017 it served as a main reference for his theoretical contribution.
A rural environmental and village improvement programme launched in Zhejiang in 2003 under Xi Jinping, now promoted as a model for rural revitalization nationwide.

en: Three Bestowals and One Conducive To
q: Three Bestowals and One Conducive To
py: sān gè fùyǔ, yī gè yǒulìyú
ex: Xi Jinping's formula for Tibet's development, used in the text as a general requirement for its economic and social work. The article does not spell out its content.
Lenin's account of Marxism as made up of philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. It follows Engels's earlier division in Anti-Dühring.
A policy formula from the Third Plenum Decision directing state capital towards national security and key sectors, public services and strategic emerging industries.
Xi's 2021 formulation naming three groups of personnel for religious work: Party and government cadres, religious representatives, and researchers on religion.

A 1943 formulation by Mao that Marxism should be deeply combined with China's revolutionary practice, history and culture. The article treats it as the point at which culture entered the idea of integration.

A principle promoted by Xi Jinping for handling cadres' mistakes. It asks Party organisations to distinguish error from misconduct, exploratory error from wilful wrongdoing, and unintended from deliberate fault.
A formula taken from Xi Jinping: fairness of rights, of opportunity and of rules, as the main content of a social fairness guarantee system.

lit: three 'whether it is beneficial to' criteria
ex: Deng's criteria from his 1992 southern tour for judging reform: whether it promotes productive forces, increases national strength and raises living standards.

lit: three great fine styles of work
ex: Mao Zedong's formulation at the Seventh Congress (1945): integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, and self-criticism.
Official term for terrorism, separatism and religious extremism, used in Chinese policy discourse on Xinjiang. The article adopts the official characterisation.
A system in which village funds, assets and resources are managed on the village's behalf by the township. Xiao presents it as a way of regulating rural finances.
The Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative and the Global Civilization Initiative, put forward by Xi Jinping between 2021 and 2023.

lit: three goings down to the countryside
ex: A long-running summer programme in which university students take culture, science and technology, and health services to rural areas. Education support teaching is a common form.
The Party's three resolutions on history, from 1945, 1981 and 2021, which assess its past and set an authoritative line on major events and figures.

Official shorthand for the laws governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and the development of human society. The Party presents deepening understanding of them as a basis of its theory.

A zoning-based environmental management framework made up of ecological protection red lines, environmental quality bottom lines, resource utilisation ceilings and an environmental access negative list. Localities are directed to build it.
Mao's summary of the Party's revolutionary experience: the united front, armed struggle and Party building.

en: Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention
q: Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention
py: sān dà jìlǜ bā xiàng zhùyì
ex: Conduct rules for Red Army and later People's Liberation Army soldiers, first formulated under Mao Zedong in 1928. They govern relations with civilians, such as not taking property.
Political, military and economic democracy in the Red Army, including soldiers' committees that took part in management and supervised officers.
The differences between town and country, workers and peasants, and mental and manual labour. Marxist tradition expects socialism to abolish them.

en: three major questions of the era
q: three major questions of the era
ex: In the Party's formulation, the three questions Xi Jinping Thought sets out to answer: what socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold and how, what modern socialist country to build and how, and what long-governing Marxist party to build and how.
A basic system of Party branch life: regular branch meetings, branch committee meetings, small group meetings and Party lectures.
Xi Jinping's 2018 formulation: founding the Communist Party, founding the PRC, and reform and opening up with socialism with Chinese characteristics.

A formula Xi Jinping presented at the 20th Party Congress (2022), urging the whole Party to keep its original aspiration and mission, stay modest and hardworking, and dare to struggle. It echoes Mao Zedong's 1949 "two musts".

Shorthand for new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups, such as private firms, non-governmental bodies and platform or gig workers. Party documents treat them as priority areas for Party building.
A statistical category covering new industries, new business forms and new models, used to measure the share of emerging activity in GDP.

lit: Party building in the three new
ex: Shorthand introduced in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) for Party building in new economic organizations, new social organizations and new employment groups.
An anti-corruption formula: officials should be unable, unwilling and not daring to be corrupt, combining deterrence, institutional constraint and ideological education.
Japan's long-standing policy of not possessing, not producing and not permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons.
Vietnam's declared defence-policy stance: no military alliances, no foreign military bases on its soil, and no reliance on one country against another.
An official line on special functions: no further publicity in the press, no criticism and no organised debate until the science was settled. Tu says it left criticism absent.
Deng Xiaoping's 1983 inscription that education should face modernization, the world and the future.
Shorthand for a person's worldview, outlook on life and system of values. It is a standard term in Chinese education and ideological work.
An official description, used from about 2013, of the simultaneous slowdown in growth, structural adjustment pains and digestion of earlier stimulus policies.
A Party formulation for political judgement, political understanding and political execution, which officials are asked to build.
Sun Yat-sen's political doctrine of nationalism, democracy and people's livelihood, later the ideology of the Kuomintang.
Zhu De's ideological, organizational and military consolidation of the surviving uprising troops in late 1927. Party history treats it as a model of 'political army-building'.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

zh: 思想、技术、文化三大革命
py: sīxiǎng, jìshù, wénhuà sān dà gémìng
lit: the three great revolutions of ideology, technology and culture
ex: A long-standing DPRK line for building socialism through ideological remoulding, technical modernisation and cultural advance. The congress reaffirmed it, with ideological work placed first.

A rural land arrangement that separates the collective's ownership right, the household's contracting right and the operator's land-management right, so that land use can be transferred while contracting rights stay with farm households. It became national law through the 2018 revision of the Rural Land Contracting Law.
A shorthand for problems of agriculture, rural areas and farmers, used in Chinese policy since the late 1990s.
A Party education campaign launched around 1998 under Jiang Zemin. It stressed study, politics and integrity among officials.

A 2014–2015 Party education campaign for leading cadres. It stressed being strict in self-cultivation, power use and self-discipline, and honest in conduct, in starting a career and in dealing with people.
The disciplinary, academic and discourse systems that Chinese leaders call on scholars to build, so that Chinese social science has its own distinctive framework.

zh: 中国特色历史学三大体系
py: Zhōngguó tèsè lìshǐxué sān dà tǐxì
lit: the three major systems of historiography with Chinese characteristics
ex: Refers to the discipline system, academic system and discourse system of history. The formula derives from Xi Jinping's 2016 call to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

The traditional pairing of Confucianism, Buddhism and Daoism as China's main intellectual and religious traditions. The author also notes an older sense referring to the Xia, Shang and Zhou cultural traditions.

lit: three major battles to storm fortifications
ex: The official priorities of preventing major financial risks, targeted poverty alleviation and pollution control.
Mao Zedong's definition of a class for itself as a proletariat that understands the essence of capitalist society, the exploitative relations among classes, and the proletariat's historical task.
An official label for content deemed vulgar, kitsch and low in taste. It has been used in Chinese media regulation since around 2009–2010.
A Russian Social-Democratic slogan summarising the minimum programme of the democratic revolution: a democratic republic, confiscation of landlord land, and the eight-hour working day.
Mao's 1945 summary of the Party's distinguishing practices: integrating theory with practice, close ties with the people, and self-criticism.
The three targets of the 1942 campaign: subjectivism in study, sectarianism in Party work, and stereotyped Party writing.
Mao Zedong's 1970s division of the international order into the superpowers, other developed states and the developing countries. It placed China among the third world.
A campaign launched in 1951 against corruption, waste and bureaucracy within Party and state organs.
A campaign launched in 1951–52 against corruption, waste and bureaucracy within Party and government organs. The Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan case was an early prominent example.
Yang Fenggang's model dividing China's religious sphere into a red market (officially recognised), a black market (groups the state classes as "evil cults") and a grey market (ambiguous status).
The author's own framework combining systematic research, scenario-based communication and coordinated advancement in theory dissemination.

lit: 'three views' education (hate, despise, look down on US imperialism)
ex: An ideological campaign during the movement that sought to teach hostility, contempt and disdain towards the United States and to remove pro-American or fearful attitudes.
A macroeconomic framework that combines stabilisation, growth and structural policies. The article presents it as an alternative to purely demand-side countercyclical regulation.
An official description of China's economy as being simultaneously in a period of slower growth, structural adjustment and digestion of earlier stimulus policies.
The principles of self-governance, self-support and self-propagation for Protestant churches in China, associated with the officially recognised Three-Self Patriotic Movement founded in the 1950s.
The officially registered Protestant church in China, organised under the Three-Self Patriotic Movement. Unregistered Protestant congregations are commonly called house churches.

Deng's phased plan, written into the 13th Party Congress report (1987): secure basic subsistence, reach a moderately prosperous level by 2000, then reach the level of a mid-developed country by the mid-21st century.
A system of power-sharing in the anti-Japanese base areas. Communists, non-Party left-progressives and middle-of-the-road figures were each to hold roughly one third of government seats.
A model used in the Communist-led base areas in which Communists, left-progressives and middle forces each held roughly one third of government seats.

lit: education by all staff, through the whole process, in all dimensions
ex: An official policy concept requiring that all staff, every stage of schooling and every aspect of campus life contribute to students' ideological and moral education.

A classical Chinese notion of "all under heaven", describing a harmonious political order beyond the nation-state. Some Chinese scholars use it as a source for non-Western international relations theory.

lit: joint governance of all under heaven
ex: The article's term for a vision of shared global governance. It draws on the traditional Chinese notion of tianxia, 'all under heaven'.
An anarchist journal founded in Tokyo in 1907 by Liu Shipei and He Zhen. It published translated Marxist texts alongside anarchist writing.
Xi Jinping's shorthand for pursuing both senior officials ('tigers') and low-level officials ('flies') in the anti-corruption campaign.
The article's term for the gap in years or centuries between countries in reaching a given stage of capitalist development. It is Xu's own synthesis, not a phrase Marx or Engels used.

A concept used in Chinese scholarship for latecomer modernization, in which stages that took centuries elsewhere are compressed into a short period. The author applies it to nineteenth-century Germany.
A principle Xi Jinping set out for propaganda work: choose the right moment, calibrate the intensity, and aim at real effect.

zh: 治国必治边、治边先稳藏
en: to govern the country, one must govern the borders; to govern the borders, one must first stabilise Tibet
q: to govern the country, one must govern the borders; to govern the borders, one must first stabilise Tibet
py: zhì guó bì zhì biān, zhì biān xiān wěn Zàng
ex: A strategic formula associated with Xi Jinping that treats Tibet as the key to border security and thus to national governance.
The International Military Tribunal for the Far East (1946–48), which tried senior Japanese leaders as Class A war criminals.

lit: International Military Tribunal for the Far East
ex: The International Military Tribunal for the Far East, convened by the Allies in Tokyo (1946–1948) to try Japan's leading wartime figures.

lit: having capacity for inclusion, one becomes great
ex: A classical Chinese saying about the greatness that comes from broad-mindedness. Here it is used to characterise Chinese civilisation's inclusiveness towards ethnic groups and other countries.
A mechanism that allows leniency toward cadres' mistakes made in good-faith innovation or reform, while requiring that errors be identified and corrected.
A policy of tolerating certain mistakes made by officials in the course of reform, intended to encourage them to take initiative while accountability is still enforced.

A three-part policy towards intellectuals in the army set out in a 1942 General Political Department directive. It means accepting them, changing their petty-bourgeois outlook, and assigning work suited to them.
A term for centralised, overall planning of reform objectives, paths and sequencing by the central leadership. It is commonly contrasted with local experimentation.
A policy term for exceptionally gifted students and researchers expected to drive scientific and technological breakthroughs. It features in national talent and education strategies.
An economic measure of the output growth not explained by increases in capital and labour inputs, usually linked to technology and efficiency.

The Annales ambition to study the whole of past society, including economy, society, culture and mentalities, rather than political events alone. Marc Bloch, Lucien Febvre and Braudel are its best-known advocates.

A Hegelian-Marxist category, stressed by Lukács, in which the whole determines how its parts are understood. The article treats it as the method that foreign Marxism inherited and then partly rejected.
Sartre's term for the dynamic, never-completed process of unifying society and knowledge, as opposed to a fixed totality.
Subsidy programmes encouraging households to replace old appliances, vehicles and other goods with new, more efficient ones.
In Lenin's usage, a politics limited to improving workers' conditions within the existing order, without a socialist or revolutionary aim.
A reform-era policy of giving foreign firms access to the Chinese market in exchange for technology transfer, often through joint ventures.

The widespread revival of interest in classical culture, Confucianism and national studies in China since the early 2000s. The author treats it as a social, political and economic phenomenon, not only a cultural one.
The theoretical framework, from the third wave of democratization, that assumes authoritarian regimes will eventually move to Western-style liberal democracy.
The five years after 2020 in which poverty-alleviation policies were kept in place to consolidate results and link them with rural revitalisation. It ended in 2025.
In Marx, Engels and Lenin, the historical stage between capitalism and a developed socialist or communist society. Lenin described Soviet Russia as being in this stage.
A category the author uses to group successive revisions by one translator or body as a single lineage. It lets each revision be recognised without counting it as a wholly new translation.
A characterisation of the current stage in which multinational corporations and international organisations are the main vehicles of capital's global expansion.
A maxim attributed to Kim Il Sung and taken up by Kim Jong Il and Kim Jong Un. The article treats it as the ideological source of the concept.

The first form of ownership in Marx and Engels's account of pre-capitalist history. Chinese scholars disagree over whether it means primitive communal society, an early class society or the 'Asiatic mode of production'.
The hierarchical imperial-era order in which neighbouring states such as Vietnam sent tribute to the Chinese court in return for recognition.
Zheng's preferred term for what Western scholarship calls the tributary system of imperial China. He argues the usual term is a Western imposition.

A paradox formulated by the economist Robert Triffin. A country whose currency serves as the global reserve currency must run external deficits to supply it, which in turn undermines confidence in that currency.
The practice of one person holding the posts of Party general secretary, state president and chairman of the Central Military Commission.

Marx's term in Capital Volume III for the vulgar-economic scheme land–rent, capital–interest, labour–wages, in which each factor appears to generate its own revenue. Marx treats it as a mystified surface form of capitalist relations.
The governing alliance of the African National Congress, the South African Communist Party and the Congress of South African Trade Unions, which won the 1994 election.

The alliance of the ANC, the SACP and COSATU, which has underpinned the post-apartheid government in South Africa since 1994. The SACP and COSATU do not stand separately in elections but support the ANC.

zh: 需求收缩、供给冲击、预期转弱三重压力
py: xūqiú shōusuō, gōngjǐ chōngjī, yùqī zhuǎnruò sānchóng yālì
lit: triple pressure of demand contraction, supply shock and weakening expectations
ex: A formula from the Central Economic Work Conference (December 2021) naming demand contraction, supply shocks and weakening expectations as the main pressures on China's economy. It was repeated in the 2022 Government Work Report.
The nickname for the European Commission, the European Central Bank and the IMF, which oversaw austerity programmes in debtor eurozone countries such as Greece.
Marx's term, in The German Ideology, for a community of freely associated individuals. It is contrasted with the "illusory" or "false" community represented by the bourgeois state.

A German intellectual current of the 1840s (Karl Grün, Moses Hess and others) that recast French and English socialism in terms of Feuerbachian human essence and love. Marx and Engels criticised it in The German Ideology and the Communist Manifesto.
A phrase from Engels's Anti-Dühring for a morality that transcends class antagonism, which he held possible only after class opposition had been abolished and forgotten.
The view, associated with Robert Tucker and Allen Wood, that Marx did not criticise capitalism as unjust. The authors take it as their main target.
A phrase used in Party discourse for converting risks and setbacks into chances for advance. Xi Jinping has repeatedly urged officials to master this skill.
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for the long-term goal of work-style building. Good Party conduct is meant to become everyday habit among officials and then a social norm.
A formulation in official discourse for the latest stage of Marxism, which presents Xi Jinping's thought as its contemporary Chinese form.

A formulation in Chinese Party theory presenting socialism with Chinese characteristics as the contemporary development of Marx's scientific socialism. The article offers it as the answer to liberalism's crisis.

Official shorthand for two replies to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of dynastic rise and fall. The first is Mao Zedong's 1945 answer, popular supervision of government. The second is Xi Jinping's, the Party's self-reform.
The core standard of the poverty alleviation campaign: assurance of adequate food and clothing, plus guarantees of compulsory education, basic medical care and safe housing for rural poor people.
The official standard that cultural products should be judged by both social benefit and economic benefit, with social benefit given priority.
Shorthand for Xi Jinping's 2021 instruction to build the revolutionary old areas better and enable their people to live better lives. It is used as a guideline for old-area development policy.
The Chinese programme of the 1950s–1960s to develop atomic and hydrogen bombs, missiles and an artificial satellite. Official narratives treat it as a model of self-reliant research.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

Vietnam's goals set by its 13th Congress: developed-country status by the 100th anniversary of the state's founding in 2045, with a goal for 2030 tied to the Party's centenary. The article notes they echo the Chinese term.
The school classroom and the "big classroom" of society and practice, which ideological and political teaching seeks to link.
The village Party branch committee and the villagers' committee, the self-governing body elected by villagers. Their relationship is a recurring concern in rural governance.
An official formula about consolidating the Communist Party's ruling position and consolidating the socialist system. It is used to frame ideological work as a matter of political security.

en: two corridors and one economic circle
q: two corridors and one economic circle
ex: A plan proposed by Vietnam in 2004 for the Kunming–Hanoi–Haiphong and Nanning–Lang Son–Hanoi corridors and the Gulf of Tonkin economic circle.
The compulsory university courses in Marxist theory and in ideological and political education, taught to all students. The article treats them as a main channel for anti-cult education.

A label the authors give to Engels's idea that people must first understand nature's laws and the effects of their interventions, then understand and regulate the social effects of production. It is not a standard term in Engels's own text.
The collective name for Mao Zedong's philosophical works "On Practice" and "On Contradiction", written in Yan'an in 1937. They are treated in Chinese Marxism as the core of his philosophical thought.
A formula adopted in 2022 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party's regular commendation of outstanding Party members, outstanding Party workers and advanced grassroots Party organisations.
Engels's description, in his 1883 speech at Marx's graveside, of historical materialism and the theory of surplus value as Marx's two great discoveries, which he said made socialism a science.
Engels's phrase for Marx's materialist conception of history and the theory of surplus value, which together turned socialism from utopia into science.

Official shorthand for the great social revolution led by the Party and the Party's own great self-reform. Since the 20th Party Congress (2022) the stated requirement is that the second should lead the first.
Xi Jinping's periodisation of socialist practice: a first half that built the basic system, and a second half that perfects and develops the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Shorthand for the semi-colonial and semi-feudal theory of modern Chinese society. It was given systematic form in Mao Zedong's 1939 writings.

py: liǎng shǒu zhuā, liǎng shǒu yìng
lit: grasp with two hands, both hands hard
ex: A slogan, associated with Deng Xiaoping, that calls for equal vigour in economic construction and in spiritual or cultural construction.

lit: two historical initiatives (seizing the initiative of history)
ex: Xi Jinping's 2025 formulation of what anti-corruption work has secured: keeping the Party from changing in nature, and the Party's ability to unite the people for national rejuvenation.
A formulation attributed to Xi Jinping describing Guangdong as a window for showing China's reform and opening-up achievements to the world, and for the world to observe them.
Shorthand in Chinese Marxism for the Communist Manifesto thesis that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable.
A phrase summarising the Manifesto's statement that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are equally inevitable. It is used here as a statement of historical law.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Xi Jinping's 2016 formulation that philosophy and social sciences hold an irreplaceable position and their scholars an irreplaceable role in developing socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Engels's formulation in the preface to The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State: the production of the means of life and the production of human beings themselves (reproduction of the species). Chinese textbooks use it to explain early social structures.
Engels's idea that history is determined by the production of the means of life and by the production of human beings themselves, that is, reproduction.
The requirement to strengthen ties between state organs and people's congress deputies and between deputies and the people. The 2025 Deputies Law revision expands the mechanisms for both.
Projects serving major national strategies and building security capacity in key areas, supported by central funding such as ultra-long-term special treasury bonds.
